text:
It was 7:34 pm, and dinnertime was suffering a slight setback. 
 
 `` Get on the floor now!'' barked the masked man. He meant it in a threatening way, not in a way that implied spontaneous vigorous dancing. 
 
 The man pressed the cold barrel of his revolver into the sweaty forehead of Mike. 
 
 `` I do n't wan na get on the floor. The carpet's dirty. I have n't vacuumed it yet, vacuum day is on Saturday-'' 
 
 `` Get on the floor!'' snarled the robber. He pushed Mike onto the carpet. 
 
 Mike did n't have time for this shit. See, he was a busy man. 
 
 `` You are cutting into my fapping time for christ's sake.'' complained Mike. 
 
 `` Hey, did you take the roast out of the oven?'' yelled Rosie from across the hall. She was also held at gunpoint while another robber ransacked their home. 
 
 `` Thought you did.'' answered Mike. 
 
 `` Jesus, you idiot, Mike you had one job-'' 
 
 See, this house belonged to Mike and Rosie Conway. They were a pleasant couple who loved each other very much. 
 
 `` It's 7:30 already. We both know 7:30 is my private time.'' 
 
 `` Who cares about your fun time? That roast is ruined!'' 
 
 The robber's head darted back and forth at he bickering couple who loved each other very much. 
 
 `` Well, maaaaybe, if the both of us had some private time for once-'' 
 
 The robber tried to maintain his intimidating posture, but was stuck wondering why the fuck these people are more concerned about a pot roast than their lives. 
 
 `` Hey both of you, shut the hell up, or you will both die! I mean it!'' yelled the robber. `` I'm going to put a bullet in your brain, you got that?'' said the robber to Mike. 
 
 Rosie snorted. `` His brain is n't up there, aim it towards his dick.'' 
 
 `` Real funny.'' said Mike, dripping with sarcasm. 
 
 `` Should you tell them, or should I?'' said Rosie 
 
 `` Ruins the surprise.'' 
 
 `` Right. Just like that roast. Ruined.'' 
 
 `` Godsakes Rose-'' 
 
 The robber guarding Mike shoved the barrel of the gun into his mouth. 
 
 `` Hey you,'' he motioned for Rosie's attention. `` tell me the combo to your safe right now, or your husband is dead, right here, right now.'' 
 
 Rosie stared into Mike's pleading blue eyes. 
 
 `` Kill him.'' 
 
 Mile threw Rosie a'are you serious?' look. `` Really?'' 
 
 `` This is for that time we spent in London.'' 
 
 `` Rose, baby, I had no idea she was a prostitute. Honest!'' 
 
 `` Oh, here we go...'' 
 
 Suddenly Rosie collapsed to the floor. A red polka dot surrounded her head. 
 
 `` Don, what the hell are you doing? We're here to rob, not kill folks!'' exclaimed the robber near Mike. 
 
 `` You done messed up Don!'' snickered Mike. 
 
 `` I could n't take it man, they just do n't respect us.'' replied the other robber, staring at Rosie's corpse. 
 
 `` Why are n't you afraid, or pleading for mercy? We fucking killed your wife, and now you're laughing? Think this is funny?'' asked the robber. 
 
 Rosie blinked. 
 
 Mile smiled. `` I have this condition... see... it's kind of a funny story.'' 
 
 Rosie put her left arm up. 
 
 `` We brought this expresso machine from this antiques roadshow a while back... you with me here?'' 
 
 Rosie put her right arm up. 
 
 `` Turns out it has a infinite supply. Never runs out. Great right?'' The robbers were ensnared to Mike's story like a moth to a flame. 
 
 Rosie shook it all about. 
 
 `` Oh yeah, I forgot. The stuff that comes outta there? Makes us immortal.'' Mike grinned. 
 
 Rosie stood up and stretched, wiping blood off her forehead. 
 
 `` Sup.'' Rosie cracked her knuckles. 
 
 See, this house belonged to Mike and Rosie Conway. They were a pleasant, immortal couple who loved each other very much. 
 
 And it all started with a cup of coffee.

title: story-32
text:
John walked fast over the green grass. The brow of the hill rose above him, still damp with the morning dew. Around him, the old sheep followed faithfully, while the new lambs ran on ahead, skipping over the cornflowers and pasture-daisies. The standing stones, circling the crown of the hill, collected moisture overnight. Rivulets of water ran down them. They almost seemed to be weeping. 
 
 
 John used his crook to help him up the last, steep climb. His breath came in white pants. The sheep had found the soft grass growing at the base of the stones, and milled around them happily. He leaned his head against a stone, sliding down to sit on the grass. From a pocket he retrieved a little knife, from another a knobbly chunk of wood. Already marks had been made in it: he was turning it into a knotted rope for Margaret. Expertly, he twisted the wood in his hand and set back to whittling. One eye he kept on the sheep. 
 
 
 
 The rays of early morning sun broke through the clouds. In the valley below the hills, the thatched roofs caught it and shone golden. John whistled. An old children's song. At first he did n't recognise it, but then the words came back to him. 
 
 
 
 *The fallen kings are sleeping, child* 
 
 
 *Fear them if they wake, * 
 
 
 *None so cruel as the broken man* 
 
 
 
 *This land is theirs to take. * 
 
 
 The sun slipped behind a cloud and John shuddered. Gooseflesh formed on his arms and the knife slipped, cutting a gash in the base of his thumb. 
 
 
 `` Fuck!'' The expletive echoed from the stones. Hot blood fell onto the grass. John placed the cut to his mouth and licked it clean. The ground beneath him shook. His wound forgotten, John scrambled to his feet and braced against the stones, unsure if he'd been imagining it. The wooden knot fell to the ground, bounced twice in the soft grass and was lost: tumbling into a rabbit hole. Again, the ground shook. This time, John lurched to his knees. 
 
 
 The rabbit hole widened, cracks like hairs tearing away at the ground. Clods of earth began moving, trembling under the force of the shaking. Sheep lost their footing as the hill began to open. 
 
 
 `` No!'' John cried. A lamb toppled, scrabbling towards the ever widening hole. In the centre of the stones it opened, like a black mouth with a thousand tear-trails of white roots running through it. They hung like blind worms, pointing towards the centre of the hill. John held himself against a standing stone, heart pounding. His sheep hurried away from the hole, bolting back for the safety of the village. He wanted to do the same, but the black opening in the hilltop transfixed him. 
 
 
 
 When John had been a child, his father had taken him out to the old Cal road to see troops pass. They had been brightly armoured, sun catching their breastplates and their pointed helmets. Many coloured standards flew above them, wind-whipped and hopeful. They bore the signs of bears, of lions, of huge dogs with snarling teeth. Most of all, John remembered the noise. The jingle and the fresh stamp of the horses, the grate of metal on metal and the low sound of horns. 
 
 
 
 Now the horns sounded from the depths of the hill, and the grate scraped against John's teeth. Tears came from his eyes at the sound of marching feet and he clutched the stone, bloodied hand smeared against it. 
 
 
 
 From the mouth of the hill, between the crown of standing stones, came an army of death. Their faces rotted and peeling: a thousand staring sockets of eyes from where the crows and the worms had eaten them. Yellow ligaments and whitening bones smiled at John, the teared and tattered banners flying from rusting petards. Their swords were red with it, their armour burnished with age. At their head rode a corpse on a deathly white horse, wearing a crown made from broken iron and black stones. 
 
 
 The man on the horse looked down at John with empty eyes. 
 
 
 
 `` All hail King John,'' he said. With a skeletal hand, he removed the iron crown. `` First of his name, last of his blood.'' 
 
 
 
 The corpse placed the crown on the shepherd's head, and the horns bellowed for the world to hear.

title: story-33
text:
Her bright eyes fluttered open, clouded with sleep and confusion. A handsome face and a gentle smile floated above her. 
 
 “ Welcome back, ” the face whispered tenderly. Lovingly. 
 
 Snow ’ s forehead furrowed in worry. She couldn ’ t quite remember, but “ back ” was someplace she was quite certain she didn ’ t want to be. “ Back ” was bad, for some reason. She didn ’ t want to be welcomed to it. 
 
 “ Can you move? ” the face asked again. “ You ’ ve been asleep for a long time. ” 
 
 “ Asleep? ” she murmured, puzzled. “ Thought I was dead. ” 
 
 The face broke into an even wider grin. “ True love is a force greater than death. ” 
 
 Snow looked, really looked, at the face for the first time. It belonged to a devastatingly attractive man, who was firm, slender, muscled and thick in all of the right places. His clothes were well-made and his finger glinted with a signet ring. 
 
 “ I ’ ve been searching for you, ” he supplied as Snow took him in. “ For months, I ’ ve been looking. I ’ d almost given up hope of finding you. And when I did, I thought – I thought it was too late. I thought you ’ d already slipped away from the living. ” 
 
 Clarity returned in bits and pieces with each word he spoke. Words like “ searching ” and “ hope ” and “ living ” stuck out especially. She could remember doing the first and losing the second, which had made the third … unappealing. 
 
 “ There was an apple, ” Snow said, uncertainly, as she fought to sit up. She looked around in mild surprise at the flowers that lined her body, strewn across a satin shroud. The dwarves, then. She smiled at the roses and felt a rush of sadness at the thought of who had put them there, and the terrible costs they had borne while she lived among them. 
 
 “ What happened to the dwarves? ” she asked. “ I tried – I was trying to keep them – safe … ” she trailed off as she caught sight of the seven white stones that stood in a solemn row at the foot of the pyre. 
 
 “ I ’ m sorry, ” the man said as he followed her gaze. “ There were five stones already here when I arrived. I found the bodies of two more. It seemed fitting to bury them with the others. They looked like they ’ d been tending to the graves. ” 
 
 She choked back a sob. She ’ d failed, then. It had all been for nothing. 
 
 “ Please don ’ t cry, ” the man said as he knelt in front of her and gathered her cold hands into his warm ones. “ You ’ re still here. I found you! I scarcely dared hope that I would ever see you like this, with life inside of you. Do you remember your kiss? Do you remember how I woke you? ” 
 
 “ A true love ’ s kiss? ” Snow asked scornfully through her tears. “ Did you kiss the dwarves? Did you try and breathe life back into them? I don ’ t even know your name. ” 
 
 “ But it woke you! ” he argued. “ Only a true love ’ s kiss can break spells like the one you were under. That must mean it ’ s true love! ” 
 
 She swung her feet down from the pyre and pushed herself up unsteadily. “ You know nothing of love, ” she said quietly as she approached the seven white stones. “ Love is taking in a stranger for no other reason than she needs your help. ” 
 
 She heard the man ’ s sharp intake of breath as she pulled a small dagger from the sheath hidden in the sash at her waist. 
 
 “ Love is finding her interests, her favorite songs, her favorite foods, so that you can make her dinner and laugh and sing with you. Love is giving companionship and warmth and kindness to a girl who ’ s never had any of that in her life and has done nothing to deserve it. ” 
 
 Snow knelt in front of the stones and touched each in turn, a small caress over the names carved into their faces. 
 
 “ Love is defending her against all comers, at the cost of your own life, ” she said. “ Love is watching your brothers die, and continuing to defend her even though you know the cost. ” 
 
 “ No! ” the man cried as she laid open her wrist with the dagger, blood flowing forth from her flesh like water from a spring. Snow ’ s eye ’ s flashed with pain and anger, a silent warning to keep his distance as she cut deeply into the other. 
 
 “ Love is eating a poisoned apple in the vain hope that your death will mean that those who remain might live! ” she shouted and sobbed. “ They loved me! And I loved them so dearly and all I could do for them was die! Why would you take that from me? How could you take that away? ” 
 
 She collapsed in front of the stones, crying as though her heart had been torn out, until the crying faded and then stopped. 
 
 He finally found himself able to move again, long after he could have done any good. He knelt beside the girl and the seven graves for a long time before he rose and began to dig an eighth.

title: story-34
text:
After pacing back and forth for exactly nine minutes and sixteen seconds, you finally stop and look around. Glancing down, you see you're still clutching your cell phone in your sweaty palm. A torrent of fear, dread, anxiety, panic, depression and slight hunger crashes relentlessly against your chest. This has been going on for nine minutes and fifteen seconds. You ca n't breathe. You ca n't think. You feel like eating some chips but most of all you feel like screaming until someone hands you a large cold glass of lager because maybe drinking away problems 
 
 
 You were in trouble. 
 
 
 Oh yes. 
 
 
 You nervously unclench your hand though it is n't easy at this point, the joints locked in their position. When you finally pry your hand apart, you see the damage as be done, not undone as you had been childishly hoping. The text had been sent to the wrong person. It happens from time to time and usually the damage is nothing, people understand that mistakes happen all the time. People get confused or fingers slip, no big deal right? Not for you. You had just sent your ex-girlfriend a rather heated rant about her when it had meant to go to your mate, Justin. 
 
 
 You and Jen had broken up a week ago, she had burrowed your new car to go down to the local pub. On the way there, she wound up hitting a lorry and managed to scratch the side of it pretty badly. Since she was unemployed, the damage had to be paid by you, and while you had a decent job teaching at the local university, the pay was rubbish. The whole indecent may have an accident, and rather minor, it was the final straw to break the camel's back. You and Jen had a massive fight that night, you called her names, she threw glasses, you complained about her mother, she mocked your new haircut, you called her some names, and she left. 
 
 
 So to cheer yourself up, you took some time off and planned to go up North for a few days to clear your head. Justin said he'd tag along and you'd both have a great time. But as you were texting with Justin, both of you pointing out Jen's flaws and horrid habits, you ended up texting her by mistake. Since you had broken up, it could have seemed harmless but Jen's mother was a rather frightening woman who also happened to be an officer of the law, which would explain why most of your paycheck goes to paying off rubbish tickets and fines. You and Justin were just messing around, talking about the trip and Jennifer and now you were losing your mind. 
 
 
 Bits of the big fight were starting to come back. 
 
 
 Your stomach churned as you remembered her marching outside to your new car and keying it, adding to the damage she had done. You had to see if she had checked her texts or not. Or if her mother had. That was even worse! Quickly texting the situation to Justin, you waste no time running outside and jogging down to where Jen would be. Would you apologize or would another fight push you two further apart? As you ran, you saw her mother was calling. A wild shudder threatened to rip your spine to shreds. Did you dare let it go or would you bravely pick it up? 
 
 
 `` H-hello?'' You answer as you slow your jogging to dodge the elderly couple in front of you, taking their sweet time. Before her mother can begin to shew you out, you make the first strike. `` I'm so so sorry, truly I am.'' You ramble, out of breath. 
 
 
 `` You have some nerve!'' The woman's shrill voice cried back. 
 
 
 `` It was an accident, I'm sorry!'' You finally get across the crosswalk and are almost there. `` She's the one who left, I could n't stop it.'' You point out as you stop dead in your tracks. The phone slips from your hand and the hunger fades away, despite the smell of fish and chips coming from the pub across the street. The laughter of drunken men and women fades away as you push the iron gate open and step onto the solemn property. Quickly you snag the phone before you fully enter. Once back on track, your heart slows down. Where could Jennifer be? Was she ready for round two? Or maybe you'd both share a laugh over a pint and reminisce? 
 
 
 As you stare into space, someone approaches you. `` You're late, Devon.'' She says. It's Jen's mother and you smile to her, mostly at your idiocy. 
 
 
 `` Sorry, sorry. I know the text was awful but it wasan accident. I was hoping to talk to Jen and maybe work things out. I mean it's silly to throw three years away over a silly accident.'' You shrug and look around. `` I thought she'd be here by now, ready to punch me in the arm and call me a pillock or something.'' 
 
 
 The woman's eyes water and she looks down at your hand. `` That's her cell phone, Devon.'' She pointed out. `` You know the crowd should n't be kept waiting. It's due to rain soon too, she loved the rain. She would have loved today.'' She said and reached down for your hand. You give her a look of confusion. `` Her funeral, it's today.'' She began to lead you down the gray pathway. `` She got into a car accident last week, she did n't make it.'' 
 
 
 `` No, I just texted her. I mean I did n't mean to, we broke up last week.'' 
 
 
 `` Devon, she died, she died looking at your text.'' Her mother said, voice wavering between pity and agony. `` Please, come speak. It's okay...'' 
 
 
 But it was n't okay. How could it be okay? You had just texted her something awful meant for someone else. How could her mother just brush it off? You had to make it right, you shook your head and ran ahead of her and found Jennifer. `` Jen! There you are, that text was a joke, I know you did n't mean to walk out on me, but I want you back. I'm sorry. I know you're sorry. I'm sorry too. I'm so sorry, please... just come home.'' You fell to your knees as you looked down at her white casket, your selected family and friends just watch as you struggle to accept the reality that has been created by a stupid mistake.

title: story-35
text:
Mark scowled at the heat. 
 
 The last wisps of air-conned cold retreated quickly, allowing the ashen winds to lash sharply at his exposed face. Gripping the metal railing to steady himself, he struggled briefly with his glare-shades and drew his hood down protectively in time for another spray of sand that lashed the hull, then that sickening lurch as they plunged down another wave. It had been exhilarating, gliding across the sea of glass like birds on the wing. Of course, even birds had to drink and his enthusiasm had dried up with their stores on this fools errand. 
 
 Kara whooped as they began another sharp assent. Mark clenched his teeth at the change but looked ahead to where exposed raven hair and white robes fluttered quickly in the winds. He called out but she could n't hear, her hands clutched to the railings at the bow and voice whooping loudly to the sky. He cursed his luck, working his way carefully forwards between each rise and fall. 
 
 Slowly dying of thirst had put a lot of things in perspective. Firstly, he should never have left the ocean, that snaking great lake that surrounded the Antarctic territories. At least then the money had been easy, life a simple matter of visiting each island and city-state and even the occasional skirmish with a Raider from the Dust lands. He understood now what sent those savages crazy - this endless sea of glass was barren in a way the ocean never was, the heat scrambled the mind and those roving bands of Rad-dust... well. 
 
 Kara actually let go of the railing, screaming happily and leaning into the next fall as they cut down the next dune. Ellie was right, the heat had cooked her... 
 
 `` Well we need a Captain''. He'd looked at the man in his odd penguin suit curiously, always baffled by the people of Cent-Gov but drawn as always by the money. `` And that *thing* can cross the Wastes'' he'd replied sceptically. The man laughed and patted a sleek metallic hull no different from his own ship, but bearing strange flat protrusions that faced the ground and wierd machinery to her aft. `` she'll do better than that'' the man assured him, he was given a sad smile and led around it's length,'once, we dreamed of sailing the stars... this was to be our engine, to save what was but, like so much else, we were too slow and too late...' Mark resisted rolling his eyes and patted the admittedly sleek vessel skeptically, `` so she flies across the stars?'' The man had laughed, `` No, we do n't have the fuel to get her into space''. Mark felt his dissapointment trump his skepticism and scowled,'so is there a point to this story?' At that the man had perked up and gave him a broad, knowing smile.'*We* do n't have the fuel, but this vessel can take you to our long lost brothers, and maybe, just maybe...'' 
 
 He hit the prow hard, too hard. He cried out as he began tumbling forwards but a hand yanked him back hard, and laughed heartily as he clung ever tighter to the rail. `` Kara, you need to come inside'' he yelled, the winds snatching his voice. Kara laughed madly, clearly lost, and he sighed internally, grabbing at her wrist to begin the inevitable struggle back inside. She resisted, but to his surprise embraced him warmly. He stiffened up at the contact, suddenly at a loss, he needed to... 
 
 `` It's okay'' she muttered into his ear, and when he looked up her eyes were sparkling, alight with joy. 
 
 `` Kara...'' 
 
 She smiled, `` Mark, It's okay'' and she nodded past him, whooping as they fell again into a dune. He cursed, having to turn and grip the rail, sand lashing his cheeks, hands blistering and... 
 
 It ended. 
 
 Mark gasped, only catching a glimpse before they descended again, but he had seen it. Blue. Water. An end to the wastes. Four years, done at last and. 
 
 Kara laughed, and he joined her, whooping at the top of his lungs. They'd made it. 
 
 Kara hugged him again and they cried and embraced. She kissed his head, sobbing and giggling. `` Did you see?'' 
 
 Of course he'd seen.'Water'. A dream. 
 
 Kara laughed and shook her head rapidly.'No, Mark, beyond the water was a mountain, and on that mountain, I saw *light*...''

title: story-36
text:
The sound of sirens in the distance brought a wicked smile out beneath his bearded, mud caked face. He stood there in the heavy rain, feet planted in the wet soil of my father ’ s garden, crooked teeth catching the reflection of the lightning striking nearby. In the dark torrent of thunder and wind I can hear his low laugh. He ’ s enjoying this. 
 
 I lower my rifle, moving it slowly from his face down to his feet. “ You ’ re not going to get away with this. ” I say plainly, mostly to reassure my sister, whom the creep is holding tightly against himself some 15 feet in front of me. 
 
 “ I already have, dear boy! ” He calls back, as he casts a glance to his left at my brother lying face down in the mud, the bloody hilt of an old kitchen knife sticking out from his side. “ I did what I came here to do, now I will be going. ” His filthy yellow poncho rippled in the wind, occasionally revealing the pistol he had pressed against my sisters back. 
 
 “ Let me go! ” my sister shrieked, as the police cars slammed into the front yard. My brother had managed to call them just before the creep chased my sister and him outside and attacked him with the knife. The look of madness on his face has only grown more intense since I leveled the rifle at him just minutes ago, and with the sound of car doors opening and closing and the flashing red and blue lights bouncing between the rain drops, his face twisted beyond sane. 
 
 As the police approached my eyes widened, I knew their arrival would only make the creep more dangerous. As if in slow motion, I watched as they drew their pistols, rifles, and shotguns on him. They all barked orders at him, and he just stared back with that sick smile. He let out one last heavy snicker before turning his gaze on me. He pulled the gun off of my sister and raised it toward me. I watched as it climbed through the air, breaking the rain drops destined for the earth beneath it. I saw the black hole from which my fate would soon be dispensed staring deep into my chest. I witnessed his finger begin to tighten around the trigger. Then I saw his eye change from insane delight to udder confusion. The world fell silent around us, and the red and blue police car lights bounced off the handle of the kitchen knife, which was now wedged up into his chest just beneath his heart. The creep let out his final breath in a muddled whimper, a whimper that told me he had suddenly realized what happened. A whimper that was half frustration, half bewilderment, but without a drop of regret. Slowly the world around us came back into focus. The quack of the ducks nearby eased the volume back on, and then the sirens and the thunder chimed in. 
 
 My brother collapsed back to the mud after his quick return of the blade back to the creep. My sister grabbed him and suddenly paramedics and police were as abundant as the rain drops. We all ended up at the hospital shortly after. Thankfully, only the creep ’ s soul left it ’ s earthly vessel that day.

title: story-37
text:
Three appeals, fifteen years, four months, nine days, two hours, and some number of minutes and seconds ago I was convicted of murder in the first degree by a jury of my peers. That term always irked me: `` a jury of my peers''. I guess they were able to track down twelve other people with sons or daughters held hostage in a secluded barn for weeks before being violently raped to death. They must have been saints. They must have been able to see beyond the monster who took my Michelle from me; they must have been able to see humanity. Such a pity they were n't actually there, otherwise they would have seen the smugness and arrogance. Untouchable. After all these years, it still brings a smile to my face. Untouchable. The detectives on the case were told to back down, one even got demoted for pursuing the case in his free time. Untouchable. Rich kid with connected parents. He had a history: handful of DUIs, possession with intent to distribute, alleged rape. Untouchable. *She screamed for you until her voice was hoarse. How does it feel to know I got away with it and there's not a damn thing you can do? I'm fucking untouchable. * 
 
 Maybe nobody ever told him about the rage of a grieving father, maybe it never crossed his mind, but when I put my fist in his face, I'm pretty sure'untouchable' was the last thing he was thinking. The rest was easy. Chloroform on a rag kept him down. His fake friends were too busy with the bottle service I provided to even notice he'd been in the bathroom just a bit too long. And nobody batted an eye at the caring friend helping his overly drunk buddy out into the alley to puke. Or get loaded into my trunk. 
 
 From there we went to the barn. After his being acquitted, the son of a bitch gifted the land to me. The prick. Originally, my plan was to burn it to the ground and build a memorial. But memorials were for people whose justice had been served. Hers had n't been. I spent months preparing. Playing the lost and broken father, I took their out of court settlement to drop any civil charges. They financed my revenge. I do n't see a need to go into details about what occurred. What happened is between him, me, and whatever deity is in charge of torture. Suffice it to say, I made it last. Evidently, the first officers on the scene quit the force a month later. For that, I do feel bad. When they showed up at my apartment I went quietly. I'd been dead since they found her, now I was just waiting for my body to catch up. 
 
 The trial was quick. The judge condemned me for my'heinous and medieval premeditated atrocity'. A family friend, I'm sure. The jury deliberated for an hour and if there was a very guilty verdict, I would have received it. Prison was n't awful. No picnic in the park, but it's not like I really had much to live for. On my third day an inmate decided to take a shot at the belt. I served him stainless steel lunch table as his last meal. Maniacal laughter warded off any other would be hot shots. After that, I spent my days in my cell reading. 
 
 Some lawyer contacted me to let me know because of the nature of my crime, they were going to use a new and experimental drug for my execution. Supposedly, it makes you hallucinate your worst fears until you die of cardiac arrest. Wonder who pulled the strings on that one. Dying is dying, nobody knows that better than me and I told him so. He started packing up and before he left, he said one last thing. *They want you to suffer. * I do n't think he saw me smile. 
 
 I asked for a medium rare ribeye, garlic mashed potatoes, cheesy broccoli and some scotch. They gave me a stale burger and saltines. That was the first time since the barn I actually felt angry. Influence can really be a bitch. 
 
 `` Mark Webb. You have been found guilty of murder in the first degree by a jury of your peers and sentenced to death by lethal injection. Chemicals will be injected into your bloodstream causing cardiac arrest and your demise. May God have mercy on your soul. Do you have any last words?'' 
 
 They have me strapped to this uncomfortable cross of a bed. In the other room the family, friends, and lawyers watch with unblinking eyes. I smile as I turn my head to face them. 
 
 `` For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. He screamed your name until his voice went hoarse. Burn in hell you fucks.'' 
 
 I get comfortable and close my eyes as they prep the injection. I'm chasing Michelle around our yard while Jane weeds the garden. There's a slight pinch as the needle slides into my arm. Michelle shrieks with joy running wildly away from me. My body suddenly feels heavy, my head groggy. *Daddy! Daddy! * she screams. Everything begins fading to black. *Daddy! Daddy! * 
 
 *Please! Save me! *

title: story-38
text:
I rammed the dining room table against the front door as Bulbasaur used vine whip to close all of the curtains and shutters in the house.'What's happening?' mother asked frantically, clutching an over-fed Pidgeotto to her chest. I gestured for her to *shush* as I swept through the house to ensure every window and door was locked and bolted. 
'Keep it down, there's somebody outside' I hissed through gritted teeth, as I peeped through a gap in the living room black-out curtains. We held our breathe, and through the heavy silence could be heard the the unmistakable sound of crackling fire. 
 
 
'Shit' I grunted, as I caught the silhouette of something with large wings and a flame'd tail pass by the front window. I threw Bulbasaur a quick nod before ducking and crawling back towards mother, who was still huddled with her useless bird. Bulba followed along behind me quietly, and then we all sat hunched in the middle of the darkened living room, our breathes held in unison.'What's happening?' my mother asked again, in a whisper that was almost a whimper. Her eyes frantically searched each of the window curtains for further silhouettes, but there were none, for the moment. 
 
 
 I begun to unclasp the four pokeballs that were attached to my belt and place them on the floor in front of me.'We need to get out of here' I said softly, placing my hand on her shoulder. Bulbasaur was lay beside me, and had extended a vine to stroke the shivering Pidgeotto's head gently. I could n't help but smile at the gesture. I turned to my mother, my eyes leveling with hers,'It's called The Purge. People are using their Pokemon to kill each other. Team Rocket issued the ultimatum a day ago; anybody not participating will have their Pokemon seized. They're invoking anarchy for their own ends.' I picked up one of the pokeballs from the floor and held it between my right index finger and thumb, expanding and contracting it in what was an unconscious habit.'That's what the commotion was earlier; people were fighting outside. I'm glad you did n't see it. But we're not safe here; we're not safe inside. We're only safe if we're hidden; if people do n't know where we are. People know we're in here, and they'll try to break in to steal our Pokemon, to give themselves a better chance out there'. Mother's grasp on Pidgeotto tightened, and her eyes widened, almost comically.'No... Not Pidge...' she muttered, tears beginning to pool in her eyes. I smiled at her then, feeling a sort of relief in her quiet, desperate response, which was favourable to a frantic one.'We'll be okay. I'll get us out of here, we're going somewhere safe' I reassured her. She returned my comfort with a weak smile and looked about to speak when a sudden and resounding *crash* came from the front door. It was unmistakably the sound of somebody, or rather *something big*, trying to force entry. 
 
 The door rattled violently on it's hinges for a moment and my mother crawled back frantically toward the farthest wall, with Pidgeotto still in her arms. Bulbasaur stood beside me growling almost inaudibly and awaiting command. I looked to the expanded pokeball in my hand and tried to think. The door crashed again. Then there was quiet, for a moment. Then the low voice of a man shattered that silence.'Alright folks, ah' know you're in there. May as well throw whatever pokeballs ya' got out the window and we'll let you live. Otherwise mah' Kangaskhan here gon na' rip your doors off and come in and kill you all, and then we'll jus' be takin' your pokemon anyway. What's it gon na be, then? I'll give you five seconds to make up yer' minds. Come on now, I do n't really wan na do nothin' nasty today to nobody'. 
 
 I looked back at mother, who lay crumpled in a terrified heap on the floor with that ridiculous fat bird all feathers and beak wedged between her arms, and felt an overwhelming feeling of sadness that almost knocked me to the floor. I could n't stand to see her so scared. I heard the man outside sound up again and shout, in an almost gleeful tone'Time's up.' 
 
 At that point I think I blacked out, as a hundred different things happened all at once. I remember the door crashing down and the sound of it being so incredibly loud that I wondered whether the house might come down on top of us. I remember bulbasaur leaping toward the light, that had come flooding through a huge hole where the door had been, and I remember seeing him be flung across the room like a plush toy and then lying still, having landed not far from where my mother was lay. I think she was screaming and saying something but I ca n't recall what it was. I remember the kangaskhan's beady eyes as they flitted around the room, identifying it's targets. Pidgeotto had managed to free itself from mother's grasp and had flown directly at the kangaskhan's face, in an attempt to ward it off. Stupid, fat, brave thing. I remember the sight of it disappearing into the kangaskhan's mouth in a flash of feathers. Everything seemed to go quiet, then. I was vaguely aware that my mother was still screaming. I was vaguely aware that I was bleeding from my head as I could taste that familiar metallic taste dripping into my mouth. I felt something cold in my hand; it was a pokeball. Yes, my father's pokeball. One of his most treasured ones. I'd forgotten I'd even been holding on to it. He always told me not to use his pokemon. Maybe he would n't mind me using it just this once. In what felt like extreme-slow motion I flung the ball in the kangaskhan's direction, and it bounced of of it's chest, hit the floor and then a blinding light exploded in the room. 
 
 I rushed to my mother, who was lay a crippled and sobbing mess, and took her by the hand to drag her to her feet. Turning I rushed to bulbasaur, who was still motionless, and hoisted him over my shoulder. Finally with my free hand I scooped the remaining pokeballs off of the floor and dumped them into my coat pocket.'We're leaving' I muttered to my mother, who groaned something in response. The kangaskhan and it's trainer both were stood motionless in my doorway still, paralyzed with fear of the new threat that had presented itself. I had no time for mercy now; we had to move. To get far away from there. I shouted the command and hoped with everything I had that it would be obeyed, 
 
 **'Dragonite, Hyper Beam! `` ** 
 
 A moment passed and nothing happened. I held my breathe. Gradually another bright light began to fill the room, and then came utter destruction. But, for that day at least, it was n't our own.

title: story-39
text:
`` Hey babe, what's up?'' I said, answering my smartphone as I casually strolled home from another day at the office. 
 
 `` Hey honey! How was work today?'' 
 
 `` Pretty great! Tom played a prank on someone this morning, something about a stapler in jello. Funny shit.'' 
 
 `` HA! He always comes up with the craziest stuff, you'll have to tell me all about it when you get home. You pick up a gallon of milk for dinner?'' 
 
 `` Got it right here, I'm headin' home right now.'' 
 
 `` Wonderful, I'll see you soon then! One more thing; you hear about that new app everyone's going crazy about?'' 
 
 `` Nah I have n't, what is it?'' 
 
 `` It's called iFuture. Download it asap, it's like, revolutionary shit. I better go, Chelsey is crying again, this parenting stuff is no joke. Love you!'' 
 
 `` Alrighty sweetie, I love you too! Be home in the nigh'' 
 
 I tap the red end button and immediately go to the App Store. 5 starred, 1.5 million reviews. This really must be'revolutionary shit,' then. 
 
 I roll my eyes, tap download and double click out, immediately tapping Reddit and scrolling through the front page for a couple seconds. 
 
 After giving it a minute to download, I click out of Reddit and tap iFuture, starting up the app and letting it hum to life. The typical loading circle appears, and the app requests to use the front facing camera. I tap `` yes,'' and I'm promptly brought to a start up paragraph.. 
 
 `` Welcome to iFuture, your future self lies only seconds away! Simply take a selfie and let our time machine transfer your brain waves into the future, and you'll be face-to-face with your future self!'' 
 
 Sounds like bullshit to me; it'll probably just add some wrinkles on my forehead, gray my hair, maybe recede my hairline. But fuck it, right? I'll try it. 
 
 I lift up my phone and snap a picture of my face, and let the app crank it's gears to scan my face to make a shitty photoshop of a 50-year-old me. 
 
 The app buzzes with a satisfied tone, but instead of an expected, oldified picture of my face, an error message appears that reads, `` Future not found. Deepest apologies.'' 
 
 `` The fu..'' 
 
 A speeding, cherry red sports car smashes into my right side and breaks almost every bone on the impact side of my body, along with impaling my lungs and breaking my neck clean off from my spine. A woman screams in horror behind my lifeless body and a man starts to dial the local police station. 
 
 Another man watches my crippled, demolished body almost joyfully, a smirk dancing on his face. `` Serves the dumbass right,'' he utters. `` Even kids know to look both ways and get their heads out of their phones before they cross the fuckin' street.''

They do n't hear. 
 
 No... They hear. They do n't... what call it? They do n't... *get. * 
 
 Bright come up, many times since I do this thing. Dark go over, too. Many dark. Many *many* darks. I make sounds at them. Sounds that mean things. They look at me. Their eyes make... bad shapes. They grunt and point to first thing I give sound. 
 
 `` Fire.'' I say. They grunt and point. 
 
 They not want me. They want me to stay with fire... I sit. I work with fire. I play with stick. They sit, too, after hunt. They watch me play with stick. I make shape of game they hunt. Game that is over fire. Game we... what call it? Game we... cook? Yes, good word. *Cook*. 
 
 I make shape of game we cook. Game we...'is' for many? No,'is' for one. *Are* for many. Sounds good. I make shape of game we ARE cook... Are cook-*ing*. This thing. When this thing happen to me? Why sound for everything? I make shape... I *draw* the game we are cooking over the fire. I... *am* draw*ing* the game we are cooking over the fire. 
 
 How I tell them if I still not know all the sounds? Like... What do I call the Bright in sky? Rude to give it a sound by myself. Bright is so important. Bright warms the land. Bright makes us see. Bright is very bright and big and far... More far and more big... no... Far-more, big-more... Far*ther* and big*ger* than any thing. And I still do not have a sound for Bright. 
 
 `` This is hard.'' I say. 
 
 They make bad noises and bad shapes with their eyes. 
 
 `` Ffis Ard,'' my son says. I smile and pat him. He smiles and points at my drawing. `` Uh! uh? BAAAFFF. uh? lo!'' 
 
 Baaaff-uh. Lo. What is he saying? Maybe he will do this with me... maybe he... *helps*? 
 
 `` Ba. Fu. Lo.'' I say. I tap my drawing with my stick. `` Ba-fu-lo. Buffalo. Yes. Good.'' 
 
 My son makes happy noise. `` Yss! Goo! Ba-fulo!'' He smiles. He pushes his face in my arm and holds me. I feel good and hold him, too. 
 
... Son needs a sound. NO. Son needs special sound. Son needs *name*. I open my mouth and I make the first sound I can think. `` Jhon,'' I say. `` You... You Jhon.'' I poke him with the stick. `` This...'' I poke my drawing. `` This is Buffalo.''

 `` Dadyyyyh!'' he says, and puts arms in the air. 
 
 `` Yes... good. I am Daddy. You are Jhon. This is Buffalo.'' 
 
 Jhon makes small happy sounds, g-g-g-g-g... Gi... *giggles* at me. He rubs his eyes. He pushes his face in my chest. `` Lah voooo...'' he says, quiet. I do not know for sure. But I think so... 
 
 `` Lah voo too,'' I say. 
 
... They not look at me so bad after that...

title: story-42
text:
The aged hilt glinted where it lay against her cloak. In a swift, smooth motion, she drew the blade out, holding it to her side in a still, casual grip. 
 
 Light rippled off the surface of the blade like water. 
 
 `` What... is that?'' 
 
 It was n't a sword. It could n't be a sword. It was a treasure, it was a relic of some long forgotten spirit. It could n't, should n't have belonged to a mere vagabond wandering along the open roads. 
 
 Yet it did. 
 
 He gripped his own weapon tighter, his men fanning out around him as they attempted to surround the lone traveller. 
 
 `` Gut her.'' their leader muttered roughly. The bandits rushed forward. He rushed forward when someone pushed him forward. 
 
 She wasted no time. In a flurry of cloak and robe she was moving, slipping delicately between their cudgels and spears. That sword, that glorious sword was flowing through the melee, leaving behind a tide of red. 
 
 He almost did n't notice when she appeared right in front of him, cutting him down. He met her eyes, calm and dark and tinged with that weary, mild sorrow that only those with no home could understand. 
 
 Unexpectedly, the sword slipped. 
 
 Perhaps the wielder was not used to the unusual length of the blade. Perhaps the sword itself had decided to spare him, shifting away in that brief moment of chance when he stumbled back. 
 
 He fell, covered by another body. 
 
 It was over too quickly. She stood alone amidst fallen men. Her sword blazed in the dying light of the sun. 
 
 There was not a single drop of blood on its perfect form, nor on the maiden who carried it. It was sharp, too sharp. 
 
 He watched her walk down the winding, wilderness road. Soon her figure was swallowed by the evening mists. 
 
 He stared around the clearing of corpses, feeling as if he'd woken from a dream. 
 
... 
 
 *This is the Leafblade, a cutting from the great World Tree. * 
 
 The lone traveller wandered down the empty dirt roads, following the setting sun. The blade hung heavy at her back. 
 
 *This sword... its yours' now. * 
 
 Old memories were stirring inside her, swirling inside her mind as the mists of the world around her. 
 
 *You're not dead yet, old man. Why are you passing this old thing to me? * 
 
 *Heh. This is one blade that is meant to be passed down. I had to make sure you possessed it... for the next hero. * 
 
 *Next... hero? * 
 
 She traced her way towards the distant mountains, drawing her cloak close as the chill of the night set in. 
 
 *There must always be a hero, for darkness always falls. This is the duty of our line... to preserve a legacy of honour and salvation. * 
 
 *That's too big a word for me to handle, old man. * 
 
 The sky darkened. Stars began to glow faintly in the firmament far above, wreathed in purple, sunlit clouds. 
 
 *I do n't believe it is. You'll rise to the challenge when the time comes. * 
 
 The mountains loomed before her. Beyond the mountains lay a kingdom, shrouded in darkness. Beyond the kingdom, her home, one of many villages devastated in the wake of the dark mists. 
 
 *Believe me, you'll rise. *

title: story-43
text:
Decisions always seem easier when you do not actually have to make them. Easier to say you'd do things differently than an individual, without the knowledge of what you've promised. 
 
 `` Hurry back, the doctors do n't think she'll make it much longer, and you know they're ready to close air travel.'' 
 `` I promise I'll be there. You know I ca n't control her condition. But, I will be there.'' 
 `` I love you. Try to get some sleep on the flight.'' 
 `` Thanks. I love you, too.'' 
 `` See you soon.'' 
 
 I sit in the first coffee shop of the Abidjan airport. My flight back is in an hour. Through checkpoints, and red tape, and inspections. Looking around, you could n't imagine it would happen. This place is so much cleaner than the horrible depiction of Africa in today's media. If you wiped the language away, you would n't be able to tell the difference between this and any normal populace. Amazing how perceptions defines reality until met with the very harsh truth. 
 
 A man sits down across from me. A jean-jacket pulled over a dirty black hoodie. Hood pulled all the way up, leaving only a stark-white, well defined chin, scratched and scarred from years of weathering. He pulls a smoke out from his jacket pocket, lights, and drags. 
 
 `` What the fuck do you think you're doing?'' It almost slid out from the darkness, instead of being spoken. I glanced around the shop. Countless sleeping people, no one awake, even the kid who sold me this coffee must have disappeared somewhere on break. I coughed and wiped away the spittle with a napkin. 
 
 `` I'm drinking a coffee... This is a coffee shop. Conventional norm says buy something.'' I replied vindictively. 
 
 `` What do you think will happen if you make it home?'' Again, it seemed to materialize into existence. 
 
 `` What the hell is it to you? I do n't need to tell you anything.'' I said, as the room became colder. Everything around me started to fade, and fuzz. 
 
 `` You're ignorance is usually appreciated'' the man chuckled, `` but this is far more important than just you. You must feel it in you, yes?'' 
 
 I'm fighting back a sneeze while a feeling of dread bleeds into my stomach. The caffeine is making me nauseous. 
 
 `` Look, I'm not interested in your paranoia. And quit blowing that goddamn smoke in my face, I have asthma.'' I growled angrily as I started to cough. 
 
 `` I wish you could recognize what you're doing. Not just to me... but to everyone. Not that I care about the health of others, moreso the continuation of others. If you stay on this path, I will become pointless.'' I could feel the vibration rattle in my chest with every word that he uttered. 
 
 `` Who... who are you? How do you know?'' 
 
 `` Do n't be simple. I'm here to ask you to stop. To walk back to your hotel. And wait for my knock again.'' He ashed in the middle of the table. 
 
 `` I ca n't do that. I need to be there for her.'' 
 
 `` Ah, humanity. Self-serving til the end. For what? Two more minutes of time together? Quite a sacrifice for something so miniscule.'' His speech cold and collected. 
 
 `` Those two minutes mean everything to me.'' I breathed. 
 
 `` To the world?'' An angry retort. 
 
 But what of the world? Should it be condemned? For my selfishness? I cough again, harder. 
 
 `` I'm going.'' I stood up. I left him alone. I made my my flight. A promise is a promise. 
 
 Back at the shop, a weathered creature sighs. It pulls a list from inside his jacket. The list begins extending, unfolding over and over. 
 
 `` I suppose it's time to work.''

text:
# # # # # # [ ] ( # dropcap ) 
 
 The room which Faith had been given was small but well furnished, its owners proudly displaying their modest power and prosperity. The walls were made of thick timbers and covered with heavy tapestries and paintings. A blue and white quilt lay on the newly made bed, a narrow mirror tucked away in a corner of the room. 
 
 Her clothes had been taken away to be washed last night and she given new ones to wear. They were a compromise, Faith knew, between the realities of modern living and the legacy of the Old World. The denim jeans had been modified from Pre-Arrival stock, the inseam reinforced with soft doeskin for horseback riding. The green gingham shirt was of recent make as were her leather boots. The master of this hall was obviously a man of great import, able to afford clothing strangers and travelers freely. 
 
 She brushed her hair, relishing once more the rediscovered luxury of ridding herself of tangles and knots. Sharing a broken-toothed comb over a cold fire was doable, but the chance to feel Elven again was no small treat. 
 
 A knock on the door roused her from her thoughts, a young, feminine voice on the side of the heavy door. 
 
 `` Miss? Are you up?'' 
 
 `` Yes. I am,'' answered Faith, pulling her hair back and tying it with a ribbon of green silk. She moved over to the door and opened it, seeing before her a girl about her size, though many, many years younger. The girl curtsied slightly and said, `` Your clothes have just finished drying and will be delivered to your room here in a little while. Should you need anything, pen and paper, candles, rags, you merely need to ask. Breakfast is set out in the main hall, Miss Alathir. You'll find your Ranger there already.'' 
 
 She said that last line with a tinge of excitement. Gone were the days when one could travel the breadth of the world and back in a matter of hours or days. Most of those born since the Arrival Wars had n't gone farther than a few miles beyond their homes, so treacherous was the ever expanding wilderness and war-torn world they lived in. Only those belonging to the far ranging orders traveled with any regularity and so were one of the few reminders of a larger, greater world. Faith smiled. 
 
 `` Thank you. I'll follow you if that's alright.'' 
 
 The girl led Faith down the narrow hall of the guest quarters chatting all the while. Her name was Emily, she learned, and that she would seventeen come Sunday. Her father was a crofter and that she worked three days a week in service to their lord doing various chores and tasks. Today was a mustering day, when the militiamen from the various outlying villages would gather for inspection and drill. It was also a time of trading and feasting with the last of the snow finally melted and the meager roads dry enough for travel. Faith answered whatever questions Emily had but was happy enough to listen to the girl speak. Each new person she met was a font of newfound knowledge and Faith had come to believe that only with greater understanding of this world could she successfully uphold her duties to her family and her name. 
 
 The hall was a large space able to fit at least a hundred persons, with tall timber pillars and a floor of finely set stone. Two massive fireplaces burned at either end of the room with massive logs of oak and maple burning brightly within. Long tables ran the length of the room with benches underneath. Servant girls and women bustled to and fro, carrying platters stack high with pancakes and strips of bacon. Tureens laden with oatmeal sat at regular intervals, bits of dried berries and nuts mixed in with the oats. The air was thick with the scent of frying dough and meat, the noise of laughter and proud voices woven throughout. 
 
 Hilary Flint sat at the table on a raise dais, deep in conversation with the lord of the manor. His beard was freshly washed and trimmed, and his green cloak showed evidence of having been mended during the night. A brooch of bright silver clasped the cloak round his shoulders, its fine features decorated with emeralds. A half-eaten plate sat in front of him, thick slabs of toast and sausage mixed with scrambled eggs. 
 
 `` So you truly believe there will be war again, Captain?'' the manor's lord asked. Flint nodded. 
 
 `` It's been twenty years since the Arrival, Lord Franklin. An entire generation has reached their prime and are eager to prove themselves. The Fae have had two decades to rest and rearm. They know that every year we grow stronger and know well enough what that means for their hopes of dominion. The Order's leaders are in communication with one another, the various Colonels and Force Captains preparing to their regiments and companies. The elimination of high ranking targets is already underway.'' 
 
 `` Assassination you mean,'' the lord said. `` I have good relations with the Uthlo, the Clan of Spriggans to the South of here. We share grazing and forest rights. I have almost ten thousand souls under my care. War would mean hardship and privation for my people.'' 
 
 `` War is already underway, Lord Franklin. The Peninsular War has been waged for nearly decade without end. My brothers and sisters die daily to protect our *Race*. The Order has been at war since Arrival Day, since before it was even imagined-'' He stopped, his eyes turned to Faith and his grave look softened. `` Morning, Dove. Sleep well?'' 
 
 She nodded and sat at the proffered chair besides the two men. `` I did. You?'' 
 
 `` Well enough,'' said Flint looking out over the sea of people. `` Lord Franklin here has offered us guest-rights for as long as we desire. I intend to stay long enough to get our kit repaired and supplies replenished. Perhaps a week or a little more. That sound right to you?'' 
 
 `` It does. You intend to drill with the Lord's militia?'' 
 
 `` Yes. One of the most important missions of my Order is to collect and disseminate the skills and knowledge need in our war against the Fae. Lord Franklin here,'' he said with an incline of his head, `` Has taken every step in his power to train and equip his followers, but they are farmers and woodsmen, not professional soldiers.'' 
 
 `` And what would you have me do?'' asked Faith. 
 
 Flint smiled and took a sip of his chipped coffee mug, the chicory laced heavy with cream. `` Live. Enjoy yourself and the time you have. Sing, dance, and learn. You've spent too long in the company of Death, Faith. It's time to learn how to live.''

title: story-45
text:
Selena stood at the window waiting. There no signs of anything outside, and she ’ d begun to wonder whether the town had become deserted overnight. She checked her watch again. 11:03. The postman was running late. She knew that he would be, today of all days, but that made it all the more unbearable. She felt as though she ’ d been waiting forever. 
 
 Selena took a deep breath and adjusted the pillows on the couch. She ’ d adjusted them already this morning, once before vacuuming and again afterwards but they didn ’ t seem to be sitting quite right. They were too lumpy. Or maybe it was the colour that offended her. She ’ d cleaned the apartment from top to bottom, but everything seemed suspended in time, as though it did not quite fit in her home. She checked her watch again. 11:03. 
 
 As she ’ d been doing all morning, Selena recited her application to the Committee. They ’ d spent so long fretting over every little detail; writing and revising, carefully weighing every word and then consulting with the lawyer. She could recite every word by heart. Even at night, when she closed her eyes and tried to sleep, The Ministry of Population Management, written in the official script, floated endlessly across her dreams. 
 
 *I, Robert Jayden Mutchmor of Gen. XX2, along with my spouse, Selena Anne Mutchmor ( née Smith ) of Gen. XX2, do herein submit an application for the status of Gen. XX3 Parenthood. * 
 
 Selena exhaled. She thought of Robert who ’ d been called away from breakfast to deal with some emergency; coal shipments from Peru had been intercepted by pirates or the Chicago reactor was failing, again. She couldn ’ t remember which it was, only that she ’ d protested his departure: how could anyone be expected to resolve a crisis on a day like today? 
 
 Belatedly, Selena registered that her communicator was buzzing, with Robert ’ s name on the display. She accepted the call, and his face appeared but she could not bring herself to speak. She stood, frozen and silent in her living room. Robert sighed. 
 
 “ Nothing? ” 
 
 Selena shook her head, but the air in the room had turned to molasses and she felt exhausted from the effort. Robert sighed again. 
 
 “ Alright. Call me right away. I have a meeting with The Minister, but I want to know as soon as youfind out. ” 
 
 He was gone before Selena could react, and so she stood, staring out the window a while longer. She checked her watch. 11:05. 
 
 Suddenly, she needed to be rid of her watch. Her hands trembling, she tried to unfasten the clasp as quickly as she could. She fumbled with the watch, felt trapped and grew angrier all at once. Finally, the watch came loose and in one violent motion that flowed smoothly out of her body, she hurled it across the room. It landed on one of the sofa cushions, left a dent where she ’ d meticulously smoothed the fabric only moments before, and slid to floor. 
 
 Selena hugged her arms around herself and began to cry. 
 
 She needed the postman to arrive. All around the world, members of Gen XX2 were receiving their letters: *Congratulations. The Ministry of Population Management wishes to inform you that your application for Parenthood has been successful, to commence with the birthing of Gen XX3 on January 1, 14017... * 
 
 Selena ’ s letter of congratulations was supposed to arrive at 11:01 with the postman. She was supposed to be celebrating with all of the other new parents who had received their congratulations. She walked across the floor, bent to pick up her watch, and checked the time. 11:06. She was supposed to be celebrating. 
 
 A part of Selena knew that she might not receive a letter of congratulations. She knew she might receive the letter that read simply: * The Ministry of Population Management wishes to inform you that your application for Parenthood has been unsuccessful. Your contribution to the well-being all generations remains invaluable... * 
 
 But even a letter of denial would be better than the waiting. Selena reminded herself of her value, just as she ’ d been taught at school. Selena had been trained as a sixth form teacher, and when the time came, she would teach Gen XX3 the importance of long division and the basics of essay writing. Even if she could not be a parent herself, she would spend a year with 20 children of her own. 
 
 And Robert would have to understand. He had worked on the carrying capacity projections for Gen XX3 in his first position at the Ministry. He knew that society could only be successful if each generation was carefully planned and taught to use its remaining resources with care. He had worked through the calculations himself during his school days, and he knew that if each couple from Gen. XX2 were granted parenthood, war and famine and destruction were all but inevitable by the time the children reached adulthood. Robert, like every member of Gen. XX2 had been reminded time and time again that it was selfish to bring a child into this world, when their whole life would be one of suffering. 
 
 Still, Selena thought she might explode if she were forced to wait much longer. Although she ’ d always dutifully recited her Responsibility to the Collective, she knew there was a secret buried deep inside of her: she wanted nothing more than to be a mother. She ’ d applied to be a teacher just so that she could be a mother to as many children as possible during her 60 years on Earth. She hadn ’ t told a soul, because she knew it was a crime to admit such narcissism aloud – except once, when Robert was fast asleep, she ’ d whispered into his ear her desire to be a mother. 
 
 Six months later, they were wed – early for their generation, but Selena knew that the match was right. Robert ’ s grandparents were part of Gen. XY1, scheduled to ascend on December 31, 14016. Robert was considered an exception in Gen. XX2, because his parents had been killed in conflict when he was younger, and his grandparents had taken on the responsibility of raising him. 
 
 When they ’ d gone to their lawyer to begin their Application for Parenthood, he ’ d stressed the importance of explaining Robert ’ s upbringing. Once his grandparents ascended, he would be completely alone, yet the death of his parents reinforced the need for strong family bonds. Especially considering his position at the Ministry of Natural Resources, he was a prime candidate for Parenthood. 
 
 Selena knew in her heart that her and Robert would be parents. She just needed to hold the letter of congratulations in her hands, to feel its weight and breathe its scent. And then they would celebrate. 
 Selena thought of their lawyer, who was already celebrating. His life ’ s work was complete now that all of their generation ’ s applications for Parenthood had been decided. And since he worked so closely with the Ministry of Population Management, it was certain that he ’ d secured a child for him and his wife through legitimate means or otherwise. 
 
 But what about all of the other women on their block, who would not be celebrating? What about the women who were not married to lawyers, who could not secure their future happiness? Selena tried to remember her Responsibility to the Collective, but for all of the times she ’ d recited it, she could not find the words. All she could seem to find inside of herself was a feeling of loneliness that seemed seep in from the deserted world outside. 
 
 And then Selena saw the first signs of life she ’ d seen all day. Through the window, she could see the postman, walking up the drive. In his hand, he held her letter.

title: story-46
text:
My eyes adjust to the blinding light shining down on me, and in a moment I see a walkway leading to a large, circular platform. I walk towards it, slowly, cautiously. As I approach, a circular table with a red button comes into view. I do n't know where I am, but for some reason I do n't care. A mysterious force guides me toward the center of the platform, and as I finally reach it, a voice calls out to me, a raspy whisper that sends shivers down my back. 
 
 `` You who have lost your physical existence. It is time to determine your eternal fate.'' 
 
 I look around, startled. Where is the voice coming from? Then, from the floor of the platform, a dark, shadowy figure slowly starts to form out of nowhere, and a loud crackling noise invades my ears as it builds upward. Soon, the figure of a man stands before me, dressed in a business suit with a red tie. However, where his head should be, there is only the shadow of a head. It seems to have shape but reflects no light, so it is impossible to see the exact outline of the nose and mouth unless he were to turn his head sideways. His hands are of the same composition, and as this shadow figure walks toward me I feel a damp coldness overtake me more with each step. 
 
 I barely manage to stammer, `` Wh-who are you?'' 
 
 He seems unaffected by my question and continues drawing closer. As he approaches the small table he places his shadow hands down, one on each side of the button. `` I am the host,'' he says in that mysterious whisper. `` And you are the contestant.'' 
 
 I am about to ask what he means when I notice a bright flash of light coming from the right. I look up to see a large, lit-up board, filled with two lists of of words, one colored red and the other blue. On the blue side are phrases such as `` Be with loved ones lost'' and `` Live in a state of euphoria,'' while on the left I read, among others, `` Wander the Earth as a spirit'' and `` Burn in eternal hell fire.'' 
 
 Needless to say I am thoroughly confused at all this; I do n't even really remember anything that happened before coming to this place. This entity standing in front of me seems to be pulling all the strings at the moment though, so I simply wait for it to continue speaking. 
 
 `` Your life as a human has come to an end, mortal, and the time has come to decide how you will spend your afterlife. There are twenty-six fates on the board between which you must choose.'' The figure holds out its hand and above it appear glowing numbers, from one to twenty-six, ordered numerically from bottom-left to top-right in four rows. `` However, the choice is not so simple as you think. You must pick only one of these numbers, without knowing what fate lies behind it. I will then offer you a fate to live out for eternity, and you may choose to accept or decline it. Should you decline, I will ask you to pick more of these numbers, and they will eliminate the possible fates that your number contains. If you decline all of the fates I offer you, you shall be left with only the one you picked at the beginning. However, know that none of the fates I offer you will be as good as the ultimate fate of happiness and joy.'' 
 
 He points to the board, and I look again. At the bottom on the blue side reads, `` Create your own fate.'' 
 
 `` Should you receive that prize, you may construct your fate as you wish. There are no restrictions or boundaries, and your fate can cross over into the realm of reality as well as every plane of existence. You will be immortal, and an eternity of the ultimate happiness and satisfaction will be at your fingertips.'' 
 
 My imagination runs wild at this realization. Thoughts of grandeur and power race through my mind as I think of the incredible things I could do with such an opportunity. 
 
 I snap back to the present as the figure continues. `` However, be warned, for the opposite fate is not so favorable.'' 
 
 I look over again at the top of the red side, which reads `` nonexistence.'' 
 
 `` Your mind will still be alive, but nothing else will be. You will have no physical form, feeling, or memory. You will be doomed to wander in eternal darkness, never knowing where, who, or what you are.'' 
 
 The thought of this possibility made me shiver once more as I considered the extremity of the chance that I would be taking by participating in this strange ritual. 
 
 `` Now then...'' The numbers floating in mid air blew up to a much larger size and stood in front of me like a great wall. `` Choose your fate.''

title: story-47
text:
It was February first, and Shawn had arrived an hour before school. It was a time of meditation for him, just him and the occasional wandering teacher. It almost seemed peaceful. He breathed in deeply, smelling the sweat and grime as he walked past the gym. A glance in the library window provided a moment's rest from his whirlwind of thoughts. The glaring reflection of the sun off of the tile floors in hall B reminded him of the glare off of his window in the long-term ward where he had become an on and off patient. His friends knew he was sick. He did n't want to be overbearing, so he did n't tell them how bad it was. They'd be there at eight o'clock with the other 3,567 students that would flood the halls and provide a raucous cacophony more than able to send Shawn to the nurse's office with a migraine. 
 
 A quick stop by the music department granted an earful of a slow jazz ballad. His last dance with her had been to that very tune. Tuesday nights were swing dance. But now she had a new partner, one who could dance unafraid and unashamed. His body would not fail him as Shawn's had begun to. His smile would reach his eyes, and he was n't tailed constantly by his fretting mother. Looking in, he sees her sitting in the back row of the band room, unobserved by the class before her. 
 
 Clammy palms and skip in his heartbeat, were a sign to Shawn as he approached the door cautiously. A petite frame, a smattering of freckles across her nose, face framed in full by long dark hair let down her back casually. Her hazel eyes boxed in with glasses they'd always joked about. She did n't know that in less than a year, he would never see his own reflection in her eyes again. 
 
 Walking in quietly, he nodded to the director. 
 
 `` The Cost of Living. From the top.'' 
 
 Shawn approached her slowly. Unable to avoid choking up, he sat next to her for several minutes in silence, tears streaming down his face. 
 
 A hand on his shoulder. 
 
 A voice in the distance. 
 
 `` Hey. Shawn. It's ok'' She leaned in closer, pulling his head onto her shoulder, where he wept freely. Unable to gather words to speak, he began the task of swallowing what remained of his tears. 
 
 `` It's ok'' Her voice helped. She felt his lurching sobs settle down, and released him gently before asking a single question. 
 
 `` You're not ok, are you.'' 
 
 It was more of a statement, but Shawn understood. The words that passed unsaid would've filled a dozen books, as the truth she'd been trying to deny was confirmed before her eyes. Shawn pulled her close as her world fell apart. 
 
 The sharp edges of the room were muted before their eyes. The world could be damned, they were limited. Finite creatures, who wished to live forever. The only solace from their pain was each other, but it was enough. 
 
 `` Stay with me,'' she pleaded. She held him tight, as though captive to her will. He was n't planning on leaving anyway. 
 
 `` I've got seven months left.'' 
 
 It was February first. Every minute was a memory.

 Reaping Highlights

 Kile: Of course, we wo n't know just how strong they are until after they get their ranking. So do n't place your bets just yet, Panem, we could have more than a few surprises in store for us this year.

Then the rest of the tributes will leave her alone for the first half and then BAM, before they know it, she's slitting their throats in their sleep and crowning herself victor.

 Orion: So you're going for brawn over brains this year, Uta? 
 
 Uta: Well, I think that we have a lot of strong contenders and I do n't know how easy it'll be for the other tributes to outsmart this batch. 
 
 Orion: ( chuckles ) You know me, Uta. I'm a sucker for smart tributes and I think we have a few this year that might just put your picks to the test. 
 
 Uta: That right? 
 
 Orion: I think so; we have Belle from district 3. Let's replay her reaping. There she is and is n't she a beauty. I bet she'll have more than a few sponsors here in the Capitol. We can also see her father, standing right over there near the justice building. We have the closeup on him coming up just now. Lots of strong emotions there. Now, he looks a little crazy, but I heard that he's a genius of an inventor and that that daughter of his reads more than anyone else in the district. I think she's a surefire contender for this year's games and I know that for now, my bets are on her. 
 
 Kile: So those are our first picks: Snow White, Belle, and Uta, you did n't pick just one tribute.

 Uta: And may the odds be ever in your favour.
