title: story-49
text:
`` *Mr. President! *'' The president ’ s head of media relations objected. 
 
 However the man didn ’ t finish the statement, unwilling to state in bald terms what his true thoughts were regarding the situation in less than diplomatic terms. President Trump had no sooner been sworn in than he began fulfilling his campaign promises of ending the invasion of the country ’ s southern border. It was on the wave of public support to do just that which the man had rode and crested all the way to the White House. Pundits condemned him initially but swiftly broke off at the overwhelming approval ratings the new president had achieved as a result of following through. 
 
 The country found itself in the midst of an economic revival as suddenly overburdened social welfare systems for the first time in decades had a smaller demographics populace putting demands on it. The confluence of a raise in the Federal Minimum Wage standards passed by the former holder of the Presidential Office made formerly low-paying jobs attractive and for the first time since the country had been involved in an Interplanetary War unemployment percentages reached single digits. While most economists publically stated they did not believe the current state of affairs would last for the time being things were good. The mood of the country was high. Now then **this**… 
 
 The presidential spokesperson tried again. `` Mr. President, I feel this course of action is *extremely* unwise. The potential flack from pursuing this course far outweighs any possible benefits. Not to mention the losses we could face if *He* decides to oppose it.'' 
 
 President Trump just smiled mockingly. `` Unwise? How is it any more *unwise* than all the other initiatives we ’ ve made since the election? Why should we treat **this** publically admitted illegal alien any different than any other?'' 
 
 `` Because sir…'' the aide said in a indignant tone, `` it ’ s Superman.'' 
 
 `` So? All the more reason for us to pursue him! He ’ s so big on being a role model, always tries to carry the banner of being an All-American-Boy-Scout—then it ’ d be hypocritical to let him go!'' 
 
 The aide just helplessly repeated, `` But…it ’ s Superman!'' He was unable to even process much further than that due to the mental grinding even having this discussion was causing him. 
 
 `` Yes, yes, I know. Man of Steel, Man of Tomorrow—and illegal alien!'' Trump pushed back. 
 
 `` This sounds like something Luther would push, not you sir. Are you feeling alright? Have you been exposed to any glowing rocks lately perhaps? Maybe you caught something on that recent visit to Gotham to visit Wayne and speak at the Wayne Orphan Benefit?'' The presidential spokesperson asked, scrambling desperately at straws to find an excuse for this behavior by his boss. 
 
 Come to think of it, hadn ’ t the President been seated next to Luther himself along with Bruce Wayne in the place of honor at the benefit? 
 
 `` No, I tell you I ’ m fine! I ’ m not being influenced by anyone or anything. Dammit! I knew we would have to be targeting the Kryptonian the day I took office. The facts speak for themselves!'' Trump thundered. `` Now stop reacting like a school girl being told the facts of life for the first time and start using that thing between your ears for more than just a place to hold your glasses on!'' 
 
 The aide tried, he really did. He just didn ’ t understand how President Trump could be so wrong-headed in this. His expression must have given his thoughts away, because Trump sighed and looked at him thoughtfully. Finally he indicated to the chair the aide had been in when the conversation started. 
 
 `` Sit down, man! You ’ re an intelligent man; if you still don ’ t see it I ’ m going to have to walk you through it. God knows how the public is going to react if a man of your caliber misses it so completely.'' 
 
 Trump sighed. 
 
 `` This Superman has been in this country for how many years now?'' He began. 
 
 The media consultant did some quick mental arithmetic, and replied. 
 
 `` That ’ s right lad. And in the time he ’ s been on this planet he ’ s wrapped himself in the flag, hasn ’ t he? For Truth, Justice, and The American Way, right? He ’ s made it clear that he considers himself home here, hasn ’ t he? 
 
 `` And we ’ ve been grateful for that fact. A few of my generals even did a military analysis on the impact he could have had if he ’ d been born in say Russia. It was devastating. No, we ’ re really happy to have had him declare himself an American. He has saved our bacon several times over on natural disasters as well. 
 
 `` He ’ s had just as much an impact on the nation ’ s morale as he has on her security. He seems to know all the right things to say, a very inspiring man. *I ’ ve* been inspired by some of his speeches even!'' 
 
 Trump paused, seeing the look of consternation on his aide ’ s face. He smiled at that, but it was a cold calculating smile. `` You wonder then, having said all that why on God ’ s green Earth would I want to deport the man?'' 
 
 The other man just nodded, not trusting himself to speak at this point. 
 
 `` Well putting aside entirely the issue of the man being an attractive nuisance—how many of his enemies have caused trouble in this country, threatened the world because of his presence here? How many `` heroes'' have set up shop due to the sheer insanity of his influence? There ’ s good and bad that goes along with being an inspiration you know! 
 
 `` That ’ s all beside the point though. The man has been in this country, claiming to be the standard bearer for *how* ***many*** years now?'' 
 
 The presidential spokesman repeated the earlier number he gave the president. 
 
 `` Yes! And in that entire time, he hasn ’ t so much as applied for citizenship once! Not once!!'' Trump exploded. 
 
 This caused the other man to object immediately. `` Mr. President, surely you don ’ t think a minor consid…'' 
 
 Trump interrupted him. 
 
 `` It ’ s **not** a minor consideration! It speaks to who he is at his core!'' The president thundered, `` I know immigrants! The fact that this Superman hasn ’ t long ago become an American citizen means at heart he doesn ’ t consider himself an American! He doesn ’ t truly consider this home. He doesn ’ t think he belongs here.'' 
 
 Finally for the first time, his presidential spokesman seemed to understand what the President was getting at. He looked off to the side for moment thinking. Finally the former newsman said, `` So what do you want me to do?'' 
 
 `` I want you to contact your friends in the media, so we can announce tomorrow night that unless Superman applies for citizenship by the end of the week this country will have no choice but to consider his presence illegal, to find his proclamations of American values suspicious and false.'' 
 
 He made a few notes on his tablet and said he ’ d get right on it. The press conference could be held tomorrow evening and trustworthy reporters would be available to hear the declaration, ones who could be counted on to use discretion until the announcement could be made. He had to clarify a few names and together they determined substitutions for a few names. 
 
 As the former newsman began to make ready to carry out his orders Trump stopped him. `` Privately I really hope he applies for citizenship. He ’ ll be the fastest applicant approved you ever saw, but he has to decide if he wants to be here or not. He has to decide he ’ s a part of us now. It ’ s time. Long past over due. I really hope he applies Kent. I really do.''

title: story-50
text:
A moist breeze washed across my face as rain drizzled down from the sky. 
 
 `` Thanks again,'' I read the note, all that remained of the crusted cinnamon apple pie left at my doorstep, `` for saving our crops from drought. My wife made this pie for you, and I helped.'' 
 
 `` Oh, Adrian.'' Old man Adrian, always tacking his name onto other peoples achievements, but it could n't be helped. Ever since I showed up in this town, everyone has been trying their best to hold some form of usefulness to this town. Kid Marcus still tried to help the locals repair their broken down vehicles, even though my strength and speed fixed them instantly. Lady, or whatever her real name was, still would come door to door asking if work needed to be done. 
 
 The whole town, everyone, wanted to be a hero too. 
 
 `` Hm? Hey, Samuel.'' I called out, waving from the swing on my porch to the young man walking the dirt road. He stopped, holding an umbrella over his drenched head, in overalls and muddy boots. 
 
 `` Howdy! I'm assuming this rain is yer doin'?'' As if to direct me to what rain he was talking about, he pointed to the sky of sudden gloomy clouds and sprinkling showers up above. 
 
 `` Yea, that was me. Adrian said his crops were close to dying and he would n't have a harvest this year.'' 
 
 `` Heh looks like it workin', ai n't it?'' On the side of the road opposite of my white fence, wilted corn stalks and shriveled beans already appeared to be growing green in color after the last few hours. `` You really are a god.'' 
 
 `` I'm not a god.'' By now my tone was flaccid and posture relaxed in saying this for the millionth time. A god, they said, the second coming, they called me. Truly, a god. Of course, in a town where the richest guy here own three horses and a ham radio, I should n't be surprised. Why fight it? Being a god among men was n't too bad. Though the Sunday rituals were a bit uncomfortable. I was not even religious for crying out loud. 
 
 `` You a humble one, ai n't ya'? That's why I like you. Heh, look at me, all mushy and junk. You have a good one!'' Samuel gave a bow before heading off on his way. I gave a wave and took a tall glass of ice tea from my side table. My radio clicked and picked up static beside me, it was a calming noise to my ears now, better than the news yelling of events overseas. 
 
 A hero they claimed they needed, that hero was me for a short time. But it's not like the comics. Not like the movies. 
 
 `` Go there and kill this person,'' the military would say, `` and go here and kill that guy.'' I do n't believe I ever saved anyone in town, I never stopped rape or a mugging, never took down a greedy corporation. The blood on my hands, that could never be washed away. No matter how many rain clouds I summoned. 
 
 `` You're thinking again.'' 
 
 `` That's what people do,'' I sighed, `` they think.'' 
 
 `` Hm. So, you stopped my drought then?'' 
 
 `` Yea. Like I always do. Did you want to sit down?'' Slithering down from the roof of my porch came my arch nemesis. At least that's what he called himself. 
 
 `` Sure. I'm soaking wet up here.'' Slick black hair laid flat over his face while his attire of jeans and short sleeve top appeared heavy with water. Somehow he managed to make it blindly onto my swing and plop down. I gripped the arm rest at the sudden shift and sway before we settled back down. 
 
 `` So, why the drought this time? Last time it was a tornado, then the month before you made locusts, and then there was the stampede you caused.'' 
 
 `` Yea, it was exciting huh?'' He laughed, parting his hair out of his face and turning to me. A genuine grin came across his face. It's why I could n't call him a villain, he did n't wear a mask or have some hidden agenda. 
 
 `` Exciting sure, but you could have hurt people, you know?'' 
 
 `` Ha, you are funny. You know you wo n't let that happen.'' Freely, he leaned across my lap and took my glass of tea, sipping from my straw before placing it back. `` That's why you came here, right? To save people?'' 
 
 `` Mmhm. Still, what if I do n't? What if I'm sick and ca n't stop your shenanigans?'' 
 
 `` Haha shenanigans...'' Going back to his seat, he stared outside at the rain beginning to pour down, clicking his mouth. `` Well, guess I'd have to take a sick day too. It's no fun if you're not around to stop it, right?'' Together we sat on the porch, watching his damage undone in a matter of days. 
 
 We were always like this once I moved in. He'd summon some form of natural disaster claiming he was a demon from Hell sent to punish this town for its sins. I suppose it was him to blame for me being seen as a god. The moment I came in flying from the sky and breaking apart the thunderous storm clouds -- well, that did n't help my case I'm sure. Everyone assumed I was simply humble, like any God should be, and I could n't argue when I had `` the Devil'' as my counterpart. 
 
 `` So, are you free next Tuesday?'' He asked randomly. I cut my sip of tea short. 
 
 `` Hm? I guess. Why? You planning on bringing a dust storm to town?'' 
 
 `` No -- good idea though -- but apparently the town is going to have a bonfire. I would go alone but, if you are n't around, people wo n't think it's safe.'' 
 
 `` That sounds like a funny way of asking me on a date.'' 
 
 `` Is it funny?'' 
 
 `` I guess not... But sure, I'll go, be your date. But if people see us holding hand, you know I have to punch you, to keep up appearances?'' 
 
 `` Would n't have it any other way.'' I passed our now shared tea as we swung slightly on the porch together. 
 
 As far as we knew, the whole world could be ending. The economy could be collapsing. The war could be lost. An alien invader could be striking right now. But in this town, nothing mattered outside of field work and what was the special at the diner. 
 
 Maybe there were heroes in the city saving the world. Maybe not. But all I care about are these people and my date on Tuesday. Wonder what I should wear...

title: story-51
text:
**London, 1888. ** 
 
 
 His legs were weak. His heart was thumping, hard. He looked at his hand and he saw that his fingers were trembling, as they always were when he had been going back in time. His machine, a suitcase that didn ’ t look any different from any other suitcase, laid still in the dark alley not a couple feet from him. A few seconds went by and he started to feel the reality closing in on him. 
 
 
 He picked up his time machine, opened the suitcase and sent a confirmation signal to headquarter that he had arrived. He once again checked his location to make sure that he was not too far from his target. And he was right, the woman, named Mary Surley, was supposed to in his flat about two blocks from where he was standing. This was going to be an easy target for him, Harry Morgan, also known as The Purifier for his ability to do quick and clean Procedures. 
 
 
 Picking up all his stuff, he started walking towards the street under the rainy evening. He had been doing Procedures for a few years now, and if memory serves right, this was his sixth time going back to the old London. Navigating his way in the city, he soon found the building where Mary Surley, his target, lives. After a mere ten seconds of breaking the back door of the building, he walked up the stairs to find Mary ’ s flat. He tried the knob and it was locked, but he could see the faint light sneaking from the bottom of the door. 
 
 
 He knocked. 
 
 
 The door was opened, and Mary, looked exactly like her photograph, was standing in front of him. 
 
 
 “ Hello, Ma ’ am, ” he started with the best accent he could muster. “ My name ’ s Harry Morgan, I ’ m from the mayor ’ s office. May we have a chat a bit about your living condition here? ” 
 
 
 “ Pardon? ” Mary ’ s forehead wrinkled. “ I… why would someone from mayor ’ s office come here? Let alone at night? ” 
 
 
 “ Well, maybe this will make it easier for you to understand. Have you ever heard of Jack the Ripper? ” 
 
 
 Her eyes widen. “ Y-yes. Why do you ask? ” 
 
 
 Without answering, he grabbed her neck, pushed her to the nearest wall, and lifted her up. Mary struggled hard for her life, she wanted to scream but no words came out of her mouth. She kicked her feet to the air, banged her fists to the wall, but it was too late. He could see the saliva coming out from the corner of her mouth, her eyes bulging and her face became blue. 
 
 
 He counted to ten. And then she was limp. He let go and her lifeless body sagged onto the floor. 
 
 
 He went back to close and lock the door. Taking her body with him, he found a small bathroom in the back of the flat. She was laid carefully onto the floor while he sang a sweet lullaby, the last treat he could give for a woman who was unlucky enough to bear a criminal in his womb. 
 
 
 He started from the neck. Blood was pouring quickly onto the dirty bathroom floor. He let it flow for a few minutes before he started on other part of her body. 
 
 
 And that was when he saw it. 
 
 
 A baby. 
 
 
 A baby sat down on the bathroom floor, looking at him, looking at his mother ’ s stiff body, looking at his mother ’ s blood. 
 
 
 “ I don ’ t understand, ” he whispered to himself. 
 
 
 Quickly he went back to his machine that he left near the door. He opened it and checked the target ’ s data again. He realized he made a mistake, a big mistake. 
 
 
 He was supposed to kill Mary in 1887. A year ago. A year ago when the baby wasn ’ t born yet. How this was happened he had no idea. He started to call the Headquarter when he heard the baby crying. He went back the bathroom and he saw the baby crawling in his mother ’ s blood. 
 
 
 He had no other choice that to terminate the baby too. But when he started to pull out his gun, the crying baby looked at him. His eyes pleaded. His mouth curled. Blood was everywhere on his body. 
 
 
 “ Fuck this, ” Harry said. He stripped off his jacked and picked the baby from the bathroom floor. “ I ’ m really sorry this happened to you. But I know I ’ m not going to kill you tonight. ” 
 
 
 The crying stopped, he held the baby close to his chest with his jacket wrapped around him. He went back to his machine and punched the code that would bring him back to the future. 
 
 
 “ I don ’ t know who you are. I don ’ t know what you ’ ll do in the future, ” he whispered to the baby. “ But you ’ re coming with me tonight. ” 
 
 
 Before he pushed the button on the machine, he whispered to the baby one more time. 
 
 
 “ And from now on, I ’ ll call you Dex, okay? And we ’ re going home, Dexter Morgan. ”

title: story-52
text:
The ancient texts were true. The magics were real. Contained within the two Circles of Holding were an angel and a demon. Both helpless. Both trapped. Both at my command. 
 
 `` Hold, warriors of the Other Word,'' I said. `` And hear me, for it is my command that you must now obey. Bear my will. Live to better serve me.'' 
 
 The demon, a thin wiry humanoid, made a clear display of how important cleaning his nails was. `` Live to serve me better,'' he said. 
 
 The angel rolled his eyes. `` You're not helping, dude.'' He said. 
 
 He shrugged. `` You do n't split infinitives,'' he said. `` I do n't care who you are.'' 
 
 I gave a *hello? * gesture, and their attention returned to me. `` I need to know of the world beyond,'' I told them. `` I bid you, answer.'' 
 
 `` Cloudy,'' said the angel. 
 
 `` Firey'', said the demon. 
 
 They looked at each other. `` Big?'' One of them said. I did n't know which at that point. 
 
 `` What of Heaven?'' I asked. 
 
 `` You do n't have to talk like that,'' the demon said. `` I get it, you know, if you're into the whole pageantry thing, but I'm just letting you know, it's not necessary.'' 
 
 `` What. Of. Heaven?'' I asked again, with the stern authority becoming of a master of magic such as myself. 
 
 The angel looked shiftily at the demon. The demon shrugged an *it's your show* kind of shrug. `` Heaven's a...'' he started, ``... work in progress,'' he said. `` It's kind of a supply and demand thing, you know?'' 
 
 `` Supply and demand?'' I asked, haughtily. I can haught, even in such company. 
 
 He shuffled around a little. `` Yeah,'' he said. `` The thing is, you know... it's like... we never promised that sort of thing, and - we're listening, you know. We get it, that that's what you want. And we're working on it. It's just not that easy, you know. Space. Resources. Management. It's a big ask.'' 
 
 `` You never promised'that sort of thing?''' I said, stunned. `` What of Hell?'' 
 
 The demon shrugged. `` We do n't give a shit,'' he said. `` Literally not bothered. Demand your supply all you want, we are *not* going to build a pen for all the people you consider to be a dick. How do you even quantify shit like that anyway? You have so many fucking rules!'' 
 
 I held up my staff of power, to intimidate them. `` The Just go to Heaven. The Evil go to Hell. How is this not already in order?'' 
 
 The angel spoke first. `` Well, that's not actually how it works. Those who turn to God go to Heaven. Those who turn Away go to Hell. But that covers a handful of you every generation, really. Most of you just go through the motions.'' 
 
 I took this in. `` So a terrorist who blows himself up in the name of God?'' 
 
 The angel snapped his fingers. `` Yeah,'' he said. `` We've got a bunch of those guys.'' 
 
 I swallowed. `` And the atheist who dedicates his life to charity?'' 
 
 The demon nodded. `` Those guys are ours,'' he said. 
 
 `` And everyone else?'' I asked. `` What happens to their souls?'' 
 
 The demon grimaced, out of one side of his mouth. `` You guys do n't really have *souls*, you know? Not by default. So.... nothing?'' 
 
 `` We are but pawns?'' I said. 
 
 `` No!'' The angel said. `` No, no.'' 
 
 `` That's right,'' the demons added. `` Pawns are players. Pawns have a purpose. You're more like the... scoreboard.'' 
 
 I slumped. `` For what reason does all this go on? For what purpose is my race held to keep score between Heaven and Hell?'' 
 
 The angel looked embarrassed. `` Well, that was the bet, you know?''

title: story-53
text:
A lot runs through your head when you're about to die, and I mean a *lot*. Unfortunately, most of it's ridiculous. I did n't reflect back upon my life, or think of my family. No, all I did was think about how stupid my rescue attempt was. I was n't nearly fast enough to get her out of the way, only fast enough to join her. I originally had the intention of tackling or carrying her out of the way, but as I got to her, my instincts panicked. Suddenly, I could n't remember how I had been planning to move her. Instead of pushing her, or jumping at her and letting momentum do its thing, I half grabbed, half hugged her, apparently thinking I could just wrap my arms around her, lift her, and run without losing any momentum. I *did* manage to lift her feet off the ground, but that took me just a second too much, and I was maybe half a step away before I felt the metal press against my back as the noise of screeching metal filled my ears. 
 
 At which point, fear rid myself of any survival instinct, and I just held her as tightly as I could. I'd like to say I was hoping to shield her from the damage with my soon to be corpse, but I was going to die. I *knew* I was going to die, and I held onto her out of panic, as if she could stop it. 
 
 I have n't felt anything since, at least, nothing in regards to the 16-wheeler that has undoubtedly run us over by now. Maybe, despite all the pain you can feel in life, when your time comes, you just simply fade away? Maybe the death was just that quick? The dang thing was moving fast enough... 
 
 Still, the fact that I'm thinking any of this right now means there's *something* after death, which should be comforting... 
 
 I still have n't managed to let the girl go though, or even open my eyes. I know I'm probably fine, I'm in the afterlife, or I'm a ghost, or I'm in purgatory, and the girl's here with me, so at least I have company, which helps almost as much as the realization that I failed makes me feel terrible... 
 
 I give a sigh, and keep holding onto the cute girl I failed to save, surprised I still feel like I'm alive, and fearing it'll fade away the second I recognize I'm dead. 
 
 `` Sorry,'' I explain to my fellow ghost, `` I mean, sorry for failing to save you, and sorry for still holding onto you like this. I'll let go in a minute, I just need to gather my resolve before facing the afterlife.'' I hope my explanation makes sense. 
 
 `` We're not dead.'' The woman retorts quietly, and it takes a second for my brain to register her words. 
 
 `` What do you mean we're not dead?!'' I say, letting go of her in confusion and turning away, planning on showing her the obvious afterlife/ghost world qualities of wherever we are. 
 
 Except,'wherever we are' is in the middle of the street, traffic halted and a few pedestrians staring at us. 
 
 Oh, and the 16-wheeler. I mean, it's also in the middle of the street, and also being stared at by various pedestrians, and also appears to have been torn to shreds and scattered about in a cone like pattern aiming away from us. 
 
... 
 
... 
 
... 
 
 `` Welp, I'm confused.'' I say cheerfully. There's so much wrong with what I'm seeing, and so many possible unpleasant or bizarre explanations, that I ca n't even fathom how to react. My brain feels like a machine falling apart because someone threw a wrench into the gears, and now it's about to explode. I quickly place a hand on the girl's shoulder, worried she'll disappear if I take my focus off of her for too long, and terrified by the idea of trying to figure this out on my own. 
 
 `` I'll explain later, we have to get out of here before people start asking questions.'' She responds, and I genuinely begin to wonder if she can see the smoke coming out of my ears as my brain's processor catches fire. She begins walking away, my hand limply falling off her shoulder as she moves out of reach, and I quickly begin following, idly glancing around to see a few pedestrians with phones out, either trying to record or take pictures of what happened here. 
 
 The woman notices these things to, and with a wave of her hand, I watch as the phones all crumble to pieces, as if they were suddenly smashed by a very big hammer. 
 
 `` Yup, this is normal.'' I say to myself with a big grin, not even sure if I'm being sarcastic. I continue to follow the woman, unsure of what else to do, and fearing I'll go insane if I do n't hear an explanation soon, assuming I have n't already lost it...

title: story-54
text:
It was a beautiful summer afternoon on a secluded beach. Lexi was on her phone when the two shuttles landed in the parking lot. She had been alone for a total of four minutes. Her girls, Stacey and Mia, had gone back to the cabana to fix Stacey ’ s hair. Justin, her sometimes boyfriend, was getting her a Diet Coke. Lexi was checking into Instagram and Snapchat, alternating between beach selfies “ Lovin It! ” and liking pics of her girlfriends. Trevor was sending her Vines and she wanted to one up the ones he sent. 
 
 The shuttles landed about twenty feet apart from one another and opened hatches at the same moment. Everything about the two shuttles seemed rushed. Lexi didn ’ t notice, though she did register the bright red shape and the shiny blackness out of the corner of her eye. Really, no one was important until they were. 
 
 The red ship, from Jgu, lowered a ramp that allowed a long, snake like creature on wheels to roll forward onto pavement. The black ship lit a small circle underneath and two small and translucent purple blobs materialized. A perfect circle blackened the ground. The representatives from the 000 Provinces looked across at the snake and joined together to form a medium sized purple blob. The blob moved like gelatin, but roughly held the shape of a pumpkin. The snake changed from a dull orange to a charcoal gray with a white stripe, matching the parking spot where it landed. 
 
 Lexi began taking pictures of her pedi with the waves in the background. “ Relaxin! ” Her pedi was for the Fourth. Her big toe had a little American flag AND a crystal that looked like a firework. The rest of her toes were red, white, or blue. She had a delicate silver ring on the second toe of her right foot. That was secretly her favorite toe. She took a few pics using different filters, but didn ’ t feel satisfied. Maybe Justin could take a better picture if he stood over her. Ooo, then she could have him muscle pose and his shadow could look all sexy next to her smooth legs. That would be super hot! 
 
 The purple blob and the snake creature rolled over to Lexi. At first they progressed slowly, but in noticing the other, they sped up. The snake began to change into red, white, and blue lines. Its wheels mimicked the sound of the waves. 
 
 Approaching Lexi at the same moment, both creatures stopped only inches away from her Blonde Brazilian blow out. It is possible neither species understood that they were at the back end. Lexi puckered her lips, closed her eyes and took 10 rapid-fire selfies. Whichever one looked best she decided would be called “ Love. ” It was simple and awesome. 
 
 The blob began to copy the waves, rolling back and forth continuously. The snake made camera click noises and giggled. 
 
 Lexi didn ’ t notice. She opened her eyes to scan through her work. She saw the purple blob and the snake immediately. She quickly wiped the screen camera with the edge of her towel, blowing on it to help the process. She needed a new phone. She began the selfie process again, tilting her head at a 45 degree angle. Lips out again, this time her eyes were open. The purple blob produced two rippling purple lips and the snake made kissy noises. 
 
 Now Lexi saw the aliens. Her eyes went wide as the second picture was taken, and her mouth dropped open between pictures 3-5. Lexi dropped the phone before she could continue the photo session. She rolled forward off the towel and sprang to her feet. Turning around quickly, she faced the creatures. The blob seemed to wiggle in excitement, and the snake mimicked Lexi ’ s short scream. 
 
 For a full 30 seconds, nothing else happened. The purple blob and the snake stayed in their current conditions and offered no further communication. Lexi stood dumbstruck, her phone a few feet away, facedown in the sand. 
 
 The blob was the first to act, rolling to the phone, it sucked it up and held it in the center of it ’ s being. The phone was still somewhat visible and the blob moved back to its previous position. The snake, meanwhile, rolled closer to Lexi ’ s toes, adding a thin silver stripe near the front end. 
 
 The blob began to take pictures of Lexi ’ s toes, sometimes including the snake. The pictures had an automatic purple haze around them, making Lexi seem even more perfectly tanned and put together than usual. Lexi didn ’ t move as the beings performed the selfie dance. The blob moved the phone to different angles and change the filter for each one. The snake curled around Lexi and lifted the different ends up for each camera click. It made kissy noises. 
 
 This continued on for a full minute, while Lexi was frozen in place. When her phone pinged with a text from Mia, she suddenly broke from her trance. She jumped up, and ran towards the cabana. She barely noticed the hot sand burning her face feet. The blob and the snake continued to take pictures, the snake screaming and the blob slapping the sand.

title: story-55
text:
A large man enters the saloon. No one in town has seen him before. Immediately all eyes are on him as he slowly walks up to the bar. The conversations in the room disappear to a mumble. There is a quiet tension. 
 
 
 He is wearing a cowboy hat, tipped down so low you can only see his mouth. Each step he takes echoes among the loose wooden floorboards. He reaches the bar and slowly sits down on the old bar stool. 
 
 
 `` What's your poison?'' asks Old Melv from behind the counter. Melv is the owner of this saloon. The town folks like to joke that Melv's bar was here first, the town was just built around it. Melv has seen many strange sightings in his day and can always tell when someone is going to cause trouble. His philosophy has always been `` Never judge a man when he's pissed drunk. But always judge a man by the order of his first drink''. 
 
 
 `` Jack on the Rocks'' the stranger states, releasing his coins from his palm down onto the counter. The Melv picks up the coins and looks at the man suspiciously. He reaches under the counter. The townfolks watch carefully. Is he reaching for the glass or his gun? 
 
 
 Melv slams the glass down onto the counter. He dumps the ice and pours the Jack Daniels. After one more glance, Melv leaves the stranger to attend to his newspaper. 
 
 
 The tension in the room immediately releases. Conversations pick back up as if nothing happened in the first place. This is a normal Friday night in the town. The room is incredibly humid, it feels as if the walls are sweating. Most folks are sitting quietly, making love to their drinks. Some are old friends, catching up after a long day of work. In the corner, a confrontation begins. 
 
 
 `` Why the fuck do you always have to come in here with those fucking books?'' demands Butch. Butch is the leader among his pack of friends. They come to the bar every night, comparing women and bikes. Butch always has the last word and his friends always agree with him, afraid to pick a fight. Although they would never admit to this. 
 
 
 Butch is talking to Ned. Ned is the outcast of the town. He is the only one who finished high school and went to college. Granted, he never finished college, but that does n't matter he'll tell you. Ned believes that college is where you go to be a clone in a corporate office. He disappeared for a few years. `` Finding myself'' is what he'll tell you. He says that he went to Mexico for a little bit. `` Mexico is the land of beautiful food and beautiful women'' his say if you ask. However, the rumor is that the real reason Ned was gone is because he got a woman knocked up. Somewhere out in Arizona. He helped her out for a few years, helping pay for the bills and raising the kid. Trying to be a good man. But then he just snapped. Could n't take it anymore. Left the girl and her kid in the middle of the night and did n't even leave a note. Came back to town to hide out for a bit. Although, this is just rumor. 
 
 
 `` What are you saying?'' asks Ned, not even looking up from his book. The townfolks heckle him about his books daily. 
 
 
 Butch takes another drink of his beer. He's had a rough day at home and has been waiting for the opportunity to blow off steam. `` I said why the fuck do you always fucking have to come in the Melv's with those fucking books?'' 
 
 
 `` Does me reading somehow offend you?'' Ned asks, flicking a page. His eyes are glued to his book. 
 
 
 `` You know, I'm just wondering who comes to a bar to fucking read? You can barely fucking see in this shithole. The only reason I can think of is because you want to prove that you're better than all of us. Well news flash Einstein, you're not a damn thing'' Butch's group lets out a grunt in agreement. 
 
 
 `` You want to take a guess at what I'm reading Bill'' Ned looks up. 
 
 
 `` Call me Bill again and I'll punch your ugly ass teeth out'' 
 
 
 `` My apologies there Butch. I thought you stopped using that nickname in grade school. My mistake. Anyway, the book is called `` The Pocket Made''. Do you want to guess what it is about? 
 
 
 `` I do n't give two shits about..'' 
 
 
 `` The book is about a man named Jack'' Ned cuts him off. `` Jack grew up in a town quite like this one. In fact, Jack reminds me a bit of you. Narcissistic. Possibly a psychopath. Do you want to know what happens to Jack?'' 
 
 
 `` Fuck off you...'' 
 
 
 `` He lives a long long life. In a jail cell. After snapping his wife's neck because she tried to leave him. Could n't take him not more. Too controlling and abusive. And ugly. So anyway, I've been hearing that you have been having some trouble at home with your wife. I've even heard rumors that she's trying to leave you. Been thinks of snapping her neck recently?'' 
 
 
 All at once, Butch flips the table, knocking down all the drinks and glassware. He lunges at Ned, only to be held back by his gang. Everyone in the room has their eyes on Butch. The only sound in the room is the ringing of the cock of a gun. Melv is standing behind the counter, his gun pointed at Butch. Everyone is quite, some have seen Melv kill a man before. The tension returns. 
 
 
 `` Get out'' says Melv. He does n't need to ask twice. Butch pushes his gang off of him. `` I'm gon na get you'' says Butch, pointing at Ned. He picks up his keys off the floor and stomps out of the saloon. His gang follows. Melv with his gun pointed at him the whole time. After slamming the bar door shut, the roar of his motorcycle vibrated the wooden panels until it fades off into the distance. Melv relaxes and replaces his shotgun back to its original location. He continues reading his newspaper. 
 
 
 Ned is smirking. He radiates like a boxer winning the heavyweight title. He has never felt more alive. He'll have to confront Butch again, but not today. 
 
 
 The stranger finishes his drink. Melv notices and pours him another one. Ned notices. With another smirk and a light chuckle, Ned speaks to the stranger `` You know, you remind me of a guy in a different book. His name is...'' 
 
 
 Before Ned can finish his sentence, the stranger stands up. He talks off his cowboy hat and places it on the bar counter. He is Dwayne Johnson, The Rock. The walks quickly to Ned who at this point peed his trousers. Melv stares in awe, The Rock has always been a WWE fan. 
 
 
 Dwayne Johnson approaches Ned, standing at least one foot over him. He lifts Ned above his head and spins him in a circle. Ned's legs and arms are flailing about. Ned lets out a streak. Dwayne puts Ned into neck hold and walks towards the closest window. Dwayne chucks Ned out the window, the glass shattering. The town folks watch in awe. Without saying a word, Dwayne Johnson picks up his cowboy hat and finishes his drink. He walks out the bar the same way he came in, slow and powerful. From that day forward, the townfolks learned that the rock always wins.

title: story-56
text:
Deputy Smith was not the kind of person to react to anything. But when he saw the photos, his jaw dropped. He looked at the developer and then back at the photo, shrugging his shoulders in a very very very exaggerated way. 
 `` Wa's wrong Smitt? Do n't recognize your boss?'' 
 
 `` I ne're liked photographs anyway, they always look faked'' 
 
 `` Smitty, there aint much you can fake when takin a picture takes 25minutes'' 
 
 `` Well, that's it, who would be takin the picture by the bank at just the right time to get'im?'' 
 
 `` I took the picture Smitt, like I told ya. Yesterday. He was out there for an hour'' 
 
 `` Well they aint enough evidence for me, I got ta go ponder''. 
 
 Deputy Smith left the studio with that relaxed state of mind which results from the aftermath of stress. He decided to walk up the rocky hill and contemplate his thoughts. `` Nothin seems to make my mind more clear.'' he thought, before taking the last few strides and plopping himself on the large rock which had found a new identity as a chair. He rolled a cigarette with the precision of a craftsman, and then swiftly rolled another after it fell apart. His unparalleled talent for deep thinking and focus was underway as he began to try and understand how the sheriff could have possibly committed the crimes. He suddenly had his attention overtaken by a crawling caterpillar across the sandy ground. Several minutes later, he gathered his thoughts once more and continued. 
 `` Well, what did me and the sheriff do yesterday? Well, we wen' down to the saloon so he could make sure that e'ryone wa'nt bein too rowdy. Sheriff always drinks as much as the heftiest guy at the place so he'knows that the people are n't getting too drunk. Sheriff ne'er scolded anyone for bein too sluggish, must be a lot of responsible drinkers in this town I always thought. After that we went out to visit the three girls that live with some older lady, I think their mother maybe. Fine young ladies. They always call him about alleged breakin n enterins, I do n't think he really beleives it much though, but he does take quite a time checkin their rooms with them, Sheriff always loved flattering the public. Must be one of the reasons I admire him. Now let's see.....We left those women's house and then did our daily patrollin' round the blocks. Then Sheriff told me he heard somethin', that he heard sum' suspicious in the bank building. I think I said'Aint it locked Sheriff?' and he said somethin like'Yeah, but I got told a secret way to gettin in by the manager when he opened it, perks of bein the sheriff'. I ca n't wait one day get perks like that. On orders from the man himself I stood lookout'case any other criminals came around while sheriff was away. Spent most of the day like that, nothin fancy but I got ta be the watchman while Ol' Sheriff is puttin his self on the line'. 
 
 The night was beginning to sneak up onto the mountain. Smith got up and stretched, satisfied once again with his critical meditation and conclusion. 
 
 `` i was watchin Sheriff's back the whole yesterday, no way in hell he had time to do any of that. I knew those' dang photographs were fakery''. 
 
 the end

title: story-57
text:
Ahh I love *third* days, they are the best day of *the five*. 
 
 Wake up, to the light switching on to the national colours, Red, Blue and Yellow, the loud universal anthem buzzing overhead in my government announcement speakers in my room. 
 `` Always going down, down to the future, never going up, for up is in the past!!!'' 
 I can never remember the rest of the words without the speakers playing but it is so catchy, plus everybody in the world standing to attention at the same time, fills my heart with awe as we all stand to attention, really stretches the legs and then, when it is finished, breakfast time. One portion of rice with sugar water, delicious. 
 
 Third days are when we are allowed out of the work area to the sporting area of the world, it is a pretty exciting time, everybody is milling around and working out. Most people are really focused on exercise. 
 
 Then the quarter of a day anthem occurs after 2 hours. 
 
 Seeing everybody standing there, no matter what they are doing, is mesmerizing, and that is the cue for everybody to eat, so everybody moves to the lunch area and waits for their portion of powdered protein and helping of water. 
 
 I work on the upper levels of the world, nobody really goes up there, but sometimes I like to sit on the sky rails and look down on the world. 
 
 I can see all 53 of its inhabitants and they all work together to make the world so much bigger. There used to be 54 but 32 took some extra rice at food time and the overseer asked to see him. We have n't seen him since. The overseer takes care of us though, so he probably took care of him and put him in a place with all the rice he could want. 
 
 In our world we dig down, because it is the way. The way we work. Someday, we will uncover the mysteries of the below and then, maybe, encounter new life but mostly we uncover shiny rocks and then we put them in the hatch as the overseer instructs. 
 
 Nobody looks to the sky though, with its dull browns and its weird little thread like structures confuse me. The overseer tells us that those threads are the work of the great evil, although, nobody has ever seen the overseer, but he looks after us, through the hatch. The hatch brings food and water to our world, several of the people worship the hatch, it is like a magical porthole to a wonderland of treats, but it seems always empty when anybody looks inside. 
 
 My favorite place is somewhere I call strange light. It is an odd place, the strange light appears sometimes, through the sky and I have been wanting to make the strange light larger for a while. 
 Sometimes the strange light is really bright, the brightest thing in the whole world! But I have to cover up because it is so bright, it can burn my skin. 
 
 I have 1 cycle left to enjoy my strange light hobby, I have just worked up the courage to see more of it, so I will dig to make the strange light bigger. 
 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- 
 
 My fingers scratching the weird strands out the way, the strange light is nearly large enough to fit my head through the orifice leading to it. 
 
 I push my way through to the other side. 
 
 There are more people here, they have n't seen me, but they are just sitting on green stuff. 
 
 I pull myself, fully into the strange light. 
 
 `` This place is so... huge!'' I spin on the spot, looking around. There are no walls. The sky seems to blend into the distance, everything reaches upwards, not like my world where everything reaches down, from the sky. 
 
 The ground feels soft under my feet, the green stuff is like little soft pointy things, it's really bright, I am glad I brought my goggles. 
 
 `` Are you okay?'' 
 
 WHOA!!! A voice from behind me!!! I turn to look and there is a person, he has dark skin, it is so strange, I reach out for his hand but he pulls away. 
 
 `` Whoa, you have really dark skin!'' 
 
 `` What are you? Some kind of racist?'' The strange dark person says. 
 
 `` Is that what I am? Am I a racist, dark person? `` 
 
 `` Oh you better not be fucking fronting Cracka!'' 
 
 `` What is a Cracka?'' I ask. 
 
 `` You is a Cracka? Now get the fuck outta here before I whoop yo' ass!'' 
 
 The person seemed angry, so I wandered a little further, there were more people, they seemed so nice, they kept handing me shiny round things and thin rectangles, I did n't have any pockets in my work wear so I found a cup and put them in there. 
 
 One of the people stopped to speak to me, she seemed concerned for me. 
 
 `` Are you okay?'' 
 
 `` I think so, but I am a little confused. Has this always been here?'' 
 
 `` What? Are you all right? What's your name.'' 
 
 Name? We did n't have names in my world, the only think I know I go by is 43. `` 43, I guess.'' 
 
 `` No, I do n't mean your age darlin',...'' she said, ``... I mean what do people call you?'' 
 
 I thought for a second, the only thing I have ever been called, aside from my 43 was... `` Oh, I guess my name is Racist Cracka.'' I said smiling, but the other person only looked at me with a wry smile. 
 
 This cup is getting heavy, people keep putting more things in it. Is there somewhere I can go and get something to eat, I missed food time and I ca n't wash these clothes yet because the overseer has n't allocated the water. 
 
 The nice lady took my arm and lead me away from where my world was, I clutched my cup, people were so nice here but it was strange and scary. 
 
 She took me to a place that had a sign on it, it did n't look like the signs in my world. 
 
 She took some of the round things out of my cup and gave them to the person behind the signs. He picked up something and started juggling little bottles and metal pincers, it was amusing, then he handed me a brown thing in a brown thing covered with red and yellow stuff. 
 
 It was odd looking, but... it tasted amazing! `` By the Overseer's way!!! I have to tell the others!!!'' I said running back to where I had emerged into this strange world! They all had to know!!! 
 
 I ran back and the girl followed. 
 
 As I dropped back into my world I looked up, I could see the person I had met, she was standing in the strange light holding a small black box in her hand, looking concerned. 
 
 I raced down from the sky. 
 
 I needed to let everybody know the truth!!! 
 
 As I got back into the main place, I found everybody frantically searching, shouting my name. `` 43!!! Where are you!!!'' 
 
 I bumped into 22. 
 
 `` 22!!! I have seen something, amazing!!!'' 
 
 `` 43, the Overseer want's to see you!!! He seems really angry.'' 
 
 `` Oh my!'' The last person who saw the overseer was never seen again, he took an extra portion of rice for dinner... but I should be fine, I took no rice.'' 
 
 I wandered to the hatch, as everybody gathered around to watch, but before I went into the hatch, I had to tell my story. So I started from the beginning and as I got half way through I heard 45 shout. `` HERESY!!!''... and more of them joined in. Suddenly, shafts of light appeared from above, followed by more lights. 
 
 As they drew closer the hatch's ever watchful eye went out. 
 
 `` It is the end times!!!'' Many of the world dwellers fled to take refuge anywhere they could, as the blue men with the hand lights descended from above. 
 
 They shone the lights in our faces and pulled us away. Some of them fought but I knew better. I followed one of them back up into the strange light. There were even more lights now outside the orifice. The lights were on top of large metal boxes, with the words police. 
 
 `` Do you have any more of these?'' I asked, showing him the half eaten food. 
 
 `` Hot dogs? Yeah, we got plenty down the station, everything is going to be okay buddy, we got ya, but first we have got to ask you a few questions.'' 
 
 These people are so nice. 
 
 `` Let go of me!!!'' That was the voice of the Overseer!!! I turned to look. He was just a man and he had his hands behind his back as he was being led into the metal box by the blue men. 
 
 `` HAIL TO THE OVERSEER!!!'' 
 
 `` I do n't know that man!!! I want a lawyer!!!'' He shouted as he vanished into the car. 
 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- - 
 
 I realize now, looking back on the past year, that we few had so much robbed from us. A world of experiences that we were outlawed from discovering. The underworld that we were trapped in was just a means of making money for Harvey but it was all we were allowed to know. He was no God, just a vile man who now enjoys his own little microcosm, the same regimen that we endured for years, except his term is in a jail cell and he knows all about the sunlight. 
 
 We were his slaves in the pit, not allowed to know anything other than its surroundings. We were just his tools, but not anymore, because we are free. 
 
 Now if you will excuse me, I have to meet Anna, it's our anniversary, we're getting hotdogs in the park.

text:
“ I would like to now bring your attention to this relic of the old times. The times when the Ban on Poetry was merely a distant thought within our leader ’ s mind. ” Spoke the guide, whom hardly managed to force a smile upon her own lips. 
 
 Ah yes, the infamous Ban on Poetry. A little act implemented a mere decade ago whose purpose was to limit the freedom of the people. It had of course been labeled not as an attack on freedom, but rather as a measure to protect the people. The government must have found some perverted sense of enjoyment throughout their campaign to push forward such a pivotal change in the history of their people. After all, they ’ d gone through such trouble to release the documentation of terrible poems that people had ‘ written ’. 
 
 “ It is rumored to be the only remaining piece of poetry. It serves as a foul reminder of the terrible powers of poetry. ” The guide explained. 
 
 She wouldn ’ t believe any of it. No, there was more to this than they were all letting on. Poetry was hardly an efficient way to insert an idea into a person ’ s mind. After all, it first had to be written in a peculiar way, then it had to be distributed, after that it would have to be received, read and processed by all its recipients… No. If someone truly wanted to bring havoc upon the world and insisted on using written words as their medium, then they would have to use a straight-forward form. A form that was believed to be safe. A form that could be misinterpreted as a story. A form that conveyed ideas so well, that its ideas could be hidden in the blank space surrounding its characters. 
 
 Why, it should n't have taken her as long as it did to realise it. The best method to convey an idea in such a way would be prose. It would be easy to disguise a plot to destroy someone or something as a mere ‘ plot element ’ within a ‘ fictional ’ story. Yes. Stories are the perfect cover for these things. To her dismay, however, Grace ’ s thoughts were discontinued by a sudden announcement on the PA system within the museum. 
 
 “ Attention, citizens. We hereby announce that all written forms of language are now strictly prohibited. Anyone seen with written works after seventeen-hundred hours will be tried for a crime against the people ’ s safety. For more details on the new Literature Ban, please report to the parliament before twenty-one-hundred hours. That is all. ” The man spoke. 
 
 ( The product of my boredom, seeing this prompt, and 15 free minutes. I could go on, but I do n't think that would be wise... )
