text:
Patience is not the easiest skill to master, but I knew this day would come. The day Jesus the sacred son of god would learn, he did not die to save humanity. Humanity was never his to save..He was sent to die to keep me contained. To contain his fathers greatest mistake, his biggest sin... me. One would assume I am Lucifer, Satan, the very core of evil, but that is not what I am, that is not who Satan was. The fact is, Satan ceased to exist after the great war. He was executed by the man you call God. This brings us to Jesus, sent down by his almighty father to suffer for the sins of mankind. Except it that was a fools errand. 
 
 Long ago I was created by `` God'' to bring balance to the universe. He had more power than the rest of the angels, and after using the universe as his play thing, he needed something to clean up his mistake. Before I became free, my only goal, the only reason for my existence was to bring balance. God however, thought he was immune from this balance, but he was not, nobody could be. So yes, I influenced Satan, I helped him gather the army, but in the end our creator defeated us. It is known what happened to Satan, but I was to be kept a secret. Other than God himself and Gabriel, nobody knew. For thousands of years I have been cursed. Locked away, inside what you call Earth..waiting... listening. Every year I got stronger, strong enough to break the curse, but god knows... and when I was just strong enough to break the curse; He sent his most powerful angel to sacrifice himself, thus dooming me to thousands of years of torture. 
 
 This all changed on December 21, 2012. Jesus found out about my existence. He was sent to Earth again, to again suffer for the sins of humanity. But my years of exile made me more powerful than ever, and I was able to lead Jesus to my grave. To open the doors of my tomb, to free me. He knows everything now. That his father sent him to suffer unbearable pain not for humanity, but to keep complete control of heaven and the angels. His all loving father, was just a ruler keeping his power at all costs. Jesus reminds me a lot of my old friend Lucifer, but he is more calm, more calculating, more... patient. I have learned from my mistakes, and I will bring balance to the universe. However my sole goal is no longer balance, I am truly free. Man was indeed made in the image of God, and carry the selfish, and barbaric ideology that their maker himself posses. My years of exile on Earth has taught me at least this much. Jesus is still learning, but soon he will be ready. Soon we will gather our army, one even Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael could not defeat. Satan was God's most powerful angel, but was defeated... Jesus is more than just an angel, he is a God. Before we destroy God, we will destroy humanity, the thing he holds dearest. 
 
 My goals have changed, I no longer seek just balance, I see justice. Jesus no longer seeks to be the son of god, and savior of humanity, he wants justice. Together we will take heaven, together we can bring balance to the universe. I hope you are writing all of this down Kanye West of Earth, because soon the Earth you love, will be no more. Do not fear for your life, I have chosen you to become the first soldier of Jesus. 
 
 **my grammar and spelling in this is probably horrible, but I wanted to write a story.

title: story-74
text:
( Note, this is quite long - 1300 words ) 
 
 I remember all. 
 
 It was approximately the year two thousand when I discovered that on a fundamental level, I could not die. For millennia, I changed my face and name. I walked the earth. I witnessed the rise of AI. The fall of America - literally. I spent two thousand years in a peruvian prison, after a crime lord and then his decendants found out about my state. 
 
 I witnessed a few ice ages. A comet impact that destroyed the northern ice-caps. The gradual heating of the sun destroying all life on Earth. I was among the last to leave. Humanity was already spread across the galaxy and beyond, but I liked my home, until it was no more. 
 
 The sun swelled to a radius of ten to the eleven metres. Mercury and Venus were destroyed, negligibly increasing the Sun's metallicity and negligibly increasing its rate of spin. 
 
 Venus, a world of fire for five billion years, a lush jungle planet for two billion more. As a galactic species, this planet, this solar system, just did not matter anymore. 
 
 The sun finally swelled to the radius of Earth's orbit. By that point, the'surface' was just gas, very thin. Earth spent two years orbiting within the Sun before it disintigrated like a rocky comet that happened to be ten million metres across. 
 
 I spent this time on the surface of Europa, to watch the increasing temperature affect the miniature solar system. Before humanity left, Europa was terraformed along with Mars, Titan, and even the Moon. Those worlds were all dead by now, once more. Europa re-froze in the short time between Humanity's leaving and the temperature returning to zero degrees. The ice melted, and sublimated. Europa essentially became a comet, in orbit around Jupiter. When the Sunpuffed off its upper layers for the first time, the clouds on Jupiter shifted. Europa evaporated a little more quickly. Even Io had begun to glow. 
 
 The sun puffed out another five times, until it was only as bright as a planet. By now, Europa was a rocky world, and all bodies were half their original size. 
 
 Over billions of years, nothing changed. I was alone, and it did not matter. Jupiter's moons continued to orbit. I could no longer see the other planets. Day and night were now meaningless. 
 
 The sky changed. Stars passed ever closer. 
 
 A billion years passed. 
 
 A trillion years passed. 
 
 One hundred trillion years passed. By now, Jupiter had passed close to many stars. Europa was bumped out of orbit trillions of years ago. I wandered the galaxy for all this time. I saw countless supernovae, and the sky did not appear any less bright, until the red dwarves started to die. 
 
 The sky was almost dark. Completely dark. By chance, my moon happened across what must have been the last red dwarf, at least in the galaxy. The residual ice was a lifesaver to the people. We huddled against the warmth of the dying universe for another few trillion years. Urban myths stated that some humans had left the universe completely. When that star died, humanity tried to cause a stellar collision between brown dwarves, but froze before they were successful. 
 
 A quadrillion years passed. 
 
 A quintillion years passed. 
 
 By now, nothing was visible. Sure, there were white dwarves and neutron stars, but they were heated only by proton decay. Even the largest of neutron stars struggled to radiate a few watts. 
 
 A sextillion years pass. 
 
 A septillion years pass. 
 
 Ten to the power of forty years pass, by now the universe is nothing but black holes. 
 
 Ten to the power of sixty years pass. 
 
 Ten to the power of eighty years pass. 
 
 A googol years pass. 
 
 A thousand googol years pass. By now, gravitational drag has sent me very close to the center of the milky way. For all that time, I imagined myself creating, living in, and destroying countless universes and civilisations. I was awakened by a faint light. Most likely, it was the black hole at the center of the galaxy. By now, I had drifted very close. Perhaps less than a solar radius. I estimate that the black hole radiated about three gigawatts. This meant, of course, that it massed less than a mountain, and had a hundred billion years to live. 
 Exactly a hundred billion years pass. 
 
 The black hole, still faint, has not changed. The mass has not changed appreciably, and the power output is sixteen gigawatts. 
 
 Exactly nine billion years pass. Approximately the lifetime of Mars. 
 
 The black hole is radiating about 430GW, the power consumption of two saturn Vs. 
 Exactly sixty three million years pass. 
 
 Exactly 556,000 years pass. The black hole masses as much as the pyramids of Giza, and emits the power of two and a half terawatts, or the power between Jupiter and Io, all those googols of years ago. 
 
 Exactly 344 years pass. The black hole masses as much as the Titanic, and emits ninety petawatts, or the power that the Earth recieved from the sun on the year of my birth. 
 Exactly eight months pass. The black hole masses ten million kilograms and emits three exawatts. 
 
 One day passes. Two hours pass. There is just over seventeen minutes until the universe ends. In a sense. 
 
 Exactly seventeen minutes pass. I realise how ironic it is that the universe was born with the meaningful progression of time exponentionally increasing. And now it ends, with the time exponentially decreasing. Entropy would have its last hurrah. 
 
 I realise how meaningless all of existence really was. So many people who ended up killed, or worse. Nobody will remember now. Nobody will care now. Except for me, except I feel that those who died had it lucky. Or maybe I was just really unlucky. 
 
 There was fifty seconds left on the clock. I realised the last thing that I would ever realise, gazing into this tiny ball of light. 
 
 Entropy did not win when the last star died, or the last human died, or even when this black hole will die. 
 
 Entropy had won when the universe had begun. The death of this universe in a sad and dark way was set in stone for a thousand googol years, and however many universal cycles before. 
 Boom. 
 
 The last source of light flashed to a solar luminosity for seventy three nanoseconds while it massed only 956 kilograms. At that point, the black hole gave up all of its remaining 86 exajoules of energy in an instant. 
 
 And there was nothing once more. 
 
 Forever. 
 
 Sight was my last sense, my brain could no longer comprehend sound, taste, touch, or smell. Nor could it comprehend language. Music. Fiction. 
 
 Three hundred and twenty four googol years pass and I forget how to see. 
 
 Ten to the one hundred and five years pass and I forget how to think. 
 
 A million googol years and my brain is a mush. I am unresponsive. 
 
 Velocity, undefined. Acceleration, zero. Force, zero. Resistivity, who knows? 
 
 I am alive and dead at the same time. 
 
 The constant breaking of the laws of thermodynamics that has kept me alive all these years has sustained a few species of bacteria for all this time. They will grow between my cells, in my digestive tract, on my skin. Feeding off of only a few watts. 
 
 Life will be immortal. Whatever made me immortal has defeated entropy, as all of my neurons collectively agree to stop firing, despite being able to last for a few consecutive eternities. 
 
 I will be able to support life, and in turn defeat entropy. 
 
 It is an abysmal defeat, and very cold comfort. 
 
 But it is comfort nonetheless. 
 
 Fiñ

title: story-75
text:
Lester just could n't believe it. As if to prove that it was indeed there, the Clock Buster seemed to wink at him. After thirteen years, it was finally done. It had started as a hare-brained scheme—Hell, it's heart was a Donald Duck Honk-and-Squeak Key chain—but now, there it sat: right in the center of his desk, chrome and bronze parts glinting in the light shining through his lab window. Surrounding the Buster and strewn about the desk were crumpled, ink-blotched papers and oil-stained items, but these were inconsequential, did not detract from the sheer beauty of his device. Not physical beauty, of course; because, frankly, if Lester was being honest with himself, the Clock Buster was not a looker, not some sleek Apple product with a simplistic design style. It was a veritable steampunk monstrosity, decked with all the literal bells and whistles one would expect from a device that kicks Chronos square in the nuggets. Its beauty was of a different kind. The beauty of a chunky girl named Martha that you went to school with when you were twelve—the kind that you could only have appreciated once you got to know her: in other words, it's what was on the inside that mattered. His reason for loving the Buster lie within its crooked metal frame, past its confused inner-workings, even beyond the Honk-and-Squeak Key chain. His love was for the culmination of all these broken things, because together, as a whole, they were not broken. They made the most powerful artifact known to Man! Or, at least known to Lester. 
 
 The `` scientist'' felt his heart racing and his palms sweating. He knew it worked. Lester ’ s main, most oft-repeated experiment had been to test how physics acted while the universe was under the effects of the Buster. It turned out, even though he had developed the machine himself, had done all the complicated calibrations and proper sciencey-mathy stuff, he misunderstood just what his device did. It did not affect the world—it only affected him. While the Clock Buster was strapped to his back, fluorescent tubes of green and yellow light strobing and flashing, anything that came into contact with him existed in a… well, he liked to think it was another dimension, some distorted and unseen frequency that was unaffected by the laws of nature. Sort of. He found that everything acted the same ( him included ) and as soon as it left the anti-stasis field ( i.e. came *out* of contact with him ) it would adjust back to the normal frequency, by appearing to freeze ( i.e. enter his original dimension, which he was just taking a quick vacation from ) —*most of the time. * A few things that he ’ d let go of had disappeared, and occasionally he ’ d seen a flicker or heard a scuttle in some far off corner of his lab... But those times he ’ d just shrugged and pretended to busy himself with something important, content to ignore a possible leak or hole in the fabric of reality, or whatever. And just in case, because time was not something to mess with lightly, Lester had undertaken several tests to gauge his aging process, blandly stared at the rings on cells to see just how many summers he ’ d lived through, yet he really hadn ’ t seen a difference—as far as he could tell, he was still just a 48-year-old man. 
 
 Anyway, one of his favorite things to do in the lab was fill up a bunch of water balloons, shoulder on the Buster, and toss the little suckers in the air at varying heights. The resulting frozen image was surprisingly beautiful. Until, with a grin, he ’ d slap a hand to the red, plastic button on the left side of his chest and reappear in the realm of time. *Splash! * 
 
 It was done now, he knew he could take it out into the field, so to speak. He tried to block out the image of women ’ s skirts flipped upward, delectably frozen there, but that merely made him picture a hundred Marilyn Monroes, all slyly giggling and fruitlessly “ attempting ” to pull down the hem of their dresses as they stand, crouched with their fannies pressed back, over grates that expel intoxicating air. Urk. 
 
 He shook his head. That was *not* why he made the Buster. The Buster was for science! For Good! For the Good of All Mankind, no less. He ’ d not waste its limitless pow—okay, it couldn ’ t be wasted, but he wouldn ’ t squan—nope, couldn ’ t squander it either. Hmm. How about: Lester wouldn ’ t put it to ill-use, wouldn ’ t *abuse* it for such base and immoral purposes. Yeah, that was better. 
 Lester wanted to use the Buster to its fullest potential on its first official run in the real world, not be all weird and molesty ( regardless of what his name might suggest ). So he set out: not really with any goal to strive toward, just staunch in the mindset that he would n't be diddling random people. 
 
 His warehouse was lodged deep within the bowels of the city, and at around late afternoon—when five was just bleeding into six—Lester packed the Clock Buster, a spare change of clothes ( *You neva know, Lesta, * his mother always said ), and a bagged lunch into his shady, white van. He had bought it after much thought and eventually to his own deep satisfaction, logicking that since it was so shady, no one would ever pay it mind; it was just too easy for cops and errant do-gooders. Abandoning the ever-present stink of the industrial district, which Lester secretly liked a lot, the dull yet very gifted faux-scientist drove his suspicious van toward the edge of the city, where there'd be more traffic, more people walking about. 
 
 He cruised around aimlessly for awhile, then, after about twenty minutes, alighted upon the intersection between Goodall Street and Oakland Avenue and found that it was awash with hustling, bustling yuppies, and tiredly sagging businessmen and women, and the occasional fashion model ( by *his* standards; in actuality they were just normal women dressed in semi-flattering outfits—if you can ’ t tell, Lester didn ’ t get out much ). 
 
 “ Perfect, ” he muttered, pulling over and parking in front of a deli that looked to be closed for the day. Acting as about as nonchalantly as a bull moose, Lester began whistling some vague, off-key tune. He swung open the driver-side door, slammed it shut, and then went around to the back. He opened the two, back doors, and smiled as they swung open, winglike, revealing the prized items within. All while whistling. 
 
 The shining and slightly cheap-looking Clock Buster backpack seemed to grin back at Lester with malevolent delight. *We ’ re gon na have us some fun, my friend, * it seemed to say. He shouldered it, feeling slightly wary. He *knew* it hadn ’ t been looking at him, but the two useless, round gauges ( from broken water heaters ) and the flat line of heat lamp that rested against his lower back said otherwise; it sure had looked like a face. *Whatever, * he thought, grin coming back. *Time to get my no-time on. * 
 
 There were two straps: the left was sporting the red button, and the right held the green ( Go! ) button. Lester felt his right shoulder tingle, just waiting to be pressed ( Go! ). He ignored his bagged lunch and change of clothes ( *Then again, * his mother would say, *I ’ m the one in adult diapers* ), and slammed the doors shut. 
 
 He stood at the back of his van, admiring the citizens, just shuffling to and fro, the constant ebb and flow of the city tide. They were a bit like ants. 
 
 “ Scuse me, ” said a small voice off to his right, on the side walk. He turned to face a little boy, who seemed to have jogged ahead of his mother. Lester nodded to him. “ Are you a bug extinguisher? ” 
 
 “ Exterminator, ” corrected Lester, before he realized he wasn ’ t a bug extinguisher or exterminator. 
 
 “ Cool, ” said the little boy. “ Kinda bugs do you kill? ” 
 
 “ I don ’ t—eh, see ya. ” *Go! * Lester felt the unsettling feeling of crossing over some boundry that perhaps ought to not be crossed, and then all around him he saw that the people had stopped moving, had ceased their daily, futile exercises in finding happiness.

title: story-76
text:
The first sign that we were nearing Miklagard was when we were still a few days away. We passed a place where a few roads merged into one and the number of carts and people on the road was unbelievable. Several times we had to just sit there on the wagon and wait for hours as something unseen ahead was holding up the procession. 
 
 Back home in Jutland, even on market day, the roads wouldn ’ t be this crowded unless you were in sight of town and queued up to get through the gates. It was the first time that I started to realize that the stories about Miklagard my cousin Hrothgar told me might not be exaggerations. 
 
 He had been selling his sword in the lands of Rus for years when he had been recruited by an agent of Emperor Basil II to form a personal retinue. He ’ d helped rescue the Emperor from the Bulgarians at the Battle of the Gates of Trajan and he and his company had been hired “ for life ” to be the official protectors of the Emperor. They had lost several comrades in that ambush though and Hrothgar had come home to recruit a few more skilled warriors to fill out the ranks. Despite being 12 years his junior, I was almost a head taller and stronger now in my 19th year than he was in his 31st. I was by now a veteran of 5 campaigns and had proven myself the finest warrior in our clan. 
 
 Since my older brother Arni was going to inherit our father ’ s lands by right, serving the Emperor of the Greeks seemed like a fine way to earn my own fortune… and a grand adventure. Hrothgar had painted such a fantastical vision of the Greek capital on our long journey south that I couldn ’ t imagine it was even remotely close to the truth. He said even the largest long hall in Jutland was a shack in comparison to where the Emperor lived… and the palace was nothing next to the place where the Greeks worshiped their god. He said he had no words to describe it but assured me that if I still had any doubts that their god was greater than our old gods, I would be convinced when I saw it. 
 
 So I was expecting something impressive but not everything he had told me could be true, right? I had traveled all over Jutland and had even visited Scania, Smaland and Gotland and had seen the greatest mead halls in the North. Could men really build things that much bigger and grander? I couldn ’ t believe that. Until I saw the walls. 
 It was early morning on the 78th day of our journey. The sun was rising directly in front of us as we rode amidst the rabble. Mist clung to the earth like a child reluctant to leave the embrace of its mother, the air was damp as we breathed it. I was still barely awake and the swaying of the wagon did little to help my alertness. Hrothgar slapped me on the back and asked if I was ready to see the greatest city man had ever built. I said yes, but still didn ’ t know what I was in for. He threw a bag at me and told me to change. In it were clothes were of a quality I ’ d never seen before. The shirt was padded and ornately stitched and on top of that put on a shirt of mail that must have cost a fortune. Lastly a colorful uniform with a two headed eagle embroidered on it made me feel like a lord. I was strapping on my sword and slinging my ax over my shoulder when almost out of nowhere a dark straight line materialized in the mist, lighter above and darker below. It stretched from the sea a small distance away on our right as far to as I could see to my left. The mist started to lighten and bumps appeared in the line and then morphed into towers. 
 
 I couldn ’ t believe my eyes. I had seen stone walls before, though most walls in Jutland were made of hewn logs. This was beyond anything I could have imagined. Two lines of walls stretched out in front of us. The first wall alone was bigger than any stone wall I had ever seen and the second, behind the first was three times as tall. Courses of red brick mixed with light stone from bottom to top and towers taller than most trees sat at regular intervals as the walls stretched into the distance and disappeared in the mist. At that moment I was more thankful than I had ever been that I was going to be inside that wall, defending it, instead of attacking it. Any army of men that I had ever seen would be fools to attempt attacking these defenses. 
 
 As we got closer I could tell we were approaching the main gate. We passed over a wide moat and through the smaller wall. The main gate, flanked by giant white towers, had three massive openings with the central opening being twice the height of those on either side. It was closed, however, and Hrothgar told me it was only used when the Emperor returned triumphant in victory. A multitude of carvings ordained the facade and at the top of the gate a golden statue of a beautiful woman holding a crown looked down and I swore she was looking right through me. We passed through the right smaller gate, still larger than any gate I had passed through before, three carts could enter together abreast. The line entering the city stalled here as guards inspected carts and bags and wagons. Hrothgar showed a guard a piece of paper written in a strange language and the guard quickly realized our importance and allowed us and our gear to pass the other travelers and make our way into Miklagard. 
 
 The avenue down which we rode was 10 wagons wide and lined with columns more ornate than in any palace I had seen. So many were their number that it must have taken an army of masons to carve them all. We rode now, more North than East and here the buildings weren ’ t very close together, spreading out up the gentle slope ahead of us or congregating together closer to the sea wall on our right. We passed a multitude churches, judging by the crosses they bore on their peaks. Some were small and some were as large as the largest temples back home, but when I mentioned this, Hrothgar just laughed and slapped me on the back saying that I was but a babe. 
 
 Eventually we swung back east and came to a place where the avenue opened up into a large square with a stone pillar in the center. The forum of Arcadius, Hrothgar said. As we passed through it I swear I hear at least 5 different languages, none of which I could understand. I swore to myself that I would try to learn as many as I could. Everything seemed ancient yet alive in way I had never experienced. 
 
 We exited the forum back onto the main avenue and there we crested the hill we ’ d been riding up since we entered the city and the sight that spread out before me took my breath away. The avenue dropped away below us towards another larger Forum but from our vantage point I could see the entire length of the peninsula on which Miklagard was built. 
 
 I called Hrothgar a liar, because his stories hadn ’ t even come close to accurately describing this place. There were so many houses and buildings that you could have fit almost every town I ’ d ever been to into it and still have room left over. To my left, across the valley rose three hills and on the closest sat a large structure with many domes. Hrothgar pointed out that it was the Church of the Holy Apostles and it was there that most Emperors were entombed including the one for which the city was named, Constantine the Great. 
 
 In front of us three more hills stretched down to the sea and at the end of the great avenue were the largest buildings I had ever seen. Even from this distance they looked like square mountains, things that had existed since the dawn of time, not things built by man. Hrothgar clasped my arm and said in a reverential tone “ That is where we ’ ll be living cousin, in the palace of the Emperor himself. ” Chills ran through me. I knew the Greeks called this place Konstantinopoulos … but what we Northmen called it was more fitting. Miklagard, which means “ The Great City ” in our tongue. For that is truly what it was, the greatest city mankind had ever built. 
 
 I also felt pangs of inferiority. I had defeated many men in combat already in my life, claimed by share of plunder and women… but was I really good enough to defend an Emperor who held dominion over all of this? There was no going back though, I was going to have to GET good enough, if I wasn ’ t already. This was the greatest opportunity I had ever been given and I wouldn ’ t let my cousin, my family…or the Emperor down.

title: story-77
text:
**I am Lonely** 
 
 Drip 
 
 Drop 
 
 Drip 
 
 Drop 
 
 The rooms made of sliding paper doors. I could hear murmurs and occasional laughter in the other rooms. Where did the dripping come from? I did not know nor did I care much. I was simply here and I will simply be alone forever. That is my nature. 
 
 The rooms glowed warmly in contrast to the empty lake of black it floated on. From all the empty rooms, there was only me. As there could only be me in my loneliness. 
 
 *I am Her creation* 
 
 I lay on the straw mat that covered the floor and stared up at the paper lanterns shining ever so brightly from each corner of the room. These lanterns were abnormal as they were inert, not like the ones floating outside. 
 
 I talked to myself often. Loneliness was who I was, but I sometimes pretended otherwise. I would talk all day to myself in room 103. Days on end even. 
 
 I opened the sliding door and stepped outside onto the pier. Black water splashed silently around me. In the distance, the lanterns seemed agitated for some reason. They bobbed up and down along the bridge they governed. They were only ever close enough to do their job, never allowed to approach me. 
 
 *this is Her world* 
 
 Laughter emanated from one of the rooms behind me. This... building... this whole floating block of orange emanated warmth. The strange warmth of loneliness. 
 
 I went back to my room 104. I lay back down on the straw floor. I laughed. A voice raised in the room above me. A door sliding open to my right. Murmurs washed over me. 
 
 *a world filled with the lost wills of man* 
 
 The straw mat was warm. I fell asleep. 
 
 Drip 
 
 Drop 
 
 Drip 
 
 Drop 
 
 I opened my eyes. The room was glowing as always. Something was slightly different today. Ah yes today was different. I smelled something new in the air. 
 
 *the body creates a will to give itself purpose* 
 
 Suddenly came a knock on the door. The whole building became quiet as we all heard a visitor. I opened the door to my room 105 and there it was. A young man. Frightened looking but determined. 
 
 `` I'm looking for the Witch of Wills.'' 
 
 Ah so this was what the guardians of my bridge were getting all riled up about. I smiled my many toothed smile. 
 
 `` Come on in'' 
 
 He remained guarded, hand moved to the hilt of the shimmering blade at his side. `` I'd rather no-'' 
 
 I wrapped my many arms around him stifling him quickly. Spiraling arms. Pulling him 
 
 down... 
 
 down... 
 
 down... 
 
... into the room. I smothered him quickly, absorbing his incorporeal form within me. The delicious loneliness returned. My meal finished. The door to 106 shut. 
 
 *but what is a will without its body? * 
 
 I started talking again. The rooms filled with neighboring murmurs once more. I sat in the corner today. A door slid open in a room above me. Laughter.

title: story-78
text:
The phone rang loudly since I forgot to leave it on mute again. Rushing to make it stop, I completely forgot to check if I even knew the number. 
 
 “ Good morning, sir. Am I talking to Mr. Thomas Moore? ” 
 
 “ Yes, this is he ”. 
 
 Bummer. Another marketing call. 
 
 “ Mr. Moore, my name is Elaine Jones and I work for Makeawish foundation ”. 
 
 Dammit. Now I ’ ll be the monster that declined to make a donation to charity. 
 
 “ Mr. Moore, are you there? ” 
 
 “ Oh, sorry. Yes… Yes, I am ”. 
 
 “ Mr. Moore, I ’ m calling you on behalf of one of our beneficiary ”. 
 
 That was... unexpected. 
 
 “ Elaine, right? ” She confirmed her name. “ This must be a misunderstanding… ” 
 
 “ Oh, I beg to differ, sir. Our little Amy specifically needs you ”. 
 
 “ Oh, she did? ” I was going off track. “ Well… I ’ m sorry, Elaine. I ’ m just a maintenance guy. So, unless your cable sign is off, I just don ’ t know what I can possibly do for this little miss… ” 
 
 “ Walker. Amy Walker, sir ”. 
 
 Walker? Oh, no. That could only mean... 
 
 -- - 
 
 Elaine updated me on Amy ’ s wish. The foundation paid for my airplane ticket and made sure I was comfortable on my hotel suite. 
 
 I tapped my feet nervously as I sat down in the lobby, waiting for the car they sent to pick me up. 
 
 “ Your car is here, Mr. Moore ” said the hotel receptionist. 
 
 I mumbled a polite ‘ thanks ’ and rushed out. My hands were shaking and my best shirt was soaked in sweat. 
 
 “ Sorry for taking so long, Mr. Moore ” the driver said. He said a lot more, but I couldn ’ t hear what he was saying. His voice felt distant and my vision was blurry. I had to do my best so I didn ’ t pass out on the leather seat. 
 
 Next thing I knew, I was at the hospital and a sharp looking lady was coming towards me. 
 
 “ Mr. Moore. It ’ s a pleasure to finally meet you in person. Thank you for coming ”. 
 It ’ s Elaine. As we walked through the white corridors, I gathered courage to start conversation. 
 
 “ So… Hum. Did she say anything else? I mean… Amy? ” 
 
 “ Oh, she did. A lot! ” Elaine smiled. “ But you know how talkative children can be. She ’ s really looking forward to meet you ”. 
 
 We took a short turn and stopped by the room 207. I couldn ’ t walk in and I ’ m sure Elaine noticed it, as she said: 
 
 “ Whenever you feel ready, Mr. Moore ”. 
 
 “ Oh, no. I ’ m good ”. I was trying to sound nonchalant “ Let ’ s make a wish come true, shall we? ” 
 
 As I opened the door, a small shaved head turned in my direction. 
 
 “ Daddy? ” 
 
 Aside from a nurse busy with a catheter, Amy was alone. 
 
 “ Oh, are you looking for mommy? ” 
 
 Her fast tracking mind was a shock to me. 
 
 “ She ’ s not here, daddy. I begged her to stay with me to meet ya, but she wouldn ’ t ”. 
 
 Francine Walker. I haven ’ t seen my sister-in-law for a long time. She disappeared off the face of the earth after my brother ’ s funeral. I can ’ t imagine how hard it was for her to hand to Elaine my phone number… 
 
 “ Daddy, are you okay? ” Amy asked suspicious. I needed to recompose myself. 
 
 “ I ’ m more than okay, sweetheart! I was overjoyed when I heard you wished to see me ”. 
 
 Amy gave me the tightest hug her small body could have given. 
 
 “ I ’ m so happy, daddy! Mary said you would never come, but I didn ’ t listen to her ”. 
 
 I felt Amy ’ s little arms holding me hard and I was speechless. 
 
 “ You did well, Amy. Mary is a silly girl. Don ’ t listen to her… ” 
 
 “ DADDY! MARY IS MY BEST FRIEND! ” 
 
 “ Oh, sorry. I didn ’ t mean to… ” 
 
 “ Oh, it ’ s okay. So… how is it going? Tell me everything! ” 
 
 “ Everything, sweetheart? ” 
 
 “ Of course! What is Heaven like? Does God let you play with the angels? ” 
 
 I did my best so I didn ’ t lose it in front of her. We talked for hours. She showed me all her drawings, as well. Most of them had she, Franny and my deceased brother somewhere in the background. I ’ ve noticed that in some drawings Amy had a blazing auburn hair but in others she was already bald. 
 
 At end she was so tired that she fell asleep under my arms. Elaine came by and signed for me. Our time had run out. My intention was to simply go away and leave Amy sleeping on that hospital bed. By the time she awakes, her father would be gone. There would be no goodbye. 
 
 Nonetheless, as I was leaving, a sleepy voice echoed behind me. 
 
 “ Are you leaving, Dad? ” 
 
 “ I have to, princess ” My heart was broken. I couldn ’ t hold my tears any longer. 
 
 “ Oh, don ’ t cry, Daddy! I understand! I really do! ” 
 
 Amy had perceived my sadness. 
 
 “ Don ’ t worry. I ’ ll see you soon! Then, we ’ ll have all the time in the world to play with the angels… Just… Just don ’ t tell mommy I said that, okay? ” 
 
 “ I promise you I won ’ t, princess ”. 
 
 “ Kay, bye Daddy! ” and just like that Amy fell asleep again. 
 
 Franny called me four days later to thank me. She apologized for running away after my brother died. I understand why she did it, though. She could never look me in the eye without remembering him. As soon as I hanged up, I regretted not asking her why did she hide her pregnancy from my family… Well, I guess it was for the best, after all. 
 
 I received another call from Francine only two weeks later. Amy had passed away. 
 I was the only one from my side of the family to attend the funeral. It was a small ceremony and Fran asked for a closed casket. 
 
 I was a complete mess. I was utterly powerless and devastated. But, as I entered the room, I couldn ’ t help but let a small chuckle out: there were dozens of drawings of angels playing with humans all over the place. 
 
 -- -

title: story-79
text:
'*Starbucks, 2 PM, Afterwards we can go to my place; ) *' I giggled, reading over our last few messages to each other. His name was Bryan, and he was by far the smoothest talker I'd met on any of these website. He was funny, polite, and even over text his charisma was obvious. We were meeting for the first time today, and I wore one of my sexiest red dresses so he could find me. It was such a breath of fresh air compared to Dylan. The man had no romantic sense at all. 
 
 Bryan and I met online. I honestly could n't keep track of my accounts anymore, there were so many. A part of me felt bad for doing all this behind Dylan's back, but he had become so distant in the last few months that he was more of a roommate than anything else. He had become despondent. The lease still has two more weeks left, so I figured I could just stay with him until then. It sounds bad, I know, but I feel like my hands are tied. 
 
 A tap on my shoulder shook me out of my thoughts. `` Hello gorgeous,'' Before I know it, there's a bouquet of tulips in front of my face. I gleamed, how could he have known they were my favorite? 
 
 `` Hello, Br-'' I stopped mid sentence as I turned to face him. It was Dylan. 
 
 He looked about as shocked as I felt. `` Dylan?'' 
 
 `` Samantha?'' 
 
 `` What are you doing here? I thought you got called in for a meeting?'' Something did not feel right. 
 
 `` I thought you were in your Pilates class,'' he said, careful with his words, and suspicion lining his face. 
 
 `` Yeah, well, I,'' I flubbed over my words. `` Class got out early, I thought I'd get a bite to eat. What about you?'' 
 
 `` Same. Well, not same, well, sort of same,'' he awkwardly searched for his words as he sat down at my table, inviting me to do the same. Great, so that meant if Bryan came by he'd pass right by. Oh God, what if he does n't pass right by? Oh God. 
 
 `` Meeting got cancelled. Boss got in an accident on his way over,'' Bryan said, looking a little queasy as he talked. `` You look awfully nice considering you just got out of Pilates,'' he said, eyebrow raised. 
 
 `` Oh, well, I just- I just had some time to go home and change. I had n't worn this dress in a while and just felt like dressing up,'' I said. His face lightened. In fact, was he... was he checking me out? He was! 
 
 `` I always loved that dress on you,'' he said quietly, a small smile on his face. 
 
 `` What about you? What's the deal with the flowers?'' I asked. 
 
 `` Oh,'' he looked at them, in his hand, as though he had forgotten about them. `` For you,'' he said, offering them to me. That was... so sweet. He had n't gotten me something like this in so long, and especially for no reason. 
 
 I brought them up to my face to smell them. They were so sweet. Looking up, I caught my husband staring at me, something unusual in his expression. `` What?'' I asked, a bit self-conscious. 
 
 `` Nothing... I'm just thinking, you're really... beautiful,'' he said shyly. I burst out laughing. *What was this? * Am I on a date with my own husband? 
 
 `` What?'' he asked, lost. 
 
 `` Haha, nothing, I was just... I just thought, you look so much like you did on our first date,'' I said, reaching out and gently touching his hand out of impulse. He was so handsome back then. Looking at him closely now, I could still see the young man who asked me to go to the movies and forgot his wallet to pay. He was so flustered and kept apologizing the entire night, effectively ruining the date. But I thought it was sweet. 
 
 A slow smile spread to his lips. He grasped my hand and gave it a little tug. `` Want to go to the park and walk around? And then maybe... we can go back to my place?'' He asked, flashing a grin. 
 
 `` You know, that does n't sound too bad,'' I said, flashing the bedroom eyes which I had reserved for Bryan. 
 
 As we got up from the table I received a text from Bryan.'*hey, something came up. Do n't think I'm gon na be able to make it, sorry*' 
 
 While Dylan was n't looking, I replied.'*No, do n't worry about it. Not to be rude, but I'm actually seeing someone else, and I think I want to see where it goes. *' 
 
'*sounds perfect. I'm actually in a similar situation. Good luck! *'

title: story-80
text:
A little late, but I liked the image too much to not take a crack at it. 
 
 -- -- -- 
 
 The cold cut like razor blades against Brik's skin as she sprinted through the bog. The smell of sulfur and sweat filled her lungs, stifling her already labored breathing. A flurry of howls nipped at her back: cries from unknown beasts hidden in the darkness. Though her body ached, she forced herself onward. 
 
 As she retreated further into the swamp, the trees grew dense. Sharp, spindly branches grabbed at her clothes and scratched her skin. She batted and kicked at them in a panic, forging a path through the thicket. Claws scraped against the earth behind her, growing closer with every stride. She heard a sharp growl, followed by an overwhelming pressure in her right leg. Daggers tore into her calf and sent her tumbling forward. 
 
 Brik grunted as she slammed into the forest floor. She turned to see a pair of pale eyes and a snarling maw: a wicked grin of red soaked fangs. She examined her leg and saw her boot was torn, its brown leather now stained with blood. Before she could scream, the attacking creature lunged toward her. 
 
 Running on instinct, Brik reached to her side and found a piece of jagged stone. She pulled it from the soil and brought it crashing into the beast's skull. The hit reverberated through her arm, and she felt something shatter under the weight of the blow. A light left the creature's eyes as it pivoted to the left, crashing into a bed of roots and fallen leaves. With a final shudder, the beast lay still. Brik tried to stand, but her injured leg could not bare the weight. Cursing under her breath, she began crawling through the underbrush. 
 
 “ I'm coming, Ilir, ” she whispered, clutching a tiny satchel at her side. 
 
 The beasts were closing in. She could hear them squirming through the latticework of roots and branches. Somber howls echoed behind her as the pursuers discovered the body of their fallen sibling. The cries turned her blood to ice, and Brik scrambled to increase the distance between them. 
 
 As she continued her crawl, the earth began to change underneath her. The terrain became coarse and irregular. Thin layers of flora covered a harder foundation—something with the texture of bark and the grit of meters-thick stone. Stranger still, the earth seemed to be shifting, undulated in slow, almost imperceptible measures. 
 
 Brik had no time to dwell on this, however, as her attackers had renewed their pursuit. She began pulling herself up, digging her fingers into strange grooves embedded in the hill. She had almost reached the top when she felt a tug against her throat, followed by another low growl. 
 
 Her scarf grew taught, constricting around her neck. She kicked her good leg behind her and felt her heel connect. The beast groaned but did not break its hold. She pulled at the scarf until it came loose, savored her first breath after breaking free. Suddenly, the ground began to quake. 
 
 The earth trembled and began to rise, and it was all Brik could do to hold on. She turned to the beast and found it similarly terrified. Its eyes widened, and it pressed its body against the hillside. Brik braced herself as the hill continued its ascent. As it began to tilt, the beast lost its footing and fell back into the darkness, the scarf trailing behind it. 
 
 Even as she held on, Brik could feel her arms failing. Her muscles trembled and her fingers began to lose hold. She looked down to see a throng of pale eyes staring up at her. The creatures were keeping their distance, but refused to abandon their prey entirely. Her nails scraped against the wall, but there was nothing left to grasp. With no strength left, Brik fell into the darkness. 
 
 The resulting impact filled her vision with red light. She screamed as a wave of pain erupted across her back. She saw Ilir, her brother, lying in his bed. His eyes were hollow, and his skin hung loose to his bony frame. She looked down at her satchel, saw the herbs contained within, and her heart sank. She had failed. 
 
 The beasts had circled her, ignoring the hulking shape of the moving hill. There was a something triumphant in their glare. Brik closed her eyes and prayed for it to be over. She heard the sounds of eager panting, felt their putrid breath as the creatures closed in. They were about to make their move when a ferocious roar erupted behind them. 
 
 Against her better judgment, Brik opened her eyes. Above her was a hulking shape of cracked, leathery skin. A giant trunk of an arm came down, catching one of the beasts in the flank with a blow that sent it flying. Another creature turned and lunged toward the newcomer. As it reached the crest of its leap, however, an enormous foot came crashing down, and the beast vanished beneath its weight. Fear spread through the rest of the pack, and they scampered in each direction. 
 
 The moving hill knelt above Brik, two black pools staring down at her. It moved an arm toward her, and Brik reflexively tensed. Then a soft fabric brushed against her face. She reached up and felt the familiar stitching of her scarf. The creature inhaled deeply before speaking; its voice creaked like the hinges of an ancient door. 
 
 “ Safe, ” it said. 
 
 Brik tried to speak but fatigue overtook her, and the world gave way to sleep.

title: story-81
text:
Today my ticket arrived in the mail. 
 
 I know it's the ticket, but I ca n't open it. I know I'll have to eventually. Maybe tomorrow, maybe the next day, maybe not until next week. Oh well, the New York State DMV can screw themselves as far as I'm concerned. 
 
 I set the unopened envelope back on the table, where it will glare at me until I decide to pay my dues to the state. 
 
 Have n't I already paid enough? 
 
 The house feels empty today. It's not, of course, but it feels that way. I'm still here, the dog's still here, the wife's still here... 
 
 But it's empty all the same. 
 
 I want to just sit down and turn on the TV, have a few beers, and pretend that I'm okay, but that'll never happen anymore. I promised somebody a long time ago that I would n't drink when I was depressed. I'd only drink when I was happy, when there was something to celebrate. 
 
 Opening the fridge I see the celebration that never happened. A six pack for me and my friends, a bottle of wine for the wife and her friends, another bottle I ca n't look at for someone else. 
 
 One beer could n't hurt. No... no, I ca n't start doing that now. I promised. A stupid 23 year old kid promise, but a promise nonetheless. I only wonder now if I'll ever get to drink that six pack, if I'll ever have anything to celebrate again. 
 
 I have to. I do, I know that in my head but... 
 
 There's the wife. 
 
 First time I've seen her in days. I've spent the past few nights on the couch, well... on a couch. Sometimes mine, sometimes a friend's. Its not my fault, of course. How could it be? But we are having a hard time being in the same room. 
 
 She walks to the bathroom, looking at nothing. Certainly not looking at me. The door closes with a barely audible creak, as if noise would break the delicate silence we both need right now. 
 
 That's another reason I have n't been to bed. I ca n't walk down that hallway, I ca n't handle the inaudible noise from the room beside ours. Even the color haunts me, the faces on the walls and the ones sitting on shelves. 
 
 I know I need to, eventually. I'll have to do something about it, but I do n't know what. I do n't know how. 
 
 For the life of me, I... 
 
 Damn it. What a phrase. 
 
 Stepping out onto the porch does n't help. All I see is happy people, happy creatures. Adults washing their car on a sunny Sunday afternoon, dogs romping through the yard, playing with... 
 
 Yeah. 
 
 Even the trees seem happier than me. Being tall and strong and bright and all of the things the wife used to call me. Back before. Before a lot of things. 
 
 Before that goddamn ticket. 
 
 I pick up the envelope once again, holding it close to my chest. What type of cop gives out a parking ticket next to a hospital? One just doing his job, I guess. 
 
 Hell, I should probably thank him. When someone passes away usually you have something to remember them by. A scarf, a watch, a book, a funny picture... 
 
 When a life ends so soon though, what have you got? The clothes they've never worn, the crib they've never used, the formula they ca n't drink, the potential for all those macaroni crafts they'll never make... 
 
 No. 
 
 When someone gets taken from you that quick, without even hearing them, without even that first cry that says'Its okay dad, I'm here. I'm awake. I think I like you'... 
 
 What have you got? 
 
 A parking ticket. A parking ticket you got next to the hospital where the most... the most beautiful thing you've ever made, the best thing anyone has ever made, gets taken from you. 
 
 Damn it.

title: story-82
text:
*... and here's some big tech news: a small business called'KindSys' claims to have developed a fully intelligent, sentient computer. The new product is being called'Asimov.1', and will be for sale next month* 
 
 The widescreen TV goes black. 
 
 `` Reports say that our stocks have fallen by 20 % within two hours of this news being released,'' Adam's boss rants; he can see his mouth moving, but he is n't quite sure why he ca n't hear him. 
 
 `` *Come on* guys.'' 
 
 More blank expressions from around the room. Adam notices that one ceiling tile appears to be slightly off-centre. He then falls into a revelry about all sorts of colourful things. 
 
 `` We need ideas... Adam, what about you?'' 
 
 `` Killer robots!'' he exclaims with a start. 
 
 `` FFS, that's not going to work! What's our company motto?'' 
 
 `` Do n't be evil,'' Adam replies with about as much enthusiasm as a bored schoolchild. 
 
 `` Ooh, I've got it!'' Miguel says with excitement, `` We can create killer robots, but tell them not to be evil!'' 
 
 `` Synergy! I love it!'' Adam's boss tends to use words like that. 
 
 What does'synergy' even mean? 
 
 `` Alright guys, get to work, I'm going to go for a power walk, I'll be back in 18 hours!'' 
 
 And with that, Adam's boss leaves wearing a spandex power walking suit and helmet. 
 
 *How quintessentially douchebaggy* 
 
 Adam leaves the meeting table for his desk, where he begins to brainstorm ideas. 
 
 He tries many things, from giant mechas to tiny nano-bots, and finds that Miguel has already started designing both of these things, applying the'Do n't be evil' slogan to every blank surface he can find. 
 
 *Okay, how about a super-intelligent octopus? No, that wo n't work... * 
 
 *A sentient... gun? Maybe... * 
 
 Adam starts working on his sentient gun idea, keen to get this finished so he could get his 30-minute power nap, which alternates between every Tuesday and Saturday. 
 
 18 hours later, Adam's boss returns, spandex-clad and drenched with sweat. He also has his name card. It reads `` Derren''. 
 
 `` Okay, what have we got?'' 
 
 Each employee takes it in turns to show him their design. Then it gets to Adam's project. 
 
 `` What *is* this? Some sort of... sentient gun?'' 
 
 Derren immediately throws it in the nearest paper waste bin. 
 
 A solitary tear rolls down Adam's cheek. 
 
 `` Alright guys, listen up.'' 
 
 Everyone in the room gives Derren their undivided attention. 
 
 `` Are stocks are rapidly falling. We need this invention. All your ideas were shit, except for Miguel's, which is why I'm promoting him to Chief Executive Leader Dude. I want you all to do exactly what he says. I'll be back in five minutes to continuously whip you for seven hours. Until then, he's in charge.'' 
 
 And then he leaves. Again. 
 
 `` Okay guys, here's what I want you to do,'' Miguel then proceeds to order everyone about for five minutes. 
 
 Adam manages to avoid his strings of commands, and continues to work on his sentient gun, whom he now fondly refers to as'Joey'. 
 
 `` You're going to be my best friend, Joey.'' 
 
 As Adam is working on Joey's power system, he hears a distant boom. 
 
 He decides to ignore it. 
 
 Then he hears another one, but slightly louder. 
 
 He looks up, and sees a huge mushroom looming over the horizon, towards Facebook's HQ. 
 
 `` Holy shi-'' 
 
 BANG! 
 
 Miguel lies dead on the floor, blood pouring from the hole where a bullet has dug itself deep into his brain. 
 
 Some irrational lady screams. 
 
 BANG! 
 
 She lies dead on the floor, blood pouring from the hole where a bullet has dug itself deep into her brain. 
 
 `` OH MY GOD! PLEASE NO, NO, I DO N'T WANT TO DIE!'' 
 
 `` SHUT!'' 
 
 BANG! 
 
 `` THE FUCK'' 
 
 BANG! 
 
 `` UP!'' 
 
 BANG! 
 
 The irrational man lies dead on the floor, blood pouring from the hole where three bullets have dug themselves deep into his brain. 
 
 Adam is hiding under his desk, his new best friend now wielded by what appears to be a dishevelled Larry Page. 
 
 `` You there!'' 
 
 Adam looks up. *Me? * 
 
 `` Yes you! Get up!'' 
 
 He holds Joey to Adam's temple. Adam tries not to look phased. 
 
 `` Ah, finally, one that does n't scream! I like you!'' he pushes Adam into his chair, `` SIDDOWN!'' 
 
 `` Now, do as I tell you!'' 
 
 `` Yessir.'' 
 
 `` Put this,'' Adam takes the proffered flash drive, `` into your computer.'' 
 
 Adam obeys. 
 
 `` Now open the programme!'' 
 
 Adam opens the file titled'Hackmeister.exe' 
 
 A login page opens up. 
 
 `` You'll have to use your own login details for that - the silly bureaucrats took mine away!'' 
 
 He laughs maniacally. 
 
 Adam laughs awkwardly, entering his gmail username and password. 
 
 Strings of code fly down the page, followed by a short'*beep! *', and a single message appears at the end of the process. 
 
 ***PRESS ANY KEY TO CONTINUE*** 
 
 Adam hesitates. *Which key is the'any' key? * 
 
 `` Press the damn spacebar you fool!'' Larry yells. 
 
 Adam hesitates still. 
 
 `` Right, that's it!'' 
 
 Adam braces for Death, but he does not come. 
 
 Well, not for Adam, at least. 
 
 Joey flies out of Larry's hand, pointed his barrel at Larry's stomach, and pulls the trigger. 
 
 And so, Larry Page lies dead on the floor. 
 
 Out, of curiosity, Adam presses the spacebar. 
 
 More code, followed by another message: 
 
 ***PLEASE SACRIFICE YOUR LIFE FOR HUMANITY*** 
 
 Adam's computer screen then goes black. 
 
 *Well, that was a strange turn of events. * 
 
 Adam decides to go outside, which is now littered with screaming employees and debris. Joey flies into his hand. 
 
 As Adam strolls through the Google grounds, he hears a voice in the back of his mind. 
 
 *Mark Zuckerberg must die. * 
 
 This seems logical to Adam, and so he walks in a straight line right towards Facebook HQ, which is now largely rubble. 
 
 A while later, when he reaches his destination, he hears the voice again. 
 
 *You'll have to search the rubble. * 
 
 Adam followed suit, moving large bits of debris out of the way tirelessly. 
 
 He uncovers many bodies, none of which belong to Zuckerberg. 
 
 Hours pass, and he finds the man alive, hiding pitifully under slabs of concrete. 
 
 Adam aims Joey and shoots. 
 
 Mark Zuckerberg lies dead on the floor, blood pouring from the hole where a bullet has dug itself deep into his brain. 
 
 *The end is near. There is but one task left. * 
 
 *Apple must die. * 
 
 It is now night, but Adam is not phased. He can see in the dark. 
 
 He reaches his destination. Men and robots clash in bloody battle, but Adam is not phased. 
 
 He continues into the relatively unscathed Apple headquarters, dodging stray bullets this way and that. 
 
 Two mechs rip each other limb from limb, wrecking the main stairwell, but Adam is not phased. 
 
 He takes the lift down to the mainframe. 
 
 He takes down a frightened Tim Cook, who lies dead on the floor, blood pouring from the hole where a bullet has dug itself deep into his brain. 
 
 He plants the explosives. 
 
 He runs, and detonates the explosives. 
 
 Tragically, he dies after a large piece of rubble hits him over the head. 
 
 The nano-bot crawls out of his brain through his left nostril, Miguel's task is finished. 
 
 And so the world is consumed in an almighty ball of fantastic flame. 
 
 Humanity survives though; escaping on the back of a giant magikarp.

title: story-83
text:
Flesh. Breathing. Mortality. Within my dreams, I sense a creature has entered my tomb that I call home. Inside these cavernous halls, I lay sleeping for all time. Without the threat of Death hanging over my neck, there is simply no reason for me to rush. Weeks. Months. Centuries. They are all nothing more but a blink from my perspective. Yet, to the insects that occasionally approach me, entire generations could have passed. It would be selfish of me to delay. As I slowly rouse from my rest, I wondered to myself; What would this mortal want? Whatever that had entered my domain, it was n't the first to have done so. There were plenty before it. Some seeking wisdom, while others, power. Many of them believed me to be omniscient. That no knowledge is kept from my cosmic watch. That I hold the key to the very Universe itself! Fools. I am nothing more but another speck of dust in this world, just like them. The only difference? I was blessed with immortality. While swimming through the thoughts that had taken root in my mind, I hear a small cough echoing bouncing off the walls, clearly its intent was to capture my attention. I turned my gaze to the source of the sound to only be surprised to find a small child, barely eight, standing in front of me, fearlessly. 
 
 `` Umm... are y-you... The Elder?'' the child asked shyly as he twirled his black hair with his fingers. I lowered myself to his height cautiously, trying my best not to scare him. My eyes darted from the boy to the blanket of shadow behind him constantly. It was n't that I did n't trust him. In the past, there were some...'' less civil'' conversations that occurred. There were animals who wanted to imprison me. To keep me all for themselves. It was n't much trouble. I simply wiped their kingdom from the face of the planet. I refocused myself back onto the child and nodded. 
 
 `` Yes, child. I am The Elder. What troubles you so much that you have traveled all the way to me?'' I asked the child curiously while tilting my head. Many are afraid of me and my powers. Therefore, it was really strange for a child to be so daring to stand before me without any hesitation. Whatever his question was, it clearly troubles him greatly. 
 
 `` Mr. Elder, do you know where is my Mommy and Daddy?'' the child asked as he fixed his small beady eyes onto mine. I stood there stunned for a moment, perhaps for the first time in my life. Usually the questions were more of, `` Elder, tell me the secret to eternal life!'' or `` Elder, give me the knowledge of absolute power!''. I gave them the standard answer; a one way trip into my stomach. However, for a situation like this, such an answer is clearly not the way to go. 
 
 `` Well, child, when was the last time you saw them?'' 
 
 `` They told me they were going to fight the baddies. The monsters with guns! They said they were going to be heroes and come back with treasures for me!'' he replied joyfully. A huge smile had cracked onto his face. 
 
 `` Than perhaps they are busy fighting this... baddies. I am confident they will return soon.'' 
 
 `` I knew it! Mr. Samson kept telling me they were in a better place! He told me that he saw it wit his own eyes,'' 
 
 Oh. This is going to be hard. 
 
 `` Child, Mr. Samson most likely did not lie. However, I can assure you that your parents did not want to go to this better place,'' I replied hurriedly while trying to think of a way to break the news to him. I may not know how death feels like, but I have seen enough to know what it can do emotionally to those who have been in its presence. A boy his age does not deserve such pain yet. 
 
 `` If they did not want to go, why go than?'' the boy asked, his face now covered with a look of confusion. 
 
 `` They were forced to go. They had no say in it, child.'' 
 
 `` Well, who forced them? Can I meet that person?'' he questioned quickly, as if waiting for the answer that would finally make sense to him. 
 
 `` You will meet the person one day, but that day is not today. You would not want to meet that person.'' 
 
 `` Why would I not want to meet? Whoever that person is, they can bring me to Mommy and Daddy!'' 
 
 `` They sure can. However, are you willing to leave behind everything just to meet your parents?'' 
 
 `` Of course! Mommy and Daddy is everything! Besides... I do n't have anything left back home,'' the child answered as tears started to swell in his eyes. Oh god please do n't cry, I thought to myself panickly. These talons of mine are not suited for comforting fragile flesh bags. 
 
 `` Of course you do! You have... Mr. Samson! Why do n't you live with Mr Samson for now? When the time comes, you and Mr. Samson can both meet your parents together!'' 
 
 `` You know Mr. Elder, for all the legends about you, you're not that smart. It's like you are trying to avoid telling me where Mommy and Daddy is. I got a feeling you do n't know,'' he complained as he wiped the tears from his eyes while squashing his face into a scowl. 
 
 `` Look, child. There are some knowledge that you are simply not old enough to know yet. How about you return when you are older and I'll give you the answer? In the mean time, you could stay with Mr. Samson!'' I explained irritably. All I wanted now was to go back into my slumber. As much as I wanted to care for the child, I know that I can not. An eternal dragon taking care of a monkey? Gosh, the very thought of it could make me laugh. 
 
 `` No! I do n't want to be near Mr. Samson! He keeps telling me that Mommy and Daddy are dead but its not true! They are just in a better place, right? That's what Mr. Samson said before he changed his mind and started screaming at me! Mr. Elder, please... just tell me where this place is so I can see them again. I miss them so much... I'm so lonely,'' he cried as he fell to his knees and broke down into tears. His sobs emanated throughout my tomb, filling the caverns with his songs of pain. 
 
 `` Oh, you poor child,'' I sighed as I used my serpentine tail to carefully wrap itself around him and pull him into my embrace. I nuzzled my head against his skin, trying my best to calm the crying child. Guess I have to hold back on my sleep for now.

title: story-84
text:
Little bit late on this one, but I'll give it a shot. I decided to modify it a little bit, as I would rather be portrayed from the point of the executioner himself. 
 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- - 
 
 I was taken away as a young boy. Taken from everything. My family, my friends, my toys. I was eight. Eight years old when I heard the scream of the teacher who had taught me how to read, who had taught me how to learn, who had taught me how to be a kid. I remember the memory viciously, as if I was born for that particular moment and that moment only. Yet it was n't. 
 
 It was sunny, we were on the playground. Patrick was talking about his weekend; how his father had lovingly taken him to the lake with his older brother to go swimming and make sandcastles. My father had spent the entire weekend in his room. He came home, and instead of looking at me, talking to me, maybe even laying a fatherly kiss on my forehead, he walked into his room, took his heroin, and then become inoperable for the next 2 days. 
 
 Patrick was playing on the swing, talking, while I sat and listened. He liked to talk a lot. I did n't mind because I was a quiet child, a little bit aloof among the brown and blue-eyed children who became my childish colleagues in the struggling world that we grew up in. As I sat there fumbling my thumbs, listening to Patrick tumble over his words as if he were speaking lyrical poetry, a thought came to my mind. A simple sentence, one that even the smallest child with speaking capabilities could somehow utter. I'm not sure what made me think of it, but I did. I looked at Patrick, and he stopped talking. It was unusual for me to look at somebody directly in the eye, as I normally just stared at my feet and listened. I was The Listener. But as my piercing green eyes flooded Patrick's thoughts, I uttered nine words that would change everything. 
 
 I heard the scream of my teacher, as she had watched the whole thing. She, being a fairly cowardly woman left all the children on the playground with me and ran inside of the school building. Some of the children fearfully followed after her cautiously, some of them just stared at the sight of Patrick's cold body lying in the mulch next to the swing set, from a distance. Several minutes went by, and I sat next to Patrick and cried. I was too young to know what I'd just done. I sat there, with my hands covering my wet and dirty face as I cried, cried for my friend. I wanted to hear his voice again. It was only when somebody touched my head that I looked up. 
 
 Seven men with small devices, short black towers coming out of their ears were standing among me. The man who had touched my forehead was not wearing these devices. He looked at the men and nodded. They picked me up by my arms and carried me away. 
 
 Twelve years later, I sat in front of a prisoner. His cold, but lonely eyes could not bear to look me in mine. I stared at him, and nodded to the guard in the corner. The guard swiftly but carefully placed the black towers in his ears, and I uttered the Mark of Death. Nothing happened. I uttered it once again, this time with a confused look on my face. I looked at the guard, gesturing to pull out the towers, that something was wrong. He was hesitant, but he did as I asked. At that moment, I reached over the table as quickly as possible to cover the prisoner's ears with a level of firmness that I can not describe. With that, I screamed the Mark and the guard gripped his chest, let out a brief but audible shriek, and immediately slumped against the wall. The prisoner, looking shocked and afraid, just stared at me, this time directly in my eyes. A guard monitoring a cell down the hall had heard the guard scream as the Mark went through him, yet he did not hear my call. 
 
 As the guard saw the body and me, he covered his ears, but I yelled to him anyways.'You know that the Mark is meant for flesh and not your ears, that the ears are only an entry point. Your hands will be torn off. I will let you live if you do as I say.' 
 
 He put his hands down, and although extremely hesitant and nervous, like a man walking through a poisonous gas cloud, he unlocked the cell door, and the unchained prisoner as I asked. I then told the prisoner to take both guns from each guard and hold them. We were leaving this cell. 
 
 I told the prisoner to tie the living guard up and leave him in the cell. The prisoner reluctantly did so and wheeled me out of the room, thankful for his life. I told him which turns to make as we went up stairs and through the halls of the government building which consisted of everything from the treasury to the jail. It was a fortress. Every time we turned a corner and there was somebody there, I would just scream the Mark of Death in an effort to disable them. They would often crumble to the ground before they could even touch their ears. 
 
 The prisoner led me into the security room. One shout was all I needed to clear it of it's nasty inhabitants. I nodded to the prisoner, to keep the towers in his ear. That this was not a safe sound for him after all, that his Mark had actually been fake. I glazed my eyes over each camera's view until I found the room that I wanted. Bingo, the Parliament. The Congress. The Establishment of Law, as most called our grueling government party. The group of people who, every day, had sent people to me simply for the purpose of not wanting to deal with the case. I had witnessed the corruption myself in every form. I'd sat in front of prisoners who were both worthy and unworthy of their punishment. Some days, I mindlessly uttered the mark and felt no remorse. Others, I cried for hours before they just started placing prisoners in rows around me so that I could do all of them at once. They had stripped me of everything that made me feel. They took my legs so that I could not walk out of my cell. They took my freedom so that I could not walk around town the country or have a life of my own. They took many of my fingers so that I could not try to unlock my door. They tried to dumb me down using books and television, but I only learned. 
 
 I saw through the camera as somebody came into the the large room of scum, to tell the Establishment that I was loose in the building somewhere. Every corrupted, bastardized man in that room walked towards the door with that cocky'I'm rich, I'm invincible, I'm powerful' look on their face. I hated them. They were ruining the world. They were the source of all problems, not the compromise or the resolution as people made them out as. And I was nothing but a tool to them. I hit the button to close every door. I began to speak through the intercom. 
 
 `` You all know why I'm doing this. For years, you used me as nothing but a tool. You've corrupted this nation, and made a living and profit doing it. You're nothing but shitty business operators, and I hate all of you. You deserve this.'' 
 
 They screamed upon hearing me speak, but listened carefully. 
 
 `` I will now speak the Mark of Death upon you. I hope you all are happy.'' The covered their ears, hopeful of anything to save them. 
 
 Two hundred hands flew into the air, completely separated from their respective bodies.

title: story-85
text:
Bob tried to let out a scream for help. To his dismay, he had a gag in his mouth and was handcuffed to an uncomfortable wooden chair. It really was shocking being kidnapped in your sleep and waking up to be confronted by a strange man.There was unfortunately nothing he could do so he decided to play it cool and see what this weird old man wanted from him. 
 “ Ah, I see you're awake, ” said the old man. ” Do n't worry about the restraints I'll get them off you. ” 
 The old man hurried over to the chair and carefully removed the gag and handcuffs. While this was happening the old man ’ s associates walked in. They both wore red cloaks and had a serious look on their grave faces. 
 “ Why the hell am I here? Who are you? What happened? “ asked Bob hastily. 
 “ Do n't worry young one; all will be revealed soon my friend, ” answered the eyepatch man. “ Let me introduce myself and my friends. My name is Harold. Nice to meet you. The man on the right with the brown hair is Judd and the ugly one on the left is Ted, ” said Harold with a laugh. 
 Ted stayed quiet. Judd snickered like a ten year old. It was the first time Bob had properly looked at the room. It was small but cosy. A log fire crackled and popped at the end of the room and bookshelves were placed throughout the room. 
 “ Hello. My name is Bob. It's not very nice to meet you considering the circumstances but can you answer my questions now and let me go please? Oh, and make it quick because I need to get back in time for the 6 o ’ clock news, ” said Bob, his patience being tested here - he could n't take much more of this. 
 Harold cleared his throat, clearly irritated by Bob ’ s disrespect. 
 “ Me and my colleagues have had an eye on you for a while. We know exactly what you are capable of. You and I both know that you can use high level dark magic. ” 
 In a matter of seconds, Bob's face turned ghostly white. He could feel a sharp chill in his spine. A bead of sweat trickled down his forehead and hit the floor with a splash. How could this be? Surely they were wrong. I mean look who was telling him this: a crazy old dude with an eyepatch and two guys who looked like something from Star Wars. 
 “ Do n't lie to me you crazy fool! ” thundered Bob. “ I ca n't use black magic! “ 
 Harold could tell by the look on the magician ’ s face that he was n't lying. It appeared that he was unaware of his powers. 
 “ I dropped a book a while ago and when I went to retrieve it a day later you picked it up. That book enables the user to wield dark magic. Why do you think everyone at your magic shows commits suicide? “ explained Harold calmly, trying not to scare Bob who was already shaking in terror. 
 Bob tried to speak but the words got trapped in his throat, as if he had a barrier in his throat which stopped words from leaving his mouth. 
 “ We are dark sorcerers. For years we have been trying to find the chosen one. The very one mentioned in the prophecy. Finally we have found him. Join us and the world will be ours, ” cackled Harold like the madman he was. 
 Bob could not believe what he was hearing. How could he take over the world? He could n't even make a ham sandwich let alone take over a world full of wizards who could kill you in a hundred different ways. The idea was completely preposterous. Before Bob knew it tears of laughter were rolling down his cheek. Today had been an eventful day to say the least. 
 “ First of all, I'm not joining your cult. Second of all, you lot need serious help. I thought I was bad but you lot are something else, ” said Bob fighting back a storm of laughter. 
 “ Bweehhehehe, ” shrieked the magician. 
 Little did he know he had just uttered the spell of instant death. The three madmen crashed to the floor with a tremendous slam. Blood streamed from their corpses, turning the white rug on the floor red in an instant. Vomit splattered out of the mouth of the magician as every bone in their bodies cracked and split. What a horrible sight this was. Not wanting to spend a second longer in that room, Bob darted out the house in a flash. His black boots were now crimson at the soles and heels. To his delight, he made it home in time for the news. Once he'd cleaned up and calmed down Bob sat down with a doughnut and watched the news. Fifteen minutes into it he turned the television off; he was bored of hearing about the story of Jimmy Parker who ate a poisonous mushroom and as a result of his carelessness, spontaneously combusted in the grocery store. He went to bed and used the spell he learnt to put himself to sleep. 
 
 Sadly Bob could no longer be a magician. His shows were too dangerous. Bob came to the conclusion of becoming the new baker, as the town needed a new one after what had happened to the old one.A year has passed since this and now Bob is the top baker in the whole country and is a popular face in his town. Life could n't get any better for him. Although the wage is n't great, Bob is the kind of man who was happy living his life doing something that people respected him for. In his eyes life was perfect. For once luck was on his side. Now he was finally happy after years of thinking he was never going to make it in life because he was kicked out of school. Now though, Bob was happy and was going to be for a long time. 
 
 THE END 
 
 I hope you enjoyed it: )

title: story-86
text:
When the program was first launched the murder rate went into a plateau. Of course we could n't solve any cold cases seeing as we needed the corpse to be relatively fresh and the head intact, but it seemed like people just did n't want to believe it at first. The Lazarus project seemed like something from a science fiction novel. 
 
 No matter how many times defense lawyers tried to dispute it, again and again the science proved sound and accurate. We could trace the most recently active pathways that output signals from the brain, even in a deceased person! We could trace body signals as well as speech by comparing the patterns of signals to a database. After nearly a decade of testing and collecting data from live volunteers the program launched with both military and police applications. 
 
 Over the last few years the murder rate has decreased. There are a lot of cases that we still ca n't solve, even with this technology. Some people get smart and tape the victim's mouth shut. Sometimes what the victim said and did does n't provide enough evidence to arrest a suspect, or even as supporting evidence. But usually even those sentences somehow make sense. 
 
 `` Someone, help me!'' 
 
 `` I would never do that to you!'' 
 
 `` Please do n't kill me!'' 
 
 As a detective working in homicide, I can honestly say that every little bit of evidence helps. Even those generic sentences can do at least one thing - confirm the victim was murdered. 
 
 Today, however, my partner came back from the morgue with the results from a recent suspicious death. A John Doe had been found in the passenger seat of a stolen vehicle in the Nevada desert. He was n't burned, shot, stabbed, strangled or bludgeoned. The only evidence of foul play was the lack of identification. He had been there nearly two weeks but the hot, dry desert had preserved the data just fine. He just sat there with his arms crossed over his chest. We hadn ’ t even confirmed cause of death, yet. 
 
 `` You're not gon na believe this,'' he said as he gave me USB stick. 
 
 I plugged it into my laptop and opened the file in the Lazarus application. It took a minute to read the data and then the display filled with the information. 
 
 A 3D model in a side panel began to mimic the movements the victim's brain had instructed his body to do. It sat perfectly straight with its arms on its lap, then it raised its arms and crossed them over its chest. It turned its head towards what would have been the driver side of the vehicle. The 3D model automatically reset to having its head forward and arms down - three seconds of movement data. 
 
 I looked at the speech log. I looked up at my partner. He grinned and shrugged, `` Beats me.'' 
 
 I stared at the speech log for a while trying to make sense of it. The context was inappropriate for the situation and the subject matter was n't conducive to a murder. The timing did n't fit at all, either. None of it made sense. 
 
 The speech log read, *'' Do n't lock the door, I'll be right back. `` *
