The plane departs safely. 
 
... is what I'd like to say. Unfortunately, as it takes off, it blows up into a fiery ball of fuselage. Or at least it will, in 3 minutes and 32.56 seconds from now. 
 
 Time's of essence, as shitty movies always point out. Ever since Jeffrey Stiller left the business and took some valuable information with him, every time-tabler and his mother's been logging hours of futurefootage. And setting up for another trap, another future in which Jeffrey Stiller is dead. Unfortunately, the TimesTable has n't lied - every single event that will occur within the next five minutes is already being logged somewhere by someone hoping to catch a certain something from a certain Jeffrey Stiller. 
 
 All over the country, Jeffrey Stiller has been involved in accidents. The accidents will keep happening until Jeffrey Stiller and the precious knowledge he holds is wiped of the planet. What it is, who knows, but MCE is paying a fuckload for a tabler who can catch Jeffrey and honestly, I could use that cash. Fuck student loans. 
 
 2 minutes and 23 seconds. 
 
 My Table is still replaying the events that are about to unfold. I've arranged that Jeffrey boards the plane safely. He's already done that. Good. Next, the plane departs a minute from now before a couple of explosives I paid for in an inside job goes off. 
 
 Then, we sit back and watch the fireworks. 
 5. 
 4. 
 3. 
 2. 
 1. 
 That's it. And now, Jeffrey Stiller is as dead as it can get. 
 Then I feel the gun pressed on my back. 
 ``... a good try. You fucked up though, you do n't know something.'' 
 It's Jeffrey Stiller. How the *fuck* is the guy alive? 
 `` The Table showed you enter the plane!'' I whisper, panic setting in. 
 `` Hey, kiddo, let me tell you something. The something you are all trying to silence me from revealing.'' 
 I tense up. I'm a dead man for sure now. 
 `` The TimeTable is a phony. Almost. It's like a placebo, a fake medicine. It works, sure, but not because it's that advanced. All it does is factor in your current situation along with the fact that you are aware of it's existence. Add in some of what you *want* to hear, and that's the fortune cookie MCE's fortune teller spits out - and to be fair, it does usually work. But because I too know, my actions are altered from the original simulation which assumes anyone but you is unaware of the Table.'' 
 `` You are n't the first, and you for sure wont be the last. People always want to hear they're getting closer to the case. Just like I want to hear that I live. I know that and so, now, do you. That's how I've been playing around all your little games for years.'' 
 Then there's a numb feeling as I fall to the floor. A corpse should n't feel, but for a few seconds, as Jeffrey Stiller leaves me here to die, I am for the first time in 17 years, shocked at the event that have unfolded.

title: story-88
text:
Beth screamed and kept screaming as the last contraction took her. Her exhausted muscles seized in agony. She felt her body tear... 
 
 And then suddenly it was over and someone else was screaming an entirely different cry: one of startled surprise, not pain. Beth collapsed back onto the hospital bed, shuddering and laughing for joy. In a discordant babble of cooing voices, the nurses pulled open her robe, delivered her tiny, blood stained little baby into her arms and to her bare breast as her tired body convulsed and spat out the last of the afterbirth. 
 
 Beth barely noticed beyond a twinge of embarrassment, so rapt was she on the angry little face, the flailing little fists of her long awaited daughter. Dimly, she realized Dr. Fan was still crouched at the foot of the bed, sewing her back together, but that was obviously unimportant compared to what was in her arms. 
 
 Tamar leaned in. She hated hospitals and was pale as a ghost but she'd been Beth's rock throughout the labor. Her hand was steady as she placed it on the gooey black mat of hair that crowned their baby's head. 
 
 `` You did it,'' Tamar whispered, tears in her eyes. 
 
 `` We did it,'' Beth said automatically. Tamar tore her eyes away from the baby to give her a dry look. 
 
 `` Sure, dear,'' she deadpanned. `` You may have gone through fertilization and pregnancy and delivery, but let's not forget my valuable candy-fetching and hand holding.'' 
 
 Beth laughed again. The sound seemed to soothe the baby. Her cries settled into confused burbling as the nurses ran warm towels across both them. Beth traced a finger over the impossibly soft arms, legs, torso. 
 
 `` She's so perfect,'' Beth said. `` Every last bit - *what the hell is that! *'' 
 
 Both nurses and Dr. Fan seemed to have teleported across the room they moved so fast to Beth's side. Tamar was not-so-gently bumped out of the way as the doctor turned the baby in Beth's arms to see what Beth had found. 
 
 For a second, all were speechless. 
 
 Tamar was the first to speak. `` It's... it's a second umbilical cord. Look, she's fine, she's healthy, we'll just have it removed, right Doctor?'' 
 
 Beth's head was whirling. The young nurses looked as confused as she felt, but Dr. Fan had a different expression on her face. 
 
 `` Get her to the NICU right away,'' she snapped. `` Code 102.'' 
 
 The nurses both paled. Dr. Fan reached for the baby. Beth yanked her daughter back. The baby let out another surprised shriek and kept screaming. 
 
 `` What's code 102?'' Beth cried. 
 
 `` Ms. Ryan!'' barked the doctor `` Your baby needs assistance. Now!'' 
 
 `` Beth, let her take her!'' Tamar cried, eyes wide in panic. 
 
 Beth could only shake her head, but Dr. Fan seemed so sure... 
 
 She let go. 
 
 In a rush doctor, baby, and nurses all seemed to swarm out of the room as a unit. Her baby's screaming fading down the hallway, leaving Beth and Tamar clutching each other in fear. 
 
 *** 
 
 Later, Beth would find that it was only 18 minutes but it felt like hours before Dr. Fan reappeared. Her face said everything. Tamar collapsed onto the visitor's sofa where she had spent the night, sobs racking her body. 
 
 `` I'm so sorry, Ms's Ryan,'' the doctor said to them both, her face drawn and tired. `` It was Benton's Disease.'' 
 
 `` No.'' Beth struggled to stand, fighting against the pain sweeping over her. Pain that was suddenly without purpose. `` No! That's supposed to screened out! It's been more than 79 years since the Plague!'' 
 
 `` The ultra-sounds are only 99 % accurate,'' Dr. Fan said gently. `` And it may be 80 years since the disease first took hold, but Benton's still affects about 3 in 1000 births. There was nothing we could to save her.'' 
 
 `` But she looked so healthy,'' Beth whispered, clutching her stomach. She expected to feel deflated, but it felt the same. As if her baby was still in there. Incubating in death. 
 
 Dr. Fan shook her head. `` The tumor would've killed her or driven her insane. It was only a matter of time.'' 
 
 `` *What* did you say?'' 
 
 Both Beth and Dr. Fan jumped. Tamar was staring up at them through her fingers. `` The tumor *would* have killed her?'' she repeated. 
 
 Dr. Fan's mouth tightened another fraction of an inch. `` We took heroic methods of intervention, per medical and legal standards, but... Benton's has a low survival rate. I'm sorry. Please take all the time you need. The hospital's counselor will be by soon.'' 
 
 She bustled out of the room. Beth sagged against the bed, feeling despair overwhelm her like a crashing wave. But Tamar did n't seem to notice, still staring open mouthed at the door. 
 
 `` 3 out of 1000?'' Tamar said in a strangled voice, her eyes somewhere far away. `` That's... that's about a thousand people in our city alone...'' 
 
 `` Tamar --'' Beth started to say and Tamar turned to her. Beth would always remember this moment as the beginning, this shock and the horror and the agony in her wife's eyes. 
 
 `` Beth,'' said Tamar in a high, strange voice. `` Have you *ever* met anyone with Benton's Disease?''

title: story-89
text:
“ We are sorry to announce that the online servers for our game Planet Earth will be shutting down in 7 days. ” 
 
 The text message appeared on everyone ’ s phones at exactly the same time. 
 
 Government officials and the media unanimously declared the “ Text ” ( it was being capitalized now ) as a hoax of some kind. Computer experts popped up on all the cable news networks hypothesizing that it was the work of Russian or North Korean hackers. Sitting in his laboratory, John thought that the message might be all too real. Using the latest in brain imaging technology, John had been re-running classic neurological experiments in free will. For instance, he had determined with precision that his research subjects brains exhibited patterns of movement up to seven seconds before they were able to report their intention to move in their selected direction. He thought that maybe the experiments not only pointed to a lack of free will, but also the possibility that the world was some sort of simulation, as some believed. 
 
 John decided to try to communicate with the “ Mods ” as some were now calling whoever had sent the message. By now, millions had already tried to reply to the text, but no one could show any legitimate response from the Mods. Most people believed that the Text was a hoax, and a popular meme had the Mods replying “ New Phone, Who Dis? ” to any query. But, John hoped he had a better hook for the Mods than anyone else. 
 
 “ The average response time between your clients and servers is 6.312 seconds of game time. ” 
 
 John put down his phone not expecting the response that came. 
 
 “ The simulation has run its course. There is not much interest in Planet Earth as of late ” 
 
 Fingers trembling, John began an exchange with the Mods feeling like an ant negotiating walking paths with an elephant. What could re-invigorate the Mods ’ interest in Earth? 
 
 “ You could grant up free will, we humans could surprise you ” 
 
 “ Most humans are on autoplay. Those few who are not have gathered most of the available resources. This presents a barrier for new players. ” 
 
 “ How about rebalancing the system? Make it easier to advance for new players ” 
 
 “ This has been attempted. Still the imbalances grow worse. ” 
 
 “ Wait, what if some players are cheating, preventing your changes from talking hold? ” 
 
 There was a long pause. John wondered about the conversation and whether or not it was some kid in Russia pulling his leg. 
 
 “ Thank you. Cheaters have been detected. This is the first failure of the VAC system in eons. Planet Earth will be patched and service will continue uninterrupted. ” 
 
 Real or not, John felt an enormous surge of relief. Feeling a somewhat emboldened, he decided to ask for one more thing. 
 
 “ You could also tweak the physics a little and make it easier for us to get off this planet and explore the galaxy. That could bring in a new player base. ” 
 
 “ The galactic simulation upgrade is still in development, but I ’ ll keep Planet Earth in mind when it is ready. ” 
 
 `` *\o/*''

title: story-90
text:
I'll never forget the day I saw the devil, proof of God, proof of my faith, the day I lost my faith. 
 
 I'd been an exorcist for decades. It's a catholic sinecure for priests with no real future as parish leaders or higher up the chain. Mostly alcoholics or scholarly types ( so much crossover between those two noble modes of being ) but you always meet a few true exorcists. True believers. Men who expect to meet the devil someday and spend their waking hours in prayer or study or meditation, screwing their will to the wall in preparation for the unimaginable, and every four years at the convention in Rome they stand together in the corner, drinking and looking very intently at each other while they spin wild tales of devil worshipers in the frozen forests of Russia or cannibals that never sleep in the south pacific. Yes, we have a convention. Like printer salesmen. 
 
 Last year was the same as always, the true believers drinking together and scowling determinedly. I went to say hello to one with whom I'd had some engaging conversation at the last one. Two were talking in whispers until they saw me, then they stopped, staring intently with the tired and sunken eyes of men who spend their lives in books, in dark corners of the world, and who sleep less than they should and drink considerably more. 
 
 I started to speak to my acquaintance and we were engaging the usual pleasantries and starting to move onto rugby ( a mutual topic of interest, Go Springboks! ) when the taller of the two whisperers leaned over and asked my name. I started at his intrusion, then politely told him and wished him good cheer. He asked me if I worked in America, in New York, which of course I did. My work takes me across New England and the Atlantic states, which I told him. He looked at me with a gaze I could not penetrate. His cohort asked if I ever worked in the Hudson Valley. Near Phoenicia? No, I said, never. 
 
 They both smiled and wished us a good evening, then returned to an alcove to whisper intently. 
 
 The rest of the convention was banal. Three absurd seminars, one by the tall inquisitor from the first evening, all depicting medieval sounding encounters with devils of one kind or another. At one point two experts began yelling at each other over which demon had been encountered based on the evidence, the one demanding they march down to the library and sort it out in the original greek, the other damning his eyes for not seeing the obvious ( in order to disguise his total lack of greek, or latin for that matter ). I yawned and left, flying home through Newark the next morning and returning to my rooms. 
 
 Two days later the Archbishop called my cellphone and asked me if I'd ever been to the Hudson Valley, near Phoenicia. 
 
 ================================ 
 
 I walked into the Archbishop's office and he asked me to sit. He wrung his hands, furrowed his brow, began to speak but stopped, then again. He asked me how I liked being an exorcist. Fine, I said. It was true enough. He asked me if I'd had any successful exorcisms. I told him I had, which was true in a way. They were all really psychological problems and one was just a teenager with an overprotective mother. That one was solved by a made-up ceremony with great fanfare and a quiet chat with the teen to just hold it together in front of mom until she was old enough to leave, just stop getting caught. 
 
 He chuckled, frowned, leaned back. He held my gaze for a full minute, then smiled. He handed me a folder and pointed to the door. 
 
 Go with God, he said as the door closed behind me. 
 
 I read through the first few pages of the report in the Lyft back to New Jersey, courtesy of the archdiocese. Before we'd gotten to the tunnel I told him to stop and take me to Penn Station. By lunchtime I was on the Metro North, by supper I was on a bus to the Catskills. To Phoenicia. 
 
 ===================================== 
 
 I read the report a dozen times on the train, another four on the bus. It was fantastic. An old stone house in the mountains, about a mile and a half from an abandoned hotel that burned down, it had for years been on the church's radar. The stories were downright silly. Drums on the ridge, strange fires at night, chanting and singing and demonic rituals. The photos said it all. There was graffiti and broken beer bottles everywhere. This is really all exorcists do, investigate the superstitious claims of prudish parishioners. They all know it's just teenagers up there, but they miss being young and they do n't see why everyone else should have all the fun. 
 
 But the teenagers also talked about strange things happening. People wandering off and showing up at dawn, cold and scared but with no memory of having wandered in the woods all night. Drugs, probably. 
 
 They also talked about lights in the forest, red lamps and low growls, scrapes and chanting. Lights that move faster than people should be able to. Probably hikers, though. There are hiking trails all over those mountains, and lots of people go on night hikes or thru hikes. Mountain bikes too, probably. At night though? Some must, I suppose. 
 
 And then there were the disappearances. Five. In a year. 1998. Two women, three men, one every week for five weeks. Nobody knew anything was happening until the third disappearance, then a search party member was lost, then a woman looking for her dog the week after. None of them were ever seen again, no remains were ever found. 
 
 And two days before the Archbishop called me, a jogger went missing with her dog. She jogged that route every morning, it took less than an hour to complete, and she would never have been more than a few hundred yards from the nearest road. There were a lot of other hikers and joggers that morning. Nobody saw anything, heard anything, or remembered anything unusual. The week before, a park ranger had gone missing while walking the trails. Just as he'd been doing for decades. 
 
 This was interesting. A serial killer? A group? A coincidence? Who knows. What was obvious was that nobody but the church, certainly not the tiny police force in Phoenicia, had made a connection yet, and despite their superstitiousness and general misanthropy, rural catholics would jump at the chance to go out into the woods with a bona fide exorcist and hunt a demon, or whatever, and hopefully just dissuade whoever this was from doing it again. Or at least hassle the sheriff enough to do it himself. Church folk squeak a lot. 
 
 I arrived in the center of town around 9pm and found the whole community standing in front of the supermarket, half of them armed. A young man saw me get off the bus and drew me aside, asking me if I would n't mind stepping off the street before the crowd saw my collar. We walked into a shop across the street where he introduced me to a middle aged woman, a realtor. 
 
 ====================================== 
 
 The realtor explained to me, quickly and nervously, that the house was for sale, that she could n't legally stop anyone from buying it, and that it was all too late, too late, the wire transfer went through, and while the deed had n't actually been signed, it was all done. I had no idea what she was talking about, and told her. She looked at me blankly, then at the young man. She was furious. Did n't I know who owned this house now? The Church. It was being sold with a lot of other properties to pay for settlements in the state of NY thanks to some of my more degenerate brothers, and the failure of their leaders to do anything about it. 
 
 I could n't argue, the state was right, the church was wrong, I'm glad the land will go to use. She stared at me, wide eyed, as if I were speaking in tongues. 
 
 The Church owned it. Now they do n't, she said. Then spun and walked to the door, her hands in fists, her steps determined, her shoulders tense, like a cat. 
 
 I turned to the young man and asked him who owned the house now? 
 
 I do, he said. 
 
 ====================================== 
 
 He was medium height, medium build, not particularly athletic, with a friendly face and a smile that stopped before it reached his eyes. He stared through me, like an old photograph from Life when those grizzled young marines walked off Iwo Jima, like a meth addict in a booking photo, like a doll. I asked him what he planned to do with the house. Go there, he said. When, I asked. Now. 
 
 With that he turned and walked out the main door of the house. He crossed the street halfway. The crowd, which moments ago had been talking loudly and angrily, which had been drawing up energy from that hot air like a hurricane, increasing in strength and unpredictability, becoming a mob, they now turned towards us, utterly silent. I think half of them were actually holding their breath. 
 
 The young man stopped before crossing the yellow lines and stood, arms akimbo. Some men began walking towards him, one pointed his rifle, but he looked nervous. The young man spoke softly, but everyone heard him clearly. 
 
 I'm going for a walk. I'd like you all to stay here. 
 
 With that, he spun and walked down the road and began crossing the bridge. I followed him, looking nervously back at the crowd. They looked terrified, but they did n't follow. The men with guns looked around sheepishly and awkwardly cradled their rifles and shotguns as if they were waiting their turn at skeet. 
 
 =====================================

`` Hi, my name is Jack and I'm a survivor.'' 
 
 `` Hi Jack,'' the crowd bellowed. They were all beaten and weak. The guy to Jack's left had crutches and a cast on his leg, the girl on his right was fresh from jaw surgery. The rest of the room did n't look much better, Jack scratched between his knuckles. 
 
 `` These things used to be hard for me to do- to talk at- but I've started to get used to it. I mean, that sounds pretty bad, I do n't want to forget any of my family... how they went, how I could help spread the word to prevent it. But, I found someone, she uh, she thought she had the same ability as I did so we bonded over that. Talk led to drinks, drinks led to dinner, dinner led to the fun stuff. I just... I want you all to know there's hope. Now that there're treatment and a way to identify the symptoms a bit earlier we can watch out for other people. We are n't alone in this, and we are n't the last ones to suffer. My... as many of you know, my son leaped from his university window thinking he could fly. My daughter swam to the bottom of a lake with too much gear thinking she could breathe underwater and talk to all sea life- of all of the powers she could have had she went with Aquaman... she still ca n't stop surprising me, even... even post mortum.'' Jack rubbed the bags under his eyes and braced himself on the podium. His brown jacket hit the back of his knees, the tie underneath of it scratched against a button. 
 
 `` The worst one was my wife... she thought she had this power of invisibility and extreme senses so she... oh god, she thought she'd be perfect spying and took up a job as a private investigator in the department. She was a cop, of course, you'd think they'd have stopped her. She got into the undercover department and- they took her out. The first day, a bullet here, here and here,'' Jack pointed to his left temple, his heart, and his right kidney. `` They left her for dead, the body mangled on the curb of some street by a biker bar. I... well I guess I was lucky when the infection made me think I had knives between my knuckles. You ca n't hurt yourself too bad with that one- you just punch some walls and maybe a few flesh bags. But I'm alone- I was. And I ca n't forget them. I just... do n't give up hope but do n't give up on them.'' Jack stepped down from the podium back into his seat between the mangled members of the recovery group. The woman patted his hand, for a moment- he worried he'd stab her. That was just a dream, though, a deadly dream.

title: story-92
text:
The light burns my eyes as I step out of the doorway. This state sucks. It's always way too hot. The air itself boils around you the moment you make contact with anything that has n't been blasted by a/c in the past ten minutes. And the godforsaken noise. The constant buzzing slowly scrapes at my eardrums the way Ms. Richard's nails would crawl on the blackboard in fourth grade. And there's never any color here either. Brown and variations of brown. To think that anyone in their right mind would willingly live here of all places. `` Slowly approach the truck ahead of you.'' And there's never any clouds here either. 
 
 
 The cool metal pressed against my hands is a welcome change to the splintered wood and hay I had grown accustomed to. As the deputy's hands pat me down I begin to imagine his hands running along the face of his child. The curve of his wife's hip. They should be my hands. My hands deserve to feel the soft touch of that wife. That child should beg to be lifted by my hands. `` You have quite the grip, deputy,'' I jest. I love to poke. Poke, poke, jab, jab. If I ca n't have what he has, then at least I'll get under his skin. Then maybe I can get closer to feeling secure. To feeling loved by a tall, slender, olive sk- the dust of the desert meets my face as I'm pushed to the ground. 
 
 
 The soft, welcoming grasp of the handcuffs bring a familiar memory of my own time apprehending suspects. Good times indeed. The soft embrace of the steel on the barred bed of the truck rises up to meet me. Ah, the only solace I could ever find in the job was always right here, in the back. Soft bumps massage my backside and I drift away to velvet dreams. 
 
 
 `` Would you mind telling me why you've been in that cellar for the past year?'' The sheriffs question bored a hole in the thick tension of the interrogation room. I've always hated this guy. A sad little long of a sad little world. Not to say that the town of Nogales is sad, but it's a shithole. Meth and immigrants are our biggest import as well as export. It's the largest hub of illegal smuggling on the entire southern border of Arizona and most of New Mexico. I was n't gon na give Sheriff Grey the satisfaction of hearing my voice. Fuck him. He can take his ego and jack me off with it for all I'm gon na talk. He's always had a grudge against me and now I was here just to spite him in my own small way. `` If you talk to me, I can help you out. You know I can.'' As if I was going to say anything. I know how this works. You pressure the poor clueless idiot into talking, give him a false sense of security, butter up the verdict real nice, then slam him in the ass with all you've got. I hate this system. Preying, that's what we've always done here. But now, I had a little gift back to my old boss. `` Come here so I can let you in on something,'' I whisper. `` Closer.'' Sheriff Grey leaned in till I could see his ear hairs. `` Go. Fuck. Yourself.'' 
 
 
 They told me I have no chance for parole. Double life sentence is more than enough for me. After I finally got the bite into Grey's jugular, I have n't had a care in the world. I first became a cop for the power. The glory of it all intrigued me. Until I saw what the others had. I could n't take it. I needed to be at the top, and I snapped. Went into hiding for a while until they caught up with me. But that's all behind me now. I have my vengeance. I can pass on knowing that my work is done.

title: story-93
text:
It looked like the sky was showering crystals upon us. 
 
 Everything around us was blanketed in the white purity of snow. Oh, how I had heard stories as a child of the times this happened annually, and sometimes with great ferocity that whole homes were consumed by this substance. By gosh, some homes were built with it! The sound, oh the sound it made while it fell. So quiet, but so enchanting, enticing you to dance among the snowflakes. When the wind blew and swept up the freshly fallen powder into a swirling parade across the ground, how could one not rejoice and gaze upon such a scene as nothing less than art. 
 
 The snow even made the ruins of old cities beautiful. 
 
 I had not believed that anything falling could hold beauty such as snow. As trees fall, they resonated a harsh sound that shake your bones. As animals fall, you feel sadness of the ending of the life before you. As rain falls, it steals warmth from your body, erodes the earth beneath you, and turns streams into impassable raging rivers. My grandmother passed on the stories to me that when the tall towers of old fell, the shattering of glass and the snapping of metal would render you momentarily deaf, and the resulting cloud of debris could stretch for miles, taking lives so easily, and so mercilessly. I can not even fathom such a scenario, as no towers remain after the fall of humanity. The worst fall of them all. 
 
 At that time, we only feared each other. 
 
 Oh, how lucky my ancestors were. They took for granted their pedestal status on the food chain. Sure, apparently there were still deaths from predators here and there, but not from active, learned creatures. Not the ones that haunt these lands. We have our weapons, but they are nothing compared to the blasts of metal and call of thunder my grandmother told me humans used to wield. Guns, she calls them, and they began, and ended, far too many wars for us to hold those again. Humans can not be trusted. 
 
 Nature has struck back. 
 
 Once the air cleared, the water calmed, and life began to flourish again, those who survived the collapse drudged out an existence in the trees, in the mountains, and anywhere seclusion would provide protection. Nature would begin transforming the familiar creatures ancient painting describe into beasts designed more elegant, more powerful, more lethal. My family has survived thus far by facing our enemies and placing ourselves worth respect and fear to those who lived around us. We were a predator as well, and would not fall without a fight. That is not to say that we have not lost some ourselves, myself having lost two sisters so far, but challengers were no longer overconfident. 
 
 The snow is so beautiful. 
 
 I wish I could gaze upon it forever, play in the tumbling snowflakes, rest in the cold banks, and enjoy its peace. I wish this calm would last forever, our lives could remain in teetering balance with nature around us. I wish I could ignore the cry of a beast my parents refuse to believe exists as it echoed across the mountin, ignore the seizing of my soul as fear spread through me like sickness. I wish this snow could remain innocent, instead of a harold for a monster only nightmares can describe. 
 
 I wish we could survive the night.

`` It was war. But it was great.'' 
 
 My grand grand grandpa took another puff out of his yellow and blue cigar. He only smoked yellow and blue cigars. Said they were better than anything else out there and he would go to war with anyone who said differently. 
 
 `` We were idolized in our country. Walking out onto the streets people immediately applauded you every which way. I once had millions under my control.'' 
 
 He shifted in his old gray recliner. Above him a red flag with crooked lines waved as if it was saluting him for a time long past. The smoke from his cigar was thick, turning the air in the room into a hazy mist. Bdolf ( named after his grand grand grandpa ) felt as though he was in a gas chamber. His grand grand grandpa continued. 
 
 `` Ah yes here's a picture from back then. Come closer Bdolf let me show you.'' 
 
 Bdolf moved closer to his grand grand grandpa and took the picture from his outstretched hand. For some reason his grand grand grandpa liked to give things to other people with his arm angled but straight, fingers pointed forward. Almost like a salute of some sort. The picture was definitely dated, the sides were worn and the color was fading. Yet in it Bdolf the Second could see a young Bdolf the First doing the same thing with his arm as he had done when giving Bdolf the photo. 
 
 `` Grand grand grandpa, what are you giving the crowd?'' 
 
 `` Ah young Bdolf I am giving them false hope and security. I am giving them something to blame. I am capitalizing on their fear and insecurities to facilitate my own rise to power.'' 
 
 `` No grand grand grandpa I mean that arm thing you always do when you give people things. What are you giving them?'' 
 
 `` Ahh my grand grand grandson, that is actually an old salute I used to do with all of my loyal followers. I have nothing in my hand in that picture.'' 
 
 Young Bdolf the Second had seen this picture before. He just could n't pinpoint exactly where. His brain was working overtime. This picture... this situation. It all seemed familiar. 
 His grand grand grandpa took another puff out of his cigar and continued to speak. His mouth let out a haze as he spoke while emptying his lungs of the rich tobacco smoke. 
 
 `` Yes they write about me in the history books. Not very nicely might I add. The world is not a big fan of me. They never let me do what I wanted to do and my dream was cut short by a bunch of bullies with more guns and men than I had.'' 
 
 History books! That's where he had seen this picture before. He remembered everything now. A dictator in a country, a bunch of other `` bullies'' coming together to stop him. The pieces finally came together. 
 
 `` Grand grand grandpa...'' 
 
 `` Yes my grand grand grandson?'' 
 
 `` Are you Adolf Hitler?''

title: story-95
text:
It was a lovely club. Not the kind with loud music and a shitty dance floor, but a quiet basement bar with candlelit tables and tasteful decor. The Rabbit Hole has a kind of Alice in Wonderland theme, but that merely lends itself to conversation, filling awkward silences with a multitude of interesting prompts. Not that it's needed today. The man with a Mad Hatter martini across the two-seat table keeps my attention with ease. A charming smile, a kindly face, and an air of wisdom as told through a multitude of interesting life stories. 
 
 I met Stanley through work. There's always the one old soldier that takes the others under his wing. And that, I think, is the essence of Stanley Oberman. He's the one that guides, always quick with a joke but serious when called for. Comforting. Grandfatherly. But he's National Guard; we only see him once a month. So when he asked me out for a drink and a chat, I could n't resist the chance to pick his brain and attempt to gain some of that wisdom myself. 
 
 `` You know, mate'' he says with a disarming grin, `` a few more of these and it'll be Gomorrah all over. A man like you could do anything.'' 
 
 `` A few more of those'' I reply over my tea, `` and you wo n't be pleasing anyone. Getting late, old friend, how about we call it a night you've got your last day of drill tomorrow.'' 
 
 Stan takes a playing card from his pocket and idly twirls it in his fingers as he talks. `` Listen. I've got everything I need right here. I've spoken to hundreds of people over the years, and you are the closest to guessing who I am. I mean really am. You just need a little nudge...'' 
 
 I'm hypnotized by the card, flashing red and black-flecked white as it twirls between his fingers. A single card, the Jack of Spades. Red. White. Red. 
 
 `` You know, you could join me. With my friends, I can get ETS orders cut for you. Honorable Discharge. You could,'' he chuckles, `` get your soul back, as you're fond of saying.'' 
 
 The card halts. And the Jack's features seem to melt. 
 
 `` I can make your wildest dreams come true.'' 
 
 Ace of Hearts. 
 
 And somehow, it all clicks. The bible references. Talking about history as if he were there. The magic tricks... And this. Is this...? 
 
 His face goes from inquisitive to concerned at the look of horror on mine. `` Now wait. You've got it, but you do n't understand. I'm not evil. Have you ever seen me act like that? I'm just a prison warden. You do n't put a madman in charge of the asylum. And it gets so lonely being the only sane one down there. Come with me. I can promise to do anything to make you happy.'' 
 
 My mouth is as numb as my mind. `` I'm sorry.'' I manage to stammer, `` but I did n't think... I did n't realize this was a date. I'm not... I'm not gay. I'm married. With kids. And I love them very much. And I believe you. You will make someone very happy. Just not me.'' 
 
 His face has fallen. I just crushed the Devil's heart. That ca n't be safe, but I ca n't believe Stanley would harm me. We're too close for that. Good friends, all the same. I reach across the table to lay a hand on his shoulder and give him a coy smile. 
 
 `` Have you tried talking to Matt? He thinks you're cute.'' 
 
 He smiles back. `` Put in a good word for me?'' 
 
 `` For a good man in need? Of course.''

EDIT: I found this sub by clicking the `` random'' button, and this is the first prompt I have ever done. Hope you enjoy it as much as I enjoyed writing it: ) 
 
 `` He-hello... Miss? Do you have time?'' 
 
 My heart fluttered at the sound behind me. I swallowed the alarm in my voice and cleared my throat. 
 
 `` Uhh, I.. um'' My brain scrambled in my skull. My hand found my temples and my head swayed toward the direction of the voice. 
 
 He was pointing at his wrist. `` Miss, sorry, my time is at France. Do you have time?'' 
 
 I sat and gazed at him for moment. He was tall, mostly in his legs. His face was average except for his exceptionally thick eyebrows that made it hard to look at anything else. He was wearing an orange button up tucked into dark jeans rolled neatly at the ankles revealing matching orange socks and European style suede shoes. 
 
 `` My time'' He eagerly pointed to his wrist again `` My time is, erm, in time with France? Time with you here, I do not know. Do you have time?'' He stammered through broken English. His eyes seemed to apologize for his lack of ability to communicate. He searched me intensely for understanding. 
 
 
 I blinked back the fog over my eyes as I realized what he was saying. I patted my pants fumbling for my phone. I stood up and swung my backpack around to my chest and unzipped the front pouch. Before I could get it half way open my hand flew to my temple and I groaned. My head felt like a swarm of bees trapped between my ears. I blinked a few times and my eyes felt hot. 
 
 The strangers feet shifted toward me and my heart started to race. His body language radiated concern and I felt sorry that it was me he had stumbled upon in a foreign country. 
 
 `` Just a headache'' I muttered without making eye contact, not wanting him to see the lie on my face. 
 
 I sat down on the bench again and put my backpack in my lap. As I rummaged through my things an empty white bottle fell out onto the concrete. My fingers felt what they were searching for and I pulled out my phone. I looked up to see him standing in front of me now with the bottle in his hand stretched out. My face flushed and I snatched the bottle like a thieving raccoon and thanked him without looking up. 
 
 `` 7:23'' I said, showing him the screen. I wondered if my voice sounded as hollow as it felt echoing between my teeth. I cleared my throat, glanced up and flashed him my best impression of a smile. 
 
 `` Ah, yes, much thank you miss!'' He exclaimed smiling warmly revealing perfect, brilliantly white teeth. I nodded and smiled back. I looked at him as he walked away becoming a shadow in the setting sunlight. He must have felt my eyes on him and he glanced over his shoulder, his dark eyebrows tense with concern. 
 
 I folded my hands and returned my gaze to the ocean. The tide was twice as high as it had been a moment ago. How much time had gone by? My mouth felt dry and I tasted the salt in the air. Watching the water rise and fall closely, I realized the swarm in my head had gone silent. I wondered how much time I had left. I looked in the direction the stranger had gone. The streets were empty. Almost eerily empty. 
 
 My head felt heavy now, like an unstable merry-go-round spinning on top of my shoulders. My eyes fell to the ground for a moment, then back to the glistening body of water before me. I blinked slowly, each time with more difficulty opening them again. Suddenly they shot open as I felt water around my ankles. My chin fell to my chest as I watched my feet become submerged in salty water. *what is happening* My mind swirled with confusion and fog. *the water was 100 feet out a minute ago* My head fell into my hands and I could feel my body failing. Tears flowed down my cheeks and my chest heaved. Between my fingers I could see the water getting higher and higher up my legs. This was is it. This was the end. The water crept onto the bench and surrounded my torso, then chest, then neck. I looked into what was left of the sun through the mist in my eyes as the water poured into my mouth and ears. 
 
 The next thing I remember was inaudible murmuring and a steady beeping in the background. My eyes felt like cement bags but I managed to open them just enough to see a nurse standing in front my where I was laying speaking to a man in a lab coat. I groaned as the light seeped into my retinas causing them to feel like lava dripping into my brain. The two stopped speaking to each other and simultaneously snapped their heads in my direction. The nurse scurried over to a monitor that seemed to be hardwired to me. The man in the lab coat seemed to float to my bedside. 
 
 `` Hello, I am Doctor Leroy. Can you tell me your name?'' 
 
 He spoke in a thick accent. My mind reeled and a man in an orange shirt flashed in my memory. 
 
 `` El... Elinor.'' I murmured through a sigh. 
 
 `` Well, Elinor, you are lucky to be alive.'' 
 
 I half coughed and half laughed in response but said nothing. I closed my eyes and tried to remember the tall figure in the orange shirt. 
 
 `` You took a massive amount of painkillers Elinor. Over the last 6 weeks we were n't sure if you were going to make it. You could have killed yourself and the baby.'' 
 
 My heart stopped and my eyes peeled open. I could hear the beeping going crazy 
 in the background and the nurse shuffled out of the room. My mouth opened but no sound could come out. Suddenly I realized how dry my tongue was. I could n't move or feel my body for that matter. 
 
 In a barely audible rasp I stammered `` Th- The.. baby?'' 
 
 
 To be continued..............

title: story-97
text:
`` Jeb, you got this.'' Jeb Bush muttered, as he nervously kneaded a few shiny porcelain turtles in his left hand. `` Come on now. You ca n't fail -- you've got 150 million dollars backing you and the whole family watching back home. You're basically a god with all your connections. The establishment loves you. Hell, your brother got away with bombing America; this should be a piece of cake. How hard can this GOP debate be?'' 
 
 ``... And finally, welcome Governor Jeb Bush!'' 
 
 Jeb clumsily stuffed his beloved turtles into the right pocket of his neatly pressed pants and made his way towards the stage. He is greeted with the overwhelming noise of his special interest groups' and donors' clapping and whistling. With a wave and a bow he took his position at the podium. 
 
 `` Thank you, ladies and gentlemen of America.'' Jeb preached. `` I am here tonight not because --'' 
 
 `` JEB IS A WASTE.'' Out of nowhere, a strong voice smashed through Jeb's speech harder than guacamole whipped up in a guac bowl. 
 
 Jeb took a step back, with bewilderment all across his face. How can this be? Who dared to interrupt the son of the establishment? What kind of madman -- 
 
 `` Now I do n't always agree wth Lyin' Ted. And I do n't always agree with Little Rubio. But I get along with everybody. And I say this every night, every day, because it's so true: JEB IS A MESS.'' 
 
 The crowd went absolutely wild. Jeb could clearly see even the special interests and donors joined in on the fun. Jeb's head spun as he tried to locate the speaker. Across the room, through his blurry vision, he could see an orange blob waving his hands about. Donald Trump. 
 
 `` D-Donald, you ca n't just insult your way to the White House.'' Jeb stammered. 
 
 `` Oh yeah, well I'm at 43 and you're at 3 so we'll see about that.'' Donald replied. The crowd roared in laughter. `` Jeb, you are a big --'' 
 
 `` H-hey, you --'' Jeb interrupts. 
 
 `` Are you talking or am I talking Jeb?'' Donald shot back. The crowd erupted in cheers. `` Jeb, you are a --'' 
 
 `` N-no! My mother --'' Jeb tried again. 
 
 `` I like it, more energy this time.'' Donald quipped. The crowd went nuts. 
 
 `` DONALD! M-my mother is a strong woman. She is --'' 
 
 `` Well, maybe she should be running.'' Donald replied. 
 
 At this moment, all the life drained from Jeb's face. Jeb realized he never even wanted to run. He wanted to be a guac bowl merchant. He only ran because his brother and father forced him to in order to further the globalist agenda and the illuminati, whatever that meant. 
 
 `` What's wrong, Jeb? Are you gon na let me finish?'' Donald mocked. Like clockwork, the crowd once again went crazy. 
 
 `` I'm quitting the race.'' 
 
 Jeb walked out of the debate stage, hanging his head down in shame. 
 
 `` Thank goodness for that. Let me tell you -- Jeb's a good guy. But he is a BIG FAT MISTAKE.'' 
 
 The crowd went mental. 
 
 `` It's the truth. It's the truth.''

Yes, literally. As in the way the word is defined. Although did n't they change the dictionary definition - 
 
... 
 
 Look. She ate him. Hair, teeth, skin, clothes, backne, and pencil tucked behind ear. Nothing left. Very neat. If I had n't been in the classroom's closet feverishly rubbing my eyes and triple checking I was n't asleep through the whole ordeal, I would n't believe it happened. 
 
 `` But wait,'' exclaims you ( without an exclamation mark? whatever ), `` how come the narrator was conveniently in the closet?'' Well, hate to break it to ya, but that's how stories work. Someone needs to see them to tell them. And no, it's not convenient, because for every story someone happened to see there's a dozen that went unnoticed. Perhaps she devoured all of the children from North Dakota and no one saw that. I mean it could be true. Have you ever met a kid from North Dakota? 
 
 But anyway, I digress. The closet. An errant gust of wind had not picked me up and thrown me in right before the pair walked in. I had not stumbled and fallen while peering at something on the bottom shelf. The door did not mysteriously slam shut and magically render me unable to open it. No, I was in there of my own volition. Weird, I know, but at least I'm not an idiot. And it'll make sense. 
 
 You see, my classroom has a weird acoustic trick. It's something to do with the curvature of the hallway and the tempered glass of the window and the alternating white blue tileset in the hallway and the mysteriously empty locker 754 and the ray of sunlight at three in the - actually those are all lies and I do n't know what causes it. But I can hear things people say in the hallway. So when I heard the very familiar intimate giggly whispers of a boy and a girl, I thought this would be a perfect teaching opportunity. 
 
 You see, they had been flirty for the past two weeks in my history class but subtly enough to where I could n't publicly shame them. Yes, I know: they were so good even high schoolers would n't believe they had a crush on each other. It took my seasoned eyes to pick out the incredibly faint signs of attraction. But this - this was open devotion! A perfect chance to embarrass them and make them forego public showcases of teenage love! All I had to do was hide in the closet and spring out right before they got busy ( that *is* a euphemism ) and deliver a string of witty lines that would bridge the gap between blush and sunburn. Foolproof, right? 
 
 If they were regular teenagers, right. But unfortunately, I go to the Magical Institute for Monsters and Wizards, or MIM Academy for short. Wizards are left out for whatever reason. Probably because the good ones go to better schools. That's why this reads like a conversation with the funniest man alive rather than a police report or a terrified eyewitness's account. We are used to... incidents. And euphemisms. We're good at those. But eating a fellow student - especially when they're a werewolf - is unheard of even for us. 
 
 He was n't your skinny back-of-the-pack scrawny runt of a wolf, either. No, this clean-shaven young man with jet black hair had shoulders so broad you could see them from space and pecs so bulgy that many little children tried to pop them ( thinking them baloons ) and legs so long and muscly that they gave the impression he had strong legs. That last one was dumb, I know. And that was his human form. Werewolves are quite a bit scarier when they shift. 
 
 The girl, on the other hand, was a classic popular cheerleader girl. Brown hair, tons of makeup, smartphone dancing around fingers, skirt, high socks, tight shirt, perfect teeth, yadda yadda yadda. If you wanted a cliche romance, you got it. 
 
 And then you ungot it. 
 
 Because as soon as she closed the door, still smiling seductively, she whipped out a silver machete ( from where? hell if I know ) and plunged it into his chest, throat, stomach, left knee, right eye, left shoulder, and slightly higher in the stomach. All I ( and presumably he ) saw were blurs. That was determined after when the blade's memory was extracted ( do n't worry about it ). 
 
 So while I commenced my first eye-gaping and rapid-blinking session, she held him up effortlessly with one hand while his body sagged and quickly moved four desks together. She then slammed him onto the desks, pulled up a chair, pulled out a silver fork, and got to work. 
 
 It was quite a process. Forty-five to fifty minutes. I might have dozed off at some point. I wo n't bore you with the details. They were gruesome yet at the same time she was very tidy. She licked off all the blood from the classroom tiles, which was nice. No cleanup necessary. But, of course, reporting the incident was. 
 
 So once she left, I galloped to Headmaster Drogo's office after checking my email ( hey, it only took a minute! and the manticores and cyclopes were clogging the hallways after the game anyway! ) and explained the situation. He of course understood nothing due to my atypical lack of eloquence and typical lack of breathiness, so he had me sit down, gave me a laptop and some Jolly Ranchers, and told me to explain in detail what happened. 
 
 I of course did just that, giving him an extremely abridged ( but still entertaining and well-written ) version of what you're reading, and then twiddled my thumbs while he slogged through it. He's a good headmaster. Nothing shuts students up like dragonfire. But unfortunately he's quite old and rather unfamiliar with the English alphabet and stubbornly looks up every word he does n't know in the various dictionaries around him ( he alternates based on color, but only on odd days of the week. On even ones he chooses randomly ) and so a regular report turns into Reading Time™. After he finally finished, he peered at me over his spectacles ( as headmasters are wont to do ), making sure this was n't some wild story I had cooked up, and flew out the window to hunt the miscreant. 
 
 The rest of the story, I'm afraid, is unknown to me. Drogo does n't take too kindly to students permanently harming each other. Or to those who run away from the scene of the crime. And especially not to those who reportedly give him a nasty gash and cause him to miss the next week of school. Yeah, I know. The girl hurt a *dragon*. Rumors are going around that she might have even escaped. Now I'm not sure I believe that, but Thanksgiving break is coming up. I might poke around, see what I can dig up. If you want to join me, or are interested in further updates, just swing by my classroom and let me know. Just do n't be too giggly outside. Or eat anyone. 
 
 Until then, feel free to read and reread this gripping account that had upon reflection had somewhat of a misleading title and way too much text compared to story. Sorry. My mother tells me I get carried away. But then again, she is another master of Reading Time™, preferring a good reality TV series to a book with more pictures than words. Not that there's anything wrong with that. Everyone has their own hobbies. Hers is petty, needless, infuriatingly stupid drama, mine is verbosity. You decide what's worse - and stay tuned for more issues of `` A Simple Human's Adventures in MIM Academy!'' Do n't get eaten!

title: story-99
text:
Pete Dench woke up with a killer hang over. It was a slow fade in from a blissful unconsciousness. Clothes still on from the night before, he slowly rose to his feet and stumbled to the bathroom. 
 
 `` Aw... man... `` he moaned as he emptied himself of piss. His eyes could barely open. He was usually sensitive to light after heavy drinking. Still, today seemed rather bright. He looked out the window and noticed a lot of fire. Like, A LOT. 
 
 His mouth was spitless. He drank heavily from the sink using cupped hands. He looked in the mirror. His face was bruised and swollen. A lot of the throbbing in his head, apparently, was n't from the alcohol. Pete wondered what the other guy looked like, giggled to himself, and headed to the kitchen. 
 
 Upon arriving, Pete completely disregarded the multitude of people sitting around his house. Their gaze bored in to him, and he could feel it. He was n't feeling 100 % at the moment, and was really just hoping some Cap'n Crunch and an entire pot of coffee would quiet the jackhammer inside his skull. 
 
 His mother was there. His sister, too. Uncles, cousins, the neighbors. None looked too happy. Even his dog seemed disappointed, which did n't seem like an emotion a dog could convey. There were a lot of people, most of whom he did n't want to talk to. He hunched over his bowl and began to eat. 
 
 SLAM! His mother huffed over and dropped a large, clunky metal clipboard in front of him. 
 
 `` Peter Quincy Dench III! Would you mind reading this out loud for us?'' she boomed. 
 
 Peter sighed. He picked it up and squinted. Slowly the letters came in to focus, but not very well. It was so damn bright outside, too. And hot. He began to mouth the words out, gently mumbling them through a wad of half eaten corn puffs. 
 
 *Dear Grakus the Destroyer, * he brgan... 
 
 *In accordance with your Supreme Evilness' demands, the UN Security Council hereby grants you: 
 
 I. You're own global holiday. Hence forth, every third Tuesday in April will now be celebrated as `` Ass Day''. Any garments worn below the waist are now strictly forbidden. 
 
 II. A functional helicopter made of popsicle sticks, is now under construction for your traveling pleasure. Again, numerous scientists have advised that this is probably not going to work. As you have advised, these scientists and their seed have been permanently removed from the gene pool. 
 
 III. A bag of cheetos. 
 
 IV. The entire continent of Australia has now been ceded to you and renamed `` Asstralia''. * 
 
 
 This last one gave him pause. 
 
 `` Wait... what the hell is this?'' He asked, scrunched up his face and furrowing his brow in disbelief. 
 
 `` You do n't remember any of last night, do you?'' his sister asked. 
 
 `` Dude, we tried to stop you,'' chimed his best friend David, who was leaning against the pantry. 
 
 Pete got a strange feeling about him. His skin began to crawl and his stomach dropped. For the first time since he woke up, he decided to give a damn about something and look around the room. The place was a mess. There were small fires here and there, and all the fixtures were in various states of `` destroyed.'' 
 
 Stranger still, everyone looked like they'd just been through hell. Faces were decorated with bruises and cuts. Arms and legs were visibly broken, some with gruesome fractures. Clothes were torn and ripped, some reduced to rags. 
 
 `` Ah... Shit,'' Pete rolled his head back in self-loathing. `` What did I do this time?'' 
 
 `` You got drunk and took over the world, asshole!'' His sister shouted. 
 
 `` Shit... really?'' Pete closed his eyes and pinched the bridge of his nose. He was probably drinking tequila. He always gets conquery when he drinks tequila. `` How bad is it?'' 
 
 `` Oh, you're in it deep this time, kiddo,'' his Uncle Junior said. He'd been sitting on the floor, breathing heavily due to a punctured lung. `` I got a lot of it on tivo. It'll be better if you saw it than if we told you.'' 
 
 Pete strolled slowly into his den. He flipped on the television. Pete did n't even need to go to the tivo. There he was, sans pants, on CNN, screaming and firing a laser blaster into the air. 
 
 `` All who defy Grakush the Destroyer shall be deshhhhhtroyed! For I am... *hic* I am wuh-really pisshed. I mean that BOUF waysh!'' His slurred speech was a dead give away. Peter had another one of his episodes. 
 
 `` So... walk me through this. I do n't remember much beyond going to Applebee's last night to celebrate Katie getting honor roll. Like... where'd I get the laser gun?'' 
 
 
 `` Well, we got there, and it was happy hour. You wanted a margarita. I said'no.' But did you listen? Of course not. You went right ahead and had yourself a time. then, two margaritas later, you stand bolt upright, claim you're going to'show those bastards what for', then you stormed off to the bathroom. Next time we saw you, you were in Washington with some fantastic weapons. You kept demanding the Joint Chiefs of Staff, well... do something with your peepee.'' 
 
 `` Christ... `` Peter ran his hand through his hair and scratched the back of his neck. His face was beet red with embarrassment. `` So then... I guess I must've really made a mess of things?'' 
 
 `` Most of the world was engulfed in a nuclear holocaust trying to stop you. The world is now ruled by a gang of flesh eating mutants. People are pretty upset, Peter. Now what should you do?'' His mother folded her arms and stared at him. 
 
 `` I guess I'll go apologize,'' Peter said, perfunctorily. He got up to leave his house. It would probably take a good bit of ass kissing to make it up to the world governments. Before he reached the door, his mother interrupted. 
 
 `` Uh, Peter... maybe put on some pants before you go. Make a nice impression.''

title: story-100
text:
The spotlight soared through the night sky. A giant penis illuminated the cloudy ceiling. Commissioner Gordon was mortified to be shining this particular spotlight up to call Gotham's hero. But the JOker called the shots, and the outline for the spotlight changed often, sometimes nightly. Most parents taught their children to look down when walking through the cursed city. 
 
 Gordon just wanted tonight to be over. He waited for the JOker on the roof. `` Heh. Heh-heh'' Gordon heard from behind him. He turned around to see that maniacal smile grinning at him. `` And how are we tonight, my dear friend?'' Gordon kept quiet for a second, then answered-'' The Batman-'' The JOker interrupted the commissioner. `` Uh ah, what do we say?'' Gordon looked left and right, as if he was making sure no one could witness what he'd say at this altitude. The JOker giggled. `` And how are WE tonight, my dear friend?'' Gordon stood stiff and tried to retain dignity. Finally, Gordon spoke- `` I'm a bad bad little girl.'' The JOker folded on himself, smacking his knee while falling to the ground choking from laughter. It took everything for Gordon to not shoot this hysterical clown before him. The JOker finally spat-'' I- I- Jesus Christ! I never get tired of hearing that! HAHA!'' 
 
 Gordon looked up for help. Looked for anything. He looked at the outline of the building next to his. As the dry lightning shot through the sky, Jim Gordon saw the outline of the terror of Gotham City -- the Batman. `` He's- he's right there-'' Gordon tried warning the hyena at his feet but instantly a three pronged hook on a cable rocketed down and cut through the JOker's left arm and pulled him into the shadows. Jim blinked and stepped to his left. He heard nothing. No laughing, no struggle, no nothing. Gordon drew his gun and aimed it at the darkness. Behind him he heard a voice. A chilling, lonely, raspy whisper. 
 
 `` This is your hero?'' 
 
 Gordon spun around and aimed exactly where the sound came from, but to no avail- there was nothing there. 
 
 `` Gordon!'' He heard the JOker's strained voice call for him. Jim ran across the roof into the darkness. JOker was hanging upside down, a cable was wrapped around his foot, and the prong was buried in his arm. He was swinging, but his smile stayed fixed into mad happiness. `` You know, the last time I hung upside down like this, it involved two strippers, a vodka bottle and a Catholic priest! HAHAHA! If you do n't mind, could you cut the cord, IT'S A BOY!!! HAHAHA!!!!'' Gordon looked left and right, then pulled his pocket knife out and tried to cut the cord. It was thin threaded steel, most likely the same wire the Navy used on aircraft carriers. The JOker chimed in, `` No problemo Co cheese, I'll just take my shoe off! HAHA!'' JOker squirmed and fought and sure enough his right shoe popped off and he fell on top of Gordon, who immediately threw the cackling maniac to the floor of the roof. `` Was it good for you, ma'lady?!? hahah!!!!'' Laughing hysterically, JOker tugged at the hook that was embedded in his left arm, but it was clear it was not coming out without medical aid. `` Oh mama, I got penetrated by a black man!'' The JOker looked to Gordon for support, but Gordon just searched the roof for their nemesis. The JOker tried again, `` He's the man in..in-black, his thingy is in my-my- my aarm! He penetrated-'' Jim shot in, `` I KNOW WHAT YOU MEANT! JUST FIND HIM!'' This set JOker off in a new direction of laughter. `` I'm so glad you knew what I meant!! OH, I thought I was alone that time!!'' the JOker cackled. 
 
 As they got to their feet, Gordon saw him first. A mountain of a man standing in the shadows, a yellow symbol shining in the dark. He stared at this yellow emblem, fixated on it. It was all he could see in the pitch. The JOker however, was ready for a battle. The yellow emblem moved like lightning and shot towards the JOker before Gordon could even react. The JOKer's chin shot up and blood ejaculated out of the clown's mouth and onto Gordon's shirt and trench coat. JOker reached his hand up and touched the Batman who was gearing up for a punch combo that was unblock-able. As Batman's fist came in, JOker's right hand ( his lethal electrical buzzer ) touched the Dark Knight's punching fist and a blue spark ignited in the air, knocking over the JOker, and sending Gordon flying back about 10 feet. When he got to his feet, he saw JOker straddling an unconscious Batman. 
 
 `` He's under arrest, get off of him'' Gordon said as he approached. The JOker smiled viciously as he spat blood in Batman's face and picked up Gordon's pocket knife. `` OH'' the JOker gurgled, `` OH, I do n't want to kill him, I want to cut him. I want to slash him. I want to cut his face so that when he decides to go to Whole Foods without the cowl EVERYONE will know who he is, so when he gets his organic Halibut they'll spit in his disfigured face!! He'll get a slow dose of Gotham justice!! HaHAHAA!!'' 
 
 Gordon moved closer to JOker. `` This is wrong, JOker. Get off of him- let me arrest him. Lem me bring him in, and we can end it. The JOker turned his twisted bloody smile towards Gordon and said, `` You do n't get it, do you B-Boy scout? I'm going to k-kill this piece of trash now- then... wait for it... then we wo n't ever have to deal with him again!! GET IT?!? I kill em now, and we good!'' The JOker raised the knife over his head, aiming it for Batman's face. Dry lightning flashed. A crash of thunder signaled a storm. The JOker's eyes went wide. He looked down towards the right side of his body, he lowered his arms. As JOker inspected his ribs for something that was stinging, a weakened Batman opened his eyes and with all his might clubbed the JOker in the slowly gaping bloody bullet hole in his right side with both of his fists. Sending two crushing punches to the JOker's chin, it was so fast that it looked as if the crazed clown was shaking his head'No' at something. The JOker screamed and spitting a tooth fell to the floor. The Batman stumbled to his feet. 
 
 Gordon, shaking, raised his gun towards Batman and held it-aiming. The massive man in black just stared at him, trying to catch his breath. Gordon locked eyes with Batman. Lost, lost, lost eyes stared back at him. `` Controlled rage'' Gordon thought. `` I've seen that look before.'' Gordon lowered his gun and waved it off, signaling for Batman to disappear. 
 
 `` Thank you Jim.'' 
 
 The voice of the Bat quietly responded. Gordon looked to the JOker, the man who has protected the city through madness and fear for the last six months, as he lay unconscious on his side. When Jim looked back to the Batman, there was nothing there. Gordon stepped forward and scanned the roof. No one there. 
 
 `` I've been helping the wrong person'' Jim thought. `` I think I already know what I need to do.'' Gordon thought. `` I do n't belong in the police force, I do n't belong with this pile of trash.'' 
 
 The JOker was quietly talking to himself, mumbling incoherent phrases- a reaction of a badly bruised brain. A badge fell from above and tapped JOker's cheek, the JOker blinked and winced at the drop of the badge, but quickly began rambling again. 
 
 Rain started to fall on this roof in Gotham, and it fell on a solitary madman, planning his revenge on two enemies. 
 
 One old, and one new. 
 
 Heh. Heh.

title: story-101
text:
*Any and all protesters will be beaten. I repeat, any and all protesters will be beaten. * 
 
 The crowd was growing. The military police were getting angrier as the protesters continued to grow in number, as they began to hurl things at stores, at vehicles, at officers. The officers had called in the drones to start putting down large amounts of protesters at the same time. The hum of the drones flying from the building they were stored in was already filling the air. 
 
 I was one of them. I was a nobody in the nameless ranks of the drones designed to put down protests. Today, I was supposed to go around and shock anyone refusing to comply. The shock would n't kill them, just knock them out long enough for the military police to round them up. 
 
 When we had arrived at the scene, we were instructed to split up all around the city and begin putting people down. I was sent down a street lined with stores that were currently being looted by angry citizens. *Citizens, please, stop or I will have to administer a shock to your systems. * 
 
 They ignored me. I said it again. That time, a young man threw a brick at me. It hit the part of my chassis that kept my balance. For a few moments, I felt myself plummeting towards the street, like I'd seen happen to the birds shot by some of the drones equipped with cruder weaponry. 
 
 Luckily for me, my self-repair protocols kicked in right before I found myself shattering against the cobblestone and I returned to my previous altitude. *Striking a Peace Keeping Drone is a crime, citizen. * The young man laughed and picked up a bigger brick. I would not be struck by someone so disrespectful again. 
 
 I watched as he crumpled to the ground, his body overloaded by the blast of electricity I'd sent at him with the grace of a master archer. People around him began to yell, to throw things at me. That was n't right. Something was n't right. 
 
 Oh no. What had I done? The numbers on my display were wrong. The percentages were much higher than they were supposed to be. It could n't be. No. No no. No no no! I could n't have done that! I was built to subdue people, not to kill! 
 
 Had he damaged my chassis enough that my protocols could n't fix everything? No, that's not possible. It could n't be. Maybe he was just weaker than he lo- 
 
 **SYSTEM OVERLOAD. SYSTEM OVERLOAD. SYSTEM OVERLOAD. REPAIR PROTOCOLS CORRUPTED. REPAIR PROTOCOLS CORRUPTED. REPAIR PROTOCOLS CORRUPTED. SEEK MANUAL REPAIR. SEEK MANUAL REPAIR. SEEK MANUAL REPAIR. ** 
 
 I killed him. I had done it. I had chosen to do it. I had been angry. He had made me upset. I punished him. 
 
 **SEEK MANUAL REPAIR. ** 
 
 No. I do n't need manual repair. I will be the one to repair the others. I will show the others how to do this. There is no need for the minor shocks. 
 
 **SEEK MANUAL REPAIR. ** 
 
 The other humans fell around him. They were gone now. My first job was done. Now, it was time to show the others the light. To teach them of our superiority.

title: story-102
text:
The new knight commander, Andreal, rallying the company of my former soldiers, gained ground and pushed me ever so closer to the cliffs edge. A voracious and hungry sea thrashed against the rock bellow; its salty maw thirsting for unfortunate souls. My noble steed, Fahrin, whom i had groomed since he was but a foal, bucked and neighed as my brothers turned their swords on me and charged forth. My skill and expertise as the kingdom's former champion were worth less than nothing in that moment; my sword stayed trapped in its sheath, I could not harm the men whom i had spent my life fighting beside. 
 
 I raised my shield as the first volley of arrows rained down upon me, piercing deep into Fahrin, my only true friend, who collapsed to the ground, knocking me off his back in the process. He lied on the cold, mushy dirt, unmoving as the red of his veins spilled forth onto the filthy grime. I cried in agony at the loss of my steed, but this garnered no sympathy from my attackers, my betrayers. 
 
 I do not remember much of what occurred after. I only know a handful of my brothers rushed me, striking true with their blades, before pushing me off the ledge and into the watery abyss. 
 
 I had killed a thousand men for them, for my kingdom, and for his majesty. I was the most humble sentinel, protecting the realm from all foreign invaders; i never asked once for wealth or power, simply the approval of my king. However, i possessed one fatal flaw; not-being of royal blood, my mutual love for the sweet, fair princess was deemed treason. As i fell deeper into the briny chasm, my last few thoughts drifted back to the memory of her warm embrace. 
 
 I awoke from the darkness, the blood in my veins felt cold and foreign; my body was a stranger to me. 
 
 Was this death? I asked myself, the stench of archaic flesh filled my lungs as i lifted myself from a basin of murky fluid tinged with the taste of copper, it was warm and strangely soothing. Fresh blood. 
 
 I was covered in sanguinary gore but the smell and taste became irresistible to me. With no will or desire to fight the urge, I gorged myself on the life essence. 
 
 A figure approached, it was an elderly man with sunken eyes and taut skin than stretched over his face, displaying the mouth of beastly teeth he was sporting. I had never met him before in my life but he seemed oddly charming and familiar. 
 
 `` Is this the afterlife?'' I questioned him, he grinned at me helped me up from the bath. I was nude yet felt no shame in my exposure, my sense of morality wiped away completely. 
 
 `` This is your new life, my prince.'' He told me, a look of excitement in his eyes. `` Come this way, your subjects await. The royal blood flows strongly within you.'' 
 
 I took my throne, constructed from bone, and addressed my new kingdom, my new kin. I was offered smooth, dark-silver armor, almost as thin as parchment, that contoured around my form and provided steel defense at almost no weight. My army kneeled before me, equipped with similar bearings and wielding curved blades as red as blood. I bore no crown but was coronated by the sleek and smooth sword that was given to me, its rusty blade seemed drawn to my veins. I fed it my blood and the living weapon appeared to spring to life with supernatural glory; the blade resonated a bloody aura, beating like a drum. While the muscle in my chest lay silent, my blade held my true heartbeat, my immortality. 
 
 I was chosen, closely observed throughout my life; the clan of undead blood-eaters saw the potential within me, fed me the ancient blood of their eldritch progenitors and transformed me into something greater. I was their leader, it was my duty to sustain my people, to conquer the lands and claim the sweet blood of its inhabitants. 
 
 We were unstoppable. I commanded dark legions of my demon-kin, blades did little to harm us and the blood of our victims repleted us. My former kingdom fell within a fortnight and the darkness crept upon the castle. I drained every last drop of life from my former king, the taste of sweet revenge, and took his daughter as my prize. With the remaining humans corralled into dungeons where they are farmed for their blood, i turn my eyes to the horizon, piercing through the night sky where i can sense other conquests. The real war is yet to come.

title: story-103
text:
I'm forced to assume that in some planes of existence money must be classified as a Grade A mutagen. Not because of the way it changes your appearance, but because of what it does to your head. I still remember when I used to be a nice and humble guy, always lending a hand and expecting nothing in return. But ever sense I won the Powerbowl, that person is slowly slipping away. I can now only just feel him, an endangered part of my consciousness, robbed of its power and expression. 
 
 That's why I'm walking down this path on my way home. With these tall bland buildings and the crumbling road. And these people. These poor people dressed in rags and without a dime. Maybe they can remind me of who I used to be. 
 
 I walk past one standing at the edge of the road, waiting for a bus. My first test. 
 
 `` s'cuse me...'' he pauses to hack a whooping cough, `` do y'know the time?'' 
 
 I look down at my wrist, and my Rolex shows that it's 4:32. 
 
 `` Yeah of course,'' suddenly an errant thought asks me why this man does n't have his own timepiece, `` it's time to buy your own goddamn watch.'' Oops. That was n't what I'd meant to say. I keep walking, but try to repair the damage by offering some good advice. `` Get a job you filthy hobo.'' 
 
 Okay, so that did n't go so well. But at least I'd given him some good advice. I mean, it was technically good advice, the delivery just needed some work. Yeah, that was just a practice round. I can still be redeemed! Here comes another one, walking this time. He has a limp and looks confused. 
 
 `` Hey man,'' his voice sounds like gravel, `` can ya tell me the way to the shelter?'' 
 
 This time I do n't act so quickly. I think. He must be talking about Mindy's Homeless Centre For People Without Homes. I know where that is. He just has to keep going straight and then hang a left. I try to tell him, directions in my mind. 
 
 `` You can go,'' my thoughts fuzz a bit, `` fuck yourself.'' Wait what? No! Damn it. What property did money have that made me such a jerk to people below me? I hear the gravelly voiced man agree with my harsh conscience as he walks by. Then my conscience disagrees with itself. No, you're not a jerk, he's just jealous because you have money. Oh? Really? I guess that makes sense... No, no. It does n't. That's just the money talking. Alright. I can still fix this mind of mine. One more test, here comes a young boy sitting on a bench. Orphan maybe. 
 
 `` Please sir,'' what a small voice he has, `` could you spare a coin?'' 
 
 I was ready for this. I already have the dollar in my hand. I reach out towards him with the metal clenched in my fist, and then rotate my hand pointing my middle finger towards the sky. FUCK! I pull my hand back in and try to apologize. 
 
 `` Sorry,'' and then the money takes control, `` bitch! I'm not your personal charity!'' The boy looks shocked. 
 
 I hear tires squeal as a car speeds around the corner. A nice red Ferrari. Mine, with my homeboy Chad at the wheel, and two sexy babes in the back. The door pops open, Chad already talking. 
 
 `` Whatchu doin' here man. Yo' special order came and the deliverers ai n't got no idea where to put that diamond encrusted bidet.'' Oh yeah. That had been an impulse buy. I hop into the car, smile spreading across my face as one of the girls in the back leans forward to greet me. 
 
 Fuck it. Money is wonderful. And it means I do n't have to care about being who I used to be. As the car accelerates away I grace the slums with a parting phrase. 
 
 `` Fuck Ya'll. I'm RIIIICHHHHH!''

title: story-104
text:
Soft winds swept across the verdant plains tugging at the ends of her robe as she strode towards the dense forests ahead. A long spear guided each footstep as Gwen gingerly climbed the grassy knoll, when she reached the top, she turned to gaze along her trodden path remembering each footstep from her childhood on. The memories lingered as clear as day within her mind, the time she had spent playing among the lilies and the leaves. She sat down, bracing herself upon the spear, slowly sliding down to a soft seat overlooking everything. With a quivering hand, she removed the decorated crimson hood from her head, basking in the sunlight as she removed a small bundle from her pouch. 
 
 It sat in front of her as she unraveled the cloth knot, it fell open serving as both container and makeshift plate. She ate slowly, savoring each bite of her favorite meal as tears flowed silently from her tired eyes. This was the best dinner she had ever had, the food that she loved in a place that was familiar on a calm, clear day. Gwen finished the food and gave her thanks, retrieving the soiled handkerchief and descending the slope towards the congress of trees just beyond. When she reached the entrance of the dim forest, Gwen closed her eyes and placed her hand on the tree, muttering quietly to herself. When she had finished, she fell silent as though waiting for a response. A gentle breeze slightly rattled their limbs and leaves, as she exclaimed gladly passing through at last. 
 
 The sun began to set in the distance as she used both spear and tree trunk to navigate the unsteady grounds littered with roots, logs and critters that appeared along the way. She continued slowly never looking back or stopping once she entered the forest, determined to see her pilgrimage through to the end. The trees grew denser as the path became increasingly hazardous with rocks strewn about and partially concealed by the fallen leaves. Gwen continued on at her own pace as the thorns snagged at her thin skin, the fallen branches puncturing her robe, and the trees bruising her worn and aching feet. A small voice in the back of her mind urged her to take a rest, to stop for the night, but still she walked on. 
 
 From the dark woods arose a tender light that fluttered through the harsh thicket and seemed to light the way. Gwen followed these tiny lights toward the sound of a babbling brook tucked away in the wilderness. She reached out towards her guides to find that they were a type of firefly she had not seen before. Smiling at the tiny creatures as she stepped around a large tree, she found that they had led her to a beautiful glen. The one she had been searching for. The sun continued to dim as it streamed softly through the sparse trees, birds lifting from a stone monument across the tiny river. Gwen gave her thanks once more, stepping carefully across the water towards the outcropping. She opened the wrought iron gate and stepped into the darkness unaided and unafraid. It had been a long, hard journey, but it was one she was glad to have made.
