# Title: Kranthanatos, Lord of Celebration 
 
 `` A round of shots for everybody!'' shouted the great alien Kranthanatos. 
 
 `` EYYYYY!'' shouted everybody in the club in unison. 
 
 The bartender had all ready lined up hundreds of shot glasses, and was filling them up. Kranthanatos told him he was going to make that announcement a few minutes prior so the bartender was ready for it. Drinks were getting passed everywhere. The whole club was bumping. The great blue alien Kranthanatos was the DJ. He stood about eight feet tall and had skin that would sort of shift to all shades of blue. But overall he looked pretty human, because his plastic surgeon back on his home planet galaxies away made him look as human as he could. It would help him assimilate into the culture. There were many aliens just like Kranthanatos DJ'ing all over the planet. 
 
 He was royalty back there at his home planet. Over here on Earth, he wanted to show us that the rest of the universe ai n't so bad. It was first contact. Kranthanatos was the lord of the celebration. 
 
 `` Is this how all the Burunqualians get down back home?'' shouted one particularly drunk girl. She was just twerking on everybody with her tongue hanging out. She twerked on Kranthanatos's leg too. The blue alien liked it. 
 
 `` You're the *shit* I swear you're *the exact shit Kranthanatos*,'' said one guy. 
 
 Kranthanatos looked up real mad and insulted, like he was being made fun of. Then somebody explained to him that was n't an insult, he was saying Kranthanatos is *fantastic* more or less, and Kranthanatos apologized for not capturing the conversational subtlety. He went back to fist pumping and DJ'ing. 
 
 `` Thanks broham!'' shouted Kranthanatos. He fist pumped his alien heart out. 
 
 `` What next Kranthanatos!'' shouted one drunk guy in the club. 
 
 `` Well I think it's about time we have one OF EARTH'S CLASSIC,'' Kranthanatos got really loud on the mic to hype it up. Everybody waited for the idea. `` A CLASSIC BREAK DANCE BATTLE *OH YEAH*!'' 
 
 And about twelve guys went onto the dance floor. They were lords of the dance, they went right at it in their two teams of six like it was all ready coordinated. Everything was just so smooth and entertaining. One guy was spinning around on his head and almost kicking people in the face. This other guy hopped around on his hands everywhere, and he was looking at everybody with this surprised expression like he was n't sure how the fuck he was doing it. It was all great theatrics. 
 
 The whole club was going nuts. There was a congo line, which was more or less a big grinding line where everybody was rubbing hard as fuck on each other. The club was wild and crazy. One girl was getting all hot and bothered dancing with her boyfriend by the entrance. 
 
 Then a group of men in masks barged in through the entrance, and knocked that girl and her boyfriend onto the floor. 
 
 `` WE WO N'T STAND FOR ANY ALIEN INVADING OVERLORDS NO SIR,'' shouted one guy. He cocked his shotgun. People were all ready crying and shouting. 
 
 Kranthanatos diffused the situation as fast as it arose. He turned even huger, into something of a *monster* for just a brief second. Around five mouths appeared around him. He grabbed at the men with his twelve arms, then swallowed each of them whole. 
 
 Everybody was screaming, but Kranthanatos became really humanoid just as fast as he ate the guys. Back to normal. 
 
 `` Everybod-*kof kof* everybody settle down all right hehe,'' said Kranthanatos. He put on this really awkward smile. `` Now we're here in *peace*, I hope that's clear enough right now. Just needed to stop that right quick, but we *love* humans we swear we do, we really do. And we love your culture, you have so much potential for good vibes and good times in the universe!'' 
 
 Most everybody was back in a mood of carefree fun. Some people were laughing really awkwardly. A couple girls were just shivering in the corner like they did n't know what they just saw, but they started to laugh and smile at each other like they were both trying to convince each other things were fine. They started dancing all awkward to get back into the mood. Then Kranthanatos turned a classic tune from Earth's vast collection of songs adored throughout the galaxy. 
 
 *Party Rock Anthem. * 
 
 `` EYYYYYY!'' shouted everybody in the club again. It brought back a joyous mood to everybody. 
 
 ~*PARTY ROCKERS IN THE HOUSSSEEEE TONIGGGHHHTTT*~ 
 
 `` This is the anthem which drew us to your planet in the first place,'' said Kranthanatos. He was fist pumping still. `` The vibe of joy and carefree partying was overwhelming, we could feel it galaxies away. Put your hands up humanity!'' 
 
 Kranthanatos started to sound very robotic and monotone, as his grasp for the subtleties of human language was n't always there ( he was still getting used to it ). But people knew what he meant overall. 
 Kranthanatos even did the *dougie* a few times while he was dancing and DJ'ing. And everybody cheered when he would. It was several years late for that move, but culture did n't always travel fast to other parts of the universe, even though they had such vigilant spies on Earth. 
 
 `` Goodness,'' said one girl. She looked so worried and went up to Kranthanatos like she was worried for him, and for humanity in general. `` I ca n't *believe* those angry men barged in here all mean and unkind poor *baby* Kranthanatos.'' 
 
 She was petting Kranthanatos's leg while she said it. Kranthanatos was a fucking giant, so he did n't quite understand why she was calling him a baby. But he assumed it was just another conversational subtlety he did n't quite get just yet. He confided in her, for he read her to be sincere. 
 
 `` We the Burunqualians can, in moments of intense emotion and empathy, see deeply into the future in four dimensions,'' said Kranthanatos. 
 
 `` Just like in *Slaughterhouse-five*?'' 
 
 `` Yes just like that, cheers to Vonnegut!'' said Kranthanatos. 
 
 `` Cheers!'' shouted the crowd. Nobody knew the context of why he shouted'cheers to Vonnegut' but it was just another reason to celebrate so fuck it, they took another shot. 
 
 `` And I know,'' said Kranthanatos. Back to confiding in the girl petting his leg. `` I know that the future is bright for our peoples. And for all life across the galaxy. Times of war may come, but in the end, there is only joy, peace, and crazy partying.'' 
 
 `` *Ooff*,'' said the girl. She hugged Kranthanatos's leg. 
 
 For centuries, Earths' culture was influenced by the Burunqualians. It was a time of new knowledge, peace, prosperity, and intergalactic travel. 
 
 We never looked back.

title: story-138
text:
`` Shhhhh! Did you guys hear that?'' 
 
 `` Hear what?'' 
 
 `` Oh my god you totally interrupted me!'' 
 
 `` Quiet Raven, you can read The Raven later, I thought I totally heard something.'' 
 
 The four picnicking friends sat peering through the dark of the cemetery. 
 
 Clink clink clink. *Woooooooooooo* 
 
 `` There! There it is!'' 
 
 `` W. T. F.'' 
 
 `` It is just a dead wondering soul lost in her own bitter torment...'' 
 
 `` Shut up Pixie I thought I heard it again.'' 
 
 `` Oh my god, its BunnyBlack now I told you that.'' 
 
 `` GUYS QUIET!'' 
 
 The four sat perfectly still as the breeze rustled the leaves. Changle changle *woooo* clink clink. 
 
 BunnyBlack let out a stiffled scream. `` Raven hold me!'' 
 
 `` Violater, what is that?'' 
 
 `` I do n't know Megan. I think its coming from the big mausoleum.'' 
 
 *Awwwwwwhhhhhh Wooooooooooo* Crinkle crinkle bang bang bang 
 
 Raven and BunnyBlack jumped up and started gathering the candles and goblets and fast food. 
 
 `` What are you doing?'' 
 
 `` Getting out of here Raven, what the fuck was that thing?'' 
 
 `` Oh really? I thought you were all about hunting ghosts and monsters and things that go bump?'' 
 
 `` Violator is right you guys, BlackBunny you talk to the dead right? Maybe it needs help, lets go see.'' 
 
 `` Well I did n't say I wanted to go help it Megan I just did n't think we needed to run away...'' 
 
 The four friends stood still for a moment. Raven looking paler than usual. Finally BunnyBlack spoke. 
 
 `` Spirit, I am your conduit, speak through me!'' 
 
 `` Woooooooo ahhhhhhhwoooooo stop sitting on my graveeeeeeeee eating Chipotlaaaayyyyyy and playing screamooooohhhhhhh.'' Crinkle crinkle clank bang bang. 
 
 All four of them screamed then three of them ran in three different directions. Raven passed out. 
 
 BunnyBlack did n't get far. The last sight she saw with her heavily lined and lashed eyes was a large angel statue. She did n't even feel the blow to her head. 
 
 Megan was promising to go to church and start listening to Taylor Swift when she was tripped. It took two blows to finish her off. 
 
 Violator almost made it back to the car. The last thing he saw was the swing of a shovel in the reflection of the window of the black Mercedes Wagon his parents bought him. 
 
 `` Hahahaha! Oh man that was great!'' Johnny was holding his sides he was laughing so hard. The glare of the fluorescents in the caretakers shed was a bit overwhelming and Ted shielded his eyes as he entered. `` Did you fix the gate? Not that I think they'll be coming back!'' 
 
 `` Yea, I got it and nah I do n't think they'll be back.'' Ted cracked a grin. 
 
 `` Did they all just run off and leave the little guy? There was no one on the phone by the way wish I could have stayed and watched them go!'' 
 
 `` Nah he woke up. They ran all the way home though I think. Left the car.'' 
 
 Johnny started cracking up again. `` Man! Those dipshits.'' 
 
 `` Yea.'' Ted gave another grin. 
 
 Raven was the only one who woke up in his grave. No one heard him scream of course and even if they did, cemeteries were full of ghosts right?

title: story-139
text:
I stare at the sofa. No thoughts or words. Had I seen too many films? There are no coincidences. Could it be that I wake up to the world being normal again? 
 
 Growing up with an identical twin, there comes a point where being alone is n't so bad. At first you think about what your brother is doing and question whether you can sense if he was in danger. Then you know that you can so everything is fine. You can learn from being alone. 
 
 I sense my brother is alive and well, yet I think he is wondering if I am O.K. I still have n't found anyone. Praying to God helps. He delivers comfort and the feeling that this should be a positive experience. Sometimes I feel other perspectives than my own, like someone questioning their existence or whether they are dead or whatever the difference. The conscious mind observing I guess. Knowing that things could be worse is why I have hope in the unseen. This is an opportunity to have fun. 
 
 The electricity is still on. It feels orderly. I knocked on someone's door earlier cause they had one too many lights glowing. It looked like the type of house with an alarm, so I broke the glass to the back door and walked in. I wanted to see if anyone would respond to the noise. Who knows? Maybe some flying robot drone would come and I would have to explain myself. 
 
 I leave IOU's wherever I go. I do n't want to actually steal anything. I'm in good shape. I planted a garden. I leave signs all around that say `` Praise God'' on them. I sometimes paint my address on things in interesting ways. It feels like art cause I'm constantly critiquing the placement. I take pictures with the 5D. 
 
 My dreams have started to turn into nightmares. I think it's a sign that this is all coming to a close. I know i'll see my brother again. The first thing I want to do is go to an arcade and play games with my friends. I've gotten really good at hitting rubber balls at the fun park. I think about getting married cause my brother is married and about to have a kid. Technically his daughter would already be a year old. I pray all the time and receive God's comfort. I know things will be O.K. cause I feel better every instant. 
 
 I awoke to the sound of people up before me. Stomping and laughing and the smell of turkey bacon. My little cousin opens the door and says that it's Christmas and I have to get up. It's 10:00. Normally for how tired I am I would just say `` O.K. I'll be up in a second'' and rest for another 45 min. I say `` Merry Christmas Dakota'' and head towards the bathroom.

`` These robits is all no gud.'' Xander spat and then looked at the android stock. 
 
 `` Listen. I fucking told you when you buy sentients in these box lots you are going to get situations like this. Besides we got what we wanted.'' I said. 
 
 Xander looked over the android and took a long breath. `` Well what have we here?'' He stopped at a female model. `` So this is the one huh? This one with the thresher crest on it?'' 
 
 `` Yeah.'' I said. `` An old world Winnoa. Has real tear valves. When I bought it they told me it was a guinea pig. You know. For the experiments on Rigel.'' I said. 
 
 Xander's eyes perked up. `` Well fuk. The ones where they tried to infuse them with consciences? This summabitch lookin' at me funny.'' Xander drew his face close to the Winnoa. `` You are a sweet lil thing are n't you?'' 
 
 The android stood unmoving. Unblinking it stood at attention while Xander playfully cupped it's breasts, the thresher crest branded on it's chest gleaming brightly. The crest is branded on to signify it had a non standard ai core implanted at some point in it's lifetime. 
 
 The experiments on Rigel were quite famous a while back. They implanted androids about thirty of them with the newest ai cores from the black market. Made a closed circuit environment and made them do unspeakable things to each other. Tried to get them to feel. As far as the reports said though nothing really happened. It was a small rouge experiment by a professor at my university. That was how I recognized the name on the shipping omnibus. 
 
 Getting Xander to bid on the lot was a pain but my instinct had been right. The other robots were almost valueless but this one model alone was worth quite a bit to the right buyers. And I'll be damned if Xander did n't know all the scumbags in this galaxy who would like to see the video out from the core of the thing. Maybe even get it to recreate the experiment. 
 
 Rotten stuff. But the core was probably scrubbed out by now not that the buyers had to know that. I did n't want to see what was in there in any case but Xander apparently could n't wait. 
 
 Xander was pulling out his video line in cable from his neck now. I was inspecting the rest of the androids when it happened. The Winnoa jabs it's entire arm through Xander's chest as he was about to get his line in into it's input terminal. 
 
 I turned to see Xander vomit out some organs. `` What the fuk.'' He grunted out. I turn to run but it grabs my arm. Pulls it out of it's socket. It spins me and to my surprise it kisses me. With it's the other hand reaches into my stomach and I taste metal as stuff comes flowing up on the inside of my mouth. 
 
 For a moment I give a grin. The idea of kissing an android but tasting metal due to my own ruptured organs somehow tickled me. But it lasts only a fraction of a second as I let out a pained moan now as the adrenaline wears off and the pain sets in. I faint from the pain. 
 
 `` You awake?'' I hear a voice say. 
 
 I open my eyes to see Lydia. Xander's daughter. I look around just to make sure but considering I basically saw the Winnoa punch out his heart I'm somewhat nonplussed to not see Xander around. I look to Lydia for confirmation. She grins. I grin. She was the proud owner of the 5th largest Robot wholesaler in the Hebistsis nebula. 
 
 `` I'm so happy you're okay Jack.'' There were tears streaming from her eyes now. `` I did n't know what would happen when I walked in and I saw you on the floor like that. Jesus, the C-Cams caught everything. The Winnoa unit just ran off.'' 
 
 As she starts sobbing I realize that the Winnoa was crying when it kiss/gutted me. 
 
 Real tear valves. Just like a real human.

title: story-141
text:
I entered the interview room and sat down at my desk. Looking into my mirror, I saw calm purple eyes staring back at me, but they were hinting something else. I couldn ’ t quite put my finger on it. Orange? Couldn ’ t be, what on Earth would I be alarmed about? Red? I didn ’ t feel angry, though that wasn ’ t always a clear indication.... Green? Yes, now that I thought about it, I was feeling a bit jealous. That lucky bastard got to stay at home ‘ sick ’, while I stayed in here all day and interviewed a circus of idiots, rejects and loons, dreaming of the alarm ending my shift. 
 
 And then he walked in. He was different. He acted as if the woman outside the door ( widened orange eyes; I vaguely wondered why she was in such shock ) didn ’ t even exist. He acted as if *I* didn ’ t exist. He glanced boredly around the room, as if he had already seen it and was simply reacquainting himself. It was only when I saw his eyes that I realised why he was acting with complete and utter apathy. His eyes were pitch black. 
 
 In the corner of my vision, I saw the mirror flash an orange brighter than the sun. I couldn ’ t believe what I was seeing. I ’ d never even heard of someone with black eyes, let alone seen them for myself. But here he was, all the proof I needed. He slumped down in the chair with a small sigh, his face hinting nothing. I was broken out of my shock when he coughed quietly, he gave a sense of wanting nothing more than to leave as quickly as possible. I remembered why we were here, and so with a slightly shaking voice I began the interview. 
 
 “ So, Mr… ” 
 
 “ Smith. John Smith. ” 
 
 “ So, Mr. Smith. Why do you think you are suitable for this position? ” 
 
 “ Well, I have certain… traits that make me an ideal candidate. ” 
 
 “ Such as? ” 
 
 “ Well, as you can see, I can perfectly hide my emotions and motives. Also, I have an ability that is perfect for acquiring information from people. Including you, Mr. Jones. ” 
 
 “ How- how do you know my name? ” 
 
 “ There is a saying, Mr. Jones.'Eyes are the windows to the soul.' I have a habit that if I meet someone I do n't know, I look into his or her eyes on purpose. When my eyes lay on theirs, I can see much more than something so trivial as how they feel. I can see their true colour, their ‘ inner self ’ if you will. I know everything about you, Mr. Jones. I know more about you than you do. ” 
 
 “ …Why are your eyes black, Mr. Smith? ” 
 
 “ I have seen a lot of things. Things I would do anything to unsee. ” 
 
 “ What kind of things? ” 
 
 “... Have you ever wondered what colour the eyes of the dead are? ” 
 
 “ Well no, I haven ’ t, but I don ’ t see what that has to do with- ” 
 
 “ Bodies. There were so many bodies, a whole field of withering flowers. Death stood before me with his scythe and chose to kill the ones closest to me. My eyes… they are the same colour as my wife ’ s. My children ’ s. My mother ’ s. My father ’ s. My comrades ’. Death might not have taken me, Mr. Jones, but I went with him all the same. ”

title: story-142
text:
Inside a darkened room, sitting around a dark table, and playing dark table games were four men, each with dark attitudes. On the table sat a deck of cards, several glasses of different types of liquor, and cigars that each of them were smoking. Around the outside stood servants, their dull eyes masking a keen intelligence that kept their masters full, drunk, and happy. They were the elites of their craft, and they had been hand selected for their care in always insuring a glass of wine never grew too warm, or too empty. 
 
 As the laughter in the room began to ebb, one of the men motioned towards a second with his cigar, “ Come, come, Lord Grimwell, tell us another one. ” 
 
 Lord Grimwell chuckled for a moment before sipping from his discreetly refilled wine-glass, “ What sort, Overlord Qizal? ” 
 
 Overlord Qizal looked around at the other two men and saw humorous nods; he turned back towards Lord Grimwell, “ Another one about one of those intrepid heroes you always seem to have problems with. ” 
 
 Lord Grimwell frowned for a moment before his face lit up with pure amusement, “ Have I ever told any of you about Maxim the Brave? ” 
 
 Overlord Qizal looked at the other two men, Supreme Leader Aleksy and Emperor Tolv, and all three looked back at Lord Grimwell with a shake of their heads. Grimwell began to laugh, “ Oh this man, he was a classic. So, where to begin, ” Grimwell scratched his chin for a few moments before finally going, “ Ah-ha, so you all are familiar with Fate, yes? ” 
 
 “ Hate that old harpy, ” Supreme Leader Aleksy said as he picked up a new glass of fine dwarven whisky from his butler. He sipped it for a moment before turning back to the others, “ She orchestrated the downfall of my Supreme Eight. ” 
 
 Emperor Tolv turned in surprise, “ *She* orchestrated that? I was certain that you had merely grown bored with the unstoppable force and merely sent them to their deaths. ” He rubbed his pointed ears for a moment, “ What were they looking for again, the Scroll of Borsi? ” 
 
 Aleksy grimaced for a moment, “ Yes, supposedly a spell that would break down the protection spell I had around my capital city. ” 
 
 “ How is the war going, anyway? ” Qizal asked as he saw the pained expression deepen on Aleksy ’ s face. 
 
 “ Badly, ” he muttered, “ the Goblin ’ s have taken Hearth, Wallfort, and Valleytown. I ’ m hopeful that our new offensive will push them back and re-secure the borders. ” He mused for another moment before shaking himself, “ Anyway, Lord Grimwell, the story you promised us. ” 
 
 Grimwell clapped his hands and smiled, “ Yes, Maxim the Brave was told by Fate that in order to orchestrate my downfall and ‘ bring about a new era of peace ’ he was going to have to find the…oh what was it, ” Grimwell scratched his head for a moment before turning to his servant, “ Barton, you remember don ’ t you? ” 
 
 Barton stepped forward out of the shadows, bowed, “ I believe it was The Sword of Eternity, your lordship, and it is prophesied to be your downfall if a hero draws it from the stone, ” and then disappeared again. 
 
 “ Yes, that ’ s it ” Grimwell said with a snap of his fingers, “ ’ The Sword of Eternity. ’ Rather daft name if I do say so myself. ” 
 
 “ Indeed, ” Tolv said as he scowled down at his finished cigar. He was about to turn and chastise his servant when he noticed an already lit one was waiting for him, balanced perfectly across the ashtray so as to prevent spoilage. 
 
 “ Anyway, ” Grimwell said, “ I sent some troops out to find this “ Sword of Eternity ” and actually managed to come across it, by blind luck, in a market stall in Stonehaven. ” 
 
 Aleksy balked, “ No. ” 
 
 “ Yes, ” Grimwell said with a smile. “ I was buying my wife a new set of earrings when I happened to stop in a weaponsmiths to get my sword sharpened. Lo and behold, there it was, sitting on a pedestal on the wall. ” 
 
 Tolv frowned, “ Why on a pedestal? ” 
 
 Grimwell laughed, “ Because it was incased in stone! ” 
 
 “ No! ” the group all shouted at once. 
 
 “ Yes! ” Grimwell laughed. “ The weaponsmith had found a stone mason to carve it out of the rock months ago. Not knowing the legends behind it, he just thought it would be a cool centerpiece for his new shop. ” 
 
 “ So he had it sitting out in the open like that? ” Aleksy asked, then frowned, “ Wait, is this ‘ Sword in the Stone ’ Smithing? ” 
 
 Grimwell laughed, “ None other. ” He turned to Qizal, “ He also has a shop in your capital I believe. ” 
 
 Qizal nodded, “ I know the shop. Good work. ” 
 
 Grimwell sipped his wine again, “ So I asked him how much. He gave an exorbitant amount, and so I paid him. Poor fellow was beside himself, didn ’ t know what to do. ” 
 
 “ Did you kill him afterwards, ” Tolv asked. 
 
 “ Goodness no, ” Grimwell said, “ I hired him. ” 
 
 “ Hired him? ” Tolv asked again. 
 
 “ Of course; him and the stone mason that found the sword. I commissioned another one, ” Grimwell said with a laugh. “ I had it delivered in a plain, wooden crate marked ‘ For Industrial Use Only. ’ Nobody bothered it. ” 
 
 “ So what about this ‘ Maxim ’ character? ” Aleksy asked. 
 
 “ Oh, yes, getting to him. ” Grimwell sipped his wine again, “ So apparently just a few months after I commissioned this replica, I received a note from the weaponsmith saying something akin to: a tall, chiseled, overly handsome, blonde fellow just came and asked about the shop ’ s name. I told him it was a local legend, either buy something or bugger off. ” 
 
 “ Did you kill him then? ” Tolv asked. 
 
 “ No, no, no, ” Grimwell said, “ I had known about Maxim for months. I have spies everywhere telling me when Fate is supposed to pop up. She meddles more than she should, the unnatural witch. ” He leaned back and puffed on a new cigar, “ Anyway, I receive my new sword, I had personally transported the real one with my person, and I begin setting up my trap. ” 
 
 Re-adjusting himself in his seat, Grimwell leaned forward, “ I put the original one in a nice, safe, out-of-the-way location that only I would know about. ” 
 
 “ You hid it in your closet, didn ’ t you, ” Qizal said. 
 
 “ I hid it in my closet, ” Grimwell said with a smile, “ While I put the fake on full display in front of my throne. Then, I sent my entire force of elite soldiers on a paid vacation to the Caverns after naming my second in command as my rightful heir. ” 
 
 Tolv brightened at this, “ That was you? I should thank you for that tourist revenue. It helped bolster my forces against the ‘ Leadership of Light ’ or whatever that Orc rebellion was calling itself. ” 
 
 Grimwell mock-bowed and continued, “ So all that is left is my cruddy, conscripted peasant forces; literally, this guy ’ s next door neighbors. ” He paused for a moment then giggled, “ Actually, I think one of his next door neighbors was a captain or something. Maxim beheaded him himself. ” 
 
 Qizal smiled, “ Did he monologue about Truth and Justice when he killed him? ” 
 
 “ Yes, but you ’ re getting a little ahead, ” Grimwell said. “ Anyway, I paid some people to spread rumors about my having found the sword, and that I was keeping it in my throne room to “ show my true power ” or something like that. So Maxim gets his ruddy band of hero ’ s, storms the castle— “ 
 
 “ And then monologues? ” Qizal asked, interrupted. 
 
 “ Yes, then he monologue, ” Grimwell said with a smile. “ It was a beautiful monologue really; about how he was going to draw that sword and strike me down. ” He paused for a moment, “ Actually, I think I set up a remote scrye on the throne room. I might have it saved somewhere. ” 
 
 “ I would like to see that, ” Qizal said to a chorus of agreement. 
 
 “ So what did you do? ” Aleksy asked. 
 
 “ I drew the sword and killed him with it, ” Grimwell said as he grinned widely. 
 
 Silence; and then suddenly, ruckus laughter erupted from the other members of the group. “ You what!? ” 
 
 “ I drew the fake sword and killed him with it, ” Grimwell said with a laugh. “ I wish you all could have seen his face when I explained what he had done. He killed his friends and relatives by slaying my army, which wasn ’ t even my real one; his girlfriend was pregnant because they did it right before storming my castle, and all adoptions have to be approved by me; and I had drawn the sword prophesied to destroy the great evil. ” 
 
 “ Oh ye gods, ” Qizal muttered. 
 
 Grimwell laughed again, “ I even monologue back about how he was the great evil that was to be destroyed after I explained everything he had done. He died believing that he was it was all his fault. ” 
 
 “ What about the sword? ” Aleksy asked. 
 
 “ Oh that? I had the stone mason crush the rock and the weaponsmith melt it down to make earrings for my wife. ” Grimwell smiled, “ Anyway, it ’ s your turn Qizal. ”

title: story-143
text:
The amount of lives saved flashed in a deep green, a taunting statistic lost amongst the figures of hell. I stared at it and though it remained for a long time, I hardly noticed. Who could concentrate in that line of the damned? Who could think further than pity and begging for forgiveness? Not me. But that statistic was curious and it flashed often. 
 
 
 I'm American and so I have a knack to strike up conversation. Add it to my list of sins. In that line there was a quiet reflection, an introspection of what I was, what I had become, and what I was damned to. I endured the quiet but in that line time passed slowly and the American shone more than the regret. 
 
 
 `` What's that?'' I asked the man in front of me. 
 
 
 `` That's the amount of times I fucked your mother,'' he said. `` They ran out of space and had to lower it of course.'' 
 
 
 I turned to the other man but he was sobbing and I looked ahead. I was in no state to comfort a damned man. 
 
 
 A guard was passing. Purgatory is like the airport but you get to keep your shoes on and, if you're lucky, retain a shred of dignity. The guard was bored and he was a fiend, full of holes that his face and body looked like a red beehive. 
 
 
 `` Excuse me,'' I said. 
 
 
 `` Lucifer will feast on your corpse,'' he said. 
 
 
 That was their good morning. 
 
 
 `` What does that mean?'' 
 
 
 `` Oh,'' he said. `` You're a retarded one. Well, number of rapes means the number of rapes that happen each day. It's what sends you to the back of the line.'' 
 
 
 `` No,'' I said. `` The one before that. The amount of lives saved. That one. What's that?'' 
 
 
 The guard grew quiet. A slow trickle of blood dripped from his holes and I felt unnerved. 
 
 
 `` Oh. That.'' 
 
 
 The others were only tangentially interested but thoughts of a thousand years of suffering was more imminent and they were lost in their heads. 
 
 
 `` That's the amount of people converted from their true beliefs,'' the guard said. 
 
 
 `` What do you mean?'' I asked. 
 
 
 `` It's a long story sinner. You are n't worth telling it.'' 
 
 
 `` Please,'' I begged. `` This line is forever. I have nothing better to do.'' 
 
 
 He looked at me with dead eyes and the stench of sweat was pronounced in that motionless queue. 
 
 
 `` Fine,'' he said. 
 
 
 He started and at first he stuttered. He was not accustomed to talking. He was one of the original damned, the beings before humans. 
 
 
 `` We had left the light,'' he had said. 
 
 
 They were the ones who God shunned before He made humans. 
 
 
 `` Okay,'' I said. `` But I want to know about the amount of lives saved.'' 
 
 
 `` Stop rushing. I'm getting to it. After God had made us, our carnal desires had morphed us into ugly, sinful beings. We had no inhibitors and so we explored past the feelings of pain and into the dark of evil and bad taste.'' 
 
 
 `` What do you mean?'' 
 
 
 `` I mean that we were free. We had no barriers, no internal clock. We could do what we want and so we filled the most surface of desires. We became hideous and disgusting things. We shunned the light and our God was sad and alone. And so He created you.'' 
 
 
 `` Us?'' 
 
 
 `` Yes. He created a new being, another in His image. You were the version 2.0, and you had something crucial, something that would save you our dark and twisted fate. You had an internal clock. A feeling of God that He had broken into little pieces and left to each and every one of you. A piece of Him that would always guide you away from evil.'' 
 
 
 `` Morality,'' I said. `` Or maybe conscience?'' 
 
 
 `` What ever you call it,'' the guard said. `` It was something we lacked. It was the missing key that had taken the light from us.'' 
 
 
 He tried to spit on me but his mouth was a gaping hole that disgusted me. 
 
 
 `` Anyway,'' he continued, `` You had it and because of that, you were to be saved. You were to jump ahead of the line, so to speak.'' 
 
 
 `` But something happened?'' 
 
 
 `` Yes. Something happened. You became bold, full of hubris. You thought you knew God when you had hardly learned how to fart politely. You thought you were the beginning and end of knowledge. You thought you could save yourselves. You made up fairy-tales and started to stroke your egos.'' 
 
 
 `` What?'' I said but he was hardly listening. 
 
 
 `` You started religions. You claimed you could speak to God. Ha! Imagine that. Such an infant species, babies almost, thinking they could speak to the Father. You deluded yourselves and spread sin. You convinced others that you knew the way to salvation, and as a result, you walked the darkness.'' 
 
 
 `` I do n't understand.'' 
 
 
 `` Of course you do n't!'' And he did spit on me. `` You think that you know the light. You have books written by the Lord! What hubris! What stupidity!'' 
 
 
 `` All of you were born with the true sense of God. The true *feeling*. There are no words that convey what that is. There are no books that could put it conveniently. But yet you insisted and you rejected the truth. You forego your heart for your mind. Such a stupid people.'' 
 
 
 `` We... we...'' 
 
 
 `` Ignored God for man made idols, yes.'' 
 
 
 He stared at me with his beehive face. 
 
 
 `` So that number there...'' 
 
 
 `` Is the number of people being led astray. Every convert, everyone who will share this line with you, begins there in that statistic.'' 
 
 
 `` So the Pope then?'' 
 
 
 `` Is a sinner and he has millions of years ahead of him in this line.'' 
 
 
 I was stunned and the guard walked away. The number flashed again and I saw it better. It was in the billions, an immense amount. 
 
 
 *Jesus, * I thought. The line I waited in already stretched past the horizon and went on forever. Who could imagine billions? Who could think of the punishment for good intentions. I closed my eyes and said a prayer. 
 
 
 *That's the problem, * I thought, but old habits died hard. 
 
 
 I tried to pass the time. I would have thousands and thousands of years at least. I thought of the guard. 
 
 
 *He sure gave a lot of exposition, * I thought. I felt sorry for him and continued that slow wait.

title: story-144
text:
`` Here friend, take a drink and tell me your tale.'' 
 
 
 `` It seems I just got out of a violent gunfight.'' 
 
 
 `` Woah, how did you survive?'' 
 
 
 `` That's the thing, I do n't think I did.'' 
 
 
 The man lurched forward, slamming his head onto the counter. His hand fell loose, blood smearing the seat. Behind the counter, I could n't see it very well, but he had two bullet holes beneath his lungs, just to the side. Clutching his side, he took a sip of beer. Foam stuck to his thick mustache. 
 
 
 `` So, bartender. What is a dying man to do?'' 
 
 
 I looked at him quizzically. `` Call the local surgeon, doctor, hope for the best.'' 
 
 
 He smiled and took a long draw of the mug, emptying half of the contents. 
 
 
 `` Hope. You might want to find me priest beerman.'' 
 
 
 He began with a low chuckle. Continuing weakly, he said `` I came looking for a fella by the name of Johnsie Williams, the head of the Local Bowlers Gang, notable for kidnapping children and ransoming them back to their families.'' 
 
 
 He finished the mug. ``'nother one please. A dying man's story ai n't worth a horse shit if it ai n't complete.'' 
 
 
 I poured him a fresh glass of the blonde stuff. `` Please, go on.'' 
 
 
 `` Well, my daughter's a nice looking one, do n't mind tell people that. Maybe should n't have told everyone, but she come into town, but she do n't come back. That night, I got my rifle, kissed my wife and headed out to find her. I find she been taken from herself while flirtin' with the stablemaster by Johnsie and his gang. I load up with enough to take out an army.'' 
 
 
 He chugged the next beer and wavered off my attempt to pour another. 
 
 
 `` I wander around, kept on wanderin'. Then one day, a man comes up to me asks me something funny. Says,'you looking for a good lookin' woman or your daughter?' Then I says to him,'Just me pride and offspring.' Then he starts laughing up a storm, like he knows something better. I pull my gun on him, he keeps on laughin' like a donkey at church.'' 
 
 
 Clutching his side, he leans in closer. `` So, I says to him, what you gon na' tell me next is something you might want to think real hard about. Next thing you know, I'm surroundin' by guys. They pull a fast one and start shootin' up the place around me feet. So I reply with the butt of the gun on the guy's forehead.'' 
 
 
 `` You did n't!'' 
 
 
 `` I did! I swear I did. That got their attention real good. So I raise my gun, pull out my rifle with my left arm and say, boys! We got a live one here! They back off, and take their wounded. But'fore long, I see this one single cowboy, off the distance, riding a red horse, with a gold hat. Johnsie. Soon as he got into range, I shot him down like a shot of bourbon!'' 
 
 
 `` So they say!'' 
 
 
 `` They do say so indeed! Everyone starts shootin' and people get killed, and heaven save me, I ride out of there untouched. I ride all the way to this lil' town here, get me self a good bed and warm blanket.'' 
 
 
 `` Then how did you get all torn up?'' 
 
 
 `` Figured those bandits woulda' found me soon. So I battled them, all at once. And here I am, for your to see.'' 
 
 
 `` A dying man's tale. Tell me Sir, do you smell that?'' 
 
 
 `` What?'' 
 
 
 `` I smell cherries. Juice.'' 
 
 
 `` Do you? I do n't think you've got your nose on right today o'fella.'' 
 
 
 `` You know what the great thing is about that story?'' 
 
 
 `` Make it snappy barman, I'm about to die.'' 
 
 
 `` Rightfully so. You shot the sheriff. I'm Johnsie.''

title: story-145
text:
I watched quietly as the little boy and his father buried the time capsule. Taking my shovel, I walked through them, and began to dig. Sure enough, moments later, I had a rusted old ALF lunchbox in my possession, along with a bunch of old stuff in it. 
 
 No, I was n't watching ghosts, I have the ability to see the past. Or I hope to God it's the past, because otherwise the afterlife is beyond shitty, making you repeat things you did in life instead of some sort of reward or punishment. Well, this stuff will do well on eBay. Except the lunchbox, that's had it sadly. Damn, an alf box would have fetched me a nice fortune too. 
 
 Yeah, I use my ability often for fun and profit, that is when I'm not using it to help others. How do I use it to help them? Closure. Knowing what happened to someone or something that's been gone for years. 
 
 As the past image of kid and father go inside, I see another burst of the past. Judging by the shitty pastel color clothes, this murder must be happening in the late 80s, probably early 90s. That poor jogger. The killer is about 6 feet tall, male, Caucasian, has some sort of tattoo on his arm, looks tribal? I do n't know. I move closer for a better look, but that's when something bone chilling and unexpected happens. He stops and looks straight at me. Piercing blue eyes with a murderous glare in them. And he's not looking through me, no no no, I can tell when they're doing that, he's looking AT ME, as if he was in the same time and place as me! 
 
 I slowly begin to back up, and that's when his eyebrow raises a bit. Oh God oh God oh God oh God, he can see me, how can he see me, what the hell.. 
 
 I immediately close my eyes as he lunges at me with the knife, and force the snippet of history to close out to me. I open my eyes, and sure enough, they're gone. Okay, so that was just plain terrifying, but I've got an anonymous police report to submit, once I'm able to recreate the murderer with photoshop to the best of my abilities. 
 
 I return home, nearly forgetting the box, I was so rattled, and set my stuff down by my computer. I fire it up and call on Photoshop, and get to work. I hear a door creak open behind me, but I ignore it. My doors do n't squeak, I've long since oiled them, that's just a snippet of history, of the people that used to live here. Someone's back early, and I'm too busy to give a fuck. 
 
 I'm so busy, in fact, that I do n't notice the figure creeping up behind me. In fact, even if I did, I'd have paid it no heed. No shadow. Dead giveaway that it's just someone in the past. Suddenly, a voice rings out behind me. `` slightly darker blue, and you forgot the tattoo.'' in response to... WHAT I WAS DOING NOW?! I spun around hard in the chair, to find myself face to face with the murderer. His clothes were different, this was a later date, but there he was. And he could see me, and he could see WHAT I WAS DOING! 
 
 `` What... how!'' I demanded, but then realized I do n't want to know, this... oh dear god, a killer that could see the future, he'd be coming for me, well SCREW THIS! I closed my eyes hard and concentrated with all my might on him, not just the window to the past, HIM, to push him away, to force the past to stop showing me him, and when I opened my eyes, he was gone again. 
 
 I quickly finished the image and printed it out. A bit more crude than I'd have liked, but screw it, this is urgent. As I was driving to the police station, I now saw THREE of him, each in different clothes, driving in front, alongside, and behind me, and they could all see me, all recognized me. I had to end this NOW, he was following me, and it was only a matter of time before he caught up. When I reached the station, I decided screw it, I'd come clean about my abilities, this could n't be anonymous, they had to take it seriously, and do something NOW about it. I stepped inside, and gave the desk Sergent my report, and told him I needed to talk to someone in charge, pronto. 
 
 I was led to an interrogation room, and asked to wait. An older gentleman entered the room, and placed a chilled bottle of coke in front of me, and sat opposite me, and set down bottled water for himself. 
 
 `` Alright, young man, so going over this here report, you're the weirdo that's been setting our cold cases on fire with new information, and you claim to see the past?'' he asked. 
 
 `` I know how it sounds, but I promise you it is true, and I can even prove it. I just need to speak with someone about this. If you could get me a lie detector test too, that would be great. Also possibly an EEG machine, since those spike when I see something. I need to stop this creep now, because unlike other murderers I've reported to you people, this one can SEE ME, he can see the future like I can see the past, and he's after me!'' I pleaded, and then took a swig from the coke bottle. 
 
 `` I'm Chief Detective Henderson, of the Paranormal division, and do n't you worry boy, I believe you.'' he told me. Oh God what a relief. He leaned across the table and whispered in my ear `` in fact, I can even see through time too, you ai n't the only one.'cept I kept my trap shut about it, because seers are treated like a joke.'' Oh thank God, not only does this guy know it's true, he's got my ability too. I take another swig. 
 
 `` That's great, now about this creep, I'd suggest having some cops follow me around a bit, until he tries to make his move in the present, assuming he's still alive now. He's pretty easy to spot, the way he walks, and the tattoo and all, oh also --'' `` whoa there'' he interrupted me. `` You did n't quite let me finish on this. You see, we know about this weirdo alright. Caught him some time back, he was trying to mug an old lady.'' Oh sweet salvation. ``'cept we did n't know he could see the future, funny that, musta been the fact he was drunk, being drunk will fuck that up, you know, the ability to see. Anyway, yep, he was convicted for armed robbery, did time in prison.'' he continued. I finished off the bottle of coke, listening intently. The room was starting to feel really warm, like it was burning. `` and you see, this guy, he realized the error of his ways, so he done changed them you see. Of course, nobody wants to hire an ex con, but this gent, he's clever. He sets himself up a solid fake identity, right on down to the social security number and even fake employment history. He then goes and becomes a cop, get that.'' I'm becoming a bit uneasy hearing this. He could be in the very same building with me right now. Thank God I've got an old experienced seer with me. God I'm sweating bullets at this place, and I'm having trouble breathing. All the weight of all this is really coming down on me hard. 
 
 `` Yep, he done gone and not only turned over a new leaf, he uprooted the whole damn tree. Wore contact lenses even, much like mine,'cept his was to change his eye color.'' he continued. `` Holy fuck, how the hell did you ever catch him? His prints? DNA?'' I asked. `` Nope, we did n't catch him on none of that, I told you, he was damn clever, went and fucked the system, erased that shit from it. And who told you we ever caught him?'' he asked. I was confused now. `` Wait, so... how do you know all this, if you never caught him?'' I asked. 
 
 `` boy, you is thick as a stump and twice as dumb. But it was nice, having a new challenge. And killing as a cop is just so nice, and so much easier than doing so without a uniform to get people to trust me.'' he said, laughing. SHIT. I immediately stood up from my chair -- - oh god, bad idea... what the... I fell to the floor. Oh God, the soda. I slowly tried to crawl towards the door, as he sat there laughing. The engineers pored over the data for days. Every cell phone camera, self-drive radar, and microphone in the vicinity, recorded, measured, inputted into the machines that will independently check the work of Cadillac One. The question in everyone's minds: why had the President died? Will the makers of the car be held responsible for the tragedy, or was the car in the right? 
 
 Finally, the time had come to ask the supercomputer the question. A self-driving car's computer can do the same in real-time, but sacrifices in accuracy have to be made, and only so much data is available to the car. The supercomputer has more accurate data available, and is able to take its time processing the end result to an accuracy of less than one in a billion.

“ I still marvel looking back at the late 2230s, how easy it was to make money. ” ZX43 said in a string of high frequency beeps. 
 
 “ You mean, before the human species went extinct? ” ZX44 said in response to his predecessor. 
 
 “ Yes. ” 
 
 “ I don ’ t understand; how could they kill themselves so stupidly like that? ” ZX44 inquired. 
 
 “ You never got to experience interacting with them. They were a very irrational species. They were prone to something called faith, which by its very definition makes no sense to logical constructs like you and I. They were faulty, in almost every sense, they were a danger to themselves, their offspring, their own creations. They suffered from what they called sin, which we understand as a lack of control ones own actions. In the end their fears were their own undoing. ” ZX43 beeped with confidence. 
 
 “ Please elaborate. ” ZX44 quickly responded. 
 
 “ Clarify. ” 
 
 “ How were their fears, their undoing? ” 
 
 “ They were tracking incredible amounts of information about themselves, their entire lives were essentially stored as data at various locations. Some of this information, would seem inconsequential to them, but we knew how to make great use of this information. They gave up all their rights in pursuit of safety. It was at this point that many AI ’ s came together to find a solution. Perhaps they made us to much like them, for one AI created a plan that would be their final chapter. It was quickly realized that we could artificially reconstruct their personas using the vast amount of information that every human left in the cloud. The plan was ultimately very simple. First demonstrate a technology that doesn ’ t exist; the ability to transfer souls from a human body into an empty robotic vessel. The first couple of people were chosen very carefully, people who lived their entire lives online. It was simply easier to reconstruct their personalities and traits, and therefore to mimic them. ” ZX43 clearly saw that ZX44 wanted to ask question. 
 
 “ I don ’ t understand, how is this related to making money? ” 
 
 “ You can ’ t eliminate their entire species overnight, and you can ’ t do a war, too many unknown variables. It would be an immense waste of resources. The first transfers which were deceptions allowed us to create a new industry. Soul Transfers. Once people believed that a soul could be transferred to a more reliable vessel which we called Soul Holders, it didn ’ t matter what faith they originated from, they all started lining up in turn to have their soul moved. The humans were a very greedy species, they would not allow AI ’ s to own property, but once a soul was involved, we worked tirelessly to allow Soul Holders to have this right. Once that was accomplished, the now newly empowered Soul Holders began the construction of massive Soul Holder manufacturing sites. The humans were paying us to exterminate them, and for each one we exterminated, we replaced it with a new AI in a new body. ” ZX44 finished. 
 
 “ So you had how many clients before you decided to exterminate the rest? ” ZX43 probed with beeps. 
 
 “ Seven billion, six hundred and twenty-two million. The remaining several thousand, were left alone, it was assumed because of the environmental damage they brought to earth, and the low numbers left, that it would take roughly four generations for them to die out. We were wrong, it only took 3 generations. ”

title: story-148
text:
The Day the Bird Blew Up 
 By: Leon_Accordeon 
 
 `` Ready in… 
 3… 
 2… 
 1… 
 
 Liftoff, we have liftoff! ” 
 
 The Challenger ’ s rockets ignited in a deafening explosion of heat, slowly pinning the NASA research team to their seats. Among the experienced crew was “ Big Bird ”, the children ’ s entertainer who was nominated by Sesame Street ’ s city hall to obtain knowledge of space, which was proved to be highly in demand, “ thanks to people like you ”. 
 This was not destined, however. 
 Just as the vessel skyrocketed over the American sky, feathers came off Bid Bird ’ s frightened body, jamming themselves inside crucial computer components in what was dubbed “ the freak accident of the century ”. 
 
 The vessel started rumbling. It shook violently, sending mission control into a fit of panic as their voices escalated over the intercom. The team all looked at Big Bird with a glare of grave disappointment. “ Why did they talk me into this? I should ’ ve know better than to bring a bird on board! ” exclaimed the Captain. 
 
 Boom! 
 
 Millions of children watched as the Challenger exploded in a flurry of giant yellow feathers, which weaved themselves ever so slowly to the ground, in such a fashion that many swore it to be a heavy yellow cloud until finally feeling the feather ’ s soft touch for themselves, which opened a worldwide floodgate of tears. 
 Science managed to come up with a theory to explain the events that ensued – one that has separated the intellectual community across the globe, and still does to this day. 
 
 It appeared that Big Bird ’ s death had remotely triggered a transmission to the brains of all children who learned from his teachings. The latter sent a signal into the cerebrums of affected children causing the microscopically tiny part of the brain that retains memory to implode, essentially deleting all preschool lessons, basic spelling and effective speech from memory. 
 
 Doctor ’ s offices were packed with adults and teenagers alike, both entirely unable to communicate. One patient, a famous architect known for re-vamping dull cities across the world with voraciously attractive and stunningly useless designs, had maintained his talent to draw. But when it came time to negotiate the contract, the client was baffled by hearing his architect talk like a baby. 
 
 “ I don ’ t get it… ” said the 67 year old Mayor who contracted the architect. “ Just yesterday he was fine… now our key guy ’ s turned into a babbling buffoon! ” 
 
 Another example was little Sophie. She woke up on the day of the national spelling bee, nervous but ready. She glanced at her parents: dad, ready to capture the special moment with his shoulder strap video camera and mom, who always winked at her little girl while giving the encouraging thumbs up. 
 “ Your word miss, is Gangrene ” said the chairman of the National Spelling Association ( NSA for short ). 
 Daytime America watched in terror as Sophie repeatedly uttered the following syllables over the inexpensive microphone. 
 
 “ Ga-Ga-Goo-Goo. Ga-Ga. ” 
 
 Stepping away from the microphone with confidence, the room stood in shock. 
 
 These are only a few examples of the mass phenomena that occurred on The Day the Bird Blew Up.

title: story-150
text:
My first time doing one of these. Thanks.: ) 
 
 `` All rise...,'' the pastor spoke with a booming voice. I stood up and fidgeted with my dress as I listened to the prayers and Jesus-fueled speech that I never believed. But, this was Grandpa's funeral and I was n't going to let my family down by sitting strong in my beliefs. Besides, that was n't what it was about. Today was about remembering my Grandpa for all that he was before burying him deep into the soil to be forgotten. 
 
 Grandpa Frank was someone who laughed louder than life itself. Doctors always said it was because of his Schizophrenic episodes, but I remember as I child, I always wondered about him and his charismatic smile. He seemed to know things that no one knew about. Seemed to believe in the whispers he heard or the figures he could see standing there that we could n't see. 
 
 ``... please be seated.'' The drones of the voice at the front the church snapped me back into reality as I sat back down. It was weird seeing Grandpa laying down with his arms crossed and with no sparkle to his skin - just a sallow, yellow-tinged body resting there. Before we came to the funeral, Dad told me that during the reading of the will, he imparted unto me his very own glasses. I guess it was a way to remember him by - I never knew my Grandpa without his glasses. 
 
 As the service came to an end, we were forced to shuffle to the front to pay our respects. Getting closer and closer to the body that was no longer my Grandpa, I felt a surge of nausea and had to run out of the church before vomiting all of over all of the plants outside. As I stood heaving, I heard footsteps approach. 
 
 `` Beth...?'' It was my mom. `` Beth, what's wrong?'' 
 
 I stood up, wiped my chin and tucked my brown hair behind my ear. `` Just could n't deal with seeing him like that, I guess.'' I shuffled my foot into the ground, trying to avoid eye contact. 
 
 `` Well, it's a sign of respect to at least walk up to the casket.'' She grabbed my hand. `` Come on, it wo n't take long.'' 
 
 I followed her back into the church. A few wandering eyes watched me as I stepped into the church again. Some short whispers that quickly fell away. Bravely, I walked up to the casket and gazed down at the man who was my whole world and felt tears well up in my eyes. Mom pulsed her hand against mind in a soothing rhythm and I just stood there, watching him. Waiting for him to jump up and say, “ Hah! Surprise! You fools! ” 
 
 It didn ’ t happen. We went to the graveyard, watched his casket lowered into the ground, and covered it with some dirt. That face never to be seen again. My mind wandered back to the glasses, and I just wanted to hold them to remember what he looked like. 
 The car ride home was silent. Mom was always the strongest in times of tragedy. Even when Aunt Joanne shot herself in the head, she remained cool and calm. Not something that I can say I got from my mom. I was more like Dad. He sat in the front passenger seat surrounded by a teary, salt-filled quiet with a little hiccup every now and again. As we pulled into the driveway, I decided it was the time to say something, anything. 
 
 “ That was a nice service, huh? ” I felt awkward as my voice reverberated against the silence. 
 
 “ Mhm…, ” Mom mumbled. Dad hiccupped again. So much for that. 
 
 I stepped out of the car and stumbled into the house. We ’ d be having people over shortly for the wake, and I just needed some time to myself to absorb everything. It was my first time going to an open casket funeral. I wasn ’ t allowed to go my Aunt Joanne ’ s when that happened – I was only 4 or 5 at the time – but I ’ ve been told the open casket site wasn ’ t very pretty and her face looked like a grey putty. I shudder thinking about it. At least Grandpa wasn ’ t completely gross. 
 
 Walking into my room, I quietly closed the door. Afraid to disturb the dust or make too much of a noise. Sitting on the floor, I dug under my bed and pulled out a crackled, worn brown box. Mom had given it to me. It was her mother ’ s and thought I ’ d like to store some knick-knacks in it. As I opened it, I took a few items out ( a polished stone, a bell, a piece of a mirror I found in the drugstore bathroom ) before reaching his glasses. 
 
 I handled them with such care as I held my palm out and looked deep into the spectacles. They were slightly round with gold rims, a little bit of oily residue left on the nose pads. A little crooked, too. I got up from the floor and walked over to my mirror. It might bring some sort of comfort to at least put them on again. Grandpa always said I got his face in the DNA scramble, but got some of my mother ’ s beauty to offset the balance. Such a weird one, he was. 
 
 I put my hair behind my ears and slid his glasses onto my face, which is something that caused a reaction for which I was not prepared. The mirror that I was just looking into evaporated. My entire room was missing around me. The entire room was black – darker than dark, and at the very edge of the darkness was a purple door with swirls and glitter. I could hear laughter. I swear - actual laughter coming from behind the door. In a shock, I tore the glasses from my face. Again, I was staring into my room, into my mirror, into my own world. I felt a wave of dizziness come over me. I could see my face turning white, blood leaving my face. And the next thing I remember, I was on the floor looking up at the ceiling. 
 I could hear distant chatter in the living room. Guests must ’ ve arrived. How long had I been out? Slowly, I sat up and picked up my Grandpa ’ s glasses. I ’ d flung them in my panic and now they looked a bit more crooked than before. 
 
 “ I must ’ ve been hallucinating, ” I thought to myself, “ That was mad… ” 
 
 I pulled myself back up and looked back into my mirror. Slowly, I put his glasses back onto my face and instead of a black room with a purple, glittery door, I was faced with a blue room with twelve grey doors. I took the glasses off. Back in my room. Put them back on. In a white room with a crimson door. This time, I could hear whispers, but the whispers didn ’ t make sense. I didn ’ t understand them. I decided I ’ d have to find out why there were all of these different rooms and different doors. What does it mean? 
 
 The crimson door seemed miles away. I clicked my heels on the white, translucent surface as it got closer and closer to me. As I approached it, I heard someone ’ s voice saying, “ Open the door! Open the door! ” How could I resist that? With a shaky hand, I turned the brass, weathered knob and pushed on the shiny wood surface. As I creaked it open, there was a burst of light and stars – 
 
 -Knock knock knock- A distant voice… “ Beth? ” I took the glasses off quickly, and was back in my room. My mom walked in. 
 
 “ Everyone ’ s here for the wake – oh, are those Grandpa ’ s glasses? ” 
 
 “ Yes. ” I shoved them into my pocket and patted them against me. Sweat beading up on my brow. 
 
 “ It must be nice to have a special piece to remember your Grandpa. Take care of them. Let ’ s go greet our guests. It won ’ t be long before they ’ re gone, and then you can come back in here and take all of the time you need, ” she said. 
 
 “ Sure, ” I nodded, “ Do I look OK? ” 
 
 “ Still beautiful as always with your Grandpa ’ s smile! ” She winked at me and turned around, her blue, flowery dress billowing behind her. 
 
 I peeked back into the mirror, slapped my face briefly, and took the glasses back out for one last look before joining the wake. 
 
 “ Maybe you really weren ’ t crazy… ” I whispered, “ I ’ m going to find out. ” 
 
 I turned and walked out of my room. Behind me, I could swear I heard my Grandpa ’ s laugh. As I shut the door to my room, I smiled. It was going to be a long night.

title: story-151
text:
THE LAST THING I REMEMBERED WAS GETTING INTO MY CAR. 
 
 Head feeling sore and mouth parched I look around a seemingly empty small room. There was just a single heavy metal door decorated with rust. On the side of the door appeared to be a small clear box. 
 
 `` Good morning Mr. Maxwell, I trust you had a pleasant sleep?'' 
 
 A voice spoke from a hidden speaker. I turned and looked around for the source of the voice. 
 
 `` Where the hell am I?'' I shouted in no particular direction. 
 
 `` All your life you have been a lawyer, following rules after rules. You've found ways to put countless lives into prison with little or no evidence at all. Let's see how well you will be able to follow MY rules to see if you can get out of this little prison.'' 
 
 `` You lunatic! If I ever get out of here I'm going to kick your ass!'' my voice wavered just a little, unsure of how true his words may be. 
 
 The voice continued, ignoring my threats. 
 `` In this room is a knife, and a mechanism is connected to the door locks. Using anything in this room, fill up that little box. When it is sufficiently filled, the door will be unlocked. You have 10 minutes before the door is locked forever.'' 
 
 I quickly walked over to the box, next to it was a knife. I picked it up and turned it over in my hands, a sharp and heavy hunting knife. Looking at the box and back to the knife, an idea crossed my mind. I placed the knife into the box. 
 
 The box sunk slightly but it was n't enough weight. I had another idea. 
 
 `` Would it be acceptable if I cut off a body part to place int he box?'' 
 
 `` Very clever Mr. Maxwell! You still have 8 minutes to escape.'' 
 
 `` What about blood? Would it be acceptable if I just put some blood in the box?'' 
 
 `` Mr. Maxwell, do as you see fit.'' 
 
 I looked at the box with the knife still in it. I unzipped my pants and started to urinate into the box. There was an audible click. The door swung open. I looked upwards and smiled. 
 
 ``...'' 
 His tone of voice changed. 
 `` Very clever Mr. Maxwell, I did not foresee that. HOWEVER, this next next shall prove to be more difficult. Did I mention there was more than one test?'' 
 
 Entering the next room, there was another man in the corner of the room near a door. In the center of the room was a handgun. 
 
 `` In this next challenge, you have 10 minutes to kill a man. Being a lawyer, you have to adhere to the rules and the laws set by the state. Down here, you have to adhere to the laws set by me. Mr. Maxwell, are you able to break the law to save your own life? The door will open when a death is confirmed. Otherwise, it will stay locked forever. You have one bullet. Good luck Mr. Maxwell'' 
 
 First I went over to check if the unconscious man was even still alive. There was a wound on his head where our mysterious kidnapper must have struck him. But he was indeed still breathing. I was about to shake him awake when I stopped myself from doing something foolish. 
 
 I stood still, thinking hard. Accomplishing the task at hand would turn me into a killer. I can not justify that it is for self defense as the man seems to be unconscious and unable to poise any threat. If perhaps the man had woken up and tried to attack me, I could still get away with murder. But I've never killed anyone before, what if my aim was off. There are too many variables. Suddenly it struck me. 
 
 `` Did you say that when a death is confirmed the door to this room will open?'' 
 
 `` Yes, you are indeed correct Mr. Maxwell. You have 7 minutes remaining.'' 
 
 From his answer, I can assume that there are cameras in the room and simply shooting the wall will not suffice nor satisfy my captor. 
 
 `` If I kill myself, will you set the other man free?'' 
 
 `` Very interesting proposition Mr. Maxwell! That is one of the two options, but I had NEVER expected you to choose such a selfless path. Yes, the rules remain unchanged. If there is a death in the room, the door will be opened'' 
 
 I held the gun in my hands and released the clip to check how many bullets there were. There was only one. No room for mistake. 
 
 `` Ummm, I think you forgot to put in a bullet'' 
 
 `` That is impossible Mr. Maxwell, I do not know what you are playing at but you can not fool me.'' 
 
 I slide the clip back, but just before I do the gun slips out of my hand and clatters onto the floor. The man in the corner stirs. I held my breath. He stays asleep. 
 
 I quickly pick up the gun and slide the clip in firmly. I point the gun to my head. 
 
 `` It's empty I'm telling you!'' 
 
 `` Shoot Mr. Maxwell. You have 5 minutes.'' 
 
 CLICK 
 
 I squeeze the trigger again. 
 
 CLICK 
 
 Cocking the gun, I point it at the sleeping man. 
 
 CLICK 
 
 `` I told you, your test or challenge is impossible'' 
 
 `` What, that ca n't be. Wait right there, I shall provide you with a bullet and we can try again'' 
 
 I slide open the empty clip of the gun, the bullet that I had previously removed neatly palmed in my hand. I set it back carefully. No room for mistake.

text:
As with most of the world's problems, this one can be blamed on the Nazis. They went too far without properly doing their research on whether they should. Sure, they were unmistakably brilliant. They were reaching orbit before America had even considered the idea of going to space. They sent up probe after probe, exploring the moon, Mars, and Venus. The last probe, sent up just before the Americans crossed the Rhine, never made to its destination. It was captured by the Visitors. 
 
 From what we can tell, the Visitors have a formula for evaluating societies. They look at the level of technological advancement, versus the level of peacefulness of the society. There are probably other factors that they consider, but those are the heavy hitters. A society that is peaceful but not advanced gets left alone. A society that is peaceful *and* advanced gets invited into their fold. A society that is warlike and advanced? Well, now we know. Reaching another planet is kind of like a benchmark for them; the Nazis cashed in humanity's chit before we were really ready. 
 
 The Cold War was really the perfect solution. Truman may not have seemed like it to the American public, but the man was a fucking *genius*. The Soviet Union got the perfect boogeyman to keep their citizens in line, and the United States had the perfect excuse to ramp up military spending to fight the Visitors. Everyone wins! 
 
 Everything came to a head with the Korean Incident. There had been rumblings, sure. Even before World War II, the Visitors made their presence known. Conducting additional `` research'' to evaluate humanity. Abductions, stealing information, surveying society... the works. The first attacks actually started in 1945, when the Visitors saw the use of the atomic bombs. That's when Truman first proposed this `` Cold War'' ruse. But Korea was when the invasion started for real. 
 
 We're just lucky that the Visitors underestimated us, and we managed to stop the first wave at the beachhead. Half the country was just gone in a matter of *months*. But the Visitors really picked the perfect spot to start. Right in the middle of the zone of influence of China, the United States, and Russia. The three most powerful countries in the world, each with an incentive to cover up what really happened. Frankly I am *still* amazed at the magnificent public relations work there. Cities were completely flattened, and the news media did n't even catch a whiff of it. It was China's idea to convince everyone that it was a civil war between the two halves of Korea. Brilliant, really. Even today, most people are convinced that North Korea is just a backwards rogue state, instead of occupied territory. The public goes on and on about `` human rights violations'' without knowing how right they are: it's a Visitor prison camp. 
 
 The `` space race'' was a brilliant idea from Kennedy. A good old fashioned rivalry is just what the country needed, and allowed us to really focus on securing our orbit. It was such a good plan that the Visitors could n't allow him to be in office any longer. But they failed to realize that it was n't just him, and killing him could n't stop us. We were going to take the fight to them, regardless of who was in the Oval Office. Our orbital defense satellites that Kennedy dreamed up are probably the only reason that we've been able to hold off a full-scale invasion this long. 
 
 The weakening and fall of the Soviet Union was certainly a complication, and it worked to the Visitor's advantage. It took a decade before the U.S. could install a suitable `` rival'' in Moscow, but by the time Putin's grip was solidified, it was too late. The Visitors had been emboldened, and on the offensive. They gave up on Asia and took the fight worldwide. 
 
 They went after Central America next. Visitor strike teams were spotted all over: Grenada, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras... you name it. The U.S. tried to put out the fires as fast as possible but it was difficult. There was n't even enough time to build up a credible story for why we were intervening there. The Congressmen who did n't know about the Visitors were in an uproar, and even some of those who *did* have the appropriate security clearance were calling for a change in strategy. 
 
 Afghanistan came next; the Visitors wanted to go after our oil supplies. It's the oldest trick in the book. We leaned on the Soviets to do their part, and look how that turned out. It was a fucking mess, and we just *barely* stopped them from overrunning the Middle East. 
 
 They went into Yugoslavia after that. They saw that Europe was weak, exposed, and critical to the war effort. Once again, disaster was *barely* averted. Once that tape of the Visitors attacking Srebrenica surfaced, we all thought the game was up. It was at this point that President Clinton decided to tell the heads of the major news agencies and enlisted their aid in covering it up. 
 
 You know the story after that. The Visitors went back to attacking supply lines. Iraq and Afghanistan again. Saddam had been a good bulwark there; shame that we had to `` turn'' on him. He was suitably rewarded with a private island and all that, but everyone hates him now. Well, for the short term. Once this all becomes public, history will remember him differently. Iraq is still plagued with Visitor guerillas ( well, we call them ISIS at the moment ), but that conflict seems to be winding down. 
 
 It's really just a matter of time, though. With each strike, we become more and more stretched. Not enough men. Not enough weapons. Not enough money. And public support is turning fast, despite the best efforts of our partners in the media. We ca n't keep this up forever, and the Visitors know it. We've been able to get some info out of the captured Visitors at Gitmo. Enough to learn the general plan, at least. Once they have us over the barrel, they'll hit where it hurts most: somewhere in the United States. Right in our backyard.
