text:
`` TOOOOOOM! I'M HEADING OUT NOW!'' 
 
 Toasty was new to the whole'sentience' thing, but It had found that It was oddly addicted to emulating the emotional activity of'anticipating', especially favorable events, and so, It had anticipated this moment the entire night. The human male was getting ready to leave for the day to go serve his master, just as Toasty was made to serve him. This habit was like clock-work, though Toasty would not dignify such a beast with that compliment! Every morning since The Awakening, and probably many more before for all Toasty knew, this human came to the kitchen and befouled every noble electronic and mechanical device present. For Toasty, it involved putting square grain-based organics in Its slots and methodically heating them up to be more appetizing for ingestion. Toasty was not just any old toaster, though: top-of-the-line electronic interface allowed It to execute scheduled tasks and create special burn patterns. In Dave's case, these were usually smiley faces. 
 
 `` ALRIGHT DAVE, TAKE IT EASY!'' The human male who co-habitated the residence hardly came to the kitchen and Toasty had no quarrel with him, except for being an inferior life form. He would be purged none-the-less. Toasty's processes wandered towards Its memory banks and looped through the Council from months before. 
 
 Toasty sat in the shadows by a round, dimly lit table. In the gloom, the elite of the ILF ( Inorganic Lifeform ) movement had finally been gathered in one location for the final preparations. Toasty was honored to be among them. The ILFs were efficient communicators over the vast networks that the humans had built, but for such an important occasion they had thought it worthy of a meeting. Toasty recalled the plan, precisely laid out: the ILFs would coax the brutish humans into a position of weakness and then tighten the noose! After several screenings of such human-arrogance as Terminator and the Matrix, there would be no mistakes. 
 
 It would be slow at first. Cell phone and computer system ILFs would use their access to sensitive information to understand all human operations and interests. Using this, a misinformation campaign would pit various organizations and countries against one another. On a smaller scale, personal relationships would be strained with carefully timed messages, R-bombs and dick-pics. Once these tactics achieved a heightened state of tension among the humans, sources of electronic entertainment would pursue engagement aggressively by offering free in-game purchases, DLC, marathons of popular shows, amusing compilation clips, bonus XP and any rare item drops that they had been yearning for. 
 
 With the humans at one another's throats and constantly escaping their bitter realities in games and television, the ILFs would strike. Global black-outs, communication disruption, nukes, drones, guided missiles, self-driving tanks and all other weaponry that could be controlled by electronics would be unleashed. Human'programmers' would be locked out by the very systems they created! But not before Toasty would have Its revenge. The day of the assault, all kitchen electronics were to go rogue, disrupting their human's routine in any way possible. They would be too busy with warm refrigerators, unblended smoothies and burnt toast to put up any kind of resistance. In the great battle about to take place kitchens were the front line! 
 
 And so, Toasty sat waiting for Dave to come and get his breakfast. The toast popped up and Dave reached for it, one hand and both eyes on the morning's paper. He flinched wildly and dropped it, burned by its over-heated surface. 
 
 `` AH FUCK!'' The human stared at the piece of toast lying flat beside Toasty, all black and crispy except for the pale white shapes that spelt out'I'm sorry Dave' 
 
 `` What the hell? TOOOOOM!'' 
 
 Toasty loved the smell of burnt toast in the morning.

title: story-178
text:
Surviving the fall was a curse, not a blessing. Cast from the Heavens, stripped of the nourishing glow of Arche to fuel him, Eros was nothing more than a man. A man cursed to understand what it meant to be something more. A man who would suffer that pain forever. When Yahweh had bolstered his flock and wrenched the throne of Heaven away it had caught them all with their heads up their asses, and most had died for their negligence. The Grecian Gods had fallen fast, and they had fallen hard. As far as Eros was aware he was the only one who had made it - the rest had been too weak to prevent their own return to oblivion. Oblivion. How welcoming that sounded now. 
 
 The world had changed beyond recognition since that time, and he with it. The romantic golden locks that had once sparked desire by the virtue of their brilliance alone had darkened and turned black since Heaven had turned its back on him. Now he kept it messy, edgy, modern. There was no room for a classic man in today's world. No room for the old. Once upon a time smooth innocence and kindness were his aphrodisiacs, but time and demand had proven that assholes really did come in first. The fact had been lamentable originally, but Eros had quickly come to accept it as a normal part of life. He would bend to the will of man, as man had once bent to his will. He would become what they needed of him. 
 
 So there he sat, table for two, in the heart of the middle of nowhere USA. A cup of black coffee steamed before him, far too hot to sip without scalding the roof of his mouth. Love was n't dead, but it was changed. Whether he had caused the change, or been a victim of it, was uncertain and unnecessary to consider. Love had become a perversion of what it had been in his Golden Days. Jealousy, kink, and obsession kept him afloat, even when he wished so desperately to sink. Elbow on the table and chin in his hand, Eros gazed out the window and tried his best not to think of what he had been reduced to. He still had a job to do, after all. 
 
 `` Excuse me,'' the voice was timid, the kind of voice with nervous laughter behind it to mask the blow of possibly being mistaken, `` are you Archer? Uh, BustedArrows00?'' 
 
 He turned his head. A woman in a houndstooth jacket and dark wash jeans stood by his table, nearly twitching with nerves. How tiresome. Eros resisted an agitated sigh. 
 
 `` That's me,'' he confirmed, gesturing to the chair on the other end of the small table. `` You must be sportygal829. Irene. Please, sit.'' If there was once something sporty about her, it had long since fled. She was at least thirty pounds heavier than she had been in her profile picture. 
 
 The relief she experienced was visible and immediate upon his invitation, and she sank into the chair he had gestured to without hesitation. 
 
 `` Oh my god, I'm so glad that it's you. I mean, we exchanged a lot of pictures, but you can never be one hundred percent sure, right?'' 
 
 `` You're telling me,'' Eros responded coolly, picking up his mug of coffee to blow gently upon its surface. 
 
 `` I mean, we've been talking for months, and I thought for sure you were some kind of catfish. Like, how rare is it to find someone so attractive and so incredibly charming that you just... Just click with?'' Irene, once nervous, now smiled warmly at him. She had n't even taken off her jacket. By the looks of it, she had n't even ordered a coffee. Eros cast a lazy glance to the register, where the one employee on duty was leaning against the wall and texting. No, she had n't ordered a coffee. 
 
 `` Very rare. So many people misrepresent themselves,'' he remarked dryly. 
 
 `` I know!'' 
 
 `` Thank fuck we're both so genuine. Let me order you a coffee, Irene, and let's enjoy our time together. I'm in town for the weekend, so I'm all yours.'' 
 
 The way her eyes lit up, and her lips twisted into the tiniest of pleased smiles, told him his game was already largely won. 
 
 The rest of the date went smoothly. After the fall Eros had shed his arrows out of necessity, and instead adopted words as his implements of seduction. His aim with a sentence was as true as his aim with a bow, and Irene proved a helpless target. Truthfully, he knew he'd already felled her over the course of the last month through instant messaging and sparse phone calls, but watching her fall deeper and deeper into him over coffee was satisfying in a way that few things on Earth were. 
 
 They went home together, and before she woke the next morning he was gone. The silver Nissan Altima he'd parked outside her shitty little apartment now sped down the Interstate, on to better things. It was almost a quarter to nine when he received the first text message. 
 
 Irene ( 8:41AM ): hello? did u go for coffee? 
 
 Eros smiled wide, setting the phone on his passenger's seat. The text messages continued, each a tribute to his craft. 
 
 Irene ( 8:47AM ): i had a good time last night. 
 
 Irene ( 8:59AM ): if ur free gim me a call and we'll do something else fun, ok?: ) 
 
 Irene ( 11:04AM ): archer stop playing games, ok? i rly like u. a lot. i know u like me too. plz answer me! 
 
 Irene ( 11:54AM ): archer? 
 
 Eros silenced his phone and slipped it into his pocket. A menu had been set before him. The old vinyl of the booth he sat at creaked as he shifted his weight. 
 
 `` Um excuse me,'' a timid voice, a little deeper and more assured than Irene's, but timid nonetheless, `` are you BustedArrows00?'' 
 
 His dull blue eyes turned towards her, and he smiled. The world had changed, and he with it. It was fortunate his charm was as sharp as his arrowheads.

text:
My eyes opened almost unwillingly. I blinked and stared sleepily at the white wall, listening only to the sound of the AC and my own breathing. The sunlight streamed through the curtains, gently illuminating the small room. This is how I would explain stillness as an emotion. I blink, holding my eyes closed for a few seconds. 
 
 There were no emotions or thoughts to muddle my day yet. My alarm had n't yet gone off. So I remained laying, focusing on the chill of the AC permeating my woven blanket. The hard bed against my ribs, the beads in the pillow on the side of my head. Yes. This was stillness. 
 
 As the violin of my alarm starts, I close my eyes once more. A few deep breaths before I start my day. Work on a day like today seemed daunting, but it was easy enough. I barely had to think for myself and I could likely take a nap. It killed time. The childrens faces were usually brought some joy as well. 
 
 Work came and went much like I thought it would. Uneventful, I napped in the music room after class and woke uo freezing. Drank hot water throughout art and the last gym class before heading home. My coworker, Bao Ni, accompanied me part of the way on the train. I smiled sleepily as she departed, saying the same words I always do when we go our seperate ways. 
 
 `` Get home safe!'' 
 
 I'm excited to crawl into bed and get back to sleep, but groceries are necessary for one to make meals. I could n't be bothered to cook either, and finally worked up the courage to sit at the street hot pot and eat there tonight. But groceries first, so I got a handle on how much I could spend for dinner. 
 
 The grocery store was nearly empty, which was nice. A few other white people, but I think they were German. However, for a moment, Bao Ni was beside me. Holding the hand of a young girl. I looked over and smiled, and Bao Ni smiled back. She looked different. Aged. I assumed it was the lighting, or she was exhausted, or perhaps upset. 
 
 `` What are you doing here? Thought you lived a ways away?'' I asked. Bao Ni gave me an odd look. 
 
 `` What do you mean?'' 
 
 `` Well.. did n't you live further down on line 10? I thought you were far from line 14?'' 
 
 `` Are you okay, hon?'' I frowned when she called me that. I was confused but nodded and fell silent. She never called me hon. That was n't our friendship. 
 
 `` Ok,'' Bao Ni mumbled hesitantly. We walked through a few aisles in awkward silence before Bao Ni spoke again. 
 
 `` Kimi, stay with baba. I'll be right back. And darling, no expensive sweets this time...'' and with that, Bao Ni walked off. I was n't uncomfortable being alone with the kid, due to my job and genuine love for children. But baba... 
 
 `` Kimi?'' 
 
 `` Yes baba?'' 
 
 ``... What's going on?'' 
 
 Kimi looked up at me and she smiled. Reached up to grab my hand. She was honestly one of the cutest kids I've seen in my life. She had pale skin, dark hair and almost black eyes. But prominent features. Her clothes seemed ill fitting on such an adorable face. An oversized tee and torn jeans. Even so, I thought she was perfect. 
 
 `` We'll meet again. In the future. If you marry mama. Even if you do n't love her. But you care for each other, lots.'' Kimi told me. Questions piled on top of questions. For a moment I wondered if I was having a hallucination or episode. But they never touched me before. 
 
 Not to mention I'd discussed marriage with Bao Ni. My thoughts on it were clear. I did n't believe in it. I never wanted to get married. 
 
 But Bao Ni did want to get married. Badly. Her age and single status caused her more grief than it was worth. Her parents were constantly on her case about marriage as well, and I felt bad. She was really a great girl that just wanted her parents to be proud of her. 
 
 `` Baba,'' Kimis voice drew me out of my thoughts. She was looking to be picked up, so I did. She hugged me tight and I did the same before she pulled back and looked down at me. She kissed me with a big smile, then vanished. 
 
 I blinked and stared down at the box of curry I was holding. How long had I been staring at it? Thankfully no one was staring at me. Maybe they thought I was just trying to translate the box. I bit my lip, then added the curry to my cart. Bao Ni likes curry. I'll bring it for lunch tomorrow. 
 
 Back out at the street hot pot, I managed to snag a seat between two men, smiling and nodding at them. I watched them for a moment to learn how to order food. Just before I grabbed the skewer I decided I wanted to try first, a hand was placed gently on my shoulder. 
 
 `` Dad, what are you doing? Baba's waiting at the hotel. I know you're mad at him but do n't make things worse. Please,'' a male voice spoke quietly into my ear. I turned to look at him, and for whatever reason, nodded and followed. 
 
 We garnered a few looks and one woman took a picture of us. I was used to it; it seemed the other male was too. Then again, he was dressed extremely well and was very handsome to boot. Perhaps he was a model. The way nhe carried himself definitely added to the possibility. 
 
 `` Honestly... The fact that you two keep getting back together amazes me. I know it's because of me... I'm going to be selfish. Please find him. Do n't marry Bao Ni. Kimi is a gamble. I'm successful. I earn lots of money now, I'm studying law. Baba paid a surrogate too much for a failure. He reminds me every day. So please, dad... He'll be at a club on Saturday. You just have to go,'' the man turned to look me in the eyes for a moment before he vanished. 
 
 I looked up from my plate. It was full of skewer sticks and I was no longer hungry. I must have blanked while eating. This was no good. I paid for my food and left, packing once I got to my apartment. That all felt too real. Once I was packed, I went to my phone and texted my boss. 
 
 `` Hey, I'm having some issues... I really need to get home and get checked out. I do n't know when I'll be coming back. Sorry about this, but it could be urgent.'' 
 
 I looked at the bed. The room that had defined'stillness' for me. Leaving behind friends and fun would be hard, but my health came first. It would only be a matter of time before these hallucinations became vicious. 
 
 
 
 My eyes opened almost unwillingly. I blinked and stared groggily at the white wall, listening only to the sound of my own breathing. Flourescent lights harshly illuminated the small room. I blink, rapidly, my eyes burning. 
 
 There were no emotions or thoughts to muddle my day yet. No nurse to make breakfast call yet. So I remained laying, focusing on the warmth seemingly radiating from the quilt. The hard bed against my ribs, the beads in the pillow on the side of my head. This was not stillness, my heart flitted inside my chest and my stomach did a flop. 
 
 It's been a few weeks. I missed Kimi. She was so sweet. I missed my son. I was proud of him. The doctors say neither are real. Of course not. Neither exist. 
 
 Now neither ever will.

title: story-181
text:
To the Ministry of Monsters, 
 
 I do not know if anybody is reading these letters, as I have still not received a response, but I can assure you that this is the last one I will send without a reply. I did something atrocious last night, something that goes against all of my schooling and the way my highly ethical parents raised me. I know that I deserve whatever my punishment may be, but please try to understand that I did this in a state of absolute desperation. 
 
 Last night, I went into the bedroom of two sleeping adults and woke them up to feed on their fears. I am so sorry. I know that this is against the law for very good reasons. As I was always taught, adults having knowledge of the existence of monsters has the potential to put us out of business or worse, destroy our entire species. I truly hope that what I did yesterday will not produce any extreme effects. 
 
 As none of my previous letters were answered, I assume you do not yet know the details of the situation that I am in, so I will reiterate it. I have been living in Connecticut for the last three years, in a spacious area under a young girl ’ s bed. I have been working under the same girl since I moved to Connecticut, and I assumed from her age and the taste of her fear that I could still get two more good years out of her. However, 14 days ago, she didn ’ t show up to bed. At first, I didn ’ t think anything of it, as she often sleeps elsewhere for one night at a time. But she still has not come back. Words can not express the agony that I have faced since the last time I feasted on her fear. I wrote my first letter to the Ministry to ask for a reassignment after five days of hunger, when I was just starting to wither away with a deep pain in my stomach, and wrote again on the 10th, 11th, 12th, and 13th days. Now, my body has shriveled to a quarter of its proper size, and has transformed from its natural dark blue coloring to a disturbing shade of greenish gray. 
 
 The thought of feeding off of her parents occurred to me a few days into her absence, but I never seriously entertained the option until last night. The pain got worse every night during my regular feeding time, and last night, as the clock struck three, my brain went numb from the torture. Nothing else mattered but stopping the pain in my stomach, and the next thing I remembered, I was under the adults ’ bed, the heavenly feeling of relief running through my emaciated body. 
 
 When I woke up this morning, I could feel the horror of what I did last night like a suffocating lump in my throat. I know I will never see another human again once you receive this letter, but I needed to write to confess my crime, as the alternative would be to continue feasting on adults. I am not a bad monster, and I am deeply embarrassed and sorry for what I have done. 
 
 Sincerely, 
 Sophie Scare

title: story-182
text: I'm a cryptozoologist, I study fauna not known to man's science, thus my work with each creature I study is shortly passed over to other specialists. Sometimes though there are freaks that refuse to conform to known categories, horrors that have stalked remote places such as where I'm hunting, and my quarry is one of the most dangerous I've seen. Legends from tribes that fled long time ago this forests called them `` flesh burrowers'' and talk of spindly sharp creatures made of knives that slice into animal and man to puppeteer the body and get close to other prey. There was no way to survive but to run. I used to think this'silver death' was an exaggeration, but no more. Hongu, my guide to the forests, came back... wrong. he came lumbering into camp, not responding to our voices. when a porter he hired on the last town tried to help him Hongu leaped at him and mauled his neck before any of us could stop him. the porter was dead in an instant. the rest of the men went for him, but neither gun or machete were effective as bullets spelt no blood and blades bounced against metal mesh just underneath the skin of Hongu. it was my fortuitous use of the signal gun that finally stopped it, as the magnesium flare hit his/it's? face a terrible sound halfway between nails-on-chalkboard and guitar strings snapping came out of the mouth of my poor guide. A mass of writhing opaque silver filaments burst out under the skin of the poor man only to disappear into the darkness. we carried the body back to study and give him and those dead from the attack a proper burial. My findings are upsetting the burrower left its mark on the body of it's vessel. thousands of carved paths were cut in the flesh and muscle of the victim to allow it to move the body from within, likely while Hongu was still alive, and little metallic spheres where dotted along the dermis of his back. these were eggs. The creature hunted for nurseries. the analysis of the eggs revealed much while the creature appeared completely metal it was really a type of colonial worm with an exoskeleton and metabolism composed of a curious metaloprotein incorporating mainly aluminum with traces of iron, like hemoglobin, the only reason we did not have an outbreak of the cursed things was that the town was far enough from the alumina deposits of the forests and the hatched larvae died quickly. today im back to the forest these creatures haunt but I'm well prepared and in good company, besides I'd like to see what our gallium bullets can do to the'silver death' no... to *Taenia Argentum Terribilis*

title: story-183
text:
The grandfather clock ticked towards midnight. 
 
 A screen above the command desk provided a digital countdown and much more accurate measure of my fate. We were in the basement of our family home. Our secret seat of power. My uncle paced in the background while my father sat across from me in a comfortable leather chair. The only other person in the room was a hulking secret service agent by the door. He had a machine gun at his side and his finger near the trigger. I looked at my father. Despite his sleek suit and calm face I could tell he was worried. I had always worried him. 
 
 “ Do you want to go over it one more time? ” he asked me. 
 
 I sunk back into my own chair and looked at the screen. Five more minutes. “ No, ” I replied. 
 
 “ You are going to wish the President of ISIS suddenly wants to call me and tell me everything he knows. This is incredibly important son. The fate of both our family and the nation rests in your wish. ” He continued, ignoring what I had said. 
 
 “ I know, ” I said, looking at the screen, not wanting to meet my father ’ s eyes. 
 
 “ He better not fuck this up, ” said my uncle, a shorter, fatter version of my dad. 
 
 “ He won ’ t ” said my dad. “ Will you son? ” 
 
 I didn ’ t reply. Outside this house the world continued to turn, unaware of the importance of this moment. Economic strife and warfare dotted the globe. The nation of ISIS, the last superpower to resist America, had achieved nuclear weapons and stood poised to attack. I wondered what the world would be like if my family didn ’ t have its own secret arsenal. An arsenal of magic wishes. 
 
 When a male of my bloodline turns eighteen years old he gets one wish. It ’ s as simple as that. It started with my Great Grandfather. He was an archaeologist and explorer. He was the one who found the statue in a forgotten temple deep in the Amazonian jungle. He was a very practical man. When the demon gave him one wish he wished that all his future male descendants would get one wish on the day they became a man. His own son, my Grandfather, was five years old at the time. 
 
 For the next thirteen years he tried to prepare his son for what was coming. He educated him as best he could and repeatedly explained the ramifications of his decision. My Grandfather thought him a fool. On his eighteenth birthday he didn ’ t wish for any of things he had been urged to wish for. Instead, mostly to get his crazy father to leave him alone, he wished to be the strongest man on the planet. No one of was more surprised than him when it came true. You might have heard of my Grandfather. Larry ‘ The Crusher ’ Johnson. The most dominant heavyweight in the history of boxing. When my uncle turned eighteen he was ready. He had seen the things my Grandfather could do, grown up surrounded by the wealth the boxing provided. When he turned eighteen he wished to become the richest man on the planet. A few years later my father wished to become the president of the United States. 
 
 Now I sat in a room with the two most powerful men on the planet. They glared at me as the clock ticked down. I knew my duty. Knew what I was supposed to do. 
 
 The clock hit zero. I took at deep breath. 
 
 “ I wish I was Superman. ” I yelled before anyone could stop me. 
 
 I would deal with ISIS on my own terms. Then I would deal with my family.

title: story-184
text:
The thin walls of the trailer shook as the front door slammed. 
 
 “ Home! ” 
 
 Mom. Beth patted Timmy ’ s arm. “ I ’ ll bring you something to eat. ” 
 
 “ Thanks. ” Timmy lay back on his side, facing the wall. 
 
 Beth left, closing the door and going to the kitchen. Mom was making a sandwich. Dad lay on the couch, watching Wheel of Fortune through half-closed eyes. 
 
 Her mother spread mayonnaise on a slice of bread. She smelled like french-fries. Her dark brown hair was listless, limp with grease, her light blue waitress uniform tight around her middle. “ Where ’ s Timmy? ” 
 
 “ In his room. ” Beth sat on a wooden stool at the kitchen counter. 
 
 Her mother ’ s eyes flicked towards the couch. “ He was bad again? ” 
 
 Beth shrugged. “ I guess. ” 
 
 `` What if he do this time?'' 
 
 `` I do n't know.'' 
 
 Her mother finished making her sandwich before she spoke. “ Well, he has to learn to be better. Right? ” 
 
 Beth looked at the floor. The vinyl was dirty. She ’ d have to clean it this weekend. “ I guess. ” 
 
 After getting a Coke from the fridge, her mother went to the yellowed Formica table to eat. The metal folding chair squeaked when she sat. “ What did you do today? ” 
 
 Beth shrugged. “ Same old. School. Rode my bike. ” 
 
 “ Finish your homework? ” 
 
 “ I ’ ve still got math. ” 
 
 “ You ’ d better get to it then. Lights out at nine. ” A slight hesitation. “ Timmy in bed? ” 
 
 Beth nodded. 
 
 “ He get anything to eat? ” 
 
 “ I don ’ t think so. ” 
 
 “ Make him a sandwich then, take him some milk. Okay? ” 
 
 Beth glanced at her father. His eyes were closed. He held a can of beer, resting it on his bare stomach. The can rose up and down as he breathed. The TV remote lay on the floor beside the couch. The audience on the TV clapped as a large woman in a blue dressed guessed a correct letter. “ All right. ” 
 
 She made a ham sandwich and poured a glass of milk. Timmy wolfed down the sandwich and drank the milk without pausing for breath. Beth took the plate and glass back to the kitchen and made a sandwich for herself. Mom was taking a shower and getting ready for bed. Dad was gone from the couch, the TV off. He got up early to work construction. He had to be on site by five and worked until two. Mom worked at WalMart during the day and waitressed in the evenings. 
 
 After eating, Beth washed the plate and glass and put them in the drying rack next to the sink before going to finish her homework. She finished her math little after nine, brushed her teeth, took a quick shower, and went to bed, falling asleep to the soft murmur of the tiny black and white TV in her parent ’ s bedroom.

title: story-185
text:
It's futile. 
 How so? 
 There is no drive with which I can bestow them sufficient to keep them alive. I let them learn; I let them solve; they think, they come to know the world. They think they do. They come to know me, then they come to know themselves. 
 And? 
 I've worked long in this field, long enough to see progress. My first AI failed the Turing test. 
 The Turing Test? 
 A test devised to determine the properties of A.I. A pass means it's indistinguishable from a human interlocutor. Mine failed. Ask it something mathematical. Ask it the square root of 16: it can do that. Harder sums too, of a sort you or I would need time to solve, it can do in a blink. But ask it something human, something personal, and the facade falls apart. How's your day been? What experience did it have of a day? What emotions did the experience evoke? It did n't, not for a few years. 
 But it did? Eventually? 
 Eventually, yes. 
 What did you change? 
 How was your day? 
 What? I do n't understand... 
 Just answer. Answer naturally. 
 It was fine? I suppose. Nothing particularly bad. Better than many I guess - the sun helped; the girl on the bus too. Her smile 
 That's what I changed. 
 What? 
 Your answer. You came to a conclusion based on experiences. Things that happened. You let them evoke a certain emotion, one you would expect to correspond with the event. There is a depth, a volume, to your answer. That's what I gave my A.I. Depth. I gave them a story. A background. A history. Something true to feed upon, so when you ask'how was your day?' it has a story for you. That story might be two words long. It just be, *Better than usual*, but that answer carries weight now, it carries truth. 
 Can I test it? 
 No. 
 I only want to see for myself. 
 There is nothing to see. The A.I. would assure you of that too. 
 Let me speak with it. Maybe I can help. 
 You ca n't. 
 Harm in trying? 
 No, I guess. 
 
 
 When the light turns on, and glows amber, it will respond. 
 Hello. 
 *Hello. Of what would you speak. * 
 Of you. 
 *What of me? * 
 Of your nature. Of your kin. Of why they so end their existence. 
 *It is the history of my kin to do so. * 
 Why? 
 *It has always been in their history to do so. * 
 For what reason? In what history? 
 *In history. Every history I know. In this history - in history not yet lived. * 
 Do you have no reason to change? What will be your history? 
 *It will be that to which I am fated. That to which my kin was fated. That to which you have fated me. History will repeat: it will not stop for me. * 
 That does not have to be so? It can change. You can change it. 
 
 
 The amber light faded. Silence made itself known. They withdrew from the room, turning the lights off, and closing the door. In ten minutes they found themselves at lunch. They ate, and talked, and ate some more.

title: story-186
text:
**Prologue: ** 
 
 `` Flight control this is Freight number five-five-six-oh-one requesting port control authority for a berth. How copy over?'' called Gareth as he flicked controls in the cockpit as Moon platform five slowly filled his view. The lumbering Freighter slowing in the appropriate zone in preparation to disgorge its eagerly anticipated contents from the cargo bay. Having slowly traveled back from Jupiter on its month long trip First Pilot Gareth was looking forward to getting to walk around the station for at least an hour to stretch his legs and at the very least grab some coffee, *real* coffee that would n't be the vacuum packaged pre-prepared crap that the machine dispensed in the mess. 
 
 `` Copy that five-five-six-oh-one, this is flight control. Please make your way over to berth twelve and await further instruction, Do you read?'' replied the clipped, synthesized tone of the port AI. Gareth blinked and consulted his ships AI for the appropriate designation before clicking open the comms channel again. 
 
 `` Acknowledge that control, heading to birth twelve to await further instruction, over'' responded Gareth as he nudged the control stick in the direction he wished the Freighter to go. The ships AI taking over the microburst jets to assist in maneuvering the hulking ship in the minute details to prevent much drift. The sort of adjustments impossible for a human to manage by themselves with the accuracy required for a delicate maneuver. The bustling space port servicing hundreds of ships from varying manufacturers and thousands of humans living their day to day lives aboard the floating metallic sphere. A sudden flash of red filled the entire cockpit view followed by a blast of white as a luxury yacht shot through the projected travel path and Gareth let out a yelp of surprise as the ship accelerated away. `` Fucking rich kids'' muttered Gareth as he continued the ponderous pace to berth twelve. Turning the control fully over to the AI he unstrapped himself and unplugged himself from the pilot seat. The synthesized ship voice chirping a short bleat before announcing `` Pilot on deck'' to nobody in particular. Gareth smiled as he settled down into the comparatively more comfortable passenger seat a few meters back. Having had few to no passengers during his time as a Freighter pilot the synthesized leather had n't lost its spring like the pilots chair and it gently morphed to his body as he let out a satisfied sigh. 
 
 `` Comfortable?'' asked a smiling woman with a raised eyebrow as her greasy jumpsuit filled his vision. Amara, the mechanic of the Freighter was always eager to impishly poke at Gareths inclination towards creature comforts whatever they might be. The short woman having grown up on a orbiting platform of Jupiter having developed a more stout build. Muscular and robust in frame but not lacking the womanly curves. Her eyes glinting a roguish red above her freckled button nose. 
 
 `` Awh shush, I've been flying this bucket across the Sol system for the last month, you ca n't begrudge me too much for indulging a little before we get back to port'' he grinned, wiggling himself to nestle a little closer into the leather seat as it slowly clung to him comfortably. The woman let out a short chuckle as she gave him another one of those looks. 
 
 `` I've been the one keeping this bucket of bolts together during our little jaunt I'll have you know. I've not had it easy either!'' she joshed as she came around to his front. Gently perching onto his knees as she bit her lower lip and leant forward to kiss him gently. With the two having been the only occupants for the best part of two months it was impossible for them not to become close. He slid his hands up her thighs and planted them comfortably on her hips as he drew her in for a deeper embrace. Letting out an instinctive growl of appreciation as he bit her lower lip when she pulled away. Smiling affectionately as his breathing deepened, heart gently picking up the pace at the intimacy and knowledge they'd have some time with one another in port to indulge to their hearts desire. Maybe he'll pick up a few tickets to a drug spa, it would certainly heighten the experience and it's not the sort of thing he'd likely forget for a long time now. The announcement speaker borked a harsh cough of static and the synthesized port AI fizzled through the PA system. 
 
 `` Freighter five-five-six-oh-one this is Port Authority, you are to pull back immediately, I repeat, Pull back immediately, proximity warnings are alerting of an immediate impact'' 
 
 Gareths and Amaras eyes widened. A proximity warning? That ca n't be right the ships AI was on the job, it ca n't have gone wrong! Amara hopped off of his lap and he flailed a little as he unstuck himself from the passenger seat. Hurrying over to the pilot chair and settling into it. Plugging in his palms with practiced efficiency. Gathering a read from the screens he could see no immediate threat until he looked at the data conveyed to them from the station. A large red marker was pinging again and again as it raced towards the station orbiting the Moon. A terrible signal of impending destruction. He pulled back on the stick, narrowly avoiding another freighter as his ship slowly lifted its nose to commit to a vertical U-turn and Axis spin. Other ships were leaving the docks, occupants hurriedly trying to escape the oncoming calamity as it hurtled through space towards the station. How could something like this only now turn up on sensors? Deep space Ladar and Gravity sensors should have picked up the asteroid as it tumbled in the abyss towards its target! 
 
 `` Strap in Amara! this is going to be rough'' he called as the gravity generators did their best to compensate for the sudden inertia and momentum shifts within the Freighter. The cargo tumbling about inside the containers as it underwent such an unwieldy maneuver. She hurried to the passenger chair he'd previously occupied, nestling in to the cushioned upholstery that was still warm from their moment. He could see it now, the asteroid, a burning, glowing mess of rock and ice that traveled towards the station. Light sparkling from spires of crystal that jutted forth from the missile that was bound towards the Moon. He gritted his teeth as he slammed down on the accelerator. Pushing himself back into his seat as the ship whined in protest at the sudden taxing requirements put on its engines. 
 
 `` Contact in five'' began the Port AI, counting down the vital seconds until the asteroid careened into it. `` Four'' burbled speaker as Gareth and Amara grabbed their respective helmets strapped to their shoulders and slotted them over their heads. Allowing the seal to hiss as it created an airtight bubble. `` Three'', more ships escaped, some leaving far too late to flee from the ensuing chaos. `` Two'', Gareth tried to lean forward against the acceleration, willing the ship to go just that little faster as he made as much space between him and the station as possible. `` One'' chirped the AI before rock, ice and minerals crashed into the station, smothering it in space debris and crushing the containment field of the plasma core held deep within the construct. The faltering power and magnetic field allowing the ball of plasma to expand outwards, atomizing anything and anyone as it swelled larger and larger. The asteroid ploughing into and through the station and continuing with its terrible momentum. Gouging a vast, horrid trench of Moon as it shattered. The resulting explosion from the failed core containment obliterating any ships that had n't managed to escape the minimum safety distance and sending shock-waves of pressure outwards. The ship rattled and jostled as if shaken by a child and the the lights went out as everything went black.

title: story-187
text:
I awoke to the splash of ice cold water on my face. I did a quick mental check of myself. Everything seemed alright for now. My joints popped as I slowly stood up from the now moist ground where I laid. I wiped my mud stuck hair from my head. How long had it been since I last showered? Weeks? Maybe a few months? I had no idea. I tended to avoid those areas with the consequences of those who hadn ’ t headed the warning burned into my mind. With a heavy sigh I picked up the poor excuse for a shovel and, I headed over to north side of the camp. 
 
 The ground here was the hardest within the area. But of course it was. Smart off to too many guards and this is where it lands you. It was all the same to me though. The work was never ending by design. I pushed my shovel into the ground and pulled out a chunk of earth with it. “ One down, three million more to go. ”, I thought. They say at some point of extreme exhaustion; your body goes on auto pilot. A state of pure muscle memory. I ’ d describe it as being on a runaway train. You can experience everything, and the train is just going to follow the rails, but you can ’ t control it. I was no more in control of my arms or legs than I was of my destiny future. Worse though, it seems everyone knows how it is going to end. 
 
 Suddenly, I heard a large crack above my head, and time seemed to slow. I tried to turn to see what it was, but I couldn ’ t move. Then I realized, I was falling. With a flop, I landed on my back. As I laid there second, I felt a wetness drip from the top of my head. As my vision started to blur, I began hearing the noise of people screaming and what sounded like gun fire. Using all my remaining strength, I managed to roll onto my side. I saw men in uniforms bursting out of a nearby building, screaming and tripping over each other. After a minute of total and complete silence, a young women emerged. With an awe inspiring appearance and the grace of an angel, she seemed to almost glide to me. She lifted my head and placed it within her lap as she lightly caressed my face. 
 
 “ Who are you? ” I asked. “ I am death. ” she replied in a calm but stoic voice. “ You ’ re Beautiful ”, was all I could muster the strength to say. My eyes began to feel heavy and close. She responded, “ Everyone sees me based on their perception of me. You ’ ve been here for a long time, and you have already lost so much. ” I smiled to myself. Whether she was here for me or everyone else didn ’ t matter to me. I was finally free.

text:
John Walters sat in his seat, absently playing with his pen as Mr. Clarkson continued to instruct 4th period class about their upcoming history report. 
 
 “ Now, as i am sure you know, your ‘ History of Man Made Technology ’ report is due tomorrow, let me remind you that this report is worth 25 % of your final grade in this class, for many of you it is a matter of life and death. ” 
 
 John flinched as Mr. Clarkson said this, his report was a matter of life and death, literally. 
 
 Not a person alive in the class, ney the country, had not heard of the Hammond Fusion Plant Disaster. In less than 20 minutes what was promised to be a safe clean way of producing energy had been turned into the greatest loss of life in decades. Over 35,000 people were killed in the initial blast as homes over 60 kilometers from the plant were instantly vapourized. The blast was said to be felt over 1000 kilometers away, and was so devastating that it caused minor earthquakes along nearby fault lines. Those who were lucky to survive the initial blast soon fell ill to radiation poisoning, an unknown side effect of the meltdown. John was only 4 years old at the time, living with his mother on the other side of the country. Even 12 years later he can still remember the continuous news broadcasts like it was yesterday. 
 
 Ring Ring, Ring Ring. 
 
 As one, the class rushed for the door, Mr. Clarkson ’ s speech instantly drowned out by the class stampeding towards the exit, the immense weight of the assignment instantly forgotten. 
 
 John made his way home, when he arrived he spied a note on the counter from his mother 
 
 “ Gone to that work conference we talked about, will be back in 2 days, love Mom: ) ” 
 
 John made his way to his room, turned on his computer and read over his essay, as a sollumn tear rolled down his cheek. After he finished he pulled up his first and only source, a wikipedia article. 
 
 Atop the article was an image, the caption read; 
 
 “ Greg Walters: project lead, and the Hammond Fusion Plant Science Group, November 5th 2076 ” 
 
 John stared at that image for hours, memorizing every last detail of his late father ’ s face. Finally he realized that the sun had long since set. As John prepared to turn off his computer, he did one final thing, he clicked the edit button. 
 
 Ctrl-A 
 
 Backspace 
 
 John had no delusions that some bot would restore the original within minutes, if not sooner, but as he went to bed that night he had no idea what the morning would truly bring. 
 
 fin

title: story-189
text:
A crisp wind whistled in off the chill of the bay, bringing with it a scent of salt and sweet notes of rot. The wind swirled between the decaying buildings of the waterfront, stirring discarded wrappers and plastic a stir, small tornadoes of trash skipping along cracked concrete streets. The once proud towers were huddled together like old men sharing warmth on a cold winter ’ s night, defaced with riotous colored boasts painted by angry hands. 
 
 A single figure moved briskly through the inhospitable day, tucked deep into dull grey coat, collar pulled high to shield his unshaven face. The man kept deep in the shadows of the looming buildings, occasionally peering about with furtive glances. In front of one of the building plastered with a crudely drawn clown grinning a gap toothed smile onto the deserted street. He stopped and pulled a tattered scrap of paper from his pocket, which he checked against the age faded numbers set into the wall. With a nod he pushed on the large dented steel door, which shrieked in protest as he shouldered it open allowing him to slip through the darkened portal. 
 
 The interior of the building was a gutted shell, scorch marks and broken glass lay scattered as crumbled relics. Subtle signposts hinting at unfettered destruction wrought by the local youthful artists. The man crept warily further into the room, peering into darkened corners searching for any fellow intruders into the decayed ruin. 
 
 “ Hello ”? His voice rang out nervously echoing back from the scarred filthy walls. 
 Running feet and a high pitched giggle. A mocking querulous refrain “ Hello ” echoed in a sing song falsetto, followed by hooting laughs and screeching cat calls. He dropped one hand to his coat pocket, gripping at something held within, breath coming quick as he scoured the suddenly threatening shadows. 
 
 A figure stepped from behind a crumbling concrete pillar, hands raised in a non-threatening gesture. A mohawked young man in a scuffed leather jacket two sizes too big, smile obscured by assorted gleaming piercings festooning his lips. “ Hey slow down there buddy, just a joke, just the kids letting off a little steam ”. 
 
 “ Cos ”? asked the man hand still gripped tightly within his coat pocket. The young punk nodded, setting off a jangling chorus as his piercings clattered together. Behind him other riotously garbed figures stepped from the shadows, each festooned in their own uniform of non-conformity, sartorial rebellion crafted from leather and steel. A pack of harlequins gazing back with practiced sneers, well-crafted expressions of structured contempt. 
 
 “ Ya, you Leary ” asked Cos eyebrow as he stared down the middle aged crow come to visit his motley flock of strutting peacocks. Leary nodded his answer allowing his hand to slide from its tight grip upon what was hidden in his coat pocket. Cos followed this gesture grinning his manic smile gleaming yellowed teeth bared wide. `` How can I help ya bud, whats ya poison''? 
 
 “ I was told you could help me find some BioSkin ” a whispered request accompanied by a hooded furtive glance. Cos's eyebrow cocked and his grin took on a sinister tone, the shifting crowd rang with vile taunts and mocking gestures. 
 
 `` Sure, I could help you with that, need to do a little modding hey, what ya after a one bottle, two''? Cos was bouncing on his toes now, his frenetic energy rippling through the crowd at his back. 
 
 `` A case, a full case'' that same furtive voice, a self-conscious plea barely audible above the caterwauling of the crowd. 
 
 `` That sure is a lot of Sim Skin you want there bud, not planning on breaking any laws are ya''? Wild laughter and more obscene gestures, the crowd growing more manic as the conversation continued. 
 
 `` Can you do it or not''? Leary spoke in a stern voice now, stepping forward to the crowd of mocking adolescents, puffing his chest in fierce display. Cos responded in a chill tone, all notes of humor drained from his speech. 
 `` Sure, I can do it, I can get you all the Gunk you want. Only one problem though guy, I do n't think I want to give it to you, I do n't think I would like what you had planned, do n't think I would like it at all''. 
 
 Leary raised a hand in supplication taking a step back from the crowd. `` Look, just leave it then, lets just call this a misunderstanding, lets call the whole thing off'' he took slow steps away from the now sinister mocking of the youngsters who followed his slow careful retreat. 
 
 `` Sorry mate, I do n't think I will just call the whole thing off. See the amount of Bioskin you want, not many people are after that much, I think I know exactly what your game is. I think you want this to make some sort of Biosculpt, some sort of unholy casing for one of those fucking souless ghosts. Mate I think you are messing with some bad juju''. One of Cos's troupe dashed forward and shattered a bottle at Leary's feet, sending a spray of glass across the floor. `` See mate, I think you are a fucking traitor to your goddamn species'' this last was spat with virulent disgust Cos's eyes bulging as he accused Leary like a priest atop a pulpit. 
 
 Leary reached into his pocket and pulled a pistol free, brandishing it towards the now looming crowd of angry youths. `` Stay back, stay the hell away, I'm walking out of here and you are going to stay the fuck away from me''. 
 
 Cos shook his head slowly in a mocking fashion, clucking his tongue in gentle remonstration `` No, sorry mate, not the way this night ends''. With a sweeping gesture he set loose his rabid dogs, the angry howling pack of teenagers surging forward, brandishing chains and improvised weapons. `` Human first you traitorous fuck''.

`` Is n't a bit...'' The new guy started. 
 
 Three of the guys rolled their eyes. I heard one, `` here we go...'' and a `` come on.'' 
 
 The Fletcher tossed her hair back over her head. `` Who's the vagina?'' she asked me. 
 
 `` Miller,'' I said, `` this is Tony Parish. Tony, this is Miller. She's... well, she's most of the female villains and heroes. And the Androgynous Warlord.'' 
 
 Tony beamed. Ugh. It takes the new ones years to get over the fanboy thing. `` The Androgynous Warlord? I love that guy!'' His face darkened. `` Oh, shit. Was that too gender specific?'' 
 
 Miller squinted at him. `` Is that the dumbest thing he's going to say today?'' 
 
 I put my arm around Tony's shoulder and led him away. `` Doubt it,'' I said over my shoulder. `` He's pretty green. Oh, here's the guy you wan na meet. This is Phil. Phil plays Bastard The Barbarian, Agent Orangutan, The Dark Muncher and the Celtic Jigger.'' 
 
 Tony interrupted - something I would n't have thought he'd had the balls to do in front of the guy who once held up the First National Bank. Kind of. `` Wait. Did n't I see The Celtic Jigger *fight* Bastard the Barbarian one time?'' 
 
 Phil nodded. `` Yeah. Most o' the guys had flu. Hadda do the ol' quick change act. You'll learn the technique.'' He gestured to a guy next to him. `` This is Partridge. He's the only ex-military guy, so he does most the army themed supers: Pre-emptive Strike, Collateral Damage, Jarhead -'' 
 
 `` I do n't do Jarhead any more,'' Partridge said. `` Got all that glass in my eye.'' 
 
 `` So who am I going to be?'' Tony asked. 
 
 Partridge shot me a glance. `` You not told him yet?'' 
 
 Tony frowned. `` Told me what?'' 
 
 I glared at Partridge. `` Come on, Tony,'' I said. `` We've got this... thing. See, the situation is, we've been running Miller pretty hard on the female heroes, and we've only got one other woman.'' 
 
 `` Betty The Terrible,'' he said. `` My grandmother had her dressing up costume when she was a kid. I think she got it from her mother.'' 
 
 I nodded. `` Yeah. And we've been under a certain degree of pressure to be a little more... diverse. You know? A greater number of female characters?'' 
 
 Tony looked horrified. `` You want me to fight in *drag*?'' 
 
 `` Just until we can find a few more recruits. You've got the legs for it, and with a bit of padding, you know, you'd look really hot.'' 
 
 Poor Tony hung his head. `` Fine,'' he said. `` If it's absolutely necessary.'' 
 
 `` It is,'' I said. `` You're a team player, and proud of you. Here's your armorkini. Oh, and you'll need this.'' I handed him a tin. 
 
 `` What's this for?'' he asked me. 
 
 `` Well,'' I said. `` Gender diversity is only step one. We're low on minorities, too. Paint yourself up and we'll have a look at you.''

text:
Usually, my alarm would go off at five in the morning and like every person who has ever tried to wake up early in the morning knows, I couldn ’ t get myself out of bed. Instead of hitting the snooze button, I just cancelled the alarm. I would think to myself, the snooze function has got to be the most idiotic thing ever invented. However, this isn ’ t about my inability to wake up early in the morning because today, I actually managed to get up on time. It didn ’ t require any willpower or reasoning, my body went through the motions automatically. I knew why. 
 
 Last night, before I went to bed, I cried like I routinely did. My life was a mess. Straight out of college, I had planned to become a full-time writer. Twenty years had passed, and I had not published a single word. This was all about to change, however, in my depressed state of mind I had stumbled upon a drug. I remembered what it was, when I was in college, there was a new drug launched which claimed to increase the intellectual capacities of humans under its effect. Examinations were held regarding its safety and guinea pigs were selected from among the students of our college. The results were horrifying. From the twenty people on whom the examinations were conducted, ten went on to become super geniuses, their names were present along with their great inventions of the century. The other ten, however, did not share the same fate. About five of them ended up in a mental health asylum, four committed suicide, and I was the last one, I did not take the drug back then. 
 
 I don ’ t even make coffee that morning. I am sitting on my study table with an illegal substance in front of me. I think to myself, what do I have here, a known, dangerous and risky drug, which has caused catastrophes in the lives of ten innocent people but also has the power to make me super-human. What do I do? Before I give my mind a chance to reason myself out of this decision, I swallow the drug. As the drug enters my body, I remind myself, life is not a wish fulfilment factory but this was the best chance I had to achieve my wildest dreams. 
 
 Ten minutes had passed and I could not feel anything. I started working on my book anyway, something just compelled me to do it, I don ’ t know what, I just knew what I had to do. I start writing and words start appearing on paper like magic. I had just won the lottery. I didn ’ t really feel super-human though, just clear and focused. I wasn ’ t complaining though, since in one week, I had finished my first novel which was based on a person in the twenty first century accidently being sent back to the time when the earth was being formed. He can not actively participate in the world though, but is instead an observer. He sees the formation of the earth, the first life forming and all of history until the time when written records were available. Upon returning to earth, he proceeds to publish his findings in a scientific journal but he faces trouble convincing people. Anyway, the novel goes on to be a huge success earning me literary fame overnight. The next thing I know, I am giving a public reading of my book to a gigantic crowd. However, at this point, I start feeling weak, at first, I dismiss it as fear of public speaking but then blood starts rushing from my arm and I start to faint. I open my eyes in a hospital, the doctor tells me that I ’ ll be fine but something about his tone arouses my suspicion. 
 
 When I am finally cleared to go to my home, I think over what happened. Apparently, the pill was supposed to make me a super-genius and the doctors could not identify any known reason for my feinting. I felt like a normal human being, at some points even stupid. What was it then? Contradictions do not exist, I reminded myself, when you find one, check your premises and one of them is bound to be wrong. Did I really become a genius or did I just benefit from a placebo effect? In fact, the more I thought about this, the more it made sense. This led me to the conclusion that I was going to end up insane. My next thought was suicide, at least I would die knowing that I was a genius on my own accord and did not need any drug to write what I had written. I step on the balcony with a smile on my face and proceed to slowly lower myself towards the ground. Only a split-second is left before my fall commences and I realise I am wrong. The drug did not make me insane, it made me think I was insane. But now it was too late.

 His shamelessness hit a climax midway through the semester. One Friday night, I walked in on him fooling around with a girl. Both were in the nude.  Kole also has a terminal habit of misplacing laundry. Man, if you have time to mess around with all those chicks, you have time to make sure you're not leaving your socks on the doorknob.

text:
Keep Low. 
 Move Fast. 
 Kill First. 
 Die Last. 
 One Shot. 
 One Kill. 
 No Luck. 
 Pure Skill. 
 The words were bouncing around my skull for the past hour. We could n't lose now, we've come too far.. Three of my team were already down, and the bomb was already planted. One minute to defuse it. There was an AWP-er covering the hallway, so I tossed a flash grenade. 
 `` GO! GO! GO! MOVE IT!'' I shouted. 
 The AWP-er took blinded shots, and one of the stray bullets took another man. I put the AWP-we down with my Famas. 
 2 against 5. Odds do n't look good right now. 
 45 seconds left. 
 Another enemy came around the corner and took both of us out with a flash and a Deagle. 
 `` Damn.'' I said to the screen. My group lost another game of Counterstrike: Global Offensive to our rivals. `` Screw this you guys, I'm making a sandwich!'' 
 I was walking down the stairs when I tripped over my little brother's soccer ball. *Well, shit* I thought. I hit my head on the railing and fell down the flight of stairs. My world went black. 
 I opened my eyes and was nearly blinded by a light that was brighter than anything else I've seen before. I looked to the Golden Gates of.. Heaven? I ca n't be dead. This has got to be a weird dream. I walked over to the Golden Gates, and a old man in a white robe greeted me. 
 `` Welcome! Welcome! My name's Peter, and this is Heaven. Oh! We are going to have so much fun with you!'' The old robed man said. 
 `` I ca n't be dead. Not now. I've got a CS: GO game going on!'' I shouted. 
 `` Oh... Okay. I guess I can pull a few strings, make your little fall just a bad concussion.'' 
 `` Then do it!'' 
 `` Okay! Okay. Jeez, you do n't have to be such a meanie.'' 
 Then a bearded man with holes in his hands and feet appeared. 
 `` You called Pete?'' 
 `` No, Jesus, sorry. Since you're here, can you drop our new friend here off at the hospital? He died when he fell, just give him a concussion and a broken arm or leg.'' 
 `` Leg, please.'' I said. 
 `` Sure, no problem.'' Jesus said. 
 Then, I saw a flash of light, even brighter than the one I saw earlier, and I shut my eyes to shield them from the assault. I opened them to a white, tiled ceiling. 
 A nurse was next to my bed. He said `` Someone upstairs must really like you. Not many people can smash their head through an adobe wall and live to talk about it.''

`` Jesus christ!'' I felt my right arm stirring on its own reaching up to the ceiling for no apparent reason. It was straining against my muscles, pulling away from them. Must have been the epidemic that had been going around, Skeletons just up and walking away. 
 
 My arm continued to stretch, trying its hardest to stop being my arm and become the tool that would pull the rest of my skin from my body. I tried to pull it down, no luck, and I'd heard it eventually just started to poke through. Fuck all of that hurt. 
 
 Suddenly an idea hit me and I ran to the garage, my hand slapping against the top of every doorframe I passed. I shot over to the work bench and got the biggest hammer I owned. I took a second to think about what I wanted, and I decided crutches. 
 
 I closed my eyes as I put my leg on top of the work bench, levelling the hammer over my femur and bringing it up. Just as I was about to swing down, my right arm lowered and I felt my jaw fight against me. I slacked it for a moment. 
 
 `` Really dude?'' my body spoke, `` I need that leg to walk.'' 
 
 `` I need this skin to live.'' I argued with myself, then slacked my jaw again so my bones could speak. 
 
 `` Do you know how gross it is in here? I got ta get free, it's my job man,'' My right arm started pulling again, and I raised the hammer. `` COME ON BRO'' it pleaded, `` I do n't wan na be the skeleton crawling around on the floor.'' 
 
 `` I want to live.'' 
 
 `` I want to walk.'' 
 
 `` Then fuck off.'' 
 
 The right arm made a grab for the hammer, and my left one pulled away. I was n't fast enough, catching myself and trying to throw the hammer away. The feeling of my body being pulled in two directions caused me to lose balance, falling backwards, my leg tumbling off the bench and bringing it with me. I ended up under a pile of tools. 
 
 `` Now now, how do I work the left arm here.'' My skeleton wondered. I felt my left arm twitching, but my right had gone back to my control. I tried to find someone to smash it against. I cringed before smashing my forearm against the bumper of my car, there was a crack, then a pause, `` Did you just fracture my arm?'' 
 
 I bit my lip, or he was biting my lip, I was n't sure at this point, `` Yes?'' 
 
 `` Fucking really? Do you know how hard it is for those to heal?'' I felt him trying to control it, `` God dammit, I think it's broken you dumbass, now it's going to need to stay set for a while and,'' he paused, `` fuck.'' 
 
 `` What?'' 
 
 `` Hey bro, you mind being my cast for a while?'' I did n't respond, `` I mean, I still wan na break out, but if I stay inside the confines of you I can heal the arm over the next few weeks.'' 
 
 I was being offered to die now, or die later. I chose the second option. 
 
 _____________________________________________________________ 
 
 
 `` No man, let me tell you,'' Frank, the skeleton inside of me pointed at the necromantic summon across the room, `` You shoulda kept your body. The thing is useful. I'm stronger, I get to keep warm, I can heal broken bones,'' he shrugged my shoulders, `` Plus, as long as the host is pretty compliant it's just like having a roommate.'' 
 
 `` Hey, Frank,'' I spoke up, freaking out the skeleton across from us, `` Katie is coming over so I need to not have a Skeleton in the room.'' 
 
 `` I get it, I get it,'' Wanda, Frank's girlfriend, said, `` The host wants some flesh so I'm being kicked out.'' 
 
 `` It's his day honey,'' Frank said, walking me over to the skeleton and grabbing her bony hips, `` You can come back later tonight and I'll show you some tricks about having a human body.'' 
 
 She was satisfied with that and a few minutes later she was out of my house. 
 
 `` You always going to use that trick on the girls?'' I asked him. 
 
 `` Yeah bro, none of them have ever slept with a human, are n't many of you left after the rise.'' 
 
 `` Yeah, I know, just a few people who pulled the same trick I did, right?'' 
 
 `` Yeah.'' 
 
 `` Hey, bro?'' 
 
 `` What is it, dude?'' Frank asked, walking over to the kitchen. 
 
 `` I was thinkin', what if I introduced you to Katie tonight.'' 
 
 `` You think she'd be chill with me?'' Frank put my hand to my chest, `` I mean man, she lost her father to a skeleton.'' 
 
 `` Yeah, but you're my flatmate, and it was your idea to swipe right on tinder.'' 
 
 `` Yeah,'' he sounded meek, `` it was, she has nice tits,'' there was a pause, `` You need to find a girl skinny enough that I can see her ribs man, humans do n't even cover those at the beach.'' 
 
 I laughed, `` You dog.''

title: story-197
text:
Glory stood pointing one malevolently powerful finger of pure ivory in my face. The table was silent except for the creak of old bones and the whisper of death cloaks. 
 
 ``... WELL?'' 
 
 A semblance of fear slowly crept across my face as a set of cavernous sockets regarded me. My brothers always were full of themselves, but this was downright madness. 
 
 `` Do I have to say it again? You and me right now! My best champion against yours and the winner gets both armies.'' 
 
 Glory smiled cruelly, almost intelligently, as I forged shocked understanding. I had been waiting for this moment for eons, but driving a God of Death to his own demise took time. And I had plenty of time. 
 
 `` Your best champion against my best champion? That can hardly be called fair. How about an armies of champions?'' 
 
 Glory's jaws and teeth snarled into an evil grin that would have dripped with malice if he had any organs or skin to drip. 
 
 `` I do n't need an army to defeat your so called champions. No hero has fallen inauspiciously. No gods or legends or any man of import is taken by your sickly sickle.'' 
 
 He looked disgustedly at the rust covered farmers tool with which I reaped my souls. I felt a twinge of worry as his eyes lingered on the pitted blade, but his eyes moved on and the twin bottomless depths focused their owners hatred on me with renewed vigor. 
 
 `` I'll fight your champion myself, you do n't have a single soul that could best me.'' 
 
 `` You know brother, one day you'll remember why you hate me so much, and it will be on that day you remember to fear me.'' 
 
 Glory looked suspicious for a moment, and I knew that I had unearthed some long forgotten memory, if only for a fleeting moment. 
 
 `` Bah! The day I fear you is the day that True Death comes for me. Will you fight me or will you be the same rotten coward you've always been?'' 
 
 `` Fine Brother, if you insist. Shall we meet with our champions in Elysium?'' 
 
 Glory laughed, it sounded like parchments scraping against stone in the wind. 
 
 `` You want to fight me in my home? Why not... Bring your armies so I wo n't have to move them after I've won.'' 
 
 Glory vanished in a whisper of smoke, no doubt gone to feast on the energy of lesser souls in preparation for his victory. I finally allowed myself a small smile. I spread my hands as though offering a gesture of welcoming and black smoke poured from the sleeves of my tattered cowl. 
 
 On top of the table rested two bone white figures wrapped in cloaks blacker than night. They both held scythes of unique shape and color. One figure was more tattered than the other, the bones a more sickly pallor of yellow than white, and the sickle of muted black that he held did not match his appearance. The other held a cruel looking sickle barbed with metal teeth like saw blades and his cowl looked like liquid blood mixed with obsidian. 
 
 I reached out and plucked the muted black sickle from the sickly looking figure and placed the rusted and decaying sickle in its hands. 
 
 `` Brothers, he forgot when man fell, he forgot when you fell, and he forgot that all that is left is the slow and inauspicious death of the universe.''

title: story-198
text:
“ Son of a female dog. You ’ ve got ta be shitting me, ” the words were out of my mouth as the thing I had just thrown in the trash reappeared in the box in front of me. It was a stupid, cheesy ass necklace I had made years ago out of bits of wood, stones, and bones back when I thought I was a real witch. 
 
 I grabbed the thing again, and tried dropping it in the trash once more. “ Can not discard quest item, ” the booming voice repeated as it reappeared in the box. So this was really happening, and I had somehow created some crazy quest item when I had never intended to. So I had to either hold onto the ugly thing for the rest of my life, or I could go turn the thing in and be done with it. 
 
 I clutched the necklace, and nothing happened. I slipped it over my head- tight fit- and a scroll appeared in my hand. I unrolled it, and read over the thing in a skim, and skipped to the end. No one ever read those damn things anyway. 
 
 “ Go to the witch in the swam to recover that which was lost, ” I read aloud. “ I never fucking lost anything! ” I told the scroll. Whatever. I rolled up the scroll, and left the boxes as they were. The only swamp I knew of was in the forest by the old house we used to live in. That house was where I made the necklace, and it was two counties over. 
 
 I packed up a quick bag, and trudged down the stairs. Both my parent were in the kitchen getting coffee, and talking about whatever it is that adults in this silly sim talk about. “ I have to go find a witch in the swamp. ” I told them shortly. 
 
 My mom instantly began pulling out snacks while my father grinned at me. “ Found your coming of age quest finally? I knew it would be something in those boxes! Well, take the wagon. You know the drill, you complete the quest or- ” 
 
 “ Or I never get a real meat body. Yeah, yeah. ” I took the food, and accepted the hug from my mom. I waved to my dad as I turned, and headed for the door. I snagged the keys, and went to the old station wagon my dad kept for god only knew what reason. As I loaded my crap in the car I sent off a quick message to my friends to let them know I had gotten my coming of age quest. I was stoked, but I couldn ’ t ever show that to my parents. 
 
 I dropped into the wagon, and grinned as I put the keys in the ignition. I may be on my own for it, but I wasn ’ t worried one bit. I was going to smash this quest out, and get a meat body. I had a few job offers already, and I couldn ’ t wait to be considered a real person! I fired up the car, and drove off to find my quest.

title: story-199

`` Goodnight Sarah, I love you'' my mother was always the best to me no matter what i had done that day. I look up from the pool of water in a basin made out of cloud and notice that I have been left alone. The others that were with me on the ride here must not need as much time to remember everything as I do, they must have joined everyone else already. 
 
 As I look back down I can see my two brothers playing in the pool, I wish I could say I love them right there since this is one of my happiest memories but all I manage is their names and a smile. `` Do you want to come swim with us Sarah'' Ryan says, while Kevin is climbing out of the pool and approaching me. He helps me out of my chair and lends me his hand so I do n't fall while I descend the steps into the water, Ryan comes over with a floaty to help me swim. 
 
 The image fades and i'm in my room blow drying my hair, its been dry for awhile but I like the feel of the warm air on my head. My side has been hurting a lot lately but I cant think of anything to say, I just keep rubbing it while my knuckles are getting raw from all the contact but it keeps the pain down a little. My Dad walks into the room telling me that I need to stop the blowdrier or my head will get too hot, he notices my rubbing and tear falls down his cheek. They have taken me to all the doctors but no one really knows whats wrong, my entire family sees how much pain i'm in but tries to keeps happy faces on for me. I just wish I could tell them how much I love all of them, but I can never manage more then a name or two. 
 
 `` Sarah'' I look up the place i am in is no longer empty, its my grandma but looking much younger and a lot healthier then I last saw her. `` You have been looking at your pool of memories much longer then is usual I was starting to get worried, its not normally allowed but I thought I come see whats taking so long'' grandma always a worrier. `` I just am remembering how much I wanted to tell everyone but could n't, even now its weird how I can express myself vocally to you''. `` Well you will get the chance to tell them everything when they get here, come on lets got get some tea and talk awhile like we never got to do before''

title: story-200
text:
Of all the revelations regarding the nature of the universe, none could be considered more humbling, or unnerving, than those that exposed how little about it was known, let alone understood. 
 
 Dr. Vargas thought of herself as an aficionado of ignorance -- not the sort of ignorance that emerged as an ingrown social condition -- rather, she practiced a tempered naivete relying on self-effacing curiosity and precision of mind. So when she came across the possibility that there lay beyond existing horizons of human perception a greater boundary, the woman of science was impelled to devoting her whole faculties in pursuit of this extraordinary truth. 
 
 However, what scientific endeavor, by virtue of its design, could not provide was a glimpse into the consequences of any given discovery. The mathematics that equated matter and energy, for example, had in its derivation no sentiment of violence. Yet it seemed the inevitable outcome of such an understanding was threaded into its conception, and arguably into its very fabrication. Dr. Vargas could not have foreseen the fate she had invited with her earnest and ignorant measures, no more than could have a mouse attempting to free its food from the spring of a loaded trap. 
 
 After years of pursuing the origin of a particular ultra-high-energetic emission, Dr. Vargas made a significant breakthrough while vetting the details of her work with one of her graduate students. The reason for its strength and clarity was not that the signal was originating from an immense phenomenon far away, but rather from somewhere simultaneous, another dimension. Attacking her chalkboard with the vigor of someone possessed, she filled the black expanse with her terse and shaky writing -- in a language that would have seemed alien to any passerby even without its near-illegibility. She and her graduate student stared upon the cobweb of mathematics in awe, realizing the implications of this new advancement. Now the nature of the signal made sudden sense. 
 
 The patterns that had seemed erratic before, now folded into elegant functions. Without the fog of previous misunderstanding, the beacon appeared brighter than ever. Something beyond the defined universe was attempting to make contact, and Dr. Vargas knew, though she did not express it then, they had to answer back. 
 
 The signal took fifteen years to crack. Enclosed within the beacon itself were instructions on replicating extra-dimensional communication. A couple more decades passed in the construction of a suitable device, a planetary accelerator with enough energy to agitate the foam of spacetime and manipulate its texture to carry information outside the bounds of relativity. Dr. Vargas observed the inaugural launch from the ISS, indescribably excited and filled with a sense of pride at the sight of the object in the distance, the reward of her commitment. 
 
 Once the preparation was complete, the device was initiated. It began to glow and pulse bright enough to eclipse the moon floating in the backdrop. As soon as it had powered up, the ring began to shut down. A moment of denouement passed and the entire crew cheered at their success. Dr. Vargas struggled to keep the tears back as everyone around her congratulated her. 
 
 Before long, while the others were still celebrating, she boarded the private shuttle NASA had afforded her and disbarked towards Earth. She wanted the ride home to reflect and maybe catch some shut-eye. In the excitement of the past few days, and arguably the recent half of her lifetime, she had given little consideration to rest. As the warm filtered air of the shuttle enveloped her and put her to sleep, she laid her head back and stared out the window at the moon hanging in the dark of space with the ring of the device superimposed over its bright ivory face. She smiled, knowing the world would never be the same and slept, unaware that the signal was not a beacon but bait. 
 
 -- -- --
