title: story-201
text:
( Some ASOIAF spoilers ahead! ) 
 
 He came ashore one day on the Fingers in an old, rotted rowboat that did n't look like it could sail over a steady stream, much less the Narrow Sea. Yet nobody in the surrounding towns had heard of him, nor of House Skyrim, where he claimed to hail from. His sigil was not of the Vale; none had ever seen the Crooked Dragon in a diamond that marked his shield. Even Lord Royce did not recognize it though he had traveled all of Westeros during his tournament days. The stranger called himself `` Dovahkiin,'' leading some to wildly speculate that perhaps he was Dothraki! But unlike the horse lords, he wore armor. And not the paltry iron plates that most hedge knights had; this seemed to be made of Dragon Bone, the strongest substance known in Westeros! How could such a piece have been forged?? 
 
 His mysterious identity and origin was practically forgotten once Daenarys Stormborn, daughter of the Mad King, attacked Storm's End with her fleet of Ironborn and slaves. Lord Baelish ordered an army from the Vale be raised and sent to aid Jon Connington and the Young Dragon Aegon, newly crowned Lord of the Stormlands. The stranger volunteered immediately, and it soon became known that his skill in weapons was unmatched, be it bow, sword, or ax. He preferred a warhammer, larger than even that of Robert Baratheon, that he named `` Volendrung'' He was risen to a knight after the Battle of Bronzegate, and attracted a loyal following of men. 
 
 After his decimation of the 9,000-strong Martell army with only 200 men, the legends soon spread. His men claimed that he was untouchable: that he could stop time and move through the battlefield like water over rocks. That he could spit ice and summon lightning to destroy his foes. That the very sound of his fury would throw a man from his horse. Others even claimed that he could breath fire, just like the dragons. It was thus that he earned his nickname, `` Dragon of the Vale.'' Lord Baelish ordered that Lord Dovahkiin be given command of the Vale's army and march to Summerhall to confront Daenarys and her invader forces. 
 
 On the same day that the Arryn Falcon appeared outside the ruins of Summerhall, the first winter snows that the Reach had seen began to fall. Soft flakes covered the opposing armies in a cold blanket of white. The men huddled in their tents, seeking the warmth of the fire and putting the battle off till the next day. Only one man was unaffected by the bone-chilling wind. He went forth alone and sat in the field between his camp and Summerhall, flying the Arryn banner and his own Diamond Dragon sigil of silver on black. On the third day, Daenarys and her mightiest mount Drogon rose to meet his challenge. 
 
 They say that the sounds of the battle could be heard from King's Landing. Soldiers from both camps came together and forgot their allegiances as they stood side-by-side and watched the duel. Lord Dovahkiin was fearless in the face of the dragons, hacking and slashing with his sword and bathing them in his fire. Danaerys' dragons fought back ferociously, ripping at his skin and scorching the field over and over till nothing but charred ash remained. 
 
 But the greater of these warriors could not be determined; their battle was interrupted by a runner from the Wall. He managed to utter two words before collapsing in exhaustion: 
 
 `` White walkers!''

title: story-202
text:
Three of a kind. I got this. 
 
 Famine had already opted out of this one. His winnings were n't in danger or anything, but he never liked risks. He must've had something, but the losses would have been too much compared to the winnings he'd earn. 
 
 Pestilence barely understood the game, but he played because he enjoyed spending time with his brothers. He'd opted in as well, but his pox-scarred face and yellow eyes radiated nothing but puzzlement. He must still be thinking about what combination he could make and whether or tnot they were legit. 
 
 Death, of course, knew the stakes. He knew everything. The oldest, the wisest, the strongest in some ways. He has been around for so long he mastered mundane time-killing things like poker, blackjack, charades, even twister. His perfectly smooth, long face not betryaing any emotion, his pale green eyes might as well be made of glass. 
 
 On the table were 5 cards. Ace of clubs, four of clubs, king of clubs, queen of spades and 2 of hearts. War held 2 kings, one of hearts and one of diamonds. Three of a kind. 
 
 Death was known to bluff every once in a while, his flawless face of steel unrelenting when calling or raising. Probably got the skills from all the professional poker players he'd'collected'. He knew how this game was played. But he did n't cheat. Death was fair, even in his cruelty of manipulation of other people. Even with the brothers he sometimes could n't stand. 
 
 Famine tried to peek over Death's shoulder, but one glance of the green glass eyes turned the attempt into a readjustment of the seat. 
 
 Death held a crust of earth and placed it on the table as a bet. 
 The crust of earth represented the fate of the human continent Africa, which Death swindled off of Famine three rounds earlier. He was still pissed about that one, but in rounds like these Africa was often traded. It's value was n't that high for the Horsemen, but if the Holy Court found out they were using the fates of the people living in the cradle of man as a bargaining chip in their monthly pokergames, they would probably lose their shit. 
 
 War had to call it with something. He had a nice thing going with the IS as of late, allthough it really is the only remarkable thing he had as of late. Syria was n't really in Death's interest, but then again, nothing really was. There was nothing that he was n't involved with, which made it difficult to establish values. 
 
 The War on Drugs however, was something he was willing to put up ont he table. It was a stable little thing that kept Texas, his favorirte American state, on edge for years on end. The conflict had died down a little over the years, and would be resolved soon, unfortunately. But that was n't enough. So he loaded up the conflict in Syria as well. That could use some serious escalation, considering all the refugees were pooring out like water through a sieve. 
 
 Pest's eyes widened so far his eyes alomst popped out. Famine whistled. Death called. It was the last round, the cards went on the table. 
 
 `` Three of a kind'', War said with a sense of glee and a big smile. 
 
 `` Flush'', Death said as he tossed down his cards. A 3 of clubs and a 6 of clubs. 
 
 War's smile melted off his face. He'd lost the Syrian conflict AND the War on Drugs in one fell swoop. 
 
 He rammed his fist so hard on the table, a chuck of the stone broke off and fell on his lap. 
 
 `` You cunt! How did you know!? How could you possibly know that your cards were better then mine!? ``, War exclaimed at the very top of his lungs. 
 
 A small smile creeped on Death's face. 
 
 `` Sorry, secrets are kinda my thing'', he said as he picked up the cards all around and began shuffling them with casual ease. 
 
 `` Bullshit!''. War's eyes were on blazing a red so hot and fiery, it would n't have been suprising for him to shoot laserbeams out of them. Last time that happened, Famine had to redesign half his mansion after the raging rant War went on. They had n't played twister since. 
 
 `` Sit your fat ass down, War. I'll let you keep your things, for Christ's sake''. 
 
 ``....What?''. 
 
 Death picked up the chunk of the table, reattacted it with a carpenter's efficiency and a whiff of stone-mending power. 
 
 `` No continent or conflict or batch of souls is worth our brotherhood, now is it? ``, he said as he picked up the avatars of War's conflicts and tossed them over. 
 
 `` Yeah, you're right Death. So how about you hand me back Africa while you're at it? ``, Famine said. 
 
 `` How about *you* give it back to me? I was n't done with Ebola and now I can start over because somehow, they made a bloody *cure* for it. Now I have to make a new design all over again and have been set back for *decades*, while you-''. 
 
 `` I won that game far and square. Just because you ca n't learn how to play a card game does n't mean...'' 
 
 Death simply looked around his brothers. Famine and Pestilence, arguing over silly little things and War somewhat sulkingly toying with the big blind and small blind chips. 
 
 *If only Conquest could have been part of this... *, Death wondered.

title: story-203
text:
A lot of people have really bratty kids. Not me. 
 
 In fact, originally I was n't even going to have kids. I did n't want to deal with the screaming, the diapers, the drain of my time and money, basically all the reasons you hear from people who are childless. I wanted to explore the world, start my own business, have passionate romances, and then retire at 50. When people asked me when I was going to start a family, my face looked like they just asked me what time it was while on fire. It just did n't register as a rational question. 
 
 Then, when it was announced that we could now create perfect children however we wanted, I gave it a little more thought. *I'm 33*, I thought. *Who's going to take care of me when I get older? What about my family name? My legacy? I do n't have all the time in the world, here. * 
 
 So, I went down to the labs and got started. They give you a massive control panel with buttons and sliders controlling every aspect of your child. I wanted a smart baby. But not too smart, I wanted them to be able to connect with others. So I slid the Intelligence slider to 87. I wanted my baby to be strong. But not too strong, I hated people who get caught up in their physical attributes over their personality and mind. So I slid the Strength slider to 80. But most of all, I wanted my baby to be self-sufficient, able to take care of itself. So I slid the Independence slider to 98. 
 
 I gave my baby perfect blue eyes. Soft, blonde hair. A high metabolism. Long eyelashes. Soft skin. Of course, mistakes were made. It took a lot of failed pregnancies and trips to the lab before I finally produced a baby that met my standards. 
 
 The first 10 years were a breeze. My child could change it's diaper within a few months, get groceries at age 5, and do the taxes by 9. I took all the trips I wanted, knowing that my baby was able to care for itself for as long as I needed it to. I gave my baby the perfect life. One I've wanted for as long as I've lived. It depended on no one. The fact that I did n't have to give it a lot of care was just a bonus. 
 
 So, I guess what I'm asking you, Dr., is why did it leave? I carried it for 9 months. I sacrificed my perfect life for it. I gave it *everything*. My baby's only 14. How does it think it can survive out there? I've called their cellphone and gotten no reply. I'm pretty sure their father knows where they are and he wo n't tell me. I do n't understand how anyone could do this to their own *mother*. 
 
 I *need* my *baby*...

title: story-204
text:
*Gone. Everything is now gone. * 
 
 The thought was never too far from Dr. Bill White ’ s mind whenever he came back to visit the desolate planet. As an archeologist, Bill ’ s spent his time imagining what life was like all those years ago before the cold settled in and even bacteria couldn ’ t survive. But imagination is a funny thing, he knew at one point Earth was filled with green life and dazzling clear sunlight, and it wasn ’ t too hard to picture. After-all, every simulated education experience taught the history of Earth and how the human race had to leave – had to escape. It was as simple as fact. At one point, Earth was beautiful. What is there to imagine? 
 
 The sun shone through the dust cloud haze in a rippling redish yellow. No warmth came from its light. 
 
 This expedition was supposed to focus on the vast ancient ruins of what they called Boston – a city sunk into the landfill that it was built on - but Bill and his team of three ventured a bit off course to what was once called something along the lines of Man or Mane. The exact name of this vast desert land northeast to Boston has been lost over the years, but they knew it was one of the more lush areas of the former United States. At one point the area was so thick with trees in certain spots, one couldn ’ t see more than ten feet deep. *Ha! * Bill thought, *Good luck finding a tree now*. 
 
 “ Guys… Guys… ” Sue Green ’ s voice crackled through his ear piece, “ Come over here. I found something. ” 
 
 Bill looked in Sue ’ s direction. She was stooped over an object of some sort, her form packed neatly in her tight fitted earth suit. Joan Perkins was already there, and Greg Smiles came over with the preservation container in hand. 
 
 Bill makes it over and looks down on could what only be described as a large paper brick. 
 
 “ Dr. White… I think it may be dangerous… ” Sue looks up to Bill, here green eyes can be seen through her visor. 
 
 The team members almost worshipped Bill. Not as if he were a god, but they knew he was different; they trusted his intuition. For the sake of the team, he had to maintain composure, but he was thrown off as well. He didn ’ t know what this was, but as archeologists, they needed to examine this brick. 
 
 “ Greg, ” Bill said, “ collect the object in the preservation container. We need to take it back to the base. We need to figure out what it is. ” 
 
 “ …but Dr. White, ” Sue said. 
 
 “ Now. ” Bill said, “ It is what we are meant to do. ” 
 
 The team felt it. They all did. This object brought them to that spot. They knew they needed each other to fully understand exactly what they were dealing with, and what actions they may need to take after they understood. 
 
 -- -- - 
 
 Bill White grew up in Xenosaturn with his brother George. Their parents might as well have been on earth for the amount of time they saw them. Bill understood what it was to be a leader. George taught him that. Everyone thought George was an idiot, but Bill knew better. George and him always had a connection. George would warn Bill whenever there seemed to be trouble – even if they were miles or worlds apart. Bill felt it in his bones. He could almost hear his brother ’ s voice whisper to him, in that deep voice he has, “ This is a Titan of trouble Billy. A Titan of trouble. T-I-T-A-N… Titan of trouble. ” Bill felt it now with the brick accompanying them back to base.

title: story-205
text:
`` Silence is Safety. Safety is Silence. Speech is danger. Speech is magic,'' the man on the television says, standing at a podium. A crowd would cheer, but they ca n't. Vocal suppression systems are engaged on the crowd. Shiro can see the crystalline pillars engraved with the speech suppression diagrams. Only the military is allowed to use magic for the purposes of suppressing speech. 
 
 Shiro used to wonder what it was like to be allowed to speak anywhere but Magical Suppression Zones. She does n't anymore, though. It's no use to wonder, because soon she's going to know. If all goes well, she'll be a Witch Hunter soon and she can speak whenever she wants. She rises, walking across her one room apartment. On one wall, her weights are racked up. In front of them, a treadmill. On the wall above her bed, there are practice swords and a number of rifles. 
 
 The television sits on a shelving unit that has hundreds of books shoved on it, shelves that take up the entire wall heading to the door. The only other interesting things in her room are the longsword in its sheath hanging on the doorknob and the rifle tucked in the corner by it - and the trash can with wrappers from the meals she buys at the restaurant downstairs. 
 
 The bathroom is waiting for her. This room is close to the thaumturgic suppression pillar outside of the building. It makes her uncomfortable. It's like a terrible pressure on her skin and inside of her body, like something gripping her heart and trying to throttle her soul. Still, she does n't have to be in here long. All she needs to do is grab her clothes. 
 
 The mirror catches her eye though, or rather, her reflection does. 
 
 Did people used to look like this? 
 
 She's not sure that's the right question. 
 
 Did *anyone* look like she does? 
 
 She doubts it. But she was born like this, with white hair and white eylashes, white eyebrows, white irises barely visible against the white of her eyes. That's why they named her Shiro after all. It was fitting. The running theory among the other Witch Hunter candidates is that her dad was n't human, or her mother was n't. She was born outside of a Thaumaturgic Suppression Zone, so it's not entirely impossible. 
 
 She's not sure. But she knows that practicing magic in order to become a Witch Hunter did n't really make her condition lessen. If anything, it made her skin more paper white, drained any color from her cheeks, from anywhere. She's mutated. Inhuman. Monstrous. 
 
 Strong. 
 
 That makes her smile. 
 
 Being strong is important for a Witch Hunter. 
 
 With the concern over her appearance out of the way, she works herself into panties and a bra that is n't particularly necessary with her less than generous endowment, following with a simple if rather heavy duty shirt and some plain white pants. Socks and gloves go next, all stored in the little wardrobe tucked in the bathroom's corner. 
 
 She positions herself in front of a mirror then, making sure that she looks alright. A little bit of makeup goes a long way on someone so pale, so that does n't take much time. She does have to work around her tattoos as well, red lines of various thickness covering almost every inch of her body, forming diagrams. Tiny, almost impossibly small letters form endless lines of interlocking and complex poetry - the result of her many years of research and development with the help of some Witch Hunter Candidate friends. Brushing her hair is easy, since it's cut so short. 
 
 She pauses for a moment, peering in the mirror. Going out on a day like this, during a Silence Rally, unnerves her. The people are n't always super fond of Hunters because they use magic - just like the monsters of the wildes and wastes. Still, if anyone messes with her, she's far more physically capable and well armed than most civilians. 
 
 Returning to her room, she grabs the only article of clothing she owns that is n't white, a gray canvas jacket with a large hood. Her sunglasses count too, she supposes, since they're black. With those on, she tugs the hood up to hide most of her face. 
 
 Silence, the man on the tv says as she grabs her gun and sword and heads out the door, is safety. Safety is silence. 
 
 Downstairs, the lovely woman who runs the restaurant greets her, warning her to be careful out there - all written on a small white board. Shiro nods, keeping her head down to avoid the stares of the various customers present inside. A few of them mutter some unsavory things, but she's out the door before they can notice. Her sword gets slung over her back, her rifle held in both hands. Most people do n't bother staring at people with guns in hand, not anymore. 
 
 It's commonplace. Everyone is armed in case of an emergency. 
 
 The Witch Hunter Office is located inside of Grand Military Central, which is just down the street. Her apartment is convenient, private enough, and cheap - all bonuses considering that the pay of Candidates is extremely low. The walk is long, however. People are gathered in the streets, having conversations via text message or writing on old fashioned tablets. The energy of the celebration is still there, but it's eerily silent - the only sounds are the shuffles of feet and breathing, cloth moving on cloth, cooking utensils moving on pans, and so forth. Flashing signs proclaim people are selling things, and holograms occasionally wave at people passing by. Shiro ignores all of them, keeping to the side, keeping her head down. 
 
 No one pays much attention to the tall white haired woman. They're all too busy staring at their phones. 
 
 She digs her own out, messaging her superior. 
 
 *Sir. I have concerns about the crowds and my movement through them without a registered Witch Hunter badge. Requesting permission to speak if necessary. * 
 
 The response comes quickly. 
 
 *Negative, Shiro. Permission denied. Only Witch Hunters may speak in thaumaturgic safety zones. I am en route. Try to be safe, will be there soon.'' 
 
 Shiro sighs and tucks her phone away, returning to her measured pace. Walking too quickly will only draw attention. If only she was allowed to speak, if anyone was... but it's too easy for normal people to accidentally cast. Magic woke up, so long ago, and when it did words became powerful. It takes practice to speak without accidentally using magic - and accidental magic kills either the user by way of power overdraw or causes chaos in the world around. Such things can not be allowed. 
 
 Unfortunately for her, a strong breeze comes rips her hood back, leaving her standing there in shock as her tattooed neck and face are exposed fully. The clicking and typing and sounds aplenty around her stop dead. 
 
 And then the typing returns with a new ferocity. Every eye is on her. 
 
 She tries to walk quickly, but a strong hand closes around her arm. She wishes she could protest, explain herself, but the people remember too well the recent incident with the speech terrorist who was marked on his skin not unlike she is. Someone reaches up and drags her sunglasses off. 
 
 That's all she can take. In an instant, her rifle is up, pressed to the cheek of the woman holding her sunglasses. Her sword is out, pressed to the neck of the man holding her arm. An enraged, fearsome expression spreads across her face. Her lips pull back, exposing a mouthful of razor sharp, pointed teeth. Those part as well and a breath so hot it is as steam hisses between them, rising into the cold air of autumn. 
 
 Before she can shoot or stab, or anyone else can dray a gun, a shocking sound rings out. 
 
 `` Enough!'' a man shouts. The crowd parts before him. His heavy armor clanks slightly as he walks. Unlike Shiro, he has manifested a magical weapon - a rather thick axe that he holds with ease in one hand. The wicked blade glints black in the light. `` Unhand that young woman. She belongs to me!'' 
 
 Everyone immediately steps back from Shiro. She keeps her rifle raised one handed, trained on the woman holding her sunglasses. Her posture changes however. She drops low, almost into a crouch. Her sword waves slowly, pointing at various people close to her. She looks like a beast backed into a corner. 
 
 The crowd parts and the huge man marches right past her to the woman holding the sunglasses. His thickly armored hand is held out in front of her. It takes almost a minute for her to put the glasses in his hand before turning and fleeing fearfully. He turns and kneels next to Shiro. 
 
 `` Easy there, Shiro. Come on, calm down. You're safe now,'' he tells her, setting the glasses on her nose. Her eyes flick to him and for a long moment she remains like that, teeth bared and panting steam. Slowly, she rises, lowering her weapons. `` That's it, girl. Come on, let's get the fuck out of here.'' 
 
 She nods. He walks through the crowd and she follows quickly behind, not bothering to look at anyone around him. He understands the people's fear, but they disgust him. They are the protectors, the ones who fight the monsters and hunt the lands, protect the farms... 
 
 `` I'm sorry you have it so rough, Shiro. You're a very noticeable Witch Hunter, and your non-human qualities make it tough to resist being vicious,'' he says quietly. She looks up to him and shrugs, slinging her rifle and sheathing her sword. 
 
 *I'm really sorry, I got scared, * she signs to him, her hands doing what her mouth ca n't. 
 
 He laughs and reaches down, patting her head. Shiro is tall, at six feet, but this man... he's at least eight or nine feet tall, and broad enough that doorways are a problem. 
 
 `` Relax, little Shiro. It's alright. They would have done bad things to you, that's why I came some quickly.'' 
 
 She nods again, and they fall silent as they head for the Grand Military Central fortress. 
 
 ( Part two? Should I? )

title: story-206
text:
EXT. Australian Outback - Day 
 
 The sea of sand stretches out for miles in every direction with nothing to be seen except for a lone dwelling. A 
 
 tall slim man in a gray suit and hat walks across the plains from seemingly nowhere and steps onto the porch of 
 
 this rustic home and takes off his hat. Only the fans fighting to keep the heat at bay can be heard. 
 
 INT. House - Continuous 
 
 He enters the home hears a woman gagging. He enters the kitchen and sets his hat at the table. He sees a young 
 
 woman with tears in her eyes choking. He casually steps behind her as she is jerking violently struggling to 
 
 breathe and puts his hand on her shoulder. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 Rest and be at peace Alice. 
 
 As he says this she falls limp and her breathing stops. As soon as her face hits the table a cry is let out and for 
 
 the first time Robert looks concerned. He walks through the house towards the cry and sees legs kicking in a crib. 
 
 He stares at the crib in eyes open wide. 
 
 He walks quickly back to the kitchen and picks up the phone. There is no tone. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 Damn it. 
 
 He rushes back to the infants room and stands in the door way while he stares at the crib. His eyes are wide and 
 
 glossy and his mouth hangs low. He begins pacing the room trying to think of what to do. He grabs a curtain from 
 
 the window and breaks one of the slats from the crib. 
 
 He ties the bottom of the curtain around the slat and then shimmies the curtain under the baby. He then takes both 
 
 ends of the curtain and passes the slat through the hoops on the top of the curtain and secures the baby bundle and 
 
 hangs it around his neck. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 You'll be alright. 
 
 He returns to the kitchen with his improvised baby sling and grabs a bottle of water from the refrigerator and his 
 
 hat from the table. He puts his hat on his head and exits the home. 
 
 EXT. Australian Outback - Continuous 
 
 Robert heads off down the long unending road with the baby in tow. He walks until the day turns to night and he 
 
 stops to lay the baby down with the sling spread out. He looks for brush and gathers it into a pile. He pulls a 
 
 cigarette case from his inside pocket and retrieves his lighter and starts a fire. He sits there staring into the 
 
 fire and looking at the child. His face droops as he stares at the child. The baby kicks and lets out a small coo 
 
 with a smile staring back at Robert. Robert laughs and smiles at the baby with a small tear rolling from his eye. 
 
 He wipes the tear and chuckles as he gazes at the child. 
 
 EXT. Australian Outback - Morning 
 
 The remains of the fire are nothing but smoke and smoldering ash. Robert is already off again with his precious 
 
 cargo in tow in his sling. Eventually Robert comes upon a trailer. A weak smile comes across his face and is soon 
 
 gone as he looks down at the child. He looks back to the trailer and grimaces as he heads to it. He removes his hat 
 
 and knocks on the door. A man with no shirt and a mullet answers the door. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 
 Well, you're not Harris. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 
 Please, I need your help. I found this child abandoned at another home about twenty miles back. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 What? 
 
 Robert pulls the sling wide so he can see the baby. The baby lets out a small cry. 
 
 -- FELICIA -- 
 What is that? 
 
 A woman rushes to the door to see the source of the noise. Her face lights up at the sight of the child. 
 
 -- FELICIA -- 
 Come on in. 
 
 She reaches out to grab Robert's hand but he pulls it back and holds his hands up. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 Sorry, I'm sick. Would n't want you to catch it. 
 
 INT. Trailer - Continuous 
 
 Robert enters the home following Felicia to the kitchen. Toby shuts the door behind them. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 Well, feel free to make yourself at home mate. Can I get you a beer? 
 
 Robert sits at the kitchen table and lets out a sigh. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 Actually, if I could have some water that would be perfect. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 Yeah, of course. 
 
 Felicia reaches out to Robert with a smile on her face. 
 
 -- FELICIA -- 
 Could I hold the baby? 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 I do n't suppose it would hurt anything. 
 
 Robert stands up and holds the sling open so Felicia can grab the baby. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 I never got your name mister... 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 It's Robert. Thank you for letting us in out of the sun. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 Happy to help. So where are you heading? 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 I'm trying to find the nearest hospital I can leave the baby with. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 That's nearly two hundred miles away. 
 
 Toby sighs and looks to down the hall. He gestures to Robert. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 Here, lem me show you something. 
 
 EXT. Australian Outback - Continuous 
 
 They head out the back door together and look off into the distance where the road winds through the canyons. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 It's a long drive out that way. About 80 miles before you hit town. Then you'd need to head east another 120 miles. 
 
 Robert steps forward and places his hand over his eyes trying to see out as far as he can. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 We could give you a ride first thing tomorrow if you want. 
 
 Robert turns around to face Toby. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 Really? That'd be gr- 
 
 The crack of the wood accross Robert's jaw sends him reeling. The blood pools next to his face in the sand. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
'Licia! Come get in the car! Bring the baby! 
 
 Toby runs around the trailer kicking sand as he goes. He rips the door open on a faded red station wagon and jumps in the seat. The engine reluctantly turns over and with a cough and a wheeze it roars to life. Toby hits the gas and kicks up dirt while spinning the wheels. He whips the car in front of the house and swings the passenger door open and yells out. 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 Come on! 
 
 Felicia runs out the front door holding the baby her eyebrows raised and gets in the car. The car speeds away towards the canyons. 
 
 INT. CAR - Sunset 
 
 Felicia looks at Toby with her eyebrows furrowed. 
 
 -- FELICIA -- 
 What did you do?! 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 We're taking the baby. He wo n't be following us. 
 
 -- FELICIA -- 
 Why are we taking the baby? 
 
 -- TOBY -- 
 That's Alice Greene's kid. Thomas Greene's grandson. As in Greene Aerospace. We bring this baby back to him and we'll be sitting pretty. 
 
 -- // -- 
 I do n't think you'll be doing anything pretty anymore Toby. 
 
 Toby looks in the mirror and sees Robert in the backseat without so much as a bruise on him. Before Toby can move Robert has wrapped his hand around his throat. His neck begins to smoke and sizzle and Toby opens his mouth to scream but his voice ca n't escape, just the popping sounds of his flesh cooking echoing out his esophagus. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 I can make it as gentle as the breeze from the flap of a butterfly's wings. I can also make it the most excruciating pain ever wrought in this mortal realm. Felicia dear, now would be a good time to grab the wheel. 
 
 Felicia wheeping while holding the baby reaches one hand over to hold the wheel. Toby grabs Robert's arm with both his hands trying to get free but winces and instantly pulls his hands off of him with his skin bright read and smoking. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 You're not getting out of this Toby. 
 
 Robert tightens his grip on Toby's neck and his flesh begins to turn to ash under his hand. Toby's entire body begins to smoke and glow until there is nothing left but ash. Robert pops the car out of gear and it slows to a stop. The backdoor opens and Robert steps out and opens the front door and the ash blows away. Robert sits down and shuts the door. Felicia is shaken with tears streamed down her face. 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 I'm not going to kill you Felicia. 
 
 -- FELICIA -- 
 Wh- why not? 
 
 -- ROBERT -- 
 Someone needs to hold the baby.

title: story-207
text:
`` they're after me I do n't know who they are or what they want but they are n't going to stop!'' - @ TheFoRealK0NK0W 
 
 It all started when Shane Matherson, known as K0NK0W to his fans, began work on his latest techno album. 
 `` this time, no more mash-ups no more kid stuff I'm going to explore sound and rhythm in ways no ones ever done'' He used Twitter to keep in touch with his fans. They were few but fiercely loyal. 
 
 A month later he released the first single on Soundcloud. It was called bEASt. `` this is somthing you here all the time but not like this!'' the song consisted the warning tones of the Emergency Alert System, commonly heard on radio and TV broadcasts in required weekly tests, chopped and skewed into something resembling a melody, over a throbbing bass-line. his fans loved it but it was ignored by the internet at large. 
 
 Weeks go by and Matherson retweeted a Youtube link from one of his fans, `` check this out this shit is crazy''. The video was captured from from the desktop of YouTube user T3chn0mast3r451 as he ran the bEASt through an SSTV decoder. K0NK0W's song brought a green line to jagged life and a small window began to display line by line a black and white image of a room with drawn curtains and the upper half of a woman's head. From her nose down the picture was distorted, too garbled to make out. The the description explained that SSTV stood for Slow Scan Televison a method of sending and receiving images using sounds, similar to how an old dial-up modem works. It also gave an account of the poster's discovery of the image, the odd pulsing at certain points in the song reminded him of SSTV codes he'd played around with in college. It was n't encrypted using any of the standard codes he found online so he brute forced it using algorithms he programed into the SSTV decoder himself. he added how cool it was that K0NK0W hid this easter egg in his song for his hardcore fans to find. Those who left comments remarked about how the eyes of the woman in the picture creeped them out `` they look so dead''. Matherson himself left a comment saying he had no idea the image was there. After some back and forth Matherson and T3chn0mast3r451 agreed the rest of the image must exist in the original EAS sound file he used to make the song. 
 
 Two days later T3chn0mast3r451 returned to Youtube with a new video. Taking the EAS test message Matherson had recorded off the radio and running it through his modified decoder revealed nothing. but when the sound file was slowed down 113 % the decoder was able to display an image. 
 
 The woman's face filled in line by line revealing a dark pit of gore where her lower jaw should have been. The barrel of a shotgun disappeared into what used to be her mouth apparently propping up her lifeless body. The words `` It is done'' were written in white block letters across the bottom. 
 
 Within minutes T3chn0mast3r451's Youtube account was deleted moderators cited copyright violations. An hour later his new account, T3chn0mast3r452, posted a rant video. `` You ca n't shut me up! people Demand to know what's going on here!'' he proceeded to go on bringing up chem-trails and Benghazi and signed off by saying he would hire a `` Jew lawyer'' and `` sue Youtube back to the stone-age''. After that his account went dark. 
 
 K0NK0W's Twitter account was deleted but not before he posted a series of paranoid ravings about unknown assailants following him home and watching his house from a black van across the street. 
 
 Matherson was found dead in his mother's house. He died of an apparent drug overdose. The authorities labeled it a suicide based on the fact that he had deleted all of his social network accounts and left a note on his nightstand. `` It is done.''

title: story-208
text:
Krystal and I were sitting around one of the conference tables after a research seminar at UC Berkeley and we were discussing how to approach this biotech assignment that Professor Campbell had given. It was really late in the day and Krystal was dreary with exhaustion and wanted nothing more than to just get in her car and go home. I sympathized with her. 
 
 “ Krys, it ’ s alright. I can run up the abstract for this paper. Go on home. ” Running up abstracts is tedious work because of the wording and the verification process by the science community and finally the publication. However, I really owed her for saving my ass earlier in the quarter for running this experiment on a hormone we were testing in mice, so I offered to help out. I have nothing going on in my life right now anyway, not since I haven ’ t been able to find a TA gig this quarter and personally, I needed the break to begin with. 
 
 “ No… ” replied Krystal groggily. “ Here, just let me see your phone real quick and I should be able to upload all the documents in a heartbeat… Please? ” Abashedly, I gave up my phone. She ’ s just lucky I don ’ t have anything dirty hidden on there ( anymore ). While she was on it she muttered under her breath “ …shit. ” That caused my eyebrow to rise. “ Something the matter? ” 
 “ No, I just accidently logged into my personal account. I ’ m sorry. ” 
 “ Oh that ’ s alright, just make sure you log out. Okay Krys…? ” 
 
 Krystal eyes glazed over at the screen for a few seconds without acknowledging the question, her fingers a sloppy mess of pure function with the promise of home pushing them forward. By the end of the minute she was handing the phone back and she had her backpack slung around her shoulders, already taking great strides toward the doors. 
 
 “ I guess I ’ ll see you tomorrow then! ” I exclaimed. I was answered with a harried thud from the heavy wooden door. I wonder what could be making her so tired, I thought. Bling! went my phone, as a message popped up on the screen. Oh! I looked down to see what it was, expecting her, but it… seemed to be reminder of some sort. Pick up Alex ’ s drumsticks from Post Office. Alex was Krystal ’ s boyfriend, so it seems as though she really didn ’ t hear me when I told her to log out. Krystal was always like that: living in her own little world. 
 
 I was searching through the Google app, which I never really use so it was difficult getting myself oriented at first trying to find the Log Out button. It ’ s got ta be in here somewhere, I thought on my way out the door and back to my dorm. The app was opened right over her calendar, and boy was it full! I had never seen so many events all squeezed into one big month—and they were all color-coded too. The calendar had many business events, naturally. Things about her boyfriend, things about school, things about work. But these things never really seemed to bother my work-aholic friend in the past… I must admit, I began searching for the cause of such a change in her mental functionality. For her to leave a personal Google account open on someone else ’ s phone was something she would never do in a million years. 
 
 I started by looking at the current week, which was more full than the calendar had ever looked. It was filled with all the ordinary things… but somehow they got doubled. It was almost as if she were living two of her lives, which is a miracle she ever got anything done. I found myself taking a moment to sit down on one of the campus benches, I was so entrenched. Whatever could be the cause of such desperation? Surely she was desperate, and it was my duty as her friend to make sure she was safe. 
 I found many counseling sessions start to pop up starting about two weeks ago and then I really started to feel bad. How could I not have noticed!? I needed to confront her on all this sometime, and soon. I looked into the next week and it was just a lego box of events. What on Earth was she doing, working herself to death? 
 Wait… 
 
 The calendar… comes to a halt after next week?? “ What the…? ” I muttered under my breath. Did she simply not get to that week yet? I clicked on the date she stopped. The day was titled, `` last day on earth…'' In it was a note: 
 
 What ’ s the point. There ’ s no way I can stop the pathogen from spreading now. Game Over. 
 
 Under files for the day was a jpeg titled, “ Game Over. ” I opened it. It was a microscopic image of the virus we were currently doing a research paper on for the class.
