title: story-221
text:
They looked on as the new star blossomed on the earth. Slowly more and more of them gathered on the strange marshy land far from their conception to watch the star rise. Higher and higher the bright burning light flew leaving behind a glorious pillar of smoke, leaving behind a land broken and battered, leaving behind a cradle out grown. Leaving behind the stories and myths of a fledgling race and reaching for the stars. 
 
 The figures watched the last of them leave on their ark to the stars. Once they had taken hero and lifted them up and placed them in the heavens. Once they had fed on the smoke that rose from their fires. Once they had commanded imagination, inspiration, horror and honor. Now they commanded nothing. Now they spoke nothing. Now they could only watch and wonder. 
 
 Where were they going. The people who were both their creators and children. What would they see out among the hero's they had placed in the night sky. When they walked path made of milk that the gods themselves had spilled, what would they find. Would there be more creations like themselves out above the infinite dome of the sky? Would they remember them, at least in myth like in the ages that had already gone by? 
 
 One thing was certain, of it there was no question: man was leaving the old gods behind. 
 
 When the light of the ark was invisible, indistinguishable from all the other points in the sky, they turned to look at eachother. Faces of all shape and color looked at each other. Some looked like sisters. Some looked like brothers. Some looked like twins in slightly different cloths. Thor turned to Zeus, Zues looked and Jupiter, Jupiter glanced at Ohdinn. Shiva reached for the hand of Akman-Rah. Djinn, Fey, Sadder, and Nymph reached for their instruments. 
 
 Quietly the song began. 
 
 *Man long ago you made us. 
 In image like yours you created us 
 Reflected in us your light and your dark 
 Go forth and remember 
 
 Lessons we taught you already knew 
 The lies that we told one day you out grew 
 We'll fade away for we can not stay 
 Go forth and remember 
 
 Your home is undone the wars are unwon 
 Robbed from the cradle you have become 
 Greater than we you hoped to be 
 Go forth and remember 
 
 Though you forgot us and though we are hurt 
 Time will go by and soon out of the dirt 
 New ones to slay us and take your place 
 Go forth and remember* 
 
 And then the song could n't go on. For they were unbound. Man had cut their last ties. The gods impact finally had eroded away. As those people left any, chance they might find the books that stored the god's names died. No one would remember them. No one could remember them. 
 
 All the gods watched each other fade. 
 
 They watched their ideas die.

title: story-222
text:
`` Dear Lord Bolton, 
 
 & nbsp; 
 
 Flee while you still can. 
 
 We thought the Baratheon host was three days' ride West. We were wrong. After just half a day, our forward cavalry spotted campfires, and we made ready for battle. At daybreak on the second day after riding out of Winterfell, we joined in battle. 
 
 It seems the False Baratheon King found some unholy force of pirates, or maybe a group of corrupted maesters. Regardless, we were defeated entirely and terribly, without ever crossing a sword or enduring an arrow. 
 
 The enemy had only about a hundred men in formation, but their ranks included around five and ninety of some variance of warbeast never before seen by my eyes. Their low flat frame had no eyes, mouth, ears, or fur. Just a long snout that spit smoke and terror. I'd suggest they were crafted by the hands of man, but even with sorcery such a feat could not be possible, nor permitted by the Gods above. 
 
 With our advantage in the thousands, and the speed of our mounted troop, we rapidly encircled the Baratheon force ( who were too craven to even display the stag, or any other sigil. ) They formed a pitifully small circle, defending nothing more than a snow laden field. We charged. We died. 
 
 I was observing from the rear. You may not believe me, but the southron bastards somehow... they wielded thunder as a weapon all their own. The booms were ceaseless and ferocious, and each one somehow tore the very fibers of man and horse asunder. The men held staffs that they used to quickly whip up thundercracks, while their mounts boomed and bellowed death upon us. 
 
 Lord Bolton, the stag's Red God may well have visited the battlefield this day. 
 
 Our troops stumbled, fell, turn, and fled. Not a Frey soul ever reached their lines. I saw less than six and thirty escape the killing field. I am now writing this several miles away, and can still make out the broken whinnies and cries of my fallen force. 
 
 The Manderly host did not join the fray, either through treachorous intent, fortunate tardiness, or some other hand of fate. I do not know what became of them, but I know I will not be returning to Winterfell. 
 
 If you value your life, you will bend the knee or flee before this force. Against a normal army, skill in wit or swordplay can win a black day. But there is no earthly skill that can defend against the sudden explosion of the horse you trust in battle. There is no wall that could resist this power and these beasts. There is no hope. 
 
 I am sorry. Please spare some others this fate. 
 
 -Hosteen Frey 
 
 -- - 
 & nbsp; 
 - 
 
 Colonel Mikhail Katukov surveyed the ruined enemy charge. 
 
 *'' Stalin would be proud. `` * 
 
 He took a deep drag of the cigarette and adjusted his warm fur hat. Since the disorienting change in scenery, the temperature had dropped substantially, and he had begun to sweat. 
 
 *'' These flags do n't look German... Plus full cavalry charge against my T34's? Hmm...,'' * Colonel Katukov took another drag as he processed the incredible victory just won for the Motherland. 
 
 *''... must be Polish brigade. Crazy Bastards. `` * 
 
 Mikhail flicked his cigarette into the shallow snow, turned to address the Fourth Guards Tank Brigade, and removed his hat. It must have gotten almost all the way up to -5 or 6 degrees. He smiled. 
 
 *'' Looks like mild winter is coming. `` *

title: story-223
text:
I groaned when I spotted the package on the doorstep. Just what I needed on a Monday morning… 
 
 I carefully stepped over it and unlocked the door to my little gift shop. As I set down my bag and shrugged out of my heavy parka, woolly hat and thick-knit scarf I considered leaving the package for my assistant, Jaime, to ‘ discover ’: let her deal with it. 
 
 But that wouldn ’ t be fair. Sighing, I strode back through the shop floor. Opening and closing the door as quickly as I could to keep the chilly winter air out, I snatched up the parcel. I shivered, partly from cold and partly from what I knew was inside, and dropped the frost-covered box on the counter by the till. 
 
 Coffee. I needed coffee before I could deal with this. I turned up the heating and made for the back room. 
 
 Our little coffee machine was whirring away when I heard the bell behind the front door tinkle. Jaime ’ s heels clicked, paused, then clicked again louder and louder. 
 
 “ What is *that* on the counter? ” she asked as she burst through the door to the back room. 
 
 “ It ’ s- ” I started, unsure of how to gently explain it to my new assistant, “ it ’ s payment. An order. ” 
 
 “ Payment? ” frowned Jaime, unravelling the orange scarf from her long neck. 
 
 I sighed, with every new assistant this aspect of my business was hard to explain, “ from a customer who can ’ t come in during the day. ” 
 
 The groove between Jaime ’ s eyebrows deepened as she grew more and more confused, “ but it ’ s covered in blood? ” 
 
 “ What? ” I yelped, jumping up from my chair; the box had certainly not been covered in blood when I ’ d picked it up. 
 
 I hurried past the dazed Jaime and into the shop, groaning as I saw that my assistant was right. Now that the frost had melted, the weathered cardboard box was stained a deep red and congealed blood was oozing from the corners. 
 
 “ How many times, how many times before they learn to package it properly? Just put it in some Tupperware for goodness sake! ” I cried, exasperated. 
 
 Jaime was staring at me with an expression somewhere between amusement and concern. 
 
 “ Vampires, ” I sighed, “ ever since that stupid vampire equality act came in I legally have to accept payment in blood. ” I gestured to the sticky box, “ unfortunately, they are n't great at packaging the damn stuff. ” 
 
 I carefully pried the lid open. 
 
 “ Ew, ” said Jaime as the pungent smell reached our nostrils, she craned her neck to look inside, “ they left a note. ” 
 
 “ Their order, ” I explained. 
 
 *Dearest Shopkeep*, the note read, *I would very much like to order one pair of your blue woollen mittens, a striped scarf in blue and red and two of the delightful pink tea cosies in your window. One for my mother-in-law and one just for me! Might I also inquire when you plan to start selling Christmas wares this year? My family and I do love a good Christmas jumper we even got one for the dog last year! I enclose payment of 1 litre of blood, equivalent to 50 English pounds, I do hope this covers it. I shall return at midnight to collect the order. * 
 
 *Sincerely, * 
 
 *Ivan. * 
 
 “ Is this a prank? ” asked Jaime, “ I thought vampires were all dark and gloomy. And aren ’ t they supposed to trade in their blood at the hospital for human blood or currency? ” 
 
 “ They ’ re supposed to, ” I nodded, “ but they ’ re… well, they ’ re kind of dumb. And *stubborn*. They can ’ t think why any commodity would be more valuable than blood and of course it ’ s easier to give us blood than to exchange it first. But then I have to go exchange it for money myself, well, I do when it ’ s not spilled everywhere… ” 
 
 I picked up the blood-soaked plastic baggie the blood had been packed in. *Idiots*. 
 
 “ As for the dark and gloomy part, ” I continued dropping the whole box into the bin, “ Ivan is surprisingly nice. He ’ s always buying teapots and cups and cosies. He even sent me a Christmas card last year, with a picture of his family on it. Of course, he forgot vampires can ’ t have their photos taken so it was just some headless jumpers and a Dachshund dressed as Santa… ” 
 
 Jaime barked a laugh, “ he actually sounds kind of sweet. ” 
 
 “ He is, ” I smiled. I had to admit the handwritten letters the vampires sent as order forms made a nice change from the abrupt textspeak I usually received from online, human customers. 
 
 “ What about the order? ” asked Jaime, “ you can ’ t exchange spilled blood for sterling, so you can ’ t accept the payment, can you? ” 
 
 I shrugged, “ technically, no. But you know, I ’ m feeling festive. I might just let him have them this time. ” 
 
 The rest of my customers that day, thankfully, paid with money. At the end of the day, after waving Jaime goodbye, I closed up shop. On the doorstep I left a package of mittens, scarves and tea cosies wrapped in brown paper and placed inside a cool bag with a set of plastic Tupperware.

title: story-224
text:
“ …you ’ re not dead yet. ” 
 
 The words echoed as the dream started to fade. It was a dream I have not had in centuries, but it is still every bit as jarring as the first time. I don ’ t think I will ever forget that first time, lying on a cot in a tent in South Celtica 56 BC. I think I finally succumbed to the pain of my septic shoulder and passed out. The dream was made all the more vivid by my fevered state. I saw myself from above, my right shoulder covered by a bloodstained bandage, my skin pallid and gleaming with sweat. A man walks in to the tent and glances at the ceiling from where I am watching. Although his features are obscured, I recognize a look of grim determination. He walks to the side of my cot and looks down at my unconscious body. The man seems so familiar, although I can never see his face; I am sure I know him. After a moment he kneels beside me and whispers in my ear. 
 
 “ Faustus Salonius Vespillo, the wounds you have suffered in valiant service to Gaius Julius Caesar and his Legio IX Hispana are grave; but do not fret, the pain will soon subside. I have seen what greatness awaits for you, and you must trust me. Do not lose hope, do not despair. Now get up, soldier, you are not dead yet. ” 
 
 “ …not dead yet ” What bullshit, I totally died that night. When the dream faded that first time I woke up Here. That was 1,276 years ago. I twist the words around in my head, looking for meaning. I can not shake the heavy feeling in the pit of my stomach that this is more than just coincidence that I had that dream again today. Coffee will help. 
 
 I pull up my schedule for today as I take my first sip. “ Dammit. ” I mutter in to my mug as I look over the day ’ s docket. Today is the yearly projections meeting upstairs, it ’ s going to be a long night. Maybe that dream was an omen after all, I really hate these annual meetings. Debating between professionalism and comfort, I figure if they are ever going to take me seriously upstairs I should at least dress the part. I put on my favorite dark gray suit and head to the office. 
 
 Sheila, the boss ’ s receptionist, e-mailed on my way in to let me know I would be doing today ’ s pick-ups briefing alone, it seems Mabuz had something come up this morning. I will have to ask him about that later today. The briefing goes smoothly, and I head to the bosses office. Sheila greets me as I walk in. 
 
 “ Mornin ’ hun. Hope the briefing went well without the boss. ” 
 
 “ Just fine, nothing too tricky today. I ’ m a bit early, is he ready for our meeting? ” 
 
 “ Oh sure, go right in, he just had some tricky cases that he wanted some more time to go over a bit more in-depth before assigning them. ” 
 
 “ Thanks Sheil, have a good morning. ” 
 
 “ You too! ” 
 
 As I walk toward his door I think to myself “ That ’ s odd, we usually go over the more sensitive cases together. ” I let myself in without knocking, a habit that has been abandoned after working closely together for four centuries. Mabuz is seated at his desk, his suit jacket loosely hung over the back of his chair. He looks up from the file that he is reading. Surprisingly it is a paper copy, this must be something really special, or very, very old. A second paper file lies on his desk. 
 
 “ Faustus, you are here early. I take it this morning ’ s briefing went well? ” 
 
 “ Very well, pretty easy schedule of collections today. Is that the case that made you cancel this morning? ” 
 
 “ It ’ s one of two, I think we might have to take care of these directly. They are quite… unique. ” 
 
 “ Unique? How so? ” 
 
 “ Well this one ” Gesturing to the manila folder in his hand. ” seems as though there is some upstart Indian prince refusing to commit his forces to battle because of some crisis of conscience. ” 
 
 “ Arjuna? ” 
 
 “ Could it be anyone else? ” 
 
 “ I guess not, he really is a pain in the ass. ” A smile crosses my face. “ So how long have you been waiting to say ‘ Gaze upon me and despair, for I am become Death? ’ ” 
 
 “ Don ’ t, just don ’ t. You know how it works Here. I haven ’ t even had the chance to say it yet and the story was first written down like 1,700 years before I died. I still don ’ t think Arjuna has figured out that it was me in that chariot. It boggles the mind. ” 
 
 “ Well, that does seem worthy for a direct visit; but I don ’ t see why you needed to skip the briefing this morning, I mean you can kind of cheat. ” I joke as I motion towards a copy of the *Bhagavad Gita* on his bookshelf. 
 
 “ That I can, but this other case also requires a delicate hand, and I have been deliberating all morning. ” 
 
 “ Oh? What is so special about it? ” 
 
 “ That is something you will find out when you go do the collection. ” 
 
 “ Nothing more you can give me than that? ” 
 
 “ No need, while it is a delicate situation, it should prove to be a fairly easy job. I trust that you know what to do. ” 
 
 A smile flashes across my face. “ Well, I don ’ t think you made me your assistant just because Caesar told you he remembered promoting me to Captain. ” 
 
 “ Well, it did help. ” He replied with a laugh. “ Anyway, we should handle these before this evenings meeting, so it looks like we will have to skip our usual lunch. I will have Sheila pick us up something for when we return. ” 
 
 Mabuz rose from his chair and quickly put on his jacket and handed me the file from his desk as he walked out of his office. I flip the file open, much to my surprise it is almost fully redacted, the only thing that didn ’ t earn a thick black bar is the STC, Space-time Coordinate, code. “ What the hell am I supposed to do with this? ” I ask the empty office. Well, he did say it should be an easy pick up; I guess we will just play this by ear. As I stare at the SPC trying to commit it to memory, it tugs at a piece of my mind. It feels familiar, but I know it ’ s not a place and time that I have visited. I quickly make my way to departures, a massive room with a series doors with rolling metal shutters. After the morning rush the room is empty, and eerily quiet. I approach the closest door and concentrate on the STC. The code flashes brightly in my mind, and quickly my mind goes blank as the metal shutter raise with a quiet *thwick* revealing a familiar inky darkness. I step through the portal and into a small tent, I quickly glance up as I take in my surroundings. Before me lies a pale man, his shoulder bandaged and bloody. I stand at his side as I realize where I am. After a moment I kneel and whisper to him. 
 
 “ Faustus Salonius Vespillo, the wounds you have suffered in valiant service to Gaius Julius Caesar and his Legio IX Hispana are grave; but do not fret, the pain will soon subside. I have seen what greatness awaits for you, and you must trust me. Do not lose hope, do not despair. Now get up, soldier... ”

title: story-225
text:
Another month, another fat envelope from the Career-Comp, and the corridor of small rooms was once again filled with anxious parents waiting for their results, each with a bassinet filled with a newborn, not even one month into the world. 
 
 Here we go again. Deep breath. deep breath. First door. 
 
 `` Mr. and Mrs. Jones, with newborn son Henry? Your results are in. Would you care to read them for yourselves first or would you like me to do the honors? Very well, according to the Career-Comp, your son will become... a wasteland scavenger. Yes, I can see you're both very proud, Mr. Jones, you are a scholar by trade I understand? Mrs. Jones, a dancer? Then I'm sure you understand the value of a solid early childhood education in the basics of metallurgy, appraisal, and acrobatics? Good luck to all of you, and especially you, little scamp. Please see the nurse for your vaccination schedule, we recommend extra vigilance with the tetanus and hepatitis series for that career path.'' 
 
 Well, that one was easy. Lucky one. Sure better than starting the day off with a prediction slip that reads `` This Space Intentionally Left Blank''. Ok, next. Next. Open the door and -- only one parent, and that one a real lugoon. Fuck, bet this one wo n't go so well. 
 
 `` Good morning, Mr. Moore. Is this your son, Joseph? I have your results from the -- all righty then.'' Meathead just ripped the envelope out of my hands and... he's... smiling? Whoof! `` Um, please, sir, do n't... hug me? Please sir I'm just doing my job. Your boy is destined to become a bandit warlord... is that right now... well congratulations. I'm sure he will crush his enemies, see them driven before him, and...'' 
 
 Gone. With his son, into that ridiculous Cadillac he rolled up in. Cadillac. Seriously, there's no justice in this world. 
 
 Two lucky ones in a row. Aint no way I get a third lucky one. Next one is going to say `` slave'', I just know it. If I'm lucky the parents wo n't ask what kind of slave. For the last five months, I've had to see parents of destined slaves go one way or the other -- either break down in denial or ask me how they could train their children towards their destiny -- which, for the manual labor slaves, is an easy answer. The sex slaves, not at all. 
 
 God I miss the days when the computer would almost always spit out answers like `` doctor'', `` carpenter'', `` farmer'', `` teacher'', `` truckdriver''... 
 
 Oh sure, it still does, sometimes. 
 
 But that was six months ago, before the bombs fell.

title: story-226
text:
Earth's Savior Becomes Earth's Doom 
 By. R. Bronko 
 
 
 Late last afternoon, several large explosions took place across the world and they all seem to have come from United State's own Dr. Manhattan. It's still too early to place an exact count of the dead, but initial estimates are in the hundreds of millions. In a moment that truly shows humanities caring side, all world leaders have stepped up and vowed to work together and form a plan to keep a so called `` super'' human from doing this again. 
 
 The blast's all occurred simultaneously at 1533hours at every major global city. Those who survived the blast zones across the world have all given the same description of the blast. We were lucky enough to speak with New York's own Daisy S., 43, `` I was in the basement parking garage of the building I work in, and noticed a sudden static energy feeling in the air. I could see the cars in the parking garage raising toward the ceiling like they weighed nothing. All I could do was stare. There suddenly came a blue flash of light from all the stairwells and that's all I remember. I awoke under a pile of rubble and started screaming. It took six hours before someone finally heard me and started digging me out. My life was saved by a Knot Top ( A local gang found in New York ) he was looking for items to loot, but he said that he could n't bring himself to ignore me, not after what had happened, he kept saying that `` Humanity has to stick together now'' and `` Everything's going to be different from here on''. I remember the feeling of joy that came over me as he pulled me out, I did n't care about the things he stood for, I was just glad he cared enough to help me. As soon as I was able to move, I just hugged him and started to cry.'' Daisy ended up having emergency surgery for a minor puncture to her lung and several broken bones. 
 
 
 The motive for the attacks has not been figured out yet and those in contact with Dr. Manhattan have been pulled in for questioning. Warrants have issued to speak with any of the `` masks'' that used work with him, including his long time girlfriend who took up her mother's moniker of `` The Silk Spectre'', Rorshach, who had recently escaped from prison during a riot caused by him murdering an inmate, and `` The Smartest Man In The World'' and ex crime fighter turned business mogul Adrien Veidt. 
 
 International funds are being set up to help those impacted by this global tragedy and this reporter wants to remind you to please take some time and donate blood, many supplies were destroyed in the blast, and with the wounded count expected to be higher than we could anticipate, short supply will be stretched thin within a matter of hours from the time this is printed.

title: story-227
text:
I've never felt so alive. In harmony with everything. The lights above my head made rainbows and particles danced in the colours. 
 
 I looked to my young daughter, and I could see everything that made her who she is. The individual atoms of the molecules that made up each cell in her body. The sadness and fear floated about her like a dark mist. I could see the parts of the DNA she got from me, and from her mother. I could see her past, present, and future. I could see into her memories, and what she feels when recalling them. I felt her love and adoration of me through them, and my eyes grew hot and wet. 
 
 I felt the muscles in my face reflexively move to part my lips in order to utter the word `` Wow'' incredulously at the level of detail I could see, but I stopped myself short. The word felt hollow. It could n't convey the level of magnificence I was witness to now. Instead I raised my hands, and analyzed each cell, each pore, each hair follicle. I could tell just by looking at them that I would now live another two hundred years, at least. 
 
 `` Dad,'' my daughter said weakly. `` Are you okay? What did you do?'' 
 
 The melodious and pleasing tones generated by her vocal chords stirred my paternal instinct to respond. My lips went to speak again, but again the words fell flat before they left my mouth. How could I ever possibly communicate this to her? To anyone. 
 
 `` I fixed myself,'' I resolved simply. I reached my hand over and pat her on the head, feeling the texture of each individual strand of hair on her head. 
 
 `` Oh. Like you do with machines?'' she asked plainly. 
 
 `` Yes,'' I managed. 
 
 The extra-sensory perception was starting to overwhelm me. I took my hand away from my daughter's head and threw the sheets off of me. I could feel the microorganisms in the bed feeding off of my warmth and shed flesh. My back itched at the thought of it. I put my feet on the floor, and felt the Earth's constant turning and movement through space. 
 
 `` You're making funny faces, daddy. Is something wrong?'' 
 
 Is this wrong, or is this right? Is this how humans are supposed to perceive their reality, and our bodies are just too weak, too slow, too frail? Are we inhibited from experiencing the universe like this, as we should? And if something was putting a filter or damper on the experience, have I now removed it? 
 
 `` I do n't know,'' I said numbly, watching the molecules of the floor dance beneath my feet. 
 
 Then I looked at my daughter again. Her past, present, and future. The incredible things she would accomplish. The amazing compassion she had for others. My eyes felt warm and wet again. I gripped her in a hug, resisting the sensory overload from the fabric of her dress, her hair brushing against my arm, her noxious natural scent and the lingering scent of soaps from her bath the night before. Her life would be rich. But it would n't be long. 
 
 As her father, I felt obligated to change that. 
 
 `` Sweetie,'' I said, taking a breath. `` Would you like me to fix you too?'' 
 
 `` I do n't know. Am I broken?'' her small precious voice communicated, muffled by my shirt. 
 
 `` No. But I can still make you better.''

title: story-228
text:
Aang pries open the hatch, his rebreather on, and feels the wind against his face and pretends that he is flying. 
 
 He could fly now, if he wanted to, lash himself to the top of the maglev with cabling and be dragged behind it like a kite. But the air's wrong. The clouds overhead are black and all-encompassing, and the air's studded with soot, hanging stagnant, gone cold. There's so much heat coming off the flooded streets, the updrafts intense, swirling and eddying past the buildings, *sky-scrapers*, the wind tearing itself to pieces. It's as if the air hates him now. Or worse, it's as if the air's dead, and left to rot. Aang holds up his palm and watches the beads of sweat run together and turn black in the wind. A thousand years of blood and ash on his hands. 
 
 `` You should talk to him,'' Reiko says from below, curled up against Appa, her visor on and her stylus painting glowing characters in mid-air. Half of her is a million li away venturing through the datagrove, dismantling SatoCorp's security. And the other half of her is somehow still here in meatspace, warm against an air bison, perfectly aware of everyone around her. Mari does n't understand how her sister manages it. Appa grunt-bellows, perhaps approving. It was hell sneaking him into freight. Mari's not used to animals, not used to twelve-year-old kids, not used to elemental bending, not used to any of this, not used to hope. The synthmeat sits sour in her stomach. 
 
 `` Why me?'' she says. 
 
 `` I'm busy,'' Reiko says dully, wired in with the data plugs glinting in her shaved scalp. Mari watches her stylus move, trying to guess the characters reversed. `` And besides, I'm not good with people. You know that.'' 
 
 `` Yeah?'' says Mari, crossing her arms. `` And what do I say?'' She hears the hatch close, she can her his footsteps on the rungs, just barely. He is light, so very light, so very vulnerable. She imagines him just blowing away at a wrong move. 
 
 `` I do n't know,'' says Reiko, and stretches out with her free hand to distractedly pet at Appa's fur. He snorts and nuzzles up against her. `` Talking to people's your job.'' 
 
 Aang drops down, his face streaked and filthy, tossing down the rebreather. `` Oh, hi,'' he says, glancing at the girls, and then curling back up in his bunk. His eyes are grey and distant. He's a thousand years away. Mari shoots a glare at her sister, who as usual ignores her completely, and then awkwardly settles next to him. 
 
 `` You can relax now,'' she tells him, reaching out for his hand. She briefly traces the blue arrow tattooed across the back, across all the soft veins. It's an old-school tattoo too, pigment pierced under the skin bit by bit with a sharpened needle, across his forehead, arms, all across his back. She shudders at the thought. `` Reiko's disabled all the SatoCorp security. They have no idea where we are now.'' 
 
 `` I did n't disable the security,'' Reiko says nasally, `` I simply marked us as an authorized party while simultaneously blocking notifications to-'' 
 
 `` Right, right!'' snaps Mari, and then turns back to Aang. `` It's going to be okay.'' 
 
 `` It's not-'' Aang says, and his voice is so high and soft and childlike. He has been preserved in glass, a relic of a gentler, kinder time. `` It's not going to change anything. I - The world's so out of balance that I do n't think anything can fix it anymore.'' He pulls his knees up to his chin, his voice breaking. `` The north and south poles have melted, the Earth Kingdom got burnt to the ground, the Fire Nation got - everyone, they -'' She's seen him scared before, seen the tattoos glowing, seen the absolute overwhelming power that the Avatar can wield. There's none of that now. No fear. No desire to flee or fight back. Just an utter, complete resignation. 
 
 `` It's not your fault!'' Mari says, scootching up against him. `` You're one kid! You ca n't be expected to fix the entire world!'' 
 
 `` I'm the Avatar!'' he says, and his voice trembles. `` I ran away! And - and all this happened! If I -'' He blinks and his eyes are watery for a moment, then resolute. `` If I had just died instead-'' 
 
 `` No!'' Mari screams, and punches her fists down on the bunk. Aang flinches. Appa raises his shaggy head. Reiko does n't look up. `` That's so stupid, ca n't you see how stupid that is? Who relies on a single person to keep the entire world in balance? What about - the rest of us? What about all the kings and lords and chieftains and presidents and - and -'' She grabs at her own shirt. `` Us! The rest of us! It took millions and millions of people for the world to get this bad, so you ca n't blame yourself for it!'' 
 
 `` But I'm the Avatar!'' 
 
 `` And who cares!'' Mari shoots back. `` That's too much to ask of one person! No matter how powerful they are!'' 
 
 `` I'm-'' Aang is shaking his head, clutching at his chest. `` I'm every Avatar that ever lived, and they all managed to-'' 
 
 `` That's the past!'' Mari says. `` Look, any of them, they're all living in you, right? Or they are you, or -'' She shakes her head. `` Whatever! Could they stop a nuclear bomb? Could they fix the economy? Could they end the penta virus? Could they -'' she gestures to her sister. `` Could they end the surveillance state and fix our broken political system where only the corporatists have any power?'' 
 
 Aang sniffles and shakes his head. `` I do n't know what most of that even means, Mari.'' 
 
 `` Exactly! The world's changed! And it would have changed if you were here! And one person, one person trying to keep the whole world in balance, it would have never been enough!'' 
 
 `` Historically,'' Reiko cuts in, raising her stylus, `` the Avatars tended towards short-term solutions that led to grave repercussions for their successors to deal with. Kyoshi is credited for the formation of the Dai Li secret police in response to widespread rebellion, leading to the centralized oppressive mechanisms of Ba Sing Se in the earliest known forms of totalitarianism that were later co-opted by the Fire Nation. And Roku's lax involvement in Fire Nation expansion - forbidding outright invasion while allowing the uninhibited growth of their military-industrial sector, is credited for-'' 
 
 `` Right, right!'' Mari cut in. She turned back to the bewildered boy. `` The point is, we all brought ourselves to this point. A hundred million of us. And it's not up to you to save us.'' She takes his hands. `` The Avatar's been dead a thousand years, and we have n't managed to kill ourselves yet. There's just you now, okay? There's just Aang.'' 
 
 He shudders, shakes like a leaf on the wind, his thin shoulders heaving, carried away by some raging force. She takes him into her arms, holds him. `` I did n't want to be the Avatar,'' he whispers into her chest. `` That's why I ran.'' 
 
 `` You do n't have to be,'' she tells him. `` That's all in the past. That's all in the past.'' 
 
 There is something in him like relief and resignation, freedom and despair, an escape and a collapse. Mari does n't know if she's helping him. She does n't know if she is telling him anything he needs to hear. A thought turns her stomach: she is completely unprepared to be a mother. `` Reiko!'' she calls out, desperate for any distraction. `` There are penguins still alive, right?'' 
 
 `` Of course,'' Reiko says, frowning slightly at her sister's incredible ignorance. `` While their natural habitat is gone, we have several extant species in captivity. There's a breeding pair at the local zoo.'' 
 
 `` Plot a course,'' Mari says, and takes Aang's hand. They have all been orphaned, by time, by circumstance, by history. Aang is from a world of myth, a world of fantasy, one just as dangerous and cruel and unfair as the real world. Once upon a time people could command the elements with their will, and they used their powers to wage war and oppress each other. She and Aang have a thousand years between them, and yet they all understand an essential truth: Sometimes you need to run away. `` Let's go penguin-sledding.'' 
 
 He looks up at her, and she thinks she sees him smile.
